preguntas.pregunta: Which patient is most likely to put muscle tremor on the tracing?
opciones: One who is cold, tense or has a nerve or muscle disorder
One who has a slow heart rate or a first-degree block
One whose chest hair keeps the electrodes from sticking
One whose lead wires were left looped across the table
preguntas.explicacion: Tremor signals come from skeletal muscle, so the patients who produce them are the ones who are shivering, tense, or living with a muscle or nerve disorder. Hair under an electrode and looped wires cause different faults: electrodes that fall off and interference from the room current.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 3.5.2 Muscle Tremor Interference
preguntas.subtema: CCMA k149 k151 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(ii) · RMA III.F.6.a.ii · NCMA 2D.6

preguntas.pregunta: Which circumstances raise the chance that a needlestick from an HIV-positive patient transmits the virus?
opciones: A visibly bloody device, a needle that was in a vein or artery, and a deep injury
A solid needle, a superficial scratch, and contact limited to intact skin
A small-bore needle, a source on treatment, and a splash onto the forearm
A used lancet, a gloved hand, and a source patient with a low viral load
preguntas.explicacion: The average risk after a percutaneous injury with HIV-infected blood is about 0.3 percent, but it is not the same for every injury. A case-control study found the risk higher when the worker met a larger quantity of blood, which showed up as a visibly bloody device, a procedure that put the needle in a vein or an artery, or a deep injury. Large-bore hollow needles and a source with a high viral load point the same way; intact skin carries no meaningful risk at all.
preguntas.fuente: NIOSH, Alert 2000-108, Risk of Infection After a Needlestick Injury: HIV; StatPearls, "Needlestick", Etiology: HIV
preguntas.subtema: What makes an exposure worse · CPT D1 1H k33 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k123 · CMA I.B.4.d · RMA III.A.2.a · NCMA 2A.8

preguntas.pregunta: Which task does the data backup plan specification of the contingency plan standard require?
opciones: Creating and keeping copies of the information that can be retrieved exactly
Restoring the information that was lost once the systems are running again
Keeping critical processes going while the office works in emergency mode
Ranking which applications and data matter most to the rest of the planning
preguntas.explicacion: The contingency plan standard splits into five specifications, and the wording of each decides the answer. The data backup plan is about making and maintaining retrievable exact copies beforehand; restoring what was lost is the disaster recovery plan, and the criticality analysis is the addressable one that ranks them.
preguntas.subtema: Data backup plan · CCMA 5 k191 · CMA III.E.1.e · RMA II.B.6.b · CMAA 7 k100 · NCMA 3.5

preguntas.pregunta: A medical assistant resigns on a Friday. Which addressable specification tells the practice what to do about her access to the system?
opciones: Termination procedures, which end access when the working arrangement finishes
Access establishment and modification, which reviews and changes a user's rights
Workforce clearance, which decides whether her access was appropriate to start
Authorization and supervision, which covers staff working where records are open
preguntas.explicacion: Workforce security carries three addressable specifications, and the one written for the end of an employment or other arrangement is termination procedures. The other three answer questions asked while the person is still working there, which is why they are easy to reach for and wrong here.

preguntas.pregunta: After installing a longer, faster pneumatic tube route, a laboratory sees more hemolysed samples. Which change in how tubes are sent is supported by the literature as reducing transport hemolysis?
opciones: Using padded inserts inside the carriers, gel tubes and properly filled tubes
Sending tubes uncapped so that pressure changes do not build up inside them
Sending each tube in its own carrier at the highest speed to shorten travel time
Chilling the carriers before use so that the red cells are less fragile in transit
preguntas.explicacion: Variables shown to increase hemolysis during transport are rapid accelerations and decelerations, greater length of travel and high speeds; variables shown to reduce it are gel tubes, properly filled tubes and padded inserts within the canisters. Higher speed works in the wrong direction, and neither uncapping nor chilling appears in the evidence the study cites.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Does Pneumatic Tube System Transport Contribute to Hemolysis in ED Blood Samples?" (West J Emerg Med 2016, PMC5017839), Discussion

preguntas.pregunta: The practice is retiring three computers and donating them to a school. Which Security Rule standard governs that?
opciones: Device and media controls, which require removing ePHI before media are reused
Workforce security, which requires authorization and supervision of staff who reach ePHI
Information access management, which limits access to what a person's role calls for
Security incident procedures, which require identifying and responding to known incidents
preguntas.explicacion: Device and media controls are a physical safeguard covering the receipt and removal of hardware and electronic media holding ePHI into and out of a facility, their movement inside it, and the final disposition of both the information and the equipment. The rule adds an explicit duty to implement procedures for removing ePHI from electronic media before those media are made available for reuse.
preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Security Rule: Physical Safeguards
preguntas.subtema: Media disposal · CCMA 7 k219 · CMA III.E.2.c · RMA II.B.4.e · CMAA 7 k100 · NCMA 4.4

preguntas.pregunta: A patient's right to refuse care is founded on which ethical principle?
opciones: Autonomy, the right to make informed decisions about one's own care
Beneficence, which asks that actions be taken for the patient's benefit
Non-maleficence, which requires steps be taken so no one is harmed
Justice, which spreads benefits and risks evenly and without bias
preguntas.explicacion: Refusal of care rests on autonomy: every person may make informed decisions about their health care, and staff should not impose their own beliefs or decisions on the patient. Beneficence, non-maleficence and justice sit alongside autonomy and guide the same difficult situations, but the refusal itself is not founded on them.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Refusal of Care", section Definition/Introduction
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2F k43 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7B k216 · CMA E.3.a (both outlines) · RMA I.C.1.a · NCMA 4.7

preguntas.pregunta: What defeats a claim of battery?
opciones: Consent, whether it was expressed or implied by taking part
Absence of any lasting injury from the contact that occurred
Absence of an intention to hurt the person who was touched
Presence of a witness who saw the contact and thought it fine
preguntas.explicacion: Battery is intentional harmful or offensive contact without consent, so consent is the defense — express, such as agreeing, or implied, such as joining in a sport. No actual damages need be shown, because the contact itself counts as the injury. Intending the contact is enough; the defendant does not have to have meant it to be harmful.
preguntas.fuente: Cornell Law School LII, Wex: battery
preguntas.subtema: Torts · CCMA k221 · CMA E.4.a(6) · RMA I.C.3 · NCMA 4.8 · CMAA 3A k31

preguntas.pregunta: In which two situations is a covered entity REQUIRED, rather than merely permitted, to disclose protected health information?
opciones: To the individual who requests access or an accounting, and to HHS investigating compliance
To law enforcement on request, and to the patient's employer for workers' compensation
To any treating provider, and to the health plan paying the claim, on request
To public health authorities, and to a coroner or medical examiner determining cause of death
preguntas.explicacion: Section 164.502(a)(2) names only two required disclosures: to the individual when requested under the right of access or the right to an accounting of disclosures, and to the Secretary of HHS when required to investigate or determine the entity's compliance. Everything else in the rule, treatment, payment, operations, public health, law enforcement, coroners and workers' compensation, is permitted under conditions but not compelled by HIPAA itself, although other laws may require some of those reports.

preguntas.pregunta: The tape on a pack has changed color after the cycle. What has that told the staff?
opciones: Only that the pack was run through a sterilization cycle, not that sterility was achieved
That the pack is sterile, since the ink reacts only when every parameter has been met
That the resistant spores inside the pack were inactivated during the exposure period
That the air was fully removed from the chamber before the steam was admitted to it
preguntas.explicacion: A chemical indicator is cheap, convenient and limited: affixed outside each pack, it shows the package went through a cycle, and it does not prove sterilization happened. Only a biological indicator made of resistant spores measures the killing power of the process directly, and an indicator inside the pack is preferred as well, to verify the sterilant got in.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization (2008), Monitoring

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with asthma needs a beta blocker for a cardiac problem. Which choice fits current recommendations?
opciones: A beta-1 selective agent such as atenolol, bisoprolol, metoprolol or esmolol
A non-selective agent such as propranolol, which binds beta-1 and beta-2 alike
Sotalol, whose potassium channel blockade also protects the airway from spasm
Labetalol, whose alpha-1 blockade cancels the airway effect of beta-2 blockade
preguntas.explicacion: Beta blockers were once ruled out in asthma altogether. Recommendations now allow the cardio-selective ones, which bind only beta-1, while the non-selective agents remain out because beta-2 blockade can bring on bronchospasm. Sotalol's extra effect is on potassium channels and it prolongs the QT interval; the alpha-1 blockade of carvedilol and labetalol helps blood pressure, not breathing.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Beta Blockers", Contraindications and Mechanism of Action

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with sickle cell disease has painful joints and a history of stroke. What is the underlying defect, and why do the cells block small vessels?
opciones: Abnormal hemoglobin S deforms the cells so they lodge in narrow capillaries
Overproduction of red cells raises viscosity and slows flow in capillaries
Antibodies agglutinate the red cells into clumps that block small vessels
Thrombocytosis triggers unwanted clots that occlude the small vessels
preguntas.explicacion: Sickle cell disease is a genetic disorder in which an abnormal hemoglobin, hemoglobin S, delivers less oxygen and makes erythrocytes take a sickle or crescent shape, especially when oxygen is low. Those cells cannot fold to squeeze through narrow capillaries, so they lodge and block flow, causing problems from painful joints to strokes. Agglutination is the transfusion-reaction mechanism, not this one.

preguntas.pregunta: Which of these is the earliest and most sensitive warning that a patient is deteriorating?
opciones: A rising respiratory rate, which usually moves before the pressure falls
A falling blood pressure, which moves before the other measurements shift
A rising temperature, which is the first of the vital signs to change
A falling oxygen saturation, which precedes any change in the breathing
preguntas.explicacion: Breathing changes early. Tachypnea is a more accurate and earlier marker of deterioration than hypotension, and it commonly comes before hypoxemia as well; one study found that a rate above 35 breaths a minute was the single strongest predictor of a life-threatening event. It is also the value most often left uncounted.

preguntas.pregunta: Which statement must appear prominently at the top of a notice of privacy practices?

The names of every business associate that may receive the patient's information during care
The civil penalty amounts for HIPAA violations, from $100 up to $50,000 per violation
A list of the 18 identifiers that turn health information into protected information
preguntas.explicacion: The notice must be written in plain language and open with a prominently displayed header telling the reader that it describes how medical information about them may be used and disclosed and how they can get access to it, and asking them to review it carefully. It then describes uses for treatment, payment and operations with examples, the other permitted purposes, the uses that require authorization, the individual's rights, the entity's duties, how to complain without retaliation, a contact person and the effective date. A reportable referral, because discussing the results counts as sending the sample elsewhere
A documentation lapse, correctable by noting the exchange in the proficiency testing record

preguntas.pregunta: A citrate tube for a prothrombin time is put in the specimen refrigerator to await pick-up. Why is that the wrong choice?

Whole blood for these assays is held frozen, and chilling is not enough
Refrigeration bursts the red cells and haemolyses the whole specimen
Refrigeration hardens the gel barrier and traps the plasma underneath
preguntas.explicacion: Whole blood drawn for clotting tests is kept at room temperature, roughly eighteen to twenty-four degrees, and refrigeration is avoided because cold can activate factor VII. Capacity: the patient's understanding was never assessed
Documentation: the consent form was never signed

Care stops, but the practice must file the records with the state board
Care stops, provided the patient is handed a list of low-cost clinics

preguntas.pregunta: Among the oral antidiabetic agents, which one carries the highest hypoglycemia risk because of its long half-life and active metabolites?
opciones: Glyburide
Glipizide
Glimepiride
Repaglinide
preguntas.explicacion: All three sulfonylureas named here can drop the glucose, but glyburide carries the highest risk: it lasts a long time and leaves active metabolites behind, which is also why it is avoided once the eGFR falls under 30. preguntas.pregunta: Which safety data sheet section tells you which extinguishing agent is right for a fire involving that chemical, and which is not?
opciones: Section 5, which also warns about products given off as it burns
Section 6, which also covers containment and cleanup after a spill
Section 9, which also gives the flash point and the boiling range
Section 7, which also covers safe storage and incompatible products
preguntas.explicacion: Section 5 is written for the fire: which extinguishing equipment is suitable and which is not appropriate for a given situation, the specific hazards the chemical develops while burning, such as hazardous combustion products, and any special protection or precautions for the people fighting it. preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist is stuck at the end of her shift and says she will go to occupational health tomorrow. What is the recommendation?

Be seen within seven days, the deadline that applies to hepatitis B treatment
Be seen at the end of the shift, once the incident report has been written
Be seen within ninety days, while the baseline sample is being preserved
preguntas.explicacion: Follow-up with occupational health should be immediate rather than delayed by twelve to seventy-two hours, because the decisions that depend on it are time-sensitive: baseline testing, hepatitis B immune globulin within about a day, and antiretroviral prophylaxis started preferably within hours. The housing is coloured orange to match an insulin syringe hub

Thirty minutes early, so staff can complete the whole intake by telephone

Only the demographic fields the practice sends in a standard claim transaction

Seated upright, with the chin lifted and eyes closed
Standing, leaning back against the corridor wall
Seated backwards, with both legs stretched out flat

A gain in lean mass, which the index reads as a fall in body fat
A measurement error, since the index moves slowly by its nature

Accept the correct statement, since saying it right proves he can do it
Repeat the same explanation once more and end the teaching there
Have him write the dose and the times down and file the note in the chart

Waiting for the coordinator's shift to start before the box is touched at all

preguntas.pregunta: A differential on a patient with a bacterial infection shows 80 percent of one leukocyte type. Which type is normally the most common and rises with bacterial infection?

Lymphocytes, normally 20 to 30 percent of leukocytes
Monocytes, normally 2 to 8 percent of leukocytes
Eosinophils, normally 2 to 4 percent of leukocytes

Stop the test and report it to the provider as a failed glucose screen
Offer her a light snack to settle her stomach before the next blood draw

1 gram equals 100 milligrams, and 1 milligram equals 100 micrograms
1 gram equals 1000 micrograms, and 1 milligram equals 1000 grams
1 gram equals 10 milligrams, and 1 milligram equals 10 micrograms
preguntas.explicacion: The metric system is built on units of ten, so converting is a matter of moving the decimal point. It is a thrombolytic; it converts plasminogen into plasmin
It inactivates factor X, in the same way antithrombin does
It blocks vitamin K, so the liver makes fewer clotting factors

Once in the morning only, after a strict 12-hour overnight fast

preguntas.explicacion: The footnote of the panel states that the percentages rest on a 2,000-calorie day, offered as general advice. preguntas.pregunta: A patient's order calls for every tube on the chart. Which one is filled ninth?

The purple top tube used for haematology and cross-match
The light grey top tube used for glucose determinations
The light green tube used for chemistry panels on plasma

preguntas.pregunta: A patient without insurance asks where she can be seen for primary care on a sliding scale based on what she can pay. What fits?
opciones: A federally qualified health center, whose fees slide with the patient's ability to pay
An ambulatory surgical center, where Part B pays the facility fee for an approved surgery
A hospital emergency department, which evaluates a sudden illness that quickly worsens
A skilled nursing facility, where daily skilled nursing or therapy is given short term
preguntas.explicacion: Federally qualified health centers are federally funded nonprofit centers and clinics that serve areas and populations which are medically underserved. preguntas.pregunta: What is a Medicare Advantage Plan?
opciones: A private plan under contract with Medicare that delivers Part A and Part B benefits
A private plan sold by insurers that pays the patient's share of Original Medicare
A federal plan that replaces Part A for patients treated in a network of hospitals
A state plan that covers premiums and deductibles for people with low income
preguntas.explicacion: Medicare Advantage, also called Part C, is offered by private companies that contract with Medicare to provide all Part A and Part B benefits, usually with drug coverage as well; the types include health maintenance and preferred provider organizations. Private insurance that pays the patient's share of Original Medicare is Medigap, and help with premiums for people with low income comes through Medicaid.

preguntas.pregunta: On a paediatric ward the child's wristband is found clipped to the cot rail rather than on the child. What does the WHO instruct?
opciones: Do not use it; ask the parent or guardian for the child's full name
Use it, because the cot is assigned to that child on the ward admission list
Use the cot number as the second identifier next to the form
Ask the child directly to state the full name and date of birth
preguntas.explicacion: Chapter 6 says a wrist or foot band counts only if it is attached to the patient; a band on the bed or cot, and the bed number, are not to be used. opciones: Saturated fat, sodium and added sugars
Saturated fat, sodium and dietary fiber
Total fat, total sugars and total carbohydrate
Cholesterol, protein and trans fat
preguntas.explicacion: The label separates nutrients to get less of, which are saturated fat, sodium and added sugars, from nutrients to get more of: dietary fiber, vitamin D, calcium, iron and potassium. opciones: Prescriptions, over-the-counter drugs, vitamins, supplements and herbals
Prescriptions and over-the-counter drugs, but not vitamins or supplements
Prescriptions only, since the rest are not entered in the medication list
Prescriptions and the pill organizer, but not the original containers
preguntas.explicacion: The review covers every prescription, every over-the-counter product, all vitamins, supplements and herbal medicines, plus topicals, liquids, injections and inhalants, and the pills in both their original bottles and any organizer. preguntas.pregunta: A 4-year-old needs a finger-prick. Which puncture depth is recommended for that age?
opciones: 1.5 mm, the depth for a child over 6 months and under 8 years
2.4 mm, the depth for a child over 6 months and under 8 years
0.85 mm, the depth for any child who has not reached school age
2.2 mm, the longest lancet, because the finger has no bone risk
preguntas.explicacion: There are two finger-prick depths for children: 1.5 mm for a child over 6 months and below 8 years, and 2.4 mm for a child over 8 years. The 0.85 mm lancet is the one made for premature neonates. The 2.2 mm lancet is the longest typically used in an adult finger-prick because the depth there should not exceed 2.4 mm, and that limit exists precisely to protect bone.

preguntas.pregunta: A glucometer and its lancet platform are used for several inpatients during a round. What does best practice require?
opciones: Dedicate it to one patient, or clean and disinfect it between uses
Change the lancet and wipe the platform with a dry gauze pad
Rinse the platform under running water at the end of the round
Keep it in a clean bag between patients, which avoids contact
preguntas.explicacion: For small quantities of capillary blood the equipment is single-use: a lancet, or a retractable lancet, and a platform or glucometer that is either dedicated to one patient for the hospital stay or cleaned of all visible dirt and disinfected with alcohol between uses. The warning behind the rule is on the record: hepatitis infections have been transmitted to patients when platforms or glucometers were used on several people without that reprocessing.

preguntas.pregunta: A glucose drawn from the arm carrying a glucose infusion comes back far above the critical limit, and the patient looks well. What clears the picture?
opciones: Testing a second specimen collected properly from another site
Repeating the measurement twice on the same tube and averaging
Reporting the figure and letting the clinician judge the context
Diluting the specimen and correcting for the dilution factor used
preguntas.explicacion: Preanalytical influences are named outright as a frequent source of results that only look critical, and the example given is a glucose drawn through a venous catheter that had been used for a glucose infusion. Cases like that are normally settled by testing another, properly collected specimen; repeating the same contaminated tube only confirms the contamination.

opciones: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, a lung disease
Chronic obstructive peptic disorder, a stomach disease
Congenital obstructive pulmonary defect, a lung disease
Chronic occlusive peripheral disease, an artery disease
preguntas.explicacion: COPD is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, the long-standing lung condition that makes breathing hard. The look-alike abbreviations belong elsewhere: PUD is peptic ulcer disease, CHD is congenital heart disease and PAD is peripheral arterial disease, the arteries outside the heart.

preguntas.pregunta: A nasal cannula is running at 4 L/min. Roughly what oxygen concentration does that deliver?
opciones: Somewhere in the 24% to 40% band that 1 to 6 L/min produces
Somewhere in the 40% to 60% band that 1 to 6 L/min produces
Close to 50%, which is what a face tent reaches at high flow
Between 60% and 80%, the range of a mask with a reservoir bag
preguntas.explicacion: A cannula runs at one to six liters a minute and gives roughly 24% to 40% oxygen; the figure is approximate because how much room air is mixed in depends on the patient's rate and depth of breathing. A simple face mask at 5 to 10 L/min gives about 40% to 60%, a face tent up to 15 L/min about 50%, and a nonrebreather at 10 to 15 L/min more still.

preguntas.pregunta: A box of evacuated tubes is found to be past its expiration date. What two problems do expired tubes present?
opciones: Reduced ability to draw blood in, and additives that may have degraded
Loss of sterility of the stopper, and a gel that no longer separates serum
A higher risk of haemolysis, and colours that no longer match the order of draw
Cracks in the plastic, and an anticoagulant that turns plasma into serum
preguntas.explicacion: Expiration dates matter because expired vacuum tubes have a decreased capacity to aspirate blood and their additives may be degraded, so even small deviations can affect the results. The other options mix real problems from the tube collection review, such as a missing anticoagulant or a lost vacuum after uncapping, with effects the chapter does not attribute to expiry.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with diabetes fasted 14 hours for a hemoglobin A1C 'to be safe'. Which statement is correct?
opciones: Fasting was not needed; the A1C reflects average glucose over about 3 months
Fasting was needed; the A1C requires no caloric intake for at least 8 full hours
Fasting was needed; samples are drawn before and after a sugary drink
Fasting was harmful; the A1C result will now read falsely low
preguntas.explicacion: The hemoglobin A1C test uses one sample, needs no fasting, and reports average blood glucose over the past 3 months. The 8-hour rule with no caloric intake applies to the fasting plasma glucose, and the drink-then-resample sequence is the tolerance test. Fasting is simply not part of the A1C's preparation.

preguntas.pregunta: A transplant centre needs a package on a Sunday. Which feature of Priority Mail Express answers that need?
opciones: It delivers seven days a week, all year, with limited exceptions to that rule
It delivers on weekdays and adds a Saturday run when the label is bought online
It delivers seven days a week only to post office box addresses in large markets
It delivers on any day agreed with the receiving office when the package is sent
preguntas.explicacion: Express is the fastest domestic service and it runs seven days a week, 365 days a year, with limited exceptions. Most addresses see it in one to three days, and the delivery time carries a money-back guarantee, which the two-to-three-day estimate of Priority Mail does not.

preguntas.pregunta: What is the relationship between an ethical principle and a patient right?
opciones: A right appears when a body with authority enforces an ethical standard
A right appears when a professional society publishes it in its own code
A right appears when a majority of patients in a survey come to expect it
A right and an ethical principle are the same thing under a different name
preguntas.explicacion: Human rights are the minimum standards for how people can expect to be treated; ethics are the customary standards for how people should treat others. Every patient right rests on one or more ethical principles, and a right exists at the moment an organization with the authority to enforce that ethical standard actually enforces it. As ethics shift over time, so do rights.

preguntas.pregunta: A practice takes its first new patients through an online intake before any in-person visit. What does the notice rule require?
opciones: An electronic notice sent automatically with the first request, and an attempt at a return receipt
A paper notice mailed within thirty days of the electronic request for service being received
An electronic notice posted on the web site only, since online patients can read it there
A telephone call reading the notice aloud, since electronic delivery cannot be acknowledged
preguntas.explicacion: Where first service delivery happens over the Internet, by e-mail or otherwise electronically, the provider must send an electronic notice automatically and at the same time as the individual's first request for service, and must make a good faith effort to obtain a return receipt or other transmission in response. A covered entity must also post the notice prominently on any web site describing its services or benefits.

preguntas.pregunta: What must a safety data sheet do when its preparer finds no information for a required element?
opciones: Say that no applicable information was found for that element
Leave that element blank, which is read as not applicable
Copy the entry from a sheet for a similar product in the family
Move the element to section 16 with the other information
preguntas.explicacion: Silence is not allowed. Where the preparer finds no relevant information for a required element, the sheet has to state that no applicable information was found, and the same rule is repeated for the physical and chemical properties in section 9: an item that is not relevant or not available gets a note to that effect for that property. A blank leaves the reader unable to tell an absent hazard from an unresearched one.

preguntas.pregunta: A geriatric intake separates basic from instrumental activities of daily living. Which pair is right?
opciones: Bathing and dressing are basic; shopping and handling finances are instrumental
Shopping and cooking are basic; bathing and toileting are instrumental activities
Walking and feeding are basic; grooming and bladder control are instrumental
Driving and using the telephone are basic; dressing and feeding are instrumental
preguntas.explicacion: Basic activities are self-care: feeding, dressing, bathing, toileting, grooming and control of bladder and bowel. Instrumental ones are what independent living needs on top of that: taking medicines, shopping, cooking, transport, finances, housework and the telephone. The Katz index measures the first group and the Lawton scale the second.

preguntas.pregunta: How many elements must a written identity theft prevention program contain under the Red Flags Rule?
opciones: Four: identify, detect, respond and update
Three: identify, detect and report to the police
Five: identify, detect, respond, update and insure
Two: identify the red flags and train the staff on them
preguntas.explicacion: The program must include reasonable policies for identifying the red flags of identity theft in day-to-day operations, procedures designed to detect the flags it identified, the actions to take when one is detected, and a way of keeping the program current against new threats. A red flag is a suspicious pattern, practice or activity signalling possible identity theft, such as an identification document that does not look genuine.

preguntas.pregunta: A plan holds a Medicare Advantage contract. For how long must it keep the books and records behind that contract?
opciones: Ten years, so that the accounting and the services can be audited and inspected
Seven years from the date of service, as with orders and certifications in Part B
Five years, as with the medical records a hospital keeps to take part in Medicare
Six years from creation, as with the documentation the privacy standards require
preguntas.explicacion: Every retention period in this area belongs to a different rule, and the trap is borrowing one for another. The Medicare Advantage contract obliges the organization to keep its books, records and other evidence of accounting for ten years, enough for CMS to audit the finances and to inspect the quality and timeliness of the services.

preguntas.pregunta: An adult has a body mass index of 41.2. How is that classified?
opciones: Class 3 obesity, also called severe obesity, from 40.0 upward
Class 2 obesity, the band that runs from 35.0 to 39.9
Class 1 obesity, the band that runs from 30.0 to 39.9
Obesity without a class, since the classes stop at 40.0
preguntas.explicacion: Obesity is divided into three classes: 30.0 to 34.9, 35.0 to 39.9, and 40.0 or greater, the last of which is also called severe obesity. Naming the class matters because the risk of high blood pressure, type 2 diabetes and high cholesterol rises with it, but the index is still a screening measure, not a diagnosis.

preguntas.pregunta: What are the four types of precautionary statements found on a Hazard Communication label?
opciones: Prevention, response, storage and disposal
Physical, health, environmental and unclassified
Identification, composition, handling and transport
Danger, warning, caution and notice
preguntas.explicacion: Precautionary statements describe the measures recommended to minimize or prevent harm from exposure, storage or handling, and they come in four types: prevention, to limit exposure; response, for spills, emergencies and first aid; storage; and disposal. Physical, health and environmental are the three hazard groups of the GHS; identification, composition, handling and transport are SDS section titles; and Danger and Warning are the only two signal words, so caution and notice do not exist in this system.

preguntas.pregunta: A mother is sent home to collect urine from her 6-month-old with an adhesive bag. Which instruction is correct?
opciones: Wash the genital area, apply the bag, put a diaper over it, check the baby often and remove the bag once urine collects
Apply the bag over the unwashed skin so the adhesive holds better, and leave it in place until the next diaper change
Wash the genital area, apply the bag without a diaper so it is visible, and leave it on for exactly 24 hours
Wash the genital area with an antiseptic, pass a small catheter into the bladder and drain the urine into the bag
preguntas.explicacion: The area around the urethra is washed with the soap or wipes the provider recommends, the bag is opened and stuck on (the whole penis inside it, or over the labia), a diaper goes on over the bag, and the baby is checked often. Active infants can displace the bag, so extra bags are useful. The urine is emptied into the container without touching its inside and, at home, kept in a plastic bag in the refrigerator. Catheterization is done by a provider.

preguntas.pregunta: A prenatal clinic wants one body measurement to follow nutritional status. Which one is reported as the measurement of choice in pregnancy?

Waist circumference, taken over each hip bone at the mid-axillary line
Body mass index, worked out again from height and weight at each visit
Triceps skinfold, taken with calipers just above the midpoint of the arm
preguntas.explicacion: Mid-upper arm circumference helps grade how severe malnutrition is, and one study reports it as the anthropometric measurement of choice in the pregnant population. A preferred provider organization plan
A point of service plan with referrals
A fee-for-service indemnity arrangement
preguntas.explicacion: The exclusive provider organization is the managed care plan whose coverage stops at the edge of the network, with the emergency exception. preguntas.pregunta: How is an infant under 2 years weighed?
opciones: Undressed and with the diaper off, on a calibrated beam or digital infant scale
In a clean diaper and light clothing, on a calibrated beam or digital infant scale
Held by a parent on a floor scale, with the parent's weight subtracted afterward
Undressed, on the same floor scale used for children older than 24 months
preguntas.explicacion: For children under 2 the scale is a calibrated beam or a digital infant scale, and the child is weighed with the clothes off and the diaper removed, to the nearest 0.01 kg or half an ounce. From 24 months onward a balanced or electronic floor scale is used instead.

preguntas.pregunta: In a laboratory that works with concentrated HIV or HBV, what does the standard require of the biosafety manual?
opciones: It is reviewed and updated at least yearly, and staff must read and follow it
It is written once at start-up and kept for the duration of employment
It is posted at the door with the name and phone of the laboratory director
It takes the place of the exposure control plan for employees in that area
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (e)(2)(ii)(M) asks for a biosafety manual to be prepared or adopted, then reviewed and updated periodically, at least annually and more often if needed. What goes on the door is the warning sign of (g)(1)(ii)(A). These requirements come on top of the exposure control plan, which paragraph (c) still demands.

That the barcode was printed within the last 30 minutes

preguntas.pregunta: How long does a fainting episode usually last, and what is the typical recovery?
opciones: Usually less than a couple of minutes, with quick recovery
Usually 10 to 15 minutes, with gradual recovery over an hour
Usually a few seconds, with confusion for several minutes afterwards
Usually 5 to 10 minutes, with weakness for the rest of the day
preguntas.explicacion: Fainting is a brief loss of consciousness from a drop in blood flow to the brain, most often lasting less than a couple of minutes, with quick recovery; the medical name is syncope. Ten to fifteen minutes is how long the person is kept lying down afterwards, and confusion on waking points to a seizure rather than syncope.

preguntas.pregunta: A swab arrives labeled with the patient's name and identification number but no indication of where on the body it was taken. Under CLIA's specimen labeling policy element, what is missing?
opciones: The specimen source, which must appear on the label when appropriate
The test requested, which must be written on every specimen container
The collector's signature, which is required on all microbiology specimens
The date of birth, which is mandatory on the label for every specimen
preguntas.explicacion: 42 CFR 493.1242(a)(3) requires the laboratory's labeling procedure to cover the patient's name or unique identifier and, when appropriate, the specimen source; for a swab the site is exactly that appropriate case. preguntas.pregunta: A soft fatty lump under the skin is reported as a lipoma. Which two word parts build that term?
opciones: A root meaning fat plus an ending meaning tumor
A root meaning fat plus an ending meaning inflammation
A root meaning muscle plus an ending meaning tumor
A root meaning fat plus an ending meaning enlargement
preguntas.explicacion: Lip- and lipo- name fat, and so does adip-; the ending -oma is a tumor. The endings that crowd around it say something else entirely: -itis is inflammation, -megaly is enlargement and -osis is an abnormal condition. Muscle is my- or myo-, so a tumor built on that root would be a myoma.

preguntas.pregunta: A hospital gives its laboratory technologists access to laboratory records but not to the full medical history. What is that practice called, and does HIPAA allow it?
opciones: Selective, role-based access, which is exactly the way the rule expects internal access to work
Selective, role-based access, which the rule discourages because it slows care coordination
A limited data set, which HIPAA permits only for research, public health or health operations
A hybrid entity designation, which limits the rules to the components that do covered work
preguntas.explicacion: Limiting each worker to the part of the record their role requires is precisely what the rule asks for: policies must identify the persons or classes of persons who need access, the categories of information they need, and the conditions of that access. A limited data set is a stripped-down form of information for research and similar uses, and a hybrid entity is an organizational choice, not an access control.

preguntas.pregunta: A denial arrives stating that the billed procedure differs from the one authorized. What does the source of that problem suggest for next time?
opciones: Update the authorization before the claim goes out when the procedure changes
Send the claim unchanged, since the payer matches authorizations automatically
Bill the patient for the difference, since the authorization covered part of it
Wait for the appeal decision before asking the payer to change any authorization
preguntas.explicacion: Among the causes of denials, billing a procedure code that differs from the authorized one is listed with its own remedy: update the information before submission or justify the discrepancy clearly. Some payers will change an authorization only up to 14 days past the date of service, after which the denial tends to become permanent, so waiting for an appeal wastes the window. preguntas.pregunta: What does a tourniquet do that makes venipuncture easier?
opciones: It creates temporary pressure and an artificial occlusion, making the veins easier to identify
It stops arterial inflow so that the veins below it empty and become straighter
It disinfects the skin above the site, so the alcohol contact time can be shortened
It keeps the blood from clotting in the tubing of a winged collection set
preguntas.explicacion: The tourniquet produces temporary pressure and an artificial occlusion of blood flow, which helps the phlebotomist find the veins, and cites studies showing the veins dilate and gain surface area right after a tightly placed tourniquet. It must not stop arterial flow, it has no antiseptic role, and it has nothing to do with the air in butterfly tubing.

preguntas.pregunta: A parent asks for the lab results of their 8-year-old child. How does HIPAA treat the parent?
opciones: As the child's personal representative, acting as the individual for that PHI
As a third party who needs the child's own signed authorization first
As a family member entitled only to a verbal summary at the visit
As a personal representative only after a court has appointed the parent as guardian
preguntas.explicacion: Section 164.502(g) requires a covered entity to treat a personal representative as the individual. For an unemancipated minor, a parent, guardian or person acting in loco parentis with authority under applicable law to make health care decisions is the personal representative for the PHI relevant to that role, without any court appointment. The exceptions are services the minor may lawfully consent to alone, and situations of abuse or endangerment where the entity may decline to treat the person as the representative; state law can expand or restrict parental access.

preguntas.pregunta: A report describes one structure as cranial to another. Which directional term is used for that same idea?
opciones: Superior, toward the head end of the body
Inferior, away from the head end of the body
Anterior, toward the front of the body
Posterior, toward the back of the body
preguntas.explicacion: Most directional terms travel in pairs that mean the same thing: superior and cranial point toward the head, inferior and caudal away from it, anterior and ventral name the front, and posterior and dorsal the back. preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks how long she should scrub when washing her hands at home. What is the answer, and when does it matter most?
opciones: At least 20 seconds, including before, during and after preparing food
At least 20 seconds, but only after using the toilet or changing a diaper
At least 10 seconds, including before, during and after preparing food
At least 60 seconds, including before, during and after preparing food
preguntas.explicacion: Hands are scrubbed well and often, for at least 20 seconds. The moments that matter most are the ones where germs are picked up or passed on: before, during and after handling food, before eating, around caring for someone sick or treating a wound, after the toilet or diapers, after coughing or sneezing, and after animals or garbage.

preguntas.pregunta: A specimen stiff enough to puncture its primary container is being shipped to a reference laboratory. What does the standard add?
opciones: A secondary container that resists puncture as well as leakage, and is labeled
A secondary container that closes and holds fluids, with no puncture requirement
A red bag around the primary container, which substitutes for the outer label
A label stating which portion of the primary container remains contaminated
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(2)(xiii) builds up in three steps. The specimen goes in a container that will not leak. If the outside of that container becomes contaminated, subparagraph (B) puts it inside a second leakproof container that is labeled or color-coded. And subparagraph (C) adds the extra requirement here: when the specimen itself could puncture the primary container, the secondary one must be puncture-resistant on top of everything else. The label naming the contaminated portion is for equipment being serviced, under (g)(1)(i)(H).

preguntas.pregunta: When a parent authorizes a procedure for their 9-year-old, what is that authorization called?
opciones: Informed permission, since consent itself belongs to the patient
Implied consent, because the parent brought the child in for care
Proxy consent, given under a durable power of attorney for the child
Waived consent, the category used when a patient cannot sign for themselves
preguntas.explicacion: Children, typically those under 18, cannot give informed consent, so the parent or legal guardian permits the treatment and the process is named informed permission instead. Implied consent is inferred from the patient's own situation, such as an emergency. A waiver is when the patient voluntarily gives the consent process up, and a power of attorney is a document an adult signs about their own care.

preguntas.pregunta: How is malpractice defined as a legal term?
opciones: Professional negligence: breaching the duty to follow accepted professional standards
Any error a professional makes while a patient is under that professional's care
An intentional act by a professional that the client did not agree to beforehand
A breach of the written contract between a professional and the paying client
preguntas.explicacion: Malpractice is professional negligence: a tort committed when a professional breaches the duty owed to a client, and that duty is generally to follow generally accepted professional standards. Every other element of a negligence tort still has to be shown too: the duty, the breach, both kinds of causation and the damages. Suits are most common against doctors and lawyers.

preguntas.pregunta: At what speed does the paper run during a standard recording?
opciones: 25 mm per second, so one large square is 0.2 seconds
50 mm per second, so one large square is 0.2 seconds
25 mm per second, so one large square is 0.4 seconds
10 mm per second, so one large square is 0.5 seconds

preguntas.pregunta: Flash (immediate-use) steam sterilization was originally defined with which cycle?
opciones: An unwrapped item at 132 °C for 3 minutes at 27-28 pounds of pressure, gravity displacement
An unwrapped item at 121 °C for 3 minutes at 27-28 pounds of pressure, gravity displacement
A single-wrapped item at 132 °C for 10 minutes at 15-16 pounds of pressure, prevacuum
An unwrapped item at 135 °C for 30 minutes at 27-28 pounds of pressure, prevacuum
preguntas.explicacion: The original definition was an unwrapped object held at 132 °C for three minutes at 27 to 28 pounds of pressure in a gravity displacement machine. preguntas.pregunta: A heel-prick that goes too deep in a neonate can infect which structure?
opciones: The heel bone (calcaneus), causing osteomyelitis
The tibial artery, causing septic arteritis
The plantar fascia, causing chronic fasciitis
The posterior tibial tendon, causing tendinitis
preguntas.explicacion: Osteomyelitis of the heel bone, the calcaneus, is one of the complications of capillary sampling the WHO names. The depth rules exist to avoid it: no heel-prick beyond 2.4 mm, avoid the posterior heel where skin to bone is 2.33 mm in a 3 kg baby, and use the medial or lateral plantar surface where the distance is 3.32 mm. The tibial artery risk is laceration, not infection.

preguntas.pregunta: Which spores are used in the biological indicator for a steam sterilizer, and which for dry heat and ethylene oxide?
opciones: Geobacillus stearothermophilus for steam, and Bacillus atrophaeus for dry heat and ethylene oxide
Bacillus atrophaeus for steam, and Geobacillus stearothermophilus for dry heat and ethylene oxide
Geobacillus stearothermophilus for both, incubated at two different temperatures by method
Bacillus atrophaeus for both, with a longer incubation used for the steam sterilizer strips
preguntas.explicacion: Steam, hydrogen peroxide gas plasma and liquid peracetic acid are monitored with Geobacillus stearothermophilus spores, incubated at 55 to 60 °C; ethylene oxide and dry heat use Bacillus atrophaeus, incubated at 35 to 37 °C. These spores are chosen because they resist the agent more than the bioburden found on the devices themselves.

preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist raises a needle toward a patient who has clearly refused, and the patient recoils. No contact occurs. Which tort fits?
opciones: Assault, since the patient was put in apprehension of imminent contact
Battery, since raising the needle is itself an offensive act toward them
False imprisonment, since the patient was held in the chair by the act
Negligence, since a reasonable phlebotomist would not have done that
preguntas.explicacion: Assault is an intentional act that puts another person in reasonable apprehension of imminent harmful or offensive contact. No physical injury is needed; the actor must have intended the contact and the victim must have been aware it might occur. Battery is the contact itself, so without contact there is no battery.

preguntas.pregunta: In the WHO's venipuncture steps, the routine skin prep is a 70% alcohol swab for 30 seconds. Which collection is explicitly excluded from that routine prep?
opciones: A blood culture, which uses a different site preparation
A draw for potassium or uric acid, which uses povidone-iodine
A capillary puncture of the heel in a newborn
A draw from a patient who has an IV line in the other arm
preguntas.explicacion: Step 5 of the WHO procedure applies the 70% alcohol swab for 30 seconds, followed by 30 seconds of drying, unless the collector is drawing blood cultures or preparing for a blood collection, which have their own skin preparation. The same step notes that alcohol is preferred over povidone-iodine precisely because iodine contamination can falsely raise potassium, phosphorus and uric acid, so those tests are not an exception.

Five years from the date of service
Six years from the date of service
Three years from the date of service

70% isopropyl alcohol
Chlorhexidine
Soap and water

The unspecified code for that condition, which NOS also stands for
The excluded code above the note, which is never reported alongside

The parasagittal or lateral plane
The frontal or coronal plane
The axial or cross-sectional plane

On the inner leg, about 10 to 15 cm above the ankle

preguntas.pregunta: Which sections of a safety data sheet are meant to be read first, for quick general information about a chemical?

Sections 9 through 11 and 16, the technical and scientific ones
Sections 12 through 15, the ones OSHA does not enforce at all

preguntas.pregunta: What did comparison of dedicated phlebotomy teams with staff who have broader duties show?

The teams reached higher rates of contamination, despite equal training
The two groups performed identically once both had the same training
The teams drew more tubes per hour but haemolysed more specimens
preguntas.explicacion: Laboratory staff and members of phlebotomy teams appear to achieve lower rates of contamination than staff whose responsibilities are broader, even where the training received is the same. It is one of the arguments for formal training and supervised practice in this procedure.

preguntas.pregunta: A nurse inoculates a blood culture bottle straight from the syringe used for the draw, then fills the second bottle with 1 mL. Which two points of technique were missed?
opciones: Changing the needle before inoculating the bottle, and inoculating about 10 % of the medium volume (3 mL into 30 mL)
Cleaning the bottle bung with alcohol only after inoculation, and inoculating about 50 % of the medium volume
Warming the bottle to 37 °C before inoculation, and inoculating at most 1 mL so that the medium is not diluted
Drawing the culture after the first antibiotic dose, and inoculating 10 mL into each bottle regardless of medium volume
preguntas.explicacion: For blood cultures the syringe needle is changed before the culture bottle is inoculated, to limit contamination, the rubber bung is cleaned with iodine solution before and after the injection, and the blood volume is roughly 10 % of the medium, for example 3 mL into 30 mL. The laboratory is consulted about the right media for the suspected pathogens, and cultures are drawn, whenever possible, before antimicrobial therapy starts.

preguntas.pregunta: A haemolysed specimen arrives for an erythrocyte sedimentation rate. Why is that a particular problem for this test?
opciones: Free haemoglobin reddens the plasma and hides the boundary that is read
Free haemoglobin clots the specimen and stops the red cells from settling
Free haemoglobin binds the citrate and leaves the specimen unanticoagulated
Free haemoglobin raises the viscosity so the red cells settle far too quickly
preguntas.explicacion: The reading is taken where the settled red cells end and clear plasma begins. Haemolysis releases haemoglobin into the plasma and turns it red, so that boundary can no longer be picked out; an icteric sample causes the same trouble with dark yellow plasma.

preguntas.pregunta: Which instrument gives the most accurate recumbent length in an infant?
opciones: An infantometer, which holds the baby in position while the length is read
A horizontal length scale, the flexible scale laid alongside a small baby
A stadiometer laid on its side, with the head and the feet against it
A nonstretchable tape measure run from the crown of the head to the heel
preguntas.explicacion: Length in a baby who cannot stand is taken lying down, and the instrument matters. The horizontal length scale is a flexible scale for that job; the infantometer does the same with greater accuracy because it holds the infant securely in position. preguntas.pregunta: How far does the primary payer go before a claim passes to the secondary payer?
opciones: It pays up to the limits of its own coverage and sends on the rest of the balance
It pays the whole allowed amount and sends on only the patient's own cost sharing
It pays half of the allowed amount and sends on the remaining half of the balance
It pays up to the limits of the secondary plan and sends on the unpaid remainder
preguntas.explicacion: The primary payer pays up to the limits of its coverage and then passes the rest of the balance to the secondary payer. If the secondary payer does not cover that remainder, the patient can be left owing it. This order of payment is what coordination of benefits means. preguntas.pregunta: A colleague asks where to place the stethoscope for a blood pressure reading. Where is the brachial pulse felt?
opciones: Just medial to the biceps tendon
Just lateral to the biceps tendon
Directly over the median cubital vein
Just medial to the pronator teres muscle
preguntas.explicacion: The brachial artery crosses the fossa medial to the biceps tendon, and that is where the pulse is palpated and where the stethoscope goes when blood pressure is measured. Knowing the line matters at the bedside, because the artery lies under the same small triangle used for venipuncture.

preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist skips hand hygiene after a patient with an infection and carries the organism to the next patient without becoming infected herself. In epidemiologic terms she is which of these?
opciones: A passive carrier, contaminated but not infected
An active carrier, infected but without symptoms
A biological vector, in which the pathogen reproduces
A nonliving reservoir, like contaminated water
preguntas.explicacion: A carrier is an individual who can transmit a pathogen without showing symptoms. A passive carrier is contaminated and can mechanically pass the pathogen to another host but is not infected; the microbiology text uses precisely the example of a health-care professional who fails to wash hands after seeing an infected patient. An active carrier is infected, with or without symptoms, and may transmit during incubation or convalescence. Vectors are animals, usually arthropods, and reservoirs are where pathogens normally reside.
preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Microbiology, 16.3 Modes of Disease Transmission, Reservoirs and Carriers

preguntas.pregunta: What can poor infection control during a draw produce, besides risk to the worker?
opciones: Bacterial infection where the needle went in, and contaminated specimens
Bacterial infection where the needle went in, and a lost tube vacuum
Haemolysis of the specimen, and degradation of the tube additive
A prolonged clotting time, and a falsely low platelet count reported
preguntas.explicacion: Weak infection prevention and control practices can lead to bacterial infection at the site where the needle was inserted and to contamination of the specimens themselves. It is one reason the cleaned site is not touched again and single-use devices are never shared between patients.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 1.1.1

preguntas.pregunta: Who legally requires a positive result for a notifiable condition to be reported, and to whom?
opciones: State law requires it to the health department; notifying the CDC is voluntary
Federal law requires it to the CDC; notifying the health department is voluntary
State law requires it to the CDC, which then informs the health department
Accreditation standards require it to both, on the same reporting form
preguntas.explicacion: Hospitals, providers and laboratories report positive results or diagnosed cases to the appropriate health department under state disease reporting laws, and that case reporting is mandatory. What the state and local health departments then send on to the CDC is de-identified data about confirmed cases, and that notification is voluntary.

preguntas.pregunta: Before agreeing, the patient asks when the results will be back. How does that question relate to obtaining consent?
opciones: Answer it; consent follows once all questions, including result timing, are addressed
Decline to answer; discussing results in any form is the physician's role alone
Proceed with the draw and refer the question to the front desk afterwards
Ask the patient to sign first, then answer the question while preparing the tubes
preguntas.explicacion: Informed consent is obtained after a comprehensive explanation and discussion, once the patient has acknowledged the procedure-related information and all potential inquiries, including the time it will take for results to return, have been fully answered. Signing before answering, or deferring the question to others, reverses that order.

opciones: Answering telephones, scheduling appointments and restocking office supplies
Setting the fee schedule and negotiating the practice's contracts with health plans
Auditing the practice's claims for fraud and reporting findings to the payer
Approving which staff members may open the electronic health record system
preguntas.explicacion: Medical assistants handle both administrative and clinical work, and often concentrate on one side. The administrative tasks described include helping patients understand and obtain their insurance coverage by completing forms, coding information and contacting companies about billing, along with inventorying, ordering and restocking medical and office supplies, answering telephones and scheduling appointments.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks the scheduler whether she can take her video visit while she drives to work. What does the patient guidance say?
opciones: She should not, since a telehealth visit is not to be taken while driving or on errands
She may, if she switches to audio only and pulls over whenever an examination is required
She may, provided the car has hands-free equipment and the connection is private
She should not, unless the appointment is a brief exchange of ten minutes or less
preguntas.explicacion: Among the tips for a successful visit, the patient is told to stay on track: it is best not to eat or drink during a telehealth visit, and to be safe by not having one while driving or running errands. She is also told to sign on early so she can message or telephone the office if the video will not start, and to be patient if the clinician is running late.

An accounting entry for each report before it is filed in the record
A business associate agreement with the carrier that delivered the mail
A written authorization from each patient whose report arrived that day
preguntas.explicacion: A covered entity must have appropriate administrative, technical and physical safeguards protecting against uses and disclosures the rule does not permit and limiting incidental ones. preguntas.pregunta: A 3-year-old needs venipuncture and the mother asks whether she should hold him. What does the WHO guidance say?
opciones: Yes, if she wishes; give full instructions on how and where to hold
No; only trained staff may immobilize a child for a blood draw
No; a child must be immobilized with a mechanical restraint device
Yes, and with the mother holding no second adult is needed
preguntas.explicacion: Chapter 6 asks whether the parent would like to help by holding the child; if so, the parent gets full instructions on how and where to hold, and if not, another phlebotomist assists. One person acts as technician and a second adult, parent or phlebotomist, immobilizes the child from the opposite side of the table. Mechanical restraint devices are a last resort in psychiatric care.

The radiographer, over imaging of the arm before the puncture
The dietitian, over the fasting the patient was asked to observe
The phlebotomy supervisor, over which stopper colour to select
preguntas.explicacion: Where a patient is taking blood thinners or other medicines that could bring on unwanted complications, the pharmacist is the person to consult. preguntas.pregunta: At which point in the life of a needle do sharps injuries most commonly happen?

While the needle is being pushed into the vein
While the packaging is being opened at the tray
After the container has been sealed for collection
preguntas.explicacion: Injuries from sharps commonly occur between the use of a needle or similar device and its disposal, which is the window that recapping, disassembly and a distant sharps container all lengthen. Discarding into a puncture-resistant container straight away markedly reduces these injuries.

preguntas.pregunta: A lithium level is ordered for a patient with bipolar disorder. How long after the dose should the blood be drawn, and what is the target range?
opciones: 12 hours after the dose, for a target of 0.5 to 1.2 mEq/L
12 hours after the dose, for a target of 5 to 10 mEq/L
2 hours after the dose, for a target of 0.5 to 1.2 mEq/L
24 hours after the dose, for a target of 1.2 to 2.0 mEq/L
preguntas.explicacion: Lithium is reported with the sample taken 12 hours after the dose, and the target range is 0.5 to 1.2 mEq/L (0.5 to 1.2 mmol/L). The same 12-hour rule applies to cyclosporine, tacrolimus and sirolimus. Ranges of 5 to 10 belong to aminoglycoside levels in mcg/mL, and 0.8 to 2.0 ng/mL is digoxin: mixing the units is what makes these figures easy to confuse.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient receives ABO-incompatible blood. What happens to the transfused red cells, and which organ is at risk of failing?
opciones: Antibodies clump them; hemolysis then overloads the kidneys with hemoglobin
They sickle and lodge in narrow capillaries, starving the brain of oxygen
They are phagocytized by macrophages in the spleen, which fails under the load
Platelets coat them and form thrombi that occlude the coronary arteries
preguntas.explicacion: In a transfusion reaction, antibodies bind the foreign antigens on the donated erythrocytes and clump them together, a process called agglutination; the clumps block small vessels, and as they are degraded (hemolysis) their hemoglobin floods the blood. The kidneys cannot clear that load and the patient can rapidly develop kidney failure. Sickling and thrombi are other disorders entirely.
preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.6 Blood Typing, Antigens, Antibodies, and Transfusion Reactions

A copayment of up to $35, the ceiling that applies to a month of covered insulin
Twenty percent of the approved amount, as with most services covered by Part B
Five percent of the approved amount, which is the share for inpatient respite care
preguntas.explicacion: Covered hospice services themselves cost the patient nothing under Part A. What she may still owe is a copayment of up to $5 for each prescription drug and similar product for pain relief and symptom control while she is at home, and five percent of the approved amount for inpatient respite care. The $35 ceiling belongs to covered insulin under Part B.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient is found slumped against a floor lamp with a frayed cord and is not moving. What is the first action?
opciones: Turn off the current at the breaker before touching the patient at all
Pull the patient away by an arm and start checking for breathing
Unplug the lamp and then move the patient with a metal walker frame
Start compressions at once and have someone unplug the lamp meanwhile
preguntas.explicacion: The current goes off first: unplug the cord, pull the fuse or trip the breaker, since switching an appliance off may not stop the flow. The patient is not touched with bare hands while still in contact with the source; a non-metallic object is used to separate them. Only then are airway, breathing and pulse checked and first aid begun.

preguntas.pregunta: An unaccompanied 10-year-old arrives at a federally funded emergency department and no parent can be reached. What happens first?
opciones: A medical screening exam is done regardless of consent or ability to pay
Care waits until a parent or a guardian is reached and gives permission
A hospital administrator signs the consent form in place of the parent
The child is moved to a pediatric hospital before any examination is done
preguntas.explicacion: Federal law requires a medical screening exam for everyone who comes to a federally funded emergency department, minors included, whatever their consent status or ability to pay. If that exam finds an emergency medical condition, life- or limb-saving treatment proceeds without waiting for a parent. Once no emergency condition is found, that protection ends and consent has to be sorted out.

preguntas.pregunta: A safety needle requires the user to activate its shield after the draw. How does the FDA say an active feature should be designed to work?
opciones: It can be activated with one hand, with the hands staying behind the exposed sharp
It can be activated with two hands, so that the shield locks firmly over the needle tip
It activates on its own as the needle leaves the vein, with no user action
It is activated after the needle has been placed in the sharps container
preguntas.explicacion: For active features, those the user must trigger, FDA Table 1 recommends that activation be possible with a single-handed technique that lets the user's hands remain behind the exposed sharp. preguntas.pregunta: Which plasma protein is essential for clotting and is therefore no longer present in serum?
opciones: Fibrinogen
Albumin
Transferrin
Immunoglobulin
preguntas.explicacion: Fibrinogen is the third major plasma protein group, made by the liver and required for coagulation; in the common pathway thrombin turns it into insoluble fibrin. Because serum is plasma with the clotting factors removed, fibrinogen (factor I) is gone from serum. Albumin and the immunoglobulins are not clotting factors, and transferrin is the plasma carrier of iron.

preguntas.pregunta: What separates HCPCS Level I from HCPCS Level II?
opciones: Level I is CPT, kept by the AMA; Level II names supplies and equipment and is kept by CMS
Level I is CPT, kept by CMS; Level II names supplies and equipment and is kept by the AMA
Level I codes diagnoses and Level II codes the procedures done to treat them
Level I is used by hospitals for inpatient care and Level II by offices for visits
preguntas.explicacion: HCPCS has two subsystems. Level I is Current Procedural Terminology, a numeric system of five digits that the American Medical Association maintains and republishes each year. Level II is a standardized alphanumeric system, a letter followed by four digits, for products, supplies and services outside Level I such as ambulance and durable medical equipment, and CMS maintains it. preguntas.pregunta: Whom does the term intimate partner cover in intimate partner violence?
opciones: Current and former spouses and dating partners alike
Current spouses and people living at the same address
People in the same household, including relatives and roommates
Married partners only, once the marriage is on public record
preguntas.explicacion: Intimate partner violence is abuse or aggression inside a romantic relationship, and the term intimate partner takes in current and former spouses as well as current and former dating partners. preguntas.pregunta: Which contrast between a latent disease and a chronic infection is correct?
opciones: In a latent disease the pathogen goes dormant with no active replication
In a latent disease the pathogen replicates faster than in a chronic one
In a latent disease the pathogen is cleared and cannot ever come back
In a latent disease the pathogen is always a bacterium rather than a virus
preguntas.explicacion: In a latent disease the causal pathogen goes dormant for long stretches with no active replication, unlike a chronic infection. Herpes simplex, varicella-zoster and Epstein-Barr all do this and can wake up later, which is why chickenpox in childhood can return decades on as shingles.

Emergency access procedure, which gets a clinician to the record during an emergency
Applications and data criticality analysis, which ranks what has to come back first
Testing and revision procedures, which put the contingency plan through a rehearsal

preguntas.pregunta: A cuff that is too small for the patient's arm is used. Which way does the reading err?
opciones: Falsely high, while a cuff that is too large produces a falsely low reading
Falsely low, while a cuff that is too large produces a falsely high reading
Falsely high, and a cuff that is too large errs in the same direction
Neither, so long as the bladder still encircles the arm without a gap
preguntas.explicacion: An undersized cuff pushes the value up and an oversized one pulls it down. preguntas.pregunta: A clinic with 8 employees asks whether its emergency action plan must be in writing. What does OSHA's rule provide?
opciones: With 10 or fewer employees the plan may be communicated orally
It must be in writing regardless of size and posted at each exit
With fewer than 25 employees it may be oral; above that it must be written
It may be oral only if the clinic also has no fire prevention plan
preguntas.explicacion: Under 29 CFR 1910.38(b), as summarized in OSHA's Hospitals eTool, an emergency action plan must generally be written, kept in the workplace and available to employees, but an employer with 10 or fewer employees may communicate it orally; 1910.39(b) gives the fire prevention plan the same threshold. The two plans are independent, so having or lacking one does not change the rule for the other. With 8 employees the clinic may brief its staff orally, although the minimum elements of 1910.38(c) still have to be covered.

preguntas.pregunta: A student is asked to put the conduction system in order, from where the impulse starts to where it reaches the ventricular muscle. Which sequence is right?
opciones: SA node, AV node, bundle of His, bundle branches, Purkinje fibers
SA node, bundle of His, AV node, bundle branches, Purkinje fibers
AV node, SA node, bundle of His, bundle branches, Purkinje fibers
SA node, AV node, Purkinje fibers, bundle of His, bundle branches
preguntas.explicacion: The conducting components run in order: the sinoatrial node starts the impulse, internodal pathways carry it across the atria to the atrioventricular node, where it pauses about 100 ms; it then runs down the bundle of His in the interventricular septum, splits into the two bundle branches, and reaches the Purkinje fibers, which spread it through the ventricular muscle from the apex up.
preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 19.2 Cardiac Muscle and Electrical Activity, Conduction System of the Heart; Atrioventricular Bundle, Bundle Branches, and Purkinje Fibers

preguntas.pregunta: Roughly what share of people over 65 fall in the course of a year?
opciones: More than 30%, and about half of those falls happen more than once
More than 60%, and about half of those falls happen more than once
About 10%, which is also the share of falls causing serious injury
About 3%, rising to 10% among those living in nursing facilities
preguntas.explicacion: Over 30% of adults past 65 fall each year, and the figure climbs toward 40% past 85. In about half of the cases the falls repeat. Roughly one fall in ten causes a serious injury such as a hip or other fracture, traumatic brain injury or subdural hematoma. Falls are the leading reason this age group is hospitalized for injury.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Falls and Fall Prevention in Older Adults", Epidemiology
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A1 · NCMA 2B.2

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with severe liver disease and a vitamin K deficiency bleeds longer than usual after a draw. Why is coagulation impaired?
opciones: The liver makes most clotting factors and needs vitamin K for many
Vitamin K is factor IV, the calcium needed for the entire cascade
The liver stores the platelets that release ADP and serotonin
Vitamin K activates plasmin, so clots dissolve as fast as they form
preguntas.explicacion: Clotting factors are secreted mainly by the liver and the platelets, and the liver requires the fat-soluble vitamin K to make many of them; factors II, VII, IX and X are the vitamin K dependent ones. Severe liver disease and a lack of vitamin K are both recognized causes of bleeding disorders. Calcium, not vitamin K, is factor IV, and the spleen, not the liver, stores platelets.
preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.5 Hemostasis, Clotting Factors Involved in Coagulation and Table 18.1; and MedlinePlus, Coagulation Factor Tests, Why do I need a coagulation factor test?

preguntas.pregunta: Which job aid does the contingency guidance suggest an organization hand its staff for use during an outage?
opciones: A small self-contained card or checklist of the resources and actions available
A printed copy of the whole electronic record of every patient booked that day
A telephone list of the software developer's support engineers and their hours
A binder holding the last six months of temperature and equipment inspection logs
preguntas.explicacion: Alongside training and drills, the guidance names a concrete tool: a job aid, described as a small self-contained reference card or checklist that helps staff find the resources and the actions open to them while the record system is down. It is meant to be usable when nothing on screen can be consulted.
preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, SAFER Guide: Contingency Planning, Recommended Practice 2.1

preguntas.pregunta: A patient is given several stool collection bottles with different colored caps for a culture and a parasite exam. What should he be told?
opciones: Each bottle may carry different instructions, so read them all before starting and follow each exactly
All bottles take the same sample, so fill them from a single bowel movement in any order
Only the culture bottle matters; the others are spare containers for repeat collections
The bottles should be refrigerated for 24 hours before being returned, as for urine culture
preguntas.explicacion: Depending on which stool tests are ordered, the patient may receive several bottles, and they can come with different instructions; the advice is to read everything ahead of time and follow each set carefully. The specimen goes back to the laboratory as soon as possible, labeled with name, date and time of collection, and the patient washes the hands with soap and water afterward.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Fecal culture (003758), How to Prepare for the Test; and MedlinePlus, Lab Tests: Ova and Parasite Test, What happens during an ova and parasite test?

preguntas.pregunta: A clinic laboratory cannot perform a test and wants to send the specimen out. To which kind of laboratory may it refer the specimen under CLIA?
opciones: Only to a CLIA-certified laboratory or one CMS deems to meet equivalent requirements
To any laboratory that agrees in writing to return results within the clinic's turnaround time
To any hospital laboratory, since hospitals are exempt from the CLIA certificate requirement
To any laboratory accredited by a private body, whether or not it holds a CLIA certificate
preguntas.explicacion: 42 CFR 493.1242(c) restricts referral to laboratories that hold a CLIA certificate or that CMS has determined meet equivalent requirements. A turnaround agreement, hospital status or private accreditation on its own does not satisfy the rule. When a laboratory accepts referrals, it must in turn give its clients written instructions on preparation, collection, labeling, storage, transport, processing and acceptability.
preguntas.fuente: 42 CFR 493.1242(c), Standard: Specimen submission, handling, and referral
