preguntas.pregunta: A physician calls asking why no result was issued for a specimen sent that morning. The specimen had been rejected. What does the emergency laboratory do with rejected samples?
opciones: Stores them up to 24 hours at 4 °C and issues an immediate LIS report stating the sample was not processed
Discards them at once as biohazardous waste and telephones the ward within 30 minutes of rejection
Runs the tests anyway and reports the results with a comment noting the reason for rejection
Freezes them at –20 °C for one week in case the physician asks for the analysis to be repeated
preguntas.explicacion: Unsuitable samples are recognised at arrival by visual inspection and serum indices; those rejected are kept for up to 24 hours at 4 °C, and a report goes out immediately through the laboratory information system saying the sample was not processed. That report is how the ordering physician learns that a new specimen is needed; testing a rejected tube or discarding it unrecorded defeats the purpose.

Agglutinins
Isoantibodies
Immunoglobulins
preguntas.explicacion: With red cells the antigens may be called isoantigens or agglutinogens, and the antibodies isoantibodies or agglutinins, though the plainer words antigen and antibody are more common. Immunoglobulin is another name for antibody. The agglutinogen is the marker on the cell; the agglutinin is the Y-shaped antibody that clumps cells carrying it.

Portal self-scheduling is offered only to patients seen within the past year
Portal self-scheduling is offered only during the hours the office is open
Portal self-scheduling is offered only for visits with her own primary clinician

The non-urgent limit is part of the scheduling feature itself.

To decide whether the device should be switched off first
To measure the battery charge left inside the device
To confirm the device is safe before an MRI is done

preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist is sent to draw blood from a patient on Contact Precautions for a multidrug-resistant organism. Which PPE does the CDC call for?
opciones: A gown and gloves, put on when entering the room and discarded before leaving
A surgical mask put on at the door, with gloves only for the venipuncture itself
A fit-tested N95 respirator, with gown and gloves added only if the patient has a draining wound
Gloves alone, since Standard Precautions already cover blood contact during the draw
preguntas.explicacion: For Contact Precautions the CDC recommends a gown and gloves for every interaction that may involve the patient or the patient's environment, donned on room entry and discarded before exit to contain the pathogen. A mask on entry is the Droplet Precautions rule, and the fit-tested N95 belongs to Airborne Precautions. Standard Precautions still apply underneath, so the gloves the phlebotomist would wear anyway are not enough by themselves; the gown is added because the pathogen spreads by contact with the patient and surroundings.

preguntas.pregunta: A physician phones the laboratory to order a test and says the written order will follow. Under CLIA, how long does the laboratory have to obtain the written or electronic authorization?
opciones: 30 days from the oral request
7 days from the oral request
24 hours from the oral request
90 days from the oral request
preguntas.explicacion: 42 CFR 493.1241(b) lets a laboratory accept an oral test request as long as it asks for a written or electronic authorization within 30 days and keeps either the authorization or proof of its attempts to get it. The requirement is a written or electronic request from an authorized person in the first place; the oral route is the exception, and 30 days is its limit, not one day, one week or three months.

preguntas.pregunta: What is the burden of proof in a civil tort case such as a malpractice claim?
opciones: A preponderance of the evidence: more likely than not
Beyond a reasonable doubt, as in criminal cases
Clear and convincing evidence agreed by a unanimous jury
Proof to a certainty, the standard applied to damages
preguntas.explicacion: Tort cases are decided by a preponderance of the evidence, meaning more likely than not, or greater than 50 percent; the criminal standard of beyond a reasonable doubt does not apply, and depending on the state a verdict against a tortfeasor may not require the whole jury to agree. One is liable for a tort, not guilty of it. Damages themselves must be proved to a certainty rather than estimated, and statutes may cap them, but that requirement concerns the amount awarded, not the burden for establishing liability.

preguntas.pregunta: An imaging report describes hepatomegaly. Which ending carries the meaning of enlargement?
opciones: -megaly, which is added to the root for the organ
-sclerosis, which is added to the root for the organ
-ectasis, which is added to the root for the organ
-trophy, which is added to the root for the organ
preguntas.explicacion: The ending -megaly means enlargement, and hepat- names the liver, so hepatomegaly is an enlarged liver. The near neighbors mean other things: -sclerosis is a hardening, -ectasis an expansion or dilation of a hollow structure, and -trophy is growth in the sense of nourishment, as in atrophy and hypertrophy.

preguntas.pregunta: State law is stricter than HIPAA about disclosing HIV test results. Which rule governs the disclosure?
opciones: The more stringent rule, in this case the state law
HIPAA, since federal law always preempts state law
Whichever rule the facility's privacy official prefers
Neither; HIV results are excluded from PHI altogether
preguntas.explicacion: Many states have privacy rules stricter than HIPAA, especially for HIV, mental health, genetic and substance-use information, and federal rules on substance use disorder records are stricter as well; where a more stringent rule exists it takes precedence over HIPAA in that jurisdiction, while HIPAA still applies to everything else. The notice of privacy practices must reflect the more stringent law when it limits a use or disclosure. HIV results are ordinary PHI under HIPAA; the extra protection comes from state law, not from an exclusion.

preguntas.pregunta: A dose is drawn up wrong but caught before it reaches the patient. How is that event described?
opciones: A near miss: an error that could have harmed but was intercepted
A sentinel event: an error that reached the patient and caused harm
A reckless act: a deliberate choice to work outside the safe procedure
A latent condition: a flaw in the system that has yet to cause an error
preguntas.explicacion: A near miss is an error with the potential to harm a patient that fails to do so by chance or because someone intercepted it. Near misses are investigated the same way as worse events, because they usually come from poor communication, weak teamwork, memory overload or unstandardized procedures rather than from a careless person.

preguntas.pregunta: A complete blood count is ordered. Which tube is used, and what does the CBC measure?
opciones: A lavender EDTA tube; red cells, white cells, platelets, hemoglobin, hematocrit and MCV
A light blue citrate tube; the seconds the sample takes to clot and the INR
A grey fluoride tube; plasma glucose and the average glucose of recent months
A gold serum separator tube; electrolytes, kidney waste products and the liver enzymes
preguntas.explicacion: Hematologic assays go in the lavender EDTA tube, and a CBC counts the blood cells: red blood cells, white blood cells, platelets, hemoglobin, hematocrit and the mean corpuscular volume. preguntas.pregunta: A hospital introduces safety-engineered needles but its needlestick rate does not fall. Which contributing factors were most often reported in a study that found this pattern?

Reuse of needle holders and the mixing of components from different manufacturers
Prolonged tourniquet time and failure to activate the feature with one hand
Overfilled sharps containers and the absence of double gloving
preguntas.explicacion: A 2018 study from the Netherlands recorded 1.9 needlestick injuries per 100 healthcare workers before safety-engineered devices and 2.2 afterwards; the factors most commonly reported were difficulty operating the safety mechanism and continued improper needle disposal. preguntas.pregunta: A patient reports nausea and fatigue, and the exam records a fever and a rash. Which entries are symptoms and which are signs?
opciones: Nausea and fatigue are symptoms; fever and rash are signs
Nausea and fatigue are signs; fever and rash are symptoms
All four are symptoms, since the patient came in reporting them
All four are signs, since a provider recorded them in the chart
preguntas.explicacion: A symptom is something the person feels and can only report: pain, nausea, fatigue, anxiety. A sign is something found on the exam or on a test, so anyone can observe it: fever, swelling, a skin rash, a high blood pressure or a high blood glucose. Both matter, but only one of them can be measured.

preguntas.pregunta: Which set of findings fits a patient who is going into shock?
opciones: Rapid weak pulse, shallow breathing, pale clammy skin and confusion
Slow bounding pulse, deep slow breathing, flushed dry skin and euphoria
Rapid strong pulse, deep rapid breathing, warm dry skin and hunger
Slow weak pulse, noisy breathing, blue lips and a raised temperature
preguntas.explicacion: Shock is circulatory failure, so blood pressure falls very low and the picture is a fast but weak pulse, shallow breathing, skin that is pale, cool and clammy, low or absent urine output, and anxiety, restlessness or confusion. Bluish lips and nails may appear. One in five people who go into shock die of it, so help is called at the first signs.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with capacity refuses a treatment that the whole team believes would help him. What is the legal position?

He may refuse once a second clinician has confirmed it
He may refuse only treatments that are not life-sustaining
He may refuse only after signing a form releasing the team
preguntas.explicacion: Any patient who has capacity also has the right to refuse any treatment, regardless of whether other people consider giving it an act of beneficence, and a Supreme Court decision extended that right even to measures that decide life or death. The right comes from autonomy and travels with informed consent: capacity is the condition, and the assessment of capacity is part of the consent discussion itself.

preguntas.pregunta: Which situation is a recognized exception to the requirement for informed consent?
opciones: A life-threatening emergency with no time to obtain consent
A test the clinician considers clearly in the patient's interest
A patient who speaks a different language from the staff
A patient carrying a psychiatric diagnosis such as schizophrenia
preguntas.explicacion: The recognized exceptions are three: the patient is incapacitated, a life-threatening emergency leaves no time, or the patient voluntarily waives consent. A clinician's view that the test is good for the patient is the paternalism the consent literature warns against; language barriers call for an interpreter; and a psychiatric diagnosis by itself does not remove the right to consent.

preguntas.pregunta: A reading of 120/80 mm Hg is written in the chart. What else belongs beside it?
opciones: The arm used and the position the patient was in during the measurement
The size of the cuff and the make of the sphygmomanometer that was used
The rate at which the cuff was deflated and the peak pressure it reached
The time since the patient last ate, since food shifts the reading upward

preguntas.pregunta: Two patients on the same dose of the same drug show different levels. Which factors are named for that?
opciones: Ageing, pregnancy, illness and infection change how a drug is processed
The colour of the tube stopper and the order in which the tubes filled
The arm chosen for the draw and how long the tourniquet stayed on
The time of day alone, since every drug level follows a diurnal rhythm
preguntas.explicacion: As soon as a medicine is taken the body begins to process and remove it, so the level in the blood varies over time, and ageing, pregnancy, illness and infection all affect how quickly that happens. preguntas.pregunta: A pulse is described as irregularly irregular, with no pattern at all to the spacing. Which rhythm does that describe?

Sinus arrhythmia, whose rate changes in step with the breathing cycle
Sinus bradycardia, whose beats are widely spaced but evenly spread
Sinus tachycardia, whose beats are closely spaced but evenly spread
preguntas.explicacion: Rhythm is sorted into three descriptions: regular, regularly irregular, and irregularly irregular. preguntas.pregunta: Two tubes come back faulty from the same phlebotomist: one is haemolysed and one holds small clots. What separates the two errors?
opciones: Too much mixing haemolyses the sample; too little leaves small clots
Too little mixing haemolyses the sample; too much leaves small clots
Too much mixing leaves clots; a short draw is what haemolyses a sample
Both faults come from mixing too little, at different points in the draw
preguntas.explicacion: Tubes with an anticoagulant are inverted in a figure-of-8 until the blood and additive are properly combined. Fraud is committed by providers only; abuse is committed by patients and staff
Fraud is billed to a federal program; abuse is billed to a commercial insurer

preguntas.pregunta: Which element must a valid HIPAA authorization contain?
opciones: An expiration date or event, plus the individual's signature and date
A notarized seal and the signature of the treating physician
The patient's Social Security number and insurance identifier
A statement that the authorization cannot be revoked once it has been signed
preguntas.explicacion: The core elements in 164.508(c)(1) are a specific description of the information, the person or class authorized to disclose it, the recipient, the purpose, an expiration date or event, and the individual's signature and date, with the authority of any personal representative described. The required statements then tell the individual of the right to revoke in writing, whether treatment or benefits may be conditioned on signing, and that the recipient may redisclose the information. It must be in plain language and the individual receives a copy. Notarization is not required, and a no-revocation clause would contradict the rule.

preguntas.pregunta: Why are the cable wires pulled as straight as possible when they are attached?
opciones: Loops in them can cause alternating-current interference
Loops in them can shorten the life of the patient cable
Loops in them can slow the paper as it feeds through
Loops in them can reverse the polarity of that lead
preguntas.explicacion: Each wire is picked out of the cable distribution block, plugged into its connector, and then laid out straight. A loop in a lead wire is one of the recognized invitations to interference from the room current, an artifact that can bury the small waves the provider needs to see.

preguntas.pregunta: How often must a certified biological safety cabinet be recertified in a laboratory working with concentrated HIV or HBV?
opciones: When it is installed, whenever it is moved, and at least once a year
Every three years, the period for which training records are kept
Once at installation, and again only after a spill occurs inside it
Every six months, and after each change of the exhaust air filter
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (e)(2)(iii) requires certified biological safety cabinets, or equivalent containment such as special clothing, respirators, centrifuge safety cups and sealed rotors, for any activity that could throw droplets, splashes, spills or aerosols of infectious material. Subparagraph (B) sets the schedule for certification: at installation, at every move, and at least annually. The annual cycle is shared by the biosafety manual review in (e)(2)(ii)(M); three years is the retention period for training records.

preguntas.pregunta: A single-dose vial of lidocaine contains far more than one patient needs. What does the CDC recommend?
opciones: Do not keep the remainder for later or another patient; buy the smallest vial that meets the need
Label it with the date and use it for up to 28 days, as with a multi-dose vial
Pool the leftover contents with other single-dose vials in a clean preparation area
Save the remainder for the same patient's next visit, since it is dedicated to one person
preguntas.explicacion: A single-dose vial is approved for one patient for one case, procedure or injection, typically lacks a preservative, and must never be used for more than one patient. If it holds more than needed, the remainder is not retained for future use even on the same patient, leftover contents are not pooled or stored, and the practical advice is to purchase the smallest vial necessary. The 28-day dating rule applies to opened multi-dose vials, which contain a preservative.

preguntas.pregunta: A laboratory replaces its glucose analyzer with a different instrument. Under CLIA, what has to happen before the staff report patient results on it?
opciones: Each individual's performance is reevaluated so the evaluation covers the new instrument
Each individual repeats the six competency procedures within six months of the changeover
The laboratory enrolls in a second approved proficiency testing program for that analyte
The technical consultant attests in writing that the earlier evaluations still apply here
preguntas.explicacion: The annual cycle has an interrupt built into it: when the test methodology or the instrumentation changes, the individual's performance must be reevaluated to include the new method or instrument, and that happens before patient test results are reported. Nobody can sign the old evaluation forward, and there is no grace period.

preguntas.pregunta: What is the normal resting respiratory rate for an adult?
opciones: 12 to 20 breaths per minute, counted with the depth and the pattern
20 to 30 breaths per minute, counted with the depth and the pattern
8 to 12 breaths per minute, counted with the depth and the pattern
30 to 60 breaths per minute, counted with the depth and the pattern
preguntas.explicacion: The adult range is 12 to 20 breaths per minute, and the assessment records rate, depth and pattern rather than the number alone. The 30 to 60 band belongs to infants. Respiration is the vital sign most often left out of the chart, and it is also the one that changes earliest when a patient is deteriorating.

preguntas.pregunta: How many regions does the detailed regional scheme of the abdomen produce, and how many does the quadrant scheme produce?
opciones: Nine regions and four quadrants
Four regions and nine quadrants
Six regions and three quadrants
Twelve regions and six quadrants
preguntas.explicacion: Providers divide the abdominal cavity either into nine regions or into four quadrants, so that a complaint can be placed precisely. The regional scheme is the more detailed one and comes from two horizontal and two vertical lines; the quadrant scheme is simpler and is the one used more often in medicine.

preguntas.pregunta: Before a routine venipuncture, what does the WHO's Step 4 require for hand hygiene and gloves?
opciones: Soap and water, or 3 ml of alcohol rub if hands are not visibly soiled, then well-fitting non-sterile gloves
Use 3 ml of alcohol rub in every case, even on visibly soiled hands, then put on sterile gloves
Wash with soap and water, dry with a reusable towel, then put on sterile gloves for every patient
Put on well-fitting non-sterile gloves first, then clean the gloved hands with alcohol rub
preguntas.explicacion: Step 4 gives two options: wash the hands with soap and water and dry them with single-use towels, or, if they are not visibly contaminated, rub 3 ml of alcohol rub over palms, fingertips and backs of the hands until dry; only then are well-fitting non-sterile gloves put on. Sterile gloves are reserved for blood cultures. Gloves are never a substitute for hand hygiene.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with polycythemia has a hematocrit of 60%. What should be considered when collecting a citrate specimen from this patient?
opciones: The high hematocrit raises the citrate effect, so the anticoagulant volume may need adjusting
The high hematocrit lowers the citrate effect, so the tube should be filled only halfway
The tube is collected as usual, since hematocrit affects the EDTA tube and not the citrate tube
A larger 16 to 18 G needle is used so the viscous blood reaches the 9:1 ratio faster
preguntas.explicacion: Inadequate filling or a hematocrit above 55% increases the citrate level in the sample and interferes with the recalcification performed during analysis, and with a high hematocrit the anticoagulant volume may need to be adjusted. Half filling would make the citrate excess worse. The 16 to 18 gauge belongs to blood donation in the WHO needle table, not to coagulation draws, for which 19 to 22 G is suggested.

preguntas.pregunta: Which order of steps does the guideline require before an instrument can be high-level disinfected or sterilized?
opciones: Clean it thoroughly first, because leftover organic and inorganic matter blocks the process
Soak it in the germicide first, so the softened soil rinses off with less friction afterward
Disinfect at a low level first, so the item is safe for the person who will scrub it later
Rinse it in sterile water first, so tap-water organisms cannot dry onto the working surfaces
preguntas.explicacion: Cleaning always comes first. Material left on the surface interferes with the process in two ways: it reacts chemically with the germicide, using it up, and it shields microbes as a physical barrier. Meticulous cleaning also lowers the bioburden, which shortens the exposure needed. Sterile-water rinsing is what follows high-level disinfection, not what precedes it.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization (2008), Cleaning

preguntas.pregunta: A serum sample looks pink after centrifugation. Which result on the chemistry panel should the processor expect the laboratory to question first?
opciones: Potassium
Magnesium
Chloride
Glucose
preguntas.explicacion: Among frequent chemistry tests, the analytes most sensitive to hemolysis are lactate dehydrogenase, creatine kinase and its MB isoenzyme, potassium, conjugated bilirubin, ALT, AST and iron; potassium is the one whose distortion most often changes patient management, which is why one hospital measures the hemolysis index on every potassium sample. Albumin, glucose and other analytes showed biases that stayed within CLIA limits in the study on graded hemolysis, as did magnesium and chloride.

preguntas.pregunta: Which information must a bloodborne pathogens training record include?
opciones: Dates, a summary of the content, the trainer's name and qualifications, and attendees' names and titles
Dates, the trainer's name, and each attendee's hepatitis B vaccination status and serology
Dates, the content, and the type and brand of any device that caused an injury during the year
Dates, the attendees' names, and a copy of each attendee's signed declination or consent
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (h)(2)(i) lists four items for the training record: the dates of the sessions, the contents or a summary, the names and qualifications of whoever conducted the training, and the names and job titles of everyone who attended. Vaccination status and serology belong to the confidential medical record of (h)(1); the type and brand of a device belong to the sharps injury log of (h)(5); and the signed declination of Appendix A is a separate document required by (f)(2)(iv).

preguntas.pregunta: A patient is booked for one-step gestational testing. What should she be told to expect?
opciones: An 8- to 14-hour fast, a 75 g drink, and about 2 hours in the office
An 8- to 14-hour fast, a 100 g drink, and about 3 hours in the office
No fast at all, a 50 g drink, and about 1 hour in the office
A 3-day carbohydrate diet, a 75 g drink, and about 2 hours in the office
preguntas.explicacion: One-step testing means nothing to eat or drink except sips of water for 8 to 14 hours, a liquid holding 75 g of glucose, and draws before the drink and every 60 minutes for two hours, so at least two hours should be allowed. The 100 g / 3-hour version is the second step of the other pathway, and the 50 g nonfasting drink is its first step. Nothing may be eaten during the test.

preguntas.pregunta: Under the FDA's design recommendations for sharps injury prevention features, what must be true once the feature has been activated?
opciones: It cannot be deactivated and stays protective through disposal
It can be reset once so the device can be used on the same patient
It stays protective until the device reaches the sharps container
It may be released by a second single-handed action if needed
preguntas.explicacion: Table 1 of the FDA guidance lists, for all feature types, that the user should be able to tell easily whether the feature is activated, and that once activated it cannot be deactivated and should remain protective through disposal. Resetting or releasing the feature is the opposite of that recommendation, and protection that ended at the container would not cover the disposal step.

preguntas.pregunta: A man scheduled for a semen analysis asks how long he should abstain from ejaculation beforehand. What is the usual instruction?
opciones: From 2 to 3 days, and in no case longer than 5 days before the test
From 2 to 3 hours, and in no case longer than 5 hours before the test
At least 7 days, and preferably 10 days or more before the test
No abstinence at all, since recent activity does not change the count
preguntas.explicacion: To get an adequate sperm count the patient avoids any sexual activity that ends in ejaculation for 2 to 3 days, and the interval should not stretch past 5 days because quality falls off after that. The StatPearls account of the same test sets the window differently, at a minimum of 3 and a maximum of 7 days, so the figure a candidate quotes depends on which reference the laboratory follows.

preguntas.pregunta: According to OSHA, may a facility apply Standard Precautions instead of Universal Precautions?
opciones: Yes, as an alternative, if the facility follows all other provisions of the standard
No; Universal Precautions is the only approach the standard's definitions recognize
Yes, but only in hospitals accredited by a CMS-approved accreditation organization
Yes, and doing so exempts the facility from the exposure determination requirement
preguntas.explicacion: The eTool explains that Body Substance Isolation and Standard Precautions define all body fluids and substances as infectious, and that OSHA permits them as alternatives to Universal Precautions provided the facility adheres to every other provision of the bloodborne pathogens standard. OSHA's hazard page dates Standard Precautions to 1996 and describes them as expanding on Universal Precautions with added infection prevention elements. The exposure determination of (c)(2) is still required, and accreditation is a CLIA matter, not a condition here.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient who spends most of the day in a wheelchair asks why a cushion is needed. What is the reason?
opciones: Sitting straight on the seat surface concentrates pressure over the bony pelvis
The cushion raises the seat so the arms can reach the hand rims more easily
The cushion holds the pelvis tilted backward, which keeps the trunk upright
Sitting on the seat surface makes the chair tip forward during a transfer
preguntas.explicacion: Nobody should sit directly on a sling or solid seat. Long hours of sitting, often without protective sensation, load the ischial tuberosities and sacrum until the tissue breaks down. The cushion spreads that pressure, and pressure-relief moves such as leaning forward, leaning to the side or pushing up on the arms are taught alongside it.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Seating and Wheelchair Evaluation", Technique or Treatment: Seating Systems
preguntas.subtema: RMA III.H.3.a.ii · NCMA 2B.2

preguntas.pregunta: A clinician wants to drop a patient he finds difficult and demanding. What do the ethical guidelines say?
opciones: Being a challenging patient is not on its own a ground for ending the relationship
Any patient may be dismissed at will, since the relationship rests on mutual consent
Dismissal is allowed once the patient has been rude to a member of the office staff
Only the health plan may end the relationship, by removing the patient from the panel
preguntas.explicacion: The clinician-patient relationship usually begins by mutual consent and is governed by State law. Ethical guidance holds that a clinician may not terminate it merely because someone is a challenging patient, and that irresponsible health behaviors do not release the professional from the duties of the relationship. The expected route is to try to resolve the conflict and, failing that, seek help from a consultant.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, Terminating the Therapeutic Relationship, Introduction

preguntas.pregunta: A patient's platelet count is far below normal. What is the term for this, and what is the main risk?
opciones: Thrombocytopenia; excessive bleeding even from minor wounds
Thrombocytosis; the formation of unwanted clots or thrombosis
Leukopenia; an inability to ward off infection and disease
Thrombophilia; an inherited or acquired tendency to form thrombi
preguntas.explicacion: An insufficient number of platelets is thrombocytopenia; blood may then fail to clot properly, so excessive bleeding can follow even minor wounds. The opposite, too many platelets, is thrombocytosis and carries a risk of unwanted clots. Leukopenia is too few white cells, and thrombophilia (hypercoagulation) is a tendency to thrombosis that can be genetic or acquired.
preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.4 Leukocytes and Platelets, Disorders of Platelets; and 18.5 Hemostasis, Disorders of Clotting

preguntas.pregunta: What is the correct way to take off a gown after caring for a patient?
opciones: Release the ties, touch only the inside, and turn it inside out
Release the ties, roll it from the sleeves toward the neckline
Pull it over the head without untying, keeping the front outward
Fold it front to front and hang it for the rest of the shift
preguntas.explicacion: The gown is third in the doffing sequence. Its ties or straps are released, and it is removed touching only the inside, pulled away from the neck and shoulders, turned inside out so the contaminated face ends up enclosed, and placed in the proper container. The bloodborne pathogens standard adds the companion rule: a garment penetrated by blood comes off immediately, in a way that avoids contact with its outer surface, and a gown is never hung up for reuse.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Personal Protective Equipment", Suggested Sequence for Removal of PPE; OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(3)(vi)

preguntas.pregunta: A work surface in the draw room is splashed with blood during a procedure. What does OSHA require?
opciones: Decontaminate it with an appropriate disinfectant immediately or as soon as feasible
Decontaminate it at the end of the work shift, the time the standard sets for possibly contaminated surfaces
Remove and replace the protective covering at the end of the shift, as with plastic wrap over equipment
Flush it with water immediately, as the standard requires for skin and mucous membranes
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(4)(ii)(A) names three moments for decontaminating a work surface with a suitable disinfectant: when a procedure is finished; right away, or as soon as feasible, when the surface is visibly contaminated or blood or OPIM has been spilled on it; and at the end of the shift if it may have been contaminated since the last cleaning. A visible spill falls under the second case and does not wait for the shift to end. Protective coverings, in (d)(4)(ii)(B), are likewise replaced as soon as feasible once overtly contaminated. Flushing with water is the rule for eyes and mucous membranes in (d)(2)(vi), not for surfaces.
preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(4)(ii)(A), Housekeeping

preguntas.pregunta: A billing company discovers that it exposed patient data belonging to one of the clinics it serves. Whom must it notify, and how quickly?
opciones: The clinic, without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 days from discovering it
The affected patients, without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 days from discovery
The Secretary of HHS, without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 days from discovery
The clinic, within 60 days of the end of the calendar year in which it was discovered
preguntas.explicacion: A breach at or by a business associate is reported upward: the business associate notifies the covered entity without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 days from discovery, and it should identify the affected individuals and hand over what the covered entity needs for its own notices. The covered entity remains ultimately responsible for notifying individuals, though it may delegate the task.

preguntas.pregunta: A clinic wants to check each new hire's antibody level first and offer the hepatitis B vaccine only to those who are not immune. What does the standard say?
opciones: Screening may not be made a condition of receiving the vaccine that is offered
Screening is required before the first dose, and has to be repeated a year later
Screening replaces the vaccine when the employee signs the declination form
Screening is allowed only within ten working days of the initial assignment
preguntas.explicacion: Two sentences have to be read together. Paragraph (f)(2)(i) says the vaccine is offered after training and within ten working days of initial assignment, unless the employee already completed the series, antibody testing has shown immunity, or the vaccine is medically contraindicated. Paragraph (f)(2)(ii) then forbids making participation in a prescreening program a prerequisite for receiving it. So a result that already exists can spare the offer, but no employee can be told to be screened in order to qualify.

preguntas.pregunta: A laboratory reports repeated haemolysis from one phlebotomist. Which needle choices raise that risk?
opciones: A gauge of twenty-three or finer, or one too wide for the vessel
A gauge of twenty-one or finer, or one too short for the forearm
A gauge of sixteen or wider, or one too long for the antecubital
A gauge of twenty-three or finer, or one too short for the vessel
preguntas.explicacion: Both extremes of gauge appear on the list of factors that raise haemolysis: a needle of twenty-three gauge or under, and a needle too large for the vessel it is being put into. The wider figures, sixteen to eighteen, belong to blood donation rather than to routine sampling.

preguntas.pregunta: A contaminated wound with no major tissue loss is irrigated, debrided and watched for several days before it is closed. Which type of healing is that?
opciones: Tertiary intention, also called delayed primary closure
Secondary intention, in which granulation fills the defect
Primary intention, in which the edges are approximated at once
Maturation, the last of the four phases that every wound goes through
preguntas.explicacion: Tertiary intention, or delayed primary closure, is the route for a grossly contaminated wound that has not lost much tissue: it is explored, irrigated, debrided and observed for roughly three to seven days before it is closed or grafted. Primary intention is closure at once with sutures, staples or glue; secondary intention leaves the wound open to granulate and contract.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Wound Closure Techniques", Function

preguntas.pregunta: A patient has fainted in the chair and been eased to the floor. How high should the feet be raised?
opciones: About 12 inches (30 cm) above the level of the heart
About 4 inches (10 cm) above the level of the heart
About 3 feet (90 cm), by resting the legs on the chair seat
Level with the heart, with the head turned to the side
preguntas.explicacion: The immediate steps after a faint are: check airway and breathing, loosen tight clothing around the neck, raise the feet above heart level by about 12 inches or 30 centimeters, turn the person on the side if they have vomited, and keep them lying down for at least 10 to 15 minutes. The side position is for vomiting; it does not replace elevating the legs.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Fainting, Home Care

preguntas.pregunta: A patient recovers from a faint during a draw. Which finding afterwards is a red flag pointing away from a simple vasovagal episode?
opciones: A bitten tongue, which suggests a seizure
Pallor and sweating during the event itself
A slow pulse and low blood pressure during the event
Generalized weakness for a few minutes after waking
preguntas.explicacion: The patient is usually bradycardic, hypotensive, pale and diaphoretic during the event and should have an entirely normal examination afterwards; findings such as tongue biting, which suggests a seizure, or ongoing pallor, which suggests symptomatic anemia, call for a more thorough evaluation. The syncope chapter notes that generalized weakness on regaining consciousness is typical.

preguntas.pregunta: Which clotting factors require vitamin K for their production?
opciones: II, VII, IX and X
I, V, XI and XIII
III, IV, VIII and XII
VIII, IX, XI and XII
preguntas.explicacion: Four factors need vitamin K for their synthesis: prothrombin (II), proconvertin (VII), antihemolytic factor B (IX) and the Stuart-Prower factor (X), all made in the liver. The intrinsic-pathway set VIII, IX, XI and XII is a different grouping, and fibrinogen, proaccelerin, factor XI and the fibrin-stabilizing factor are not vitamin K dependent.

preguntas.pregunta: A physician orders blood cultures, a CBC and a fasting glucose on the same venipuncture. Which sequence follows the WHO table?
opciones: Blood culture bottle, purple EDTA tube, light grey fluoride tube
Purple EDTA tube, blood culture bottle, light grey fluoride tube

preguntas.pregunta: An 8-year-old with fever and exudative tonsils has a negative rapid strep test. What does current guidance recommend?
opciones: Send a throat swab for culture, because a negative rapid test in a child or adolescent is backed up by culture
Accept the negative result as final, because the rapid antigen test is highly specific for group A streptococcus
Repeat the rapid test at once with a second swab, and treat only if the second cassette also turns positive
Order a throat culture only if the rapid test had been positive, to identify which streptococcal group is present
preguntas.explicacion: A rapid strep test detects group A streptococcal antigen in 10 to 20 minutes, but a throat culture, which takes 24 to 48 hours, sometimes finds infections the rapid test misses. preguntas.pregunta: While washing hands at a sink for routine hand hygiene, which technique detail is correct?

Keep the hands above the elbows, as in the surgical scrub, and rinse toward the fingertips
Turn off the faucet with clean hands so the towel stays dry for drying

The airway first, then rescue breathing, then chest compressions
Rescue breathing first, then the airway, then chest compressions
The airway and two breaths, then a pulse check, then compressions

preguntas.pregunta: A patient's hematocrit result comes back as 42. What does that number mean?

That 42% of the blood volume is plasma, the liquid portion
That the red blood cell count is 4.2 million per microliter

preguntas.explicacion: A hematocrit is reported as the percentage of the blood that consists of red cells; the rest of the sample is white cells, platelets and plasma. preguntas.pregunta: A patient whose period is two days late drank several glasses of water before giving a random urine sample, and the office pregnancy test is negative. How should this result be handled?
opciones: It may be a false negative from dilute urine or early testing; a repeat on first morning urine in about a week is advised
It is reliable, because office cassettes detect hCG from 10 days after conception regardless of urine concentration

preguntas.explicacion: Drinking large amounts of fluid before collecting the sample can dilute the hCG so that it does not show on the test, and testing too soon after conception may precede detectable hormone levels; both produce false negatives. It is wiped with sterile water and dried with a towel
It is covered with a second drape without being wiped
preguntas.explicacion: The surface is disinfected and left to dry all the way through before anything sterile goes down on it. A surface still wet with disinfectant lets moisture wick through the drape, and moisture wicked from an unsterile area contaminates the field within an inch of where it appears. Only sterile supplies are allowed onto the field once it is established.

Material works only when it is mailed home instead of handed over in person
Material works only when the patient signs that she received the pamphlet

Interpreting the findings and deciding whether the patient needs an in-person visit
Recording the encounter so the clinician can review the video after the appointment

preguntas.pregunta: A patient's condition worsens after appropriate treatment and the family talks about suing. Does the outcome alone show negligence?
opciones: No: an undesirable result can happen even when the care was appropriate
No: a result only counts once the state licensing board has reviewed it
Yes: a worsening condition after treatment is what negligence means
Yes: any deviation from the expected recovery is a compensable injury
preguntas.explicacion: A medical intervention can leave the patient better, worse or unchanged, and all three are possible with entirely appropriate care. Negligence cannot be read off an unexpected result, a failure to cure or a failure to recover. Three lines of graph, with the leads printed in four groups of three
Six lines of graph, with the leads printed in three groups of four
Twelve lines of graph, with one lead printed on each of them

The color of the wristband the patient was given at admission
The order in the chart, which names the equipment to be worn

preguntas.pregunta: A provider wants to sign chart notes with a rubber stamp because handwriting is slow. What does CMS say?
opciones: Stamped signatures are not typically acceptable, apart from a disability accommodation
Stamped signatures are acceptable whenever the provider keeps the stamp locked away
Stamped signatures are acceptable if a signature log lists the stamp and its owner
Stamped signatures are acceptable on orders but never on progress notes or reports

Code both of them, and sequence the chronic code first of the two
Code the chronic one alone, since it is the longer-standing problem
Code the acute one alone, since it is what brought her in this time
preguntas.explicacion: Where the same condition is described as both acute or subacute and chronic, and separate subentries exist in the Alphabetic Index at the same indentation level, both are coded and the acute or subacute code is sequenced first. The tube is held in the other hand so the angle can be corrected
The tube is laid flat on the tray so the blood runs down its wall
The tube is held by an assistant while the worker steadies it

The alcohol makes the wax pencil marks hard to read
The marks have to be moved a space down after cleaning
The marks are copied onto the log sheet for the record

preguntas.pregunta: A staff member repeats a false and damaging claim about a patient out loud in the break room. Which tort is that, and what does it require?
opciones: Slander, and unlike libel the damages have to be proven by the person suing
Slander, and like libel the damages are presumed from the fact of publication
Libel, and the damages have to be proven by the person bringing the lawsuit
Libel, and the damages are presumed once the statement has been repeated
preguntas.explicacion: Defamation is a statement that harms someone's reputation, and it splits in two: libel is generally written or otherwise recorded, slander is generally spoken. With slander, damages are not presumed and the party suing has to prove them. Traditional libel rules go the other way and take the injury as given once the statement was published.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient's skin is oily at the electrode sites. How is each site prepared?
opciones: Rub it with alcohol and gauze about ten times
Rub it with alcohol and gauze about three times
Wipe it with dry gauze and then let it air dry
Part the hair and press the electrode down firmly
preguntas.explicacion: Each site is scrubbed vigorously with alcohol and gauze roughly ten times to take off oil, sweat and scaly skin. Applying an electrode to a surface that was not cleaned that way is one of the causes of a drifting baseline. Parting the hair is a separate trick, and it helps the electrode stick.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient refuses the plan the clinician is convinced is best. What does respect for autonomy require?
opciones: The clinician stops, having explained the reasoning and listened first
The clinician proceeds, since beneficence outranks the patient's refusal
The clinician presses until the patient accepts, then documents consent
The clinician transfers the patient, since the relationship has broken down
preguntas.explicacion: If the patient does not agree that the clinician's plan is the best option, the clinician stops, and that is respect for autonomy. Restricting a patient's freedom against their will on the argument that they will be better off is paternalism, and pushing someone toward the course the clinician prefers serves neither autonomy nor beneficence.

preguntas.pregunta: What may a research consent form never contain?
opciones: Wording that releases the investigator from liability for negligence
Wording about whom to contact if the subject is injured by the research
Wording that the study may end without the subject's own agreement
Wording that identifiers may be stripped for later, unrelated studies
preguntas.explicacion: Exculpatory language is barred: no consent may make the subject waive, or seem to waive, legal rights, or release the investigator, sponsor or institution from liability for negligence. The other three belong in a form. A contact for research injury is a basic element, and early termination by the investigator and future use of de-identified material are additional elements.

preguntas.pregunta: A citrate tube was drawn to only 67 % of its nominal volume. According to the fill-level study cited in the rejection paper, which coagulation result remains relatively reliable at that fill?
opciones: Prothrombin time
Activated PTT
Fibrinogen level
Factor VIII level

A message telling her to ring the front desk so that she can be let in
A form she has to finish on screen before the video will start at all
A recorded message that reads out the practice's policy on cancelling appointments

preguntas.pregunta: In what order do the phases of wound healing occur?
opciones: Hemostasis, inflammatory, proliferative, maturation
Inflammatory, hemostasis, maturation, proliferative
Proliferative, hemostasis, inflammatory, maturation
Hemostasis, proliferative, inflammatory, maturation
preguntas.explicacion: Vessels constrict and clotting factors act first, which is hemostasis and lasts up to an hour depending on the injury. Vasodilation then lets white cells in to clean the bed, showing as swelling, redness and exudate. The proliferative phase brings epithelialization, angiogenesis, collagen and contraction, and maturation lays down more collagen for strength.

Not less than 24 hours after alcohol, with no limit on food
Not less than 2 hours after any food or drink

preguntas.pregunta: A patient says the bladder is very full and asks whether that matters. What is the effect?

A full bladder lowers the reading by roughly 10 mm Hg through a vagal reflex

preguntas.pregunta: A patient calls the next day about a painful bruise at the puncture site. What first-aid advice applies to a bruise?

Ice placed directly on the skin for 30 minutes at a time, with the arm kept below the level of the heart

A tight adhesive strip over the bruise for 24 hours, kept on until the colour turns greenish-yellow

Family members first, then the attending physician, then a court-appointed guardian

Less than 20 percent of the calories eaten in a day
Less than 15 percent of the calories eaten in a day

preguntas.pregunta: An adult patient has a body mass index of 27.4. Which category is that?

Healthy weight, the band from 18.5 to 29.9
Obesity class 1, the band from 25.0 to 34.9
Underweight, which covers everything below 30.0
preguntas.explicacion: For adults of 20 and over the bands are: under 18.5 underweight, 18.5 to 24.9 healthy weight, 25.0 to 29.9 overweight, and 30.0 or more obesity. preguntas.pregunta: Which vein of the antecubital fossa does the WHO describe as usually the easiest to puncture, and why is the basilic vein riskier?
opciones: The median cubital vein, which lies between muscles; an artery and a nerve run under the basilic vein
The basilic vein, between the muscles; an artery and a nerve run under the median cubital vein
The cephalic vein, since it is visible with no tourniquet; the basilic is where veins are diverting
Whichever vein already has a peripheral venous access in place; the basilic is too deep to reach
preguntas.explicacion: Step 3 of the guideline singles out the median cubital vein: it sits between muscles and is usually the easiest to puncture. The basilic vein has an artery and a nerve running beneath it, so a puncture there risks damaging one of them and tends to hurt more; swapping the two veins reverses the guideline. The same step warns against putting the needle in where veins branch, because that raises the chance of a haematoma, but it does not say that of the basilic vein, and it does not single out the cephalic vein at all. And in hospitalized patients it says NOT to draw from an existing peripheral venous access, because the result may be false.

preguntas.pregunta: How does a tort differ from a crime?
opciones: A tort is a private wrong and aims to compensate; a crime wrongs society
A tort is heard by a jury and a crime is decided by a judge alone
A tort applies to institutions and a crime applies only to individuals
A tort is defined by state statute and a crime only by federal statute
preguntas.explicacion: Crimes are wrongs against the state or society at large, and criminal liability exists to enforce public justice. Tort law deals with private wrongs, and its central purpose is compensating the victim rather than punishing the wrongdoer. The same act can be both: gross negligence that endangers other people's lives can be a tort and a crime at once.

Rolling the tube between both palms briskly
Shaking the tube eight to ten times in a row

preguntas.pregunta: A result is recorded as 20/40. What does the lower number mean?
opciones: The distance at which normal eyes read that same smallest line
The distance in feet at which the patient was standing from the chart
The number of letters the patient managed to read on that line
The percentage of normal vision the patient retains in that eye
preguntas.explicacion: The top number is how far the patient stood, in feet, and the bottom number is how far away someone with normal sight could still read the smallest line the patient could read. preguntas.pregunta: Why does the CDC say that aspiration is not needed before a vaccine is injected?
opciones: The vessels near the recommended sites are too small to take a push of vaccine
The vaccine does no harm if it enters a vein, so the check adds no safety here
Aspiration is skipped only when the site chosen for the vaccine is the deltoid
Aspiration is replaced by injecting slowly, which does the same job more gently
preguntas.explicacion: Aspiration was recommended originally for theoretical reasons and has never been evaluated scientifically. The veins and arteries a needle can reach at the sites recommended for vaccination are too small to allow an intravenous push without blowing the vessel out. Aspirating also adds pain, through longer needle dwell time and the shearing of tissue; injecting rapidly without it hurt infants less in one study.

preguntas.pregunta: During a venipuncture the blood filling the tube is dark red rather than bright red. What does that color indicate?
opciones: Venous blood carrying deoxyhemoglobin, which is a darker red
Arterial blood carrying oxyhemoglobin, which is bright red
Hemolyzed blood in which hemoglobin has left the red cells
Blood with a high hematocrit from living at high altitude
preguntas.explicacion: Hemoglobin is a pigment whose color depends on oxygen: freshly oxygenated blood is bright red, and blood that has given up oxygen in the tissues is a duskier, darker red. Oxyhemoglobin is the bright red form and deoxyhemoglobin the darker form. Dark red is therefore the expected color of venous blood, not a sign of hemolysis or of a high hematocrit.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient is given a guaiac card kit for occult blood at home. How are the samples taken?

From one area of a single stool, repeated only if the result is positive
From several areas of the stool, all taken from one bowel movement

Before looking for any vein, so that all the veins stay engorged during the whole of the inspection

preguntas.pregunta: Which cost may a practice include in the fee it charges a patient for a copy of her record?
opciones: The labor of copying the information, plus postage when she asks to have it mailed
The time staff spend searching for and retrieving the chart from the storage room
The share of the electronic system's annual license attributable to storing her data
The cost of verifying her identity and documenting the request in the practice log
preguntas.explicacion: The fee has to be reasonable and cost based, and only four components may go into it: labor for copying, whether on paper or electronically; supplies such as a CD or USB drive if portable media are requested; postage where the copy is mailed; and preparing an explanation or summary if the patient agreed to one. Verification, documentation, search and retrieval, and system maintenance may not be charged, even where state law allows it.
preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Individuals Right under HIPAA to Access their Health Information: Fees for Copies
preguntas.subtema: Access fees · CCMA 5 k175 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.4.f · CMAA 3C k36 · NCMA 4.3

preguntas.pregunta: Which information is excluded from the HIPAA right of access?
opciones: Psychotherapy notes and information compiled for a legal proceeding
Laboratory results, which belong to the ordering physician until released
Billing records, which are financial rather than clinical
Records older than 6 years, which need not be retained
preguntas.explicacion: The right of access in 164.524(a)(1) covers PHI in a designated record set for as long as it is kept, with two exceptions: psychotherapy notes, and information compiled in reasonable anticipation of, or for use in, a civil, criminal or administrative proceeding. Access may also be denied without review in limited cases such as certain correctional and research situations, and with a right to review when a licensed professional judges that access is likely to endanger someone. Laboratory and billing records are part of the designated record set and remain accessible.
preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 164.524(a)(1)-(4), Standard: Access to protected health information
preguntas.subtema: Exceptions to access · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k220 · CMA II.E.1.c · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3C k36

preguntas.pregunta: Which of these is listed as an exception to a patient's confidentiality rights?
opciones: Sharing what is needed to head off imminent danger to someone
Sharing a diagnosis with a coworker who asks out of concern
Sharing a chart with a relative who is not involved in the care
Sharing a record with a magazine once the name is left out
preguntas.explicacion: The exceptions are named and narrow: sharing within the organization or with its business partners for medical, revenue, quality or risk management purposes; to head off imminent physical danger to the patient or to others; to assist a criminal investigation when a law official demands it; to preserve public health, which is why certain infections are reportable; and to communicate with a surrogate when the patient lacks the legal capacity to decide. Concern for a colleague's patient is not on the list.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Rights and Ethics", Issues of Concern: Health Information Privacy and Control
preguntas.subtema: Exceptions to confidentiality · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k213 · CMA II.E.2 · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3

preguntas.pregunta: Where does an intramuscular vaccine go in a 4-month-old infant, and with which needle?
opciones: Vastus lateralis of the anterolateral thigh, with a 1-inch 22 to 25 gauge needle
Vastus lateralis of the anterolateral thigh, with a 5/8-inch 23 to 25 gauge needle
Deltoid muscle of the arm, with a 5/8-inch to 1-inch 22 to 25 gauge needle
Ventrogluteal site, with a 1 to 1.25-inch 22 to 25 gauge needle, thigh in reserve
preguntas.explicacion: For infants from 1 to 12 months the intramuscular site is the vastus lateralis of the anterolateral thigh and the needle is 1 inch, 22 to 25 gauge. A neonate of 28 days or younger takes five eighths of an inch at the same site. The deltoid becomes the preferred site from 3 years onward, and 5/8 of an inch with 23 to 25 gauge is the subcutaneous needle at every age.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Vaccine Administration: During the Visit, Needle Length and Gauge Charts
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B k72 · CMA I.D.2.d(1) · RMA III.G.2.e · NCMA 1.9

preguntas.pregunta: A patient's platelet count is 155,000 per microliter. Is that typical, and where is about a third of the body's platelets kept?
opciones: Yes, typical is 150,000 to 160,000 per µL; about a third is held in the spleen
Yes, typical is 150,000 to 160,000 per µL; about a third is held in the liver
No, typical is 5,000 to 10,000 per µL; about a third is held in the spleen
No, typical is 2,000 to 3,000 per µL; about a third is held in the red marrow
preguntas.explicacion: A typical platelet count is 150,000 to 160,000 per microliter, so 155,000 fits. After entering the circulation, about one third of the platelets migrate to the spleen, where they are stored and released when a vessel ruptures. The 5,000 to 10,000 figure is the leukocyte count, and 2000 to 3000 is the number of platelets one megakaryocyte releases in its lifetime.
preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.4 Leukocytes and Platelets, Platelets
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k4 (applied D5) · PBT I.B.4 · CCMA 3E k122 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1

preguntas.pregunta: In an acute hemorrhage with no time to cross match, type O negative blood is transfused. Why is O negative called the universal donor?
opciones: Its cells lack A, B and Rh D antigens, so recipient antibodies do not react
Its plasma lacks anti-A and anti-B, so it cannot agglutinate any cells
Its cells carry both A antigen and B antigen, matching every recipient
It is the most common type, so it is the one always kept in stock
preguntas.explicacion: Type O erythrocytes display neither A nor B antigen, so the anti-A or anti-B antibodies in the recipient's plasma find nothing on the donated cells to attack, and Rh negative cells also lack the D antigen. One caution: type O plasma does carry anti-A and anti-B, but the transfused volume is small compared with the recipient's own blood, so the effect is usually limited.
preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.6 Blood Typing, ABO Transfusion Protocols
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k5 (applied D4 4D) · PBT I.B.4 · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1

preguntas.pregunta: What must the employer's written cleaning and decontamination schedule take into account?
opciones: The location, the kind of surface, the soil present, and the tasks done there
The brand of disinfectant and the date its container was first opened
The number of employees on each shift and the dates of their training
The volume of regulated waste the area produced during the past year
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(4)(i) makes the employer keep the worksite clean and sanitary, and then requires a written schedule for cleaning and a method of decontamination decided from four things: where in the facility the area is, what kind of surface has to be cleaned, what kind of soil is on it, and which tasks or procedures are performed there. A draw room and a storage corridor therefore do not get the same schedule. Disinfectant brands, staffing and waste volume are not the criteria the paragraph names.
preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(4)(i), Housekeeping: General

preguntas.pregunta: How does the WHO describe the order of draw for skin-puncture (capillary) specimens compared with venipuncture?
opciones: It is the reverse: haematology first, then chemistry and blood bank
It is the same: culture first, then coagulation, then the additive tubes
It is the reverse: chemistry and blood bank first, then haematology
It has no fixed order, because microtubes hold too little for carry-over
preguntas.explicacion: Section 7.1.3 says that with skin punctures the haematology specimen is taken first, followed by chemistry and blood bank, and that this is the reverse of the venipuncture order. The reason given is to limit the effect of platelet clumping. The same section adds that when more than two specimens are needed, venipuncture may give more accurate results.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 7.1.3, Order of draw

preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist reuses the same elastic tourniquet all morning without cleaning it. Why is that a problem?
opciones: Tourniquets have been found carrying hospital-acquired bacteria
Tourniquets lose their elasticity after several patients in a row
Tourniquets absorb the alcohol used to prepare the puncture site
Tourniquets have to be discarded after each patient is finished
preguntas.explicacion: Best practice for the tourniquet is a clean elastic band that is reprocessed between patients, and the reason given is direct: contamination with nosocomial bacteria has been documented on tourniquets, so one that travels from arm to arm carries them along. The related warning is that a latex glove must not be used as a tourniquet on a patient with a history of latex allergy.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010), Annex A, Table B.1: Safe blood-sampling equipment, Tourniquet

preguntas.pregunta: A quality committee reviews a one-year audit of an emergency laboratory that received 453,171 specimens. Which test group carried the highest rejection ratio?
opciones: Coagulation testing, rejected at about 13 % of what arrived
Blood gas analyses, rejected at about 10 % of everything arriving
Urine analyses, rejected at about 9 % of what arrived
Biochemistry testing, rejected at about 3 % of what arrived
preguntas.explicacion: Coagulation led that audit at 13.3 %, with therapeutic drug monitoring close behind at 12.8 % and hormone testing around 12 %. Blood gases reached 9.8 % and urine 9.2 %, while biochemistry at 2.5 % and the complete blood count at 3.2 % were the least affected. Coagulation suffers most because red cell clots and a wrong blood-to-anticoagulant ratio are exactly what ruin a citrate tube.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Specimen rejection in laboratory medicine: Necessary for patient safety?" (Biochem Med 2015, PMC4622196), Results
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5I · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3D9 k117 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a

preguntas.pregunta: A laboratory audits its identification errors and finds that most of them share one feature. Based on a seven-year study of preanalytical errors, which feature is that?
opciones: The sample carried fewer than two patient identifiers
The barcode had been printed for a different test panel
The sample had been labeled after arriving in the laboratory
The requisition and the tube listed different collection times
preguntas.explicacion: In the laboratory that measured its preanalytical quality indicators, identification problems were the second most frequent error, and most of them consisted of a label with fewer than two identifiers; in newborns the rate was ten times higher because the small tubes leave little room to write two. Wrong panels, late labeling and time mismatches are other errors, not the one that dominated.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Detection of haemolysis, a frequent preanalytical problem in the serum of newborns and adults" (EJIFCC 2020, PMC7109500), Results and Discussion
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 k89 · PBT III.B · CCMA 3D9 k117 · NCMA 2C.14 · RMA III.C.4.a

preguntas.pregunta: Which reading is usually described as hypotension in an adult?
opciones: Under 90 systolic or under 60 diastolic, read together with the symptoms
Under 100 systolic or under 70 diastolic, read together with the symptoms
Under 120 systolic or under 80 diastolic, which is the lower limit of normal
Under 80 systolic alone, since the diastolic value carries no weight here
preguntas.explicacion: There is no universal cut-off, but clinicians commonly speak of hypotension below 90 systolic or below 60 diastolic. The diagnosis leans on the context and the symptoms: light-headedness, dizziness, blurred vision, nausea and weakness. Dehydration, acute illness and medicines are the usual causes.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Blood Pressure Measurement", Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A7 k47 · CMA I.A.1.i · RMA III.E.2.e · NCMA 2B.7

preguntas.pregunta: Before home health services are certified for a patient, what has to happen?
opciones: A provider assesses the patient face to face and orders care from a certified agency
A hospice physician meets the patient face to face and recertifies the prognosis
The patient completes three days as an inpatient in a hospital that accepts Medicare
The agency files a claim so that the contractor can decide medical necessity in advance
preguntas.explicacion: A health care provider, a nurse practitioner for example, must assess the patient face to face before certifying the need for home health. A provider has to order the care and a Medicare-certified home health agency has to deliver it. The three-day inpatient stay belongs to skilled nursing coverage and the recertified prognosis to hospice.
preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Home health services: Provider requirements
preguntas.subtema: Coordinating home health · CCMA 4E · CMAA 1 k1 · NCMA 3.1

preguntas.pregunta: Why is the light grey top tube (sodium fluoride and potassium oxalate) the usual choice for a glucose specimen?
opciones: Its antiglycolytic additive keeps the glucose level stable for days
Its gel separator keeps the plasma away from the cells after spinning
Its clot activator produces serum faster than a plain red top tube
Its broth mixture keeps microorganisms alive until they can be cultured
preguntas.explicacion: The WHO table describes the additive of the grey tube as an antiglycolytic agent, that is, one that blocks the breakdown of glucose, and says it keeps the glucose value stable for up to five days. Glucose is the use the table gives for it, with a note that it needs a full draw because a short draw may cause haemolysis. Gel separators belong to the serum separator and PST tubes, the clot activator to the red top, and the broth to the blood culture bottle.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.3, Recommended order of draw
preguntas.subtema: Tubes and additives · CPT D3 k57 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E k136 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.6

preguntas.pregunta: Halfway through a suture removal the wound edges begin to gape. What is done?
opciones: Stop removing, apply Steri-Strips to pull the edges together, and notify the provider
Remove the rest quickly, since a partly sutured line pulls unevenly on the wound edges
Stop removing, cover the line with a dry sterile dressing, and reassess in seven days
Remove the rest and close the gap with a skin adhesive, then dress the line as usual
preguntas.explicacion: Open edges mean the removal stops there. Steri-Strips are cut and applied with tension so they draw the edges back together, and the provider is notified. The wound line is watched for separation the whole time the sutures are coming out, and the procedure is halted at any concern, because dehiscence is what removing them too early causes.
preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, 20.10 Checklist for Intermittent Suture Removal
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B8 k75 · CMA I.C.2.c (2027 I.C.2.c) · RMA III.D.2.m · NCMA 2B.16

preguntas.pregunta: Which identifiers are acceptable for confirming the right patient before a medication is administered?
opciones: The full name, the date of birth, or the identification number the facility assigns
The room number and the bed letter, both of which the chart lists on admission
The full name on its own, since two patients never share a name on one unit
The barcode scan on its own, which was brought in to replace two identifiers
preguntas.explicacion: Acceptable identifiers include the patient's full name, an identification number assigned by the facility, and the date of birth, confirmed against the wristband, an identification card, the patient's own statement where possible, or another method the policy allows. A room number is never used, because patients move. Barcode scanning adds a layer of safety but does not replace the requirement for two identifiers.
preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, ch. 15.2: Right Patient
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1C k22 · CMA I.D.2.a · RMA III.G.2.g · NCMA 1.5

preguntas.pregunta: A patient in a culture where health decisions are made collectively hesitates to sign a consent form. What is the culturally aware reading of that?
opciones: Written consent may be seen as a sign of mistrust; the process should allow for the family's role
Hesitation to sign means the patient lacks capacity and a surrogate must be sought
The patient is refusing care and the refusal should be documented at once
The form must be signed regardless, since the signature is the legal proof of consent
preguntas.explicacion: In certain cultures decisions are made collectively rather than by an individual signature, written consent may be perceived as a sign of mistrust, and the process may involve consulting a family patriarch or a designated male representative; undocumented immigrants may also fear signing. Cultural sensitivity is part of the consent process, and the emphasis on the signature as proof of understanding is itself being questioned.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Informed Consent", section Issues of Concern, Cultural Differences
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2A 2F k17 k43 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7B k216 · CMA E.3.a (both outlines) · NCMA 4.7

preguntas.pregunta: A clinician cannot find a pulse on the top of a patient's foot but finds every other pulse. What is one explanation?
opciones: That pulse is missing in roughly 10% of people because of anatomical variation
That pulse is missing in roughly 10% of people because of arterial stiffening with age
That pulse is felt only while the patient holds the first toe fully extended
That pulse disappears whenever systolic pressure falls below 100 mm Hg in the arm
preguntas.explicacion: The dorsalis pedis lies on the front of the foot, lateral to the tendon of extensor hallucis longus, and it is absent in about 10% of people for anatomical reasons. Asking the patient to extend the big toe lifts the tendon and helps find it when it is there. When pedal pulses are felt on both sides, peripheral arterial disease is unlikely.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Peripheral Pulse", Physical Examination Technique
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k49 · RMA III.E.3 Pulse b · NCMA 2B.6

preguntas.pregunta: A woman has pendulous breast tissue sitting over the V4 landmark. What is done?
opciones: The electrode goes on its landmark, even on top of the breast
The electrode goes below the breast, off its usual landmark
The breast is taped upward so the electrode sits on the wall
The electrode is left off and the tracing runs on five leads
preguntas.explicacion: The breasts are allowed to fall naturally, and the chest electrodes are placed on their landmarks even when that means placing one over breast tissue: correct position counts for more than closeness to the chest wall. The patient must stay very still so the tissue does not shift the electrode.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 3.3 Examination Procedures
preguntas.subtema: CCMA k150 k151 k153 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(i) · RMA III.F.6.a.i · NCMA 2D.2

preguntas.pregunta: About how far above the intended puncture site is the tourniquet applied, measured in inches?
opciones: About 3 inches above the site
About 1 inch above the site
About 6 inches above the puncture site
About 2 cm above the site
preguntas.explicacion: A preferably disposable tourniquet goes almost 3 inches above the targeted venipuncture site, tight enough to stop venous flow while arterial flow continues. The WHO expresses the same distance as four to five finger widths. Two centimetres is the minimum area the alcohol swab must cover in the WHO's Step 5, not a tourniquet distance.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Preparation (tourniquet application)
