preguntas.pregunta: A patient is frightened because a child's fever reached 40 °C (104 °F) and fears brain damage. What does the evidence show?
opciones: Brain damage is not expected below 42 °C (107.6 °F), a level infection rarely reaches
Brain damage begins above 40 °C (104 °F), which is why a reading that high is an emergency
Brain damage depends on how long the fever lasts, not on the temperature reached
Brain damage follows any febrile seizure, so a seizure with fever means lasting harm
preguntas.explicacion: Damage to the brain is not expected from fever unless the temperature climbs above 42 °C (107.6 °F), and untreated fevers from infection seldom pass 40.6 °C (105 °F) except when the child is bundled up or kept somewhere hot. Most febrile seizures are over quickly and leave no lasting harm.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Fever
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A7 k52 · RMA III.E.3 Temperature d · NCMA 2B.7

preguntas.pregunta: At what concentration in water are ethyl and isopropyl alcohol most bactericidal?
opciones: 60 to 90 percent
30 to 50 percent
95 to 100 percent
40 to 55 percent
preguntas.explicacion: Alcohols work by denaturing protein, and protein denatures faster with water present, so absolute alcohol is weaker than a mixture. The optimum band runs from 60 to 90 percent in water, and cidal activity drops sharply once the solution is diluted below 50 percent. They are rapidly bactericidal, tuberculocidal, fungicidal and virucidal, but never sporicidal.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization (2008), Alcohol: Overview
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3C5 k105 · CMA I.B.5.b (2027 I.B.4.b) · RMA III.A.4 · NCMA 2A.2

preguntas.pregunta: Booking a patient who uses a wheelchair, a receptionist tells her to bring somebody along who can help her onto the table. Is that acceptable?
opciones: No, she may come alone and the practice provides the assistance she needs
No, unless the office has no lift and no member of staff trained to transfer
Yes, so long as the same is asked of every patient who uses a wheelchair
Yes, because helping a patient undress falls outside a receptionist's duties
preguntas.explicacion: A patient may bring a friend or relative if she wishes, but she may equally come by herself, and the provider then gives the reasonable assistance that lets her receive the care: help with dressing, with getting on and off the table, with positioning, and with staying balanced once there. The staff member asks the patient what help she wants and how.
preguntas.fuente: ADA.gov, Access to Medical Care for Individuals with Mobility Disabilities: Commonly Asked Questions
preguntas.subtema: Assistance at the visit · CCMA 4 k157 · CMA II.F.3.c · RMA I.D.1.c · CMAA 7 k98 · NCMA 3.1

preguntas.pregunta: Two terms sit side by side in one report: arteriosclerosis and stenosis. Which contrast between those endings is correct?
opciones: The first names a hardening and the second a narrowing or blockage
The first names a narrowing and the second a hardening or stiffening
The first names a hardening and the second an expansion or dilation
The first names a blockage and the second a softening or weakening
preguntas.explicacion: Sclera- and sclero- mean hardness, and -sclerosis is a hardening; on the artery root that gives hardened arteries. Sten- and steno- mean narrowed or blocked. Two more parts fall into that space and mean the opposite or something else: -ectasis is an expansion or dilation, and -malacia is a softening.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix A: Word Parts and What They Mean, Good and Bad
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k11 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.a) · RMA I.B.1.a · CMAA 1 k9 · NCMA 1.2

preguntas.pregunta: A patient starts breathing again during CPR while the office waits for the ambulance. What is done next?
opciones: Roll the patient onto one side and keep watching the breathing
Sit the patient upright in a chair and offer small sips of water
Keep the patient flat on the back and raise the legs about 12 inches (30 cm)
Resume compressions at once, since breathing after a code is agonal
preguntas.explicacion: Once breathing returns, the patient is rolled onto one side with the lower arm supporting the head and the upper knee bent to a right angle, and breathing is rechecked until help arrives. Raising the legs about 12 inches belongs to shock and fainting, and compressions on someone who is breathing, coughing or moving can stop the heart.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "CPR - adult and child 9 years and older", First Aid
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k83 · CMA I.B.9.c · 2027 I.B.8.c · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2A.10 EKB 15

preguntas.pregunta: A patient is seen for a scar left by a burn two years ago. How is that coded?
opciones: With two codes, the residual condition first and the sequela code second
With two codes, the sequela code first and the residual condition second
With one code only, since a sequela is a combination code by definition
With no sequela code, because more than a year has passed since the burn
preguntas.explicacion: A sequela is the residual effect left after the acute phase of an illness or injury has ended, and the examples given include a scar left by a burn, a deviated septum after a nasal fracture and infertility after old tuberculosis. Coding one generally takes two codes: the condition or nature of the residual is sequenced first and the sequela code second. There is no time limit.
preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026, Section I.B.10
preguntas.subtema: Diagnostic coding · CMA III.G.1.b (2027 III.G.1.b) · CMAA 5 k68, 6A · CCMA 5I k184 · RMA II.A.3.a · NCMA 3.8

preguntas.pregunta: Besides written policies, which administrative duties does the Privacy Rule place on a covered entity?
opciones: Naming a privacy official and a contact for complaints, and training the whole workforce
Naming a privacy official whose approval is needed before any record leaves the office
Training only the staff who handle claims, since billing carries the greatest privacy risk
Filing the practice's privacy policies with the Office for Civil Rights before they take effect
preguntas.explicacion: A covered entity must designate a privacy official responsible for its policies and procedures and a contact person or office to receive complaints and answer questions. It must train all workforce members as appropriate to their functions, apply sanctions to those who violate the policies, mitigate harm it learns about, and refrain from retaliating against anyone who exercises a right or files a complaint.
preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Privacy Rule: Administrative Requirements
preguntas.subtema: Privacy administration · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA III.E.1 · RMA I.C.5 · CMAA 3B k33 · NCMA 4.3

preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist fills the purple EDTA tube before the serum separator tube that will be used for a chemistry panel. What problem does this kind of error create?
opciones: Anticoagulant on the needle can be carried into the following tube and contaminate it
The serum tube will fail to clot within the 10 to 15 minutes expected before it is spun
The vacuum of the second tube is lost, so it fills only partially or not at all
The EDTA tube will show platelet clumping and a falsely low platelet count
preguntas.explicacion: Under Issues of Concern, the tube review describes contamination in which anticoagulant from one tube sticks to the vacutainer needle and passes into the next tube; that is why the sequence matters. Clotting time, loss of vacuum and EDTA-related platelet clumping are all real issues in the same material, but none of them is caused by drawing the tubes out of order.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Laboratory Tube Collection", section Issues of Concern, Contamination
preguntas.subtema: Order of draw · CPT D3 3J k59 k9 · PBT II.H.1 · CCMA 3E6 k132 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.7

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with COPD reads 93% and is upset at not being in the usual range. What is the explanation?
opciones: Somewhat lower values can be acceptable in chronic lung disease and at high elevation
Any value under 95% is abnormal for everyone, and oxygen is started at that point
Chronic lung disease raises the acceptable floor, so 93% is lower than it should be
The reading has to be repeated on the earlobe, which is the site used in lung disease
preguntas.explicacion: The normal band of 95% to 100% describes healthy adults at sea level. In someone with COPD or pneumonia, or someone living where the air holds less oxygen, a value below that can be acceptable, and what matters is the patient's own usual level and the trend. The reporting thresholds of 92% and 88% still stand.

preguntas.pregunta: How does an under-filled citrate tube distort coagulation results?
opciones: PT, aPTT and thrombin time come out longer and fibrinogen comes out lower
PT, aPTT and thrombin time come out shorter and fibrinogen comes out higher
PT and aPTT are unchanged, but the platelet count comes out falsely low
PT comes out longer while aPTT and fibrinogen are unaffected by the fill level
preguntas.explicacion: When too little blood meets a fixed volume of citrate the sample-to-anticoagulant ratio is wrong, and the clotting times PT, aPTT and thrombin time become significantly longer while fibrinogen levels come out significantly lower. preguntas.pregunta: Why is a patient who has fainted kept lying flat rather than allowed to sit up right away?

Sitting up compresses the abdomen and forces blood down into the legs, raising the heart rate
The horizontal position lets the tourniquet be reapplied safely for the remaining tubes
Sitting up too soon converts the faint into a seizure with tonic-clonic activity

Crushing the structure named by the root
Binding the structure named by the root
Puncturing the structure named by the root

The person is pale and weak for a few minutes after waking
The person fainted while seated and woke up within a minute
The person reports having fainted once before during a blood draw

Looked over every week, plus a maintenance check every two years

Looked over once a year, plus a maintenance check every five years

Do it, but only on surfaces that a patient with broken skin has actually been resting on
Do it, since a stronger agent than the counter needs can never leave the surface underprocessed
Do it, provided the counters are rinsed with water and dried before the next patient enters
preguntas.explicacion: Countertops are noncritical environmental surfaces, and the recommendation on them is flat: high-level disinfectants and liquid chemical sterilants are not to be used for them. preguntas.pregunta: Where do the cephalic and basilic veins of the arm begin, and which side of the limb does each drain?
opciones: From the dorsal venous arch of the hand; cephalic on the radial side, basilic on the medial side
From the palmar venous arches of the hand; cephalic on the medial side, basilic on the radial side
From the brachial vein, which splits at the elbow into a lateral cephalic and a medial basilic branch
From the median antebrachial vein of the forearm, which divides into both of them below the elbow
preguntas.explicacion: The superficial veins of the hand arise from the dorsal venous arch on the back of the hand, which drains into the cephalic and basilic veins; the cephalic drains mainly the radial side of the limb and the basilic the medial side, and the two are joined near the elbow by the median cubital vein. The palmar arches feed the deep radial and ulnar veins, which unite to form the brachial vein.

The wet alcohol haemolyses the sample
Potassium is falsely increased
The tourniquet limit is exceeded

Removing the stopper lets the additive evaporate
Removing the stopper activates the safety mechanism
Removing the stopper breaks the order of draw

Ask the patient to bend the arm
Withdraw the needle and apply gauze
Invert the collected tubes 8 to 10 times

Hardware bought from an approved supplier and kept on the practice's asset list
Media held by the software vendor on the practice's behalf under its contract
Hardware that stores records, but not the media used only to back them up

opciones: The bevel may still be partly outside the vein; flatten the angle and advance 1 to 2 mm
The vein has been passed through completely; withdraw the needle fully and re-puncture above
The tube has lost its vacuum; pull the needle back out of the skin and change the tube
The tourniquet is too tight; remove it entirely and wait for the flow to return
preguntas.explicacion: If only a small drop of blood is seen, the needle bevel may remain partially outside the vein, and the device should be flattened slightly and advanced in 1 to 2 mm increments until flow is adequate. A lost vacuum is a separate cause described in the tube collection review and calls for a new tube, not for withdrawing the needle. preguntas.pregunta: A plasma sample will be tested for viral load now and possibly retested several times over the coming months. Why is it aliquoted before freezing?
opciones: So each retest thaws a fresh portion, avoiding the loss seen after repeated freeze-thaw cycles
So the erythrocytes settle in one portion and the plasma stays free of heme when it thaws
So the laboratory can send one portion to a reference laboratory without a referral record
So the heparin concentration falls below the level that inhibits amplification in each portion
preguntas.explicacion: Serum and plasma tolerate freezing, but the number of freeze-thaw cycles a target survives varies: one study saw a 16 % fall in HCV RNA titres after five cycles and recommended aliquoting the sample to limit the loss, while others found no loss after eight or ten. Splitting the sample lets each retest use a portion thawed only once. Erythrocytes are removed before freezing, not by aliquoting, and heparin is a reason to reject the tube, not to split it.

preguntas.pregunta: A coworker asks you to look up a neighbor's laboratory results, saying she only wants to know whether the neighbor is all right. What should you do?
opciones: Refuse, because access is limited to the information each role needs for its own job duties
Look it up but read out only the abnormal values, which keeps the disclosure to a minimum
Look it up, since a coworker inside the same covered entity is part of the same workforce
Look it up after the neighbor's next visit, once a treatment relationship has been created
preguntas.explicacion: Internal access is governed by role. A covered entity's policies must name who needs which categories of information to do their duties, and access outside that is a violation whether or not anything is repeated afterwards. preguntas.pregunta: How many times are the rights of medication administration verified before a dose is given to a patient?
opciones: At least three times, checking the six rights on each of those occasions
Once, at the bedside, at the moment the medication is handed to the patient
Twice, once against the written order and once against the pharmacy label
Five times, one for each of the five traditional rights of administration

preguntas.pregunta: How do anti-Rh antibodies differ from the anti-A and anti-B antibodies of the ABO system?
opciones: They form only in Rh− people after exposure to Rh+ cells (sensitization)
They are preformed from early exposure to antigens in foods and microbes
They form in Rh+ people after a first transfusion of Rh− blood
They are present in all type O plasma along with anti-A and anti-B
preguntas.explicacion: The two systems differ: ABO antibodies are preformed because A and B antigens are met early in life in food and microbes, whereas antibodies to the Rh antigen are made only by Rh negative individuals after exposure to Rh positive cells, a process called sensitization, which follows an Rh-incompatible transfusion or, more often, the birth of an Rh positive baby to an Rh negative parent.

preguntas.pregunta: A clinic is choosing between two safety winged-steel needles. Which feature matches what is recommended for a device with a safety mechanism?

The shield is added by the user after the needle leaves the patient's vein
The shield can be switched off when the phlebotomist needs to reuse the holder

preguntas.pregunta: Once the jerking of a seizure stops, why is the patient rolled onto one side?

So that the tongue can be held forward with a gloved finger
So that blood pressure can be taken on the upper arm at once
So that the jerking is less likely to start over on the other side

preguntas.pregunta: A patient becomes overheated. Which set of responses does the heat-loss center of the brain set off?
opciones: Skin vessels widen, sweat glands step up output, and breathing deepens
Skin vessels narrow, sweat glands shut down, and breathing grows shallow
Skin vessels widen, the thyroid speeds metabolism, and shivering begins
Skin vessels narrow, blood shifts to deep veins, and shivering begins
preguntas.explicacion: When the temperature center reads a value above the normal range it stimulates the heat-loss center, and three things follow: vessels in the skin dilate so core blood can radiate heat at the surface, sweat glands increase output so evaporation carries heat away, and respiration deepens. The narrowing, deep-vein shift and shivering belong to the heat-gain response to cold.
preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 1.5 Homeostasis, Negative Feedback

preguntas.pregunta: An outpatient ran 10 km at dawn before his morning cortisol draw. Which preparation point was missed?
opciones: Stress and exercise raise cortisol; rest before the test was needed
Cortisol requires a 12-hour fast, which the run interrupted
The draw should have been at 4 p.m., when cortisol normally peaks
Running is acceptable as long as he drank only plain water
preguntas.explicacion: Stress and exercise can raise cortisol levels, so the patient may need to rest before the test, and a blood cortisol needs two appointments in one day. General preparation also bans on excessive physical activity in the 24 hours before outpatient sampling. No fast is imposed for cortisol, and 4 p.m. is the low point, not the peak.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Cortisol Test, section Will I need to do anything to prepare for the test

preguntas.pregunta: An erythrocyte sedimentation rate rack stands on a bench beside a centrifuge, leaning a few degrees off the vertical. What does that do to the result?
opciones: The rate rises, and a tilt of only 3° can add as much as 30 % to it
The rate falls, because tilted red cells settle against the tube wall
The rate is unchanged, since the reading is corrected for the angle
The rate rises, but only when the tube was also underfilled at collection
preguntas.explicacion: Technical conditions move this test more than most. A tube tilted 3° from the vertical can raise the value by as much as 30 %, and vibration from nearby equipment raises it too. A warm room lowers blood viscosity and pushes the rate up, and direct sunlight also raises it. Underfilling adds air bubbles, which lift the reading as well, so the rack belongs upright, still and out of the sun.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate", section Interfering Factors

preguntas.pregunta: A haematoma forms at a site where the technique looked correct throughout. Which omission is the likely explanation?
opciones: Pressure was not kept up during and after the needle came out
Pressure was kept up too long after the needle had come out
The tourniquet was released before the needle was withdrawn
The site was cleaned with alcohol rather than povidone iodine
preguntas.explicacion: A haematoma can form when adequate pressure is not applied during and after the draw, which is why the gauze is taped down to give continuous pressure. Releasing the band before the needle comes out is the correct order, and alcohol is the preferred antiseptic for a routine draw.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", sections Complications and Technique or Treatment

preguntas.pregunta: A patient complains loudly that nobody called back with her results. Which two steps open service recovery?
opciones: Apologize and acknowledge, then listen and ask openly
Fix it quickly and fairly, then offer some atonement
Follow up afterward, and remember what was promised
Document the complaint, then route it to a manager
preguntas.explicacion: The six-step process runs: apologize and acknowledge; listen, empathize and ask open questions; fix the problem quickly and fairly; offer atonement; follow up; and remember your promises. Fixing and atoning come only after the person has been heard, which is where recovery is won or lost.

preguntas.pregunta: A finished tracing is checked for quality before the patient leaves. How much baseline shift between neighboring complexes is still acceptable?
opciones: A vertical distance of no more than 5 mm between them
A vertical distance of no more than 1 mm between them
A vertical distance of no more than 10 mm between them
A vertical distance of no more than 25 mm between them
preguntas.explicacion: A recording is accepted only against a short list of minimums, and one of them puts a ceiling on drift: measured from one complex to the next, the baseline may not climb or fall by more than 5 mm. Anything beyond that is sent back to be run again.

preguntas.pregunta: A vaccinated phlebotomist with a documented anti-HBs level of 10 mIU/mL or more is exposed to an HBsAg-positive patient. What does the CDC recommend?
opciones: No post-exposure treatment and no source testing; the documented response is protective
One dose of HBIG plus a vaccine booster, then anti-HBs testing 1 to 2 months afterward
Two doses of HBIG one month apart, since vaccinated workers cannot be revaccinated
A repeat anti-HBs test now, with HBIG only if the level has fallen below 10 mIU/mL
preguntas.explicacion: For a clinician with written documentation of a complete series and a recorded anti-HBs of 10 mIU/mL or more, the CDC says testing the source for HBsAg is unnecessary and no post-exposure prophylaxis is needed regardless of the source's status; the table lists a documented responder as needing no action. Immunocompetent responders have long-term protection and do not need periodic retesting, even though antibody levels wane. HBIG with revaccination is for those found below 10 mIU/mL without prior documentation, and two HBIG doses are for non-responders after two series.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Responding to HBV Exposures in Health Care Settings, Vaccinated clinicians with anti-HBs documentation and Table 1

preguntas.pregunta: A marathon runner has a resting pulse of 48 beats per minute and no symptoms. How is this read?
opciones: It fits the 40 to 60 band reported for well-trained athletes at rest
It is bradycardia in any adult and is reported to the provider before the visit ends
It is a counting error, since a rate under 60 cannot be palpated at the wrist
It fits the range for adults over 65, in whom the resting rate falls with age
preguntas.explicacion: Well-trained athletes rest at 40 to 60 beats per minute, so 48 with no symptoms fits that group rather than signalling disease. The general adult floor is 60, and resting heart rate does not fall simply because a person is older: what declines with age is the maximum rate reached on exertion.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Pulse

preguntas.pregunta: An older patient's daughter stays for the whole visit. When does the guidance suggest asking her to step out?
opciones: For part of the visit, so sensitive topics can be raised in private
Only once the patient signs a release form naming her as a contact
As a rule never, since a companion may stay through the whole visit
Only when the patient is being asked about paying for the visit
preguntas.explicacion: Companions can help the patient express concerns and reinforce what is said, but the patient is first asked how they see the companion's role. Asking the companion to step out for part of the visit gives the patient private time for sensitive matters, and it stops the companion answering for the patient or covering cognitive lapses during a test of thinking.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient reports a home reading of 99.5 °F. Which Celsius value is charted, and what does it mean by mouth in a child?
opciones: 37.5 °C, which is exactly the oral threshold for fever in a child
37.2 °C, which is the axillary rather than the oral threshold in a child
38.0 °C, which is the rectal rather than the oral threshold in a child
36.5 °C, which is the lower edge of the normal adult reference range
preguntas.explicacion: Clinical sources publish the two scales as pairs: 99 °F is 37.2 °C, 99.5 °F is 37.5 °C and 100.4 °F is 38 °C. The middle pair is the point at which an oral reading counts as fever in a child, and in an adult the mouth is said to show fever above roughly 99 to 99.5 °F, depending on the hour of the day.

preguntas.pregunta: A test must be run on serum. Which tubes from the WHO table will provide it?
opciones: The red clot activator tube and the red-grey or gold serum separator tube
The dark green sodium heparin tube and the light green plasma separator tube
The purple EDTA tube and the light blue sodium citrate tube
The light grey oxalate/fluoride tube and the pale yellow ACD tube
preguntas.explicacion: In Table 2.3 the clot activator tube lets the blood clot so the serum can be separated by centrifugation, and the serum separator tube holds a gel that separates blood from serum when spun. Every other tube listed carries an anticoagulant, so the liquid it yields is plasma: heparin in the green tubes, EDTA and citrate in the purple and light blue, oxalate in the grey and ACD in the yellow.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.3, Recommended order of draw

preguntas.pregunta: A clinic tests three walk-in patients for influenza at the same time on cassettes. When and how should each cassette be identified?
opciones: Label each cassette with a patient identifier before the sample is collected, and label samples with two identifiers
Label each cassette after the result has developed, so that the ink does not interfere with the reading window
Write the patient's initials in the log next to the result instead of on the cassette, which stays unmarked
One identifier, the patient's last name, is enough on site because the cassettes never leave the testing area
preguntas.explicacion: Samples are labeled immediately after collection with at least two unique patient identifiers, such as name and date of birth, to prevent mix-ups; the label may also carry the date, time and collector. When a test requires the sample to be applied directly to the test device, a strip or cassette, the device is labeled with a patient identifier before the sample is collected. Improperly labeled samples are among the problems that must be documented and reported.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Ready? Set? Test! (2024), Set?: Collecting the Sample (Labeling Samples); Test!: Resolving Problems

preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist cleans the antecubital site with an alcohol-containing disinfectant and, to save time, inserts the needle while the skin is still wet. Why does the CDC object?
opciones: The disinfectant has to dry on the skin before the culture is drawn
Alcohol must be replaced by a water-based iodine prep for cultures
The site should have been re-palpated with a bare finger after cleaning
Alcohol is only for the bottle septum, never for the venipuncture site
preguntas.explicacion: For blood cultures the skin is disinfected with an alcohol-containing product and allowed to dry before the draw; improper antisepsis is a recognised cause of contamination. The alcohol removes the normal skin oils so that a water-based preparation can reach the skin surface, which is why alcohol is part of the prep rather than something to replace. Touching the cleaned site again is prohibited by the WHO's venipuncture steps, and 70% isopropyl alcohol is also the agent for the septum.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Blood Culture Contamination: An Overview for Infection Control and Antibiotic Stewardship Programs (2022), section 2 Proper Skin Antisepsis; and Quality Tool SOP model step 2
preguntas.subtema: Skin preparation for cultures · CPT D4 4A k75 · PBT II.G II.F · CCMA 3E k139 · NCMA 2C.8 bacterial culture site

preguntas.pregunta: A new phlebotomist says she was vaccinated against hepatitis B as a child but has no records. How does the CDC treat her?
opciones: As unvaccinated: only written, dated records count, so she should complete the series
As vaccinated: a single anti-HBs test of 10 mIU/mL or more proves immunity
As vaccinated: childhood vaccination is routine and needs no post-vaccination testing
As a non-responder: she should receive HBIG at hire and be tested every year
preguntas.explicacion: Only written, dated records count as evidence of hepatitis B vaccination, so clinicians who cannot document three doses are considered unvaccinated and should complete the series, with anti-HBs tested 1 to 2 months after the third dose. An anti-HBs of 10 mIU/mL or more is a reliable marker of protection only when testing follows a documented three-dose series, so a lone test in someone without records should not be read as immunity. Facilities are encouraged to look for old records and enter doses in the state immunization system.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Responding to HBV Exposures in Health Care Settings, Vaccine documentation; Vaccine protection and anti-HBs testing

preguntas.pregunta: A digital sublingual thermometer is chosen over a glass one for a busy intake. Which advantage does it offer?
opciones: It reports in about 10 to 20 seconds, against the 3 to 5 minutes a glass probe needs
It reports in about 3 to 5 seconds, against the 20 seconds a glass probe needs
It reaches core temperature values that a glass probe under the tongue cannot reach
It removes any need to ask about hot or cold drinks taken shortly before the reading is done
preguntas.explicacion: Digital sublingual thermometers take a disposable probe cover and give a result in roughly 10 to 20 seconds; a glass probe needs 3 to 5 minutes in place. Neither device corrects for a recent hot or cold drink or a cigarette, so that question is asked before either one is used.

preguntas.pregunta: A fungal culture of the blood is requested. Which container is used, and where does it fall in the sequence?
opciones: The culture bottle with broth, drawn first of all the containers
The culture bottle with broth, drawn after the coagulation tube
The pale yellow ACD tube, drawn first of all the containers used
The purple EDTA tube, drawn before any of the serum tubes are filled
preguntas.explicacion: The yellow and black striped culture bottle holds a broth that keeps micro-organisms viable, and its listed uses are aerobes, anaerobes and fungi. It is number 1 in the sequence, ahead of every other container. The ACD tube preserves nothing microbiological: it is used for tissue typing and DNA.

preguntas.pregunta: The swabs packaged with a rapid strep kit have run out, and sterile swabs from the culture supply are available. May they be used to collect the throat sample?
opciones: No; only the swabs supplied with the collection or test kit are used, because different swab materials can interfere with the result
Yes, if they are sterile and individually wrapped, since sterility is the only property the manufacturer's instructions require
Yes, if they are the same length and tip size, since only the physical dimensions of the swab affect the antigen extraction
Yes, but only from another kit made by the same manufacturer, since the swab material is standardized across all of its products
preguntas.explicacion: Collection devices must be used according to the current manufacturer's instructions, which means using only the swabs that come in the sample collection kit or the test kit. Swabs are made of different materials, and substituting one can interfere with the test result. Fingerstick and venipuncture devices are single-use and never reused, and some collection devices deliver a set sample volume or contain additives the test depends on.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Ready? Set? Test! (2024), Set?: Collecting the Sample (Using Collection Devices)

preguntas.pregunta: How is a lancet described among the sharps used in health care?
opciones: An instrument with a short two-edged blade that draws drops of blood
A hollow needle with a bevel that draws blood into an attached tube
A tubing system with a needle used to deliver drugs into the body
A needle that connects to tubing for transferring fluids in and out
preguntas.explicacion: A lancet, also called a fingerstick device, is an instrument with a short two-edged blade used to obtain drops of blood for testing, and it is commonly used in diabetes care. Infusion sets and connection needles are separate categories of sharp, used to deliver or transfer fluids.

preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist fills the light grey fluoride tube before the purple EDTA tube. What is the main risk?
opciones: Additive carried from one tube into the next, giving unreliable results
Loss of the vacuum in the purple tube as soon as it is pushed on
A short draw in the grey tube, which can haemolyse that specimen
Clotting in the purple tube, because its additive was left unmixed
preguntas.explicacion: A fixed sequence exists so that the additive of one tube is not carried into the tube filled next, and falsely raised or lowered values can follow in chemistry, haematology, serology and microbiology. A short draw and unmixed additive are real faults, but they come from filling and mixing, not order.

preguntas.pregunta: An accredited laboratory is asked to show how it monitors the journey its specimens make from the collecting clinics. Which four aspects does the quality standard name?

Time frame, distance, courier training and safety
Temperature, humidity, light exposure and safety
Temperature, container type, preservatives and cost

opciones: V1, II and V5, on the fourth, fifth and sixth channels
I, II and III, on the fourth, fifth and sixth channels
V1, V2 and V3, on the fourth, fifth and sixth channels
II, aVF and V6, on the fourth, fifth and sixth channels

preguntas.pregunta: Which password practice is consistent with HIPAA security guidance?
opciones: Unique passwords for each user, never shared, written down or emailed
A single department password changed each year at annual training
Passwords posted near the workstation so that coverage staff can log in quickly
Passwords of consecutive digits, which are easier to audit
preguntas.explicacion: Every worker who accesses patient records needs a unique, strong password that mixes letters, numbers and symbols, is changed periodically, is never shared, verbalized, written down near the computer or emailed, and is not built from consecutive digits or easily guessed information; the IT department checks password quality before granting access. Uniqueness matters because HITECH requires systems to track each user's activity. Passwords alone are considered weak protection, which is why some institutions add biometric authentication.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "HIPAA Compliance", How do you ensure password protection; StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Passwords and Unique User Identification

preguntas.pregunta: A candidate is found to have copied answers during the certification exam. What may follow?
opciones: Sanctions up to permanent revocation, with the certificate returned
A written reprimand only, since no patient was harmed by the conduct
A required retake at full price, with the credential left untouched
Referral to the state licensing board, which imposes the sanction
preguntas.explicacion: Copying answers, letting someone else copy, or giving or receiving unauthorized advice about exam content is listed as grounds for discipline, alongside obtaining certification by fraud and distributing exam material. The sanctions available run from denial of eligibility and invalidated or withheld scores through probation and reprimand to temporary or permanent revocation, with the certificate and wallet card returned.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with asthma is wheezing and struggling to breathe in the waiting room. What is done?
opciones: Call for help, loosen tight clothing and help with the prescribed inhaler
Give a cup of warm water to sip and walk the patient to an exam room
Place a pillow behind the head and let the patient lie down to rest
Wait to see whether the wheezing settles before the call is made
preguntas.explicacion: Emergency help is called right away for breathing difficulty; then airway, breathing and pulse are checked, tight clothing is loosened, and the patient is helped to take their own prescribed medicine such as an asthma inhaler or home oxygen. Nothing is given to eat or drink, and a pillow under the head can close the airway.

preguntas.pregunta: A sterile drape hangs four inches below the edge of the tray table. What is the status of the part that hangs down?
opciones: Contaminated, since anything extending below the planar surface no longer counts as sterile
Sterile, since it came out of the same package and has touched no unsterile surface yet
Sterile, but only until someone walks past it, at which point it must be lifted back up
Contaminated, but it can be folded back onto the tray as long as sterile gloves are worn
preguntas.explicacion: Any part of a field that drops below the plane of the tabletop is contaminated, and it cannot be brought back: lifting it would carry the contamination onto the field. The same list rules out anything below waist level or above shoulder level, anything within an inch of the edge, and anything the person has stopped watching.

preguntas.pregunta: A skin puncture must supply a haematology specimen, a chemistry specimen and a blood bank specimen. In what order are they collected?
opciones: Haematology, then chemistry, then blood bank
Blood bank, then chemistry, then haematology
Chemistry, then haematology, then blood bank
Blood bank, then haematology, then chemistry
preguntas.explicacion: With skin punctures the haematology specimen is collected first, followed by the chemistry and blood bank specimens, an order that is essential to minimize the effects of platelet clumping. It is the reverse of the order used for venepuncture. If more than two specimens are needed, venepuncture may give more accurate results.

preguntas.pregunta: Fluid is drawn off from around a lung in a procedure called a thoracentesis. Which act does that ending name?
opciones: A surgical puncture made in order to remove fluid
A surgical opening made from an organ to the outside
A surgical binding that fixes two structures together
A crushing of something hard that has formed inside
preguntas.explicacion: The ending -centesis is a surgical puncture that removes fluid, and thorac- names the chest, so the two together say where and what. The endings around it name other acts: -ostomy and -stomy make an opening, -desis is a surgical binding and -tripsy is a crushing, as in the treatment of a stone.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient files a privacy complaint against a clinic. What does HIPAA say about how the clinic may respond?
opciones: It may not intimidate or retaliate against the patient for filing the complaint
It may decline further treatment, since the relationship of trust has been broken
It may require the patient to waive the complaint as a condition of care
It may share the complaint with other providers so they are warned
preguntas.explicacion: Section 164.530(g) forbids a covered entity from intimidating, threatening, coercing, discriminating against or retaliating against any individual for exercising a right under the rule or taking part in any of its processes, including filing a complaint, and 164.530(h) forbids requiring individuals to waive their rights as a condition of treatment, payment, enrollment or benefits. The entity must have its own complaint process, document complaints and their disposition, and mitigate any harm from a violation. Sharing the complaint with other providers would itself be an unpermitted disclosure.

preguntas.pregunta: An automated reading shows 186/122 mm Hg and the patient feels well. What does the value call for?
opciones: The provider is contacted immediately: above 180 or above 120 is a hypertensive crisis
A recheck at the next visit, since a single high value cannot diagnose hypertension
A repeat reading in five minutes and no report unless the second one is also high
Documentation only, because a patient free of symptoms is not held to be in danger
preguntas.explicacion: Readings above 180 systolic or above 120 diastolic are dangerously high and call for immediate medical attention, whatever the patient reports: high blood pressure usually carries no warning signs at all. The clot activator in the gel tube breaks down phenytoin before the serum can be separated
The gel prevents the sample from being carried on ice and in the dark as drug levels require
The gel tube cannot be centrifuged, and drug assays are run only on centrifuged specimens
preguntas.explicacion: For therapeutic drug monitoring the laboratory refuses tubes with serum separator gel because the barrier gel can absorb some drugs, phenytoin, phenobarbital, lidocaine and carbamazepine among them, which was shown by recovering the drugs from the gel after extraction with methanol; standard tubes without gel are suggested instead. About 1 in 10 women and about 1 in 20 men
About 1 in 4 women and about 1 in 3 men
More than 1 in 2 women and more than 1 in 4 men

The anticoagulant was missing from the tube during packaging
The needle bevel is lying against the wall of the vein
The tube was drawn out of sequence and its additive was spent

Too large damages the blood cells and invalidates the tests; too small tears the vein and causes a haematoma
Too large slows the draw so the sample clots in the tube; too small lets air into the tubing of the set
Too large causes haemoconcentration of the sample; too small causes the tube to lose its vacuum early

A medically unlikely edit, which the contractor applies to the claim

70 per minute, from the beats in ten seconds multiplied by five
140 per minute, from the beats in ten seconds multiplied by ten
56 per minute, from the beats in ten seconds multiplied by four
preguntas.explicacion: The square methods assume evenly spaced beats, so an irregular rhythm is counted across the whole ten-second strip and the count is multiplied by six. Fourteen complexes give 84 per minute, which falls inside the band of 60 to 100.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient says the pain is tolerable and then rates it a 7 out of 10. What does the interviewer do?
opciones: Ask more focused questions until the gap between the two answers is explained
Record the number, because a rating on a scale outranks the words the patient chose
Record the word tolerable, because the patient's own words outrank any number
Repeat the pain scale later in the visit and keep whichever value comes out lower
preguntas.explicacion: Answers that do not line up are a signal to keep going, not a reason to pick one. Following up often shows that both are true of different moments: a 7 in the knee during physical therapy exercises, and tolerable while resting in bed. Sealing it with a lid, and moving it closer to the drawing chair
Labelling it, and keeping it within arm's reach of the worker
Overfilling it, and sealing it before it has been fully filled
preguntas.explicacion: The container is sealed with a tamper-proof lid, and the two things not to do are overfilling it and decanting it. preguntas.pregunta: Why is the respiratory rate charted in an office often inaccurate?
opciones: It is estimated by eye rather than counted by a standardized method
It is counted while the patient talks, which raises the rate artificially
It is counted over 15 seconds, which is too short to be multiplied up
It is recorded from the oximeter, which reports a rate that is always low
preguntas.explicacion: Outside intensive care the respiratory rate is the least reliably measured of the vital signs: it is frequently estimated visually instead of counted by a set method, so accuracy and reproducibility both suffer. preguntas.pregunta: A medical assistant is about to take a carotid pulse. Which precaution applies?
opciones: Only one side is palpated at a time, and the patient sits or lies down first
Both sides are palpated together so that the two can be compared for symmetry
The patient stands, so that the vessel fills better against gravity in the neck
Firm pressure is applied over the thyroid cartilage until the beat is felt clearly
preguntas.explicacion: The neck vessels are pressure sensitive in some people, and pressing them can bring on fainting or slow the heart, so the patient sits or lies down before the pulse is taken. Both sides are never pressed at once: doing so cuts blood flow to the head. The fingers go beside the Adam's apple, in the soft hollow, not on the cartilage.

The plan's network directory of contracted providers
The preauthorization letter from the insurer
The claim the office files after the prescription is written

preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist finds the sharps container at her station filled to the marked line. What does the standard require before it is carried away?
opciones: Close it immediately before removal, and use a second closable container if leakage is possible
Press the contents down so the lid will close, then carry it to the soiled utility room
Open the lid and tip the sharps into a red bag that is closed before it is removed
Leave it in place until the end of the shift, the deadline set for contaminated surfaces
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(4)(iii)(A)(3) covers the moment a sharps container leaves the area where it was used: the lid goes on first, so nothing can spill or poke out while it is handled, and if the container could leak it travels inside a second one that closes, holds everything and carries the label or the color code. Paragraph (A)(2) already required the container to be replaced routinely and never allowed to overfill, so pressing the contents down is the opposite of the rule, and (A)(4) forbids opening or emptying a reusable container by hand. preguntas.pregunta: What is gained by teaching a patient to recognize the warning signs of a faint?

The faint is shortened, although the risk of a traumatic fall is unchanged
The blood pressure stays high enough for the draw to be completed
The pulse rate rises enough that the tourniquet may be left in place
preguntas.explicacion: Knowing the symptoms often prevents the episode outright and reduces the risk of a traumatic fall, because the patient lies down before consciousness goes. The toenail bed, the wrist over the radial artery or the inner elbow
The earlobe, the neck over the carotid artery or the top of the foot
The forehead, the upper arm under the blood pressure cuff or the ankle

preguntas.pregunta: What color and legend does OSHA require on a biohazard warning label?

Bright yellow with a black skull and crossbones, the GHS pictogram for acute toxicity
Red with white lettering, matching the red bags that may replace the label
Fluorescent orange-red with a black frame set on a point, as on chemical labels
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (g)(1)(i)(B) and (C) require the BIOHAZARD legend and symbol on labels that are fluorescent orange or orange-red, or predominantly so, with lettering and symbols in a contrasting color, affixed so they cannot be lost or removed by accident. Red bags or containers may substitute for the label under (g)(1)(i)(E), but the label itself is not specified as red with white text. preguntas.pregunta: In the three-step assessment of an occupational HIV exposure, what does the first step establish?
opciones: Whether an infectious fluid was involved, and by which route and how severe
Whether the source patient is on treatment and what the viral load is
Whether prophylaxis is indicated or observation alone is enough
Whether the worker completed the hepatitis B vaccine series
preguntas.explicacion: The three steps run in order. First comes the exposure itself: was blood, another infectious body fluid, or an instrument contaminated with blood involved, and if so by what route and how badly. Contact with intact skin carries no meaningful risk; for a mucous membrane the volume and duration count; for a percutaneous injury it matters whether the needle was solid or hollow-bore and whether it had been in a vein or artery. The source patient's status is the second step, and the decision on prophylaxis the third.

preguntas.pregunta: How is standing height measured with a stadiometer?
opciones: Buttocks, shoulder blades and heels touch the board, and footwear is removed first
Only the heels touch the board, and the patient looks upward at the headpiece
The patient leans back against the board with the knees slightly bent for balance
Buttocks and heels touch the board while the shoulders are rolled forward and relaxed
preguntas.explicacion: Shoes and hair ornaments come off, and the buttocks, shoulder blades and back of the head rest against the board while the headpiece is brought down onto the crown. preguntas.pregunta: Under 42 CFR 482.13(d), how may a hospital patient request access to their own medical records?
opciones: By oral or written request, in the format requested if readily producible
Only by written request notarized and signed by the attending physician
Only through an attorney, since records are hospital property
Only after discharge, once the record has been completed and coded

preguntas.pregunta: A blind patient needs to review the consent information. Which ADA auxiliary aid fits?
opciones: A qualified reader, large print, or Braille
A qualified sign language interpreter or captioning
A qualified speech-to-speech transliterator
A companion who reads and signs the form for him
preguntas.explicacion: For people who are blind or have vision loss, the ADA's auxiliary aids include a qualified reader, large print, Braille, an accessible electronic file for a screen reader, or an audio recording. preguntas.pregunta: Where does the duty of care in a clinic come from?

From the written service agreement the patient signs at check-in
From the facility's accreditation by an outside review organization
From the professional licence the state issues to the practitioner
preguntas.explicacion: Duty is the first element of negligence, and some relationships create it by themselves. The list runs from a shop and its customer, or an inn and its guest, to a landowner and a lessee and, of course, a doctor and a patient. preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist is stuck with a needle used on a patient known to have hepatitis C. What does the CDC say about prophylaxis?
opciones: No vaccine and no recommended PEP exist; follow-up testing finds infection early so it can be treated
Immune globulin is given within 24 hours, followed by baseline and 6-month antibody tests
A 28-day antiviral course is started within 72 hours, as for HIV
A single dose of vaccine plus HBIG is given if the worker's antibody level is under 10 mIU/mL
preguntas.explicacion: There is no vaccine against hepatitis C and no post-exposure treatment that prevents infection; neither immune globulin nor antiviral therapy is recommended after exposure. The 2020 guidance does not recommend routine HCV PEP with direct-acting antivirals, noting a percutaneous transmission risk of about 0.2 percent, and instead sets a testing schedule so that infection is detected and treated early. Immune globulin and HBIG with vaccine are hepatitis B measures; the 28-day course within 72 hours is HIV PEP.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with chronic pain goes from 7 out of 10 to 5 out of 10 and can now shop and sleep. Which tool captures that gain?
opciones: The pain, enjoyment and general activity tool, which scores function alongside intensity
The numeric rating scale, whose two-point change already carries the whole story
The 4-item Patient Health Questionnaire, which screens for depression and anxiety
The Geriatric Pain Measure, a 24-item questionnaire covering the preceding week
preguntas.explicacion: A drop of two points looks small on its own. The name of the courier and the vehicle used
The temperature inside the transport container
The number of tubes drawn from each patient

preguntas.pregunta: The grey top tube holds two substances. Which one is the anticoagulant, and what does the other one do?
opciones: Potassium oxalate binds calcium; sodium fluoride blocks glycolysis
Sodium fluoride binds the calcium; potassium oxalate blocks glycolysis
Sodium citrate binds calcium; sodium fluoride preserves the cells
Potassium oxalate inhibits thrombin; sodium fluoride binds calcium
preguntas.explicacion: The grey tube contains potassium oxalate, which binds calcium and so prevents coagulation, together with sodium fluoride, which acts as an antiglycolytic agent; that combination is why the tube is used for plasma glucose and lactic acid. preguntas.pregunta: How is bleeding into the skin distinguished from simple redness (erythema)?
opciones: Bleeding into the skin does not blanch when pressed; erythema does
Bleeding into the skin blanches when pressed; erythema does not
Bleeding into the skin is always larger than 2 mm; erythema is smaller
Bleeding into the skin is warm to the touch; erythema is cool
preguntas.explicacion: Redness of the skin should not be mistaken for bleeding: areas of bleeding into the skin do not become paler when pressed, whereas the redness of erythema does. The same test defines a non-blanching spot: one that does not disappear after brief pressure. Size separates petechiae (under 2 mm) from purpura (over 2 mm), not bleeding from erythema.

preguntas.pregunta: What must be done as a mask or respirator is put on, before the eye protection?
opciones: Shape the band to the bridge of the nose and check the fit
Loop the straps under the chin so it can be pulled down later
Tuck the lower edge under the collar of the gown that is on
Wet the inner layer so it seals against the skin of the face
preguntas.explicacion: In the donning sequence the mask or respirator comes second, after the gown. Its ties or straps are placed around the head and neck, the flexible band is adjusted to the bridge of the nose so that it fits, and a respirator gets a fit check. Anyone required to use a respirator such as an N95 must also have been fit tested beforehand, and where fit testing cannot be done a powered air purifying respirator may be considered.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient who signed a consent form for a procedure says she has changed her mind. What does patient-rights guidance say?
opciones: She may change her mind about consent at any time
She is bound by the signed form until the procedure is done
She may withdraw only if a second physician agrees
She may withdraw only in writing, with 24 hours' notice
preguntas.explicacion: Informed consent is a process in which the provider gives the information needed to decide, including the risks and benefits of the care and details of the condition, and the patient must understand it before consenting; a signature on a form is written consent, but the patient has the right to change her mind at any time. The CMS condition frames the same idea as the right to make informed decisions and to request or refuse treatment. No second opinion, notice period or written withdrawal is required to revoke consent.

preguntas.pregunta: A tube left the factory without the anticoagulant it should contain. What happens when it is used?
opciones: The blood clots and yields serum where plasma was required
The tube keeps its vacuum but draws only half its volume
The plasma settles above a gel barrier as in a PST tube
The red cells haemolyse because no additive protects them

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with a new walker sets it two feet ahead and steps toward it. What should be corrected?
opciones: The walker goes only a short distance ahead, and the weaker leg steps in first
The walker goes a short distance ahead, and the stronger leg has to step in first
The distance is right, but both feet must move at once with the weight on the arms
The distance is right, but the walker has to be lifted rather than rolled forward
preguntas.explicacion: The walker is pushed or lifted a few inches, at most an arm's length, ahead. All four tips or wheels have to touch the floor before any weight goes on it, and then the weaker leg steps in first, followed by the other leg placed in front of it. Space is kept between the patient and the frame, with the toes inside it, or balance is lost.

19 to 22 G, with 22 G preferred to limit hemolysis
16 to 18 G, with 16 G preferred for a faster fill
23 to 25 G, with 23 G preferred to protect the vein
preguntas.explicacion: For most coagulation tests the suggested needle range is 19 G to 22 G, and a larger needle such as 19 G may be preferable for coagulation factor and platelet function testing to minimize hemolysis and keep the sample intact. A nine-digit number that encodes the State where the provider practices
A ten-digit number that changes whenever the provider moves or is renamed
A number issued by each health plan for use in its own claims only

preguntas.pregunta: An otoscope is about to be used on a 6-month-old. Which way is the pinna pulled?
opciones: Posteriorly and inferiorly, which is the direction used under 12 months
Posteriorly and superiorly, which is the direction used in adult patients
Anteriorly and inferiorly, which shortens the canal in a small infant
Straight outward without any traction, since the canal is already straight
preguntas.explicacion: Pulling the pinna straightens the external auditory canal so the tympanic membrane comes into view. Under 12 months the pull is back and down; in adults it is back and up. preguntas.pregunta: A clinic has no airborne infection isolation room and a patient with suspected measles arrives. What does the CDC advise?
opciones: Mask the patient and place them in a private room with the door closed until transfer or discharge
Place the patient in the waiting area at least 3 feet from others, as for Droplet Precautions
Seat the patient in an exam room with the door open so air can circulate freely
Turn the patient away, since Airborne Precautions cannot be implemented without an AIIR
preguntas.explicacion: The CDC anticipates settings without the engineering resources for an AIIR: masking the patient and placing them in a private room with the door closed reduces the likelihood of airborne transmission until the patient is transferred to a facility with an AIIR or sent home. The 3-foot separation is the fallback StatPearls describes for Droplet Precautions when rooms are unavailable, not for airborne pathogens; an open door defeats the purpose; and refusing care is not among the CDC's options.

preguntas.pregunta: Why is a manually retractable evacuated tube system described as safer than a needle and syringe?
opciones: It needs no transfer of blood, and it allows many tubes per puncture
It needs no training, and it costs less than a needle and syringe does
It needs no tourniquet, and its vacuum is lower than in ordinary tubes
It needs no holder, so there is no disassembly step after the draw
preguntas.explicacion: This system is called safer because the blood never has to be transferred and several samples can be taken through one venepuncture, while its safety mechanism prevents reuse. It still requires skill and extra training, costs more, and reusing its holder brings back the disassembly risk.

preguntas.pregunta: A 9-month-old's length and weight are plotted on the WHO charts. Which band is treated as the normal range on those charts?
opciones: The 2nd to the 98th percentile, two standard deviations either side of the mean
The 5th to the 95th percentile, the band that those particular charts mark out
The 10th to the 90th percentile, one standard deviation either side of the mean
The 3rd to the 97th percentile, three standard deviations either side of the mean
preguntas.explicacion: The two chart families draw the normal band differently. On the CDC charts it runs from the 5th to the 95th percentile, with the 85th to 95th marked as overweight or at risk. On the WHO charts normal is two standard deviations either side of the mean, z-scores of −2.0 to +2.0, which works out as the 2nd to the 98th percentile.

The other specified code, the one the Index marks with the abbreviation NEC
The acute code, because acute is the nonessential modifier under that term
No code at all, until the provider has been queried about the missing detail
preguntas.explicacion: The code listed next to a main term in the Alphabetic Index is the default code. It represents either the condition most commonly associated with that term or the unspecified code for it, and the guidelines use appendicitis as the example: where a condition is documented without additional information such as acute or chronic, the default code is assigned.

The Office for Civil Rights, which oversees discrimination and privacy

The Office of Global Affairs, which leads work in global health diplomacy

Training, written procedures, patient billing, sample volume, storage, satisfaction surveys
Equipment purchase, staff rotas, patient identification, tube colour, transport, audit visits
Training, tube colour coding, patient billing, sample condition, storage, incident reports

Three guides in eight sections, starting with the section on patient safety
Eight guides in three groups, starting with the group on clinical processes

preguntas.pregunta: For a routine venipuncture (not a blood culture), how does the WHO say the site should be disinfected?
opciones: A 70% alcohol swab for 30 seconds, then let it dry completely, about 30 seconds
A 70% alcohol swab for 30 seconds, then insert the needle at once while the skin is still wet
Povidone iodine for 30 seconds, since it disinfects better than alcohol before a routine draw
A 70% alcohol swab kept wet for 10 minutes, the contact time given for bleach
preguntas.explicacion: Step 5 gives the numbers: a 70% alcohol swab applied for 30 seconds, then complete drying, which takes about 30 seconds more. Blood cultures are the one exception the step names. The guideline says that too little contact time raises the risk of contamination, so the drying is part of the disinfection rather than a delay, and inserting while wet skips it. The same step prefers alcohol to povidone iodine, because iodine can falsely raise potassium, phosphorus or uric acid results. Ten minutes wet is the contact time the guideline gives for a bleach solution on a blood spill, not for skin.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 5: Disinfect the entry site

preguntas.pregunta: Which three values does spirometry report as its most important results?
opciones: Forced vital capacity, the volume exhaled in one second, and their ratio
Total lung capacity, residual volume, and the ratio between the two
Peak expiratory flow, tidal volume, and the ratio between the two
Diffusing capacity, functional residual capacity, and their ratio
preguntas.explicacion: The test records the volume of air pushed out over time after a maximal breath in. What is reported is the total volume exhaled, the amount that comes out in the first second, and the ratio between them. Total lung capacity and residual volume come from lung volume studies, and diffusing capacity is a separate measurement again.

preguntas.pregunta: A clinician remembers an important detail three days after the visit. How should it go into the record?
opciones: As a late entry, stating when it was recalled and when it was entered
As an edit to the original note, so the chart reads as one account
As a note in the incident report, which is filed outside the record
As an addendum signed by a witness, since the visit is already closed
preguntas.explicacion: A medical record is never changed after the fact, least of all after an adverse event. When something pertinent comes to mind later, it is entered as a late entry that states plainly when it was remembered and when it was written down. Charts should be completed on time anyway: every record system logs when the note was finished, and a late one is easy to attack.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Medical Malpractice", Issues of Concern: Documentation

preguntas.pregunta: How is a double-ended needle joined to the barrel of a vacuum system?
opciones: The end covered by a rubber cuff screws in, past a central thread
The end that enters the vein screws in, past a central thread
Both ends are pushed in, and a locking collar holds them together
The cuffed end clips on, and a luer connector seals the joint
preguntas.explicacion: The needle has a point at each end. The end sheathed in a rubber cuff is screwed into the barrel, also called the tube holder, and a thread between the two ends is where that connection is made. preguntas.pregunta: A patient cuts a forearm on a broken specimen tube and the wound is bleeding freely. What is the first step?
opciones: Press directly on the wound with a sterile dressing or a clean cloth
Press on the artery above the wound at the nearest pressure point
Wrap a tourniquet above the elbow and write down the time it went on
Rinse the wound under running water until the bleeding slows down
preguntas.explicacion: Direct pressure is the first and most important step, and it stops most external bleeding; gloves go on first. Pressure points are no longer recommended, because collateral circulation defeats them. A tourniquet is a later step, for bleeding that continuous pressure has failed to control and that threatens life.

To surrender the credential immediately and reapply after the case

preguntas.pregunta: An outpatient walks in from the car park, sits down, and the phlebotomist reaches for the tourniquet at once. What is wrong with that?
opciones: Have him sit for at least 15 minutes first; posture changes alter results
He should lie down for 2 minutes first, the time it takes the veins to fill
He should stand for a few minutes first so the arm veins distend
Draw right away; posture matters only for coagulation samples
preguntas.explicacion: Changing a patient's position produces statistically significant differences in several biochemistry parameters, so the position, lying or sitting, is kept for at least 10 to 15 minutes before the draw, and office patients are advised to sit for at least 15 minutes beforehand. No later than 30 days after receiving it, with no extension available in any case
No later than 10 days after receiving it, extendable once by no more than 20 days

preguntas.pregunta: At what moment does an intravenous drug such as vancomycin reach its serum peak concentration?
opciones: Immediately after the intravenous infusion is completed
Immediately before the intravenous infusion is started
About 12 hours after the intravenous infusion is completed
About 30 minutes before the following dose is administered
preguntas.explicacion: Vancomycin has a rapid onset, with the serum peak concentration reached immediately once the intravenous infusion finishes; that is the moment a peak sample represents. The 30-minutes-before-the-dose window is the trough, and 12 hours after the dose is the collection time for lithium, tacrolimus, cyclosporine and sirolimus, none of which are given as short intravenous infusions.

opciones: The minor, since state law commonly grants confidentiality here
The parent, who is the personal representative in every case
The school nurse, who must be told of a reportable infection
The insurer, which receives the record with the claim it pays

90 degrees, because 45 degrees is used for normal-sized and obese patients

The U can read as an IV order, so the word unit is spelled out

Patients with bleeding disorders
Premature neonates below 1500 g
Patients cleaned with povidone iodine

preguntas.pregunta: A patient slumps forward in the exam room but is coughing and moving an arm. What should the assistant do?

Start 30 compressions and 2 breaths, since the patient is not fully alert
Give two rescue breaths first and then decide about compressions
Place the defibrillator pads and let the machine decide about compressions
preguntas.explicacion: Compressions are not started on someone who has normal breathing, coughing or movement: pressing on that chest can stop a heart that is still beating. The pressure in the arteries and the pressure returning through the veins
The pressure at the heart and the pressure measured out at the brachial artery
The average pressure over the cycle and the pressure added by each contraction

About 1.8 percent, roughly 1 in 55
About 6 to 30 percent, depending on the source
About 0.1 percent, roughly 1 in 1,000

preguntas.pregunta: An add-on for a viral RNA test is requested on an EDTA whole blood tube that has been in the refrigerator for two days. Under the general stability guidelines for whole blood, can it be used?
opciones: No: whole blood at 2 to 8 °C is listed as acceptable for RNA targets for only about 4 hours, though DNA holds 72 hours
Yes: whole blood at 2 to 8 °C is listed as acceptable for RNA targets for 72 hours, the same period given for DNA
Yes: EDTA whole blood is stable for RNA targets at 2 to 8 °C for 5 days, the figure the guideline gives for plasma
No: whole blood is never acceptable for RNA targets; only serum stored for 2 to 7 days at 2 to 8 °C can be used

After the needle is withdrawn, while gentle pressure is applied with clean gauze
After it has been in place for two minutes, even if more tubes remain to be filled
As soon as the needle enters the vein, before any blood flow is established
preguntas.explicacion: Step 6 is explicit: once sufficient blood has been collected, the tourniquet comes off BEFORE the needle is withdrawn; the gauze and gentle pressure come after the needle is out. preguntas.pregunta: A patient's hands are cold from the waiting room and the pulse feels weaker than usual. What explains that?
opciones: Cold constricts the vessels, and constriction reduces the intensity of the pulse
Cold thickens the blood, and the slower flow reaches the wrist with less force
Cold slows the heart, and the reduced rate is what the fingers read as weakness
Cold numbs the clinician's fingertips, so the pulse itself has not changed at all
preguntas.explicacion: Pulse intensity follows arterial pressure and the distension it produces, and it is modified by other variables, ambient temperature among them: vasoconstriction from cold reduces the intensity felt. preguntas.pregunta: How are sharp instruments passed in a procedure room so that two people are not put at risk at once?

By the person who used it, who announces the pass before letting go
With the tip capped by hand, which is allowed whenever a device is passed
Inside the sharps container, which is carried between the two workers

Change to a different ACE inhibitor, since the cough belongs to lisinopril alone
Add a second-generation antihistamine, because the cough is histamine driven
preguntas.explicacion: Dry cough is the most frequent reaction to this class, reported in 10% to 20% of patients and starting anywhere from the first week to six months in. Stopping the drug usually clears it in one to four days, although it can drag on for a month. An angiotensin receptor blocker is the usual replacement because cough recurs less often with it; if it recurs there too, the class is changed altogether.

Drugs that stop cancer cells from dividing, applied onto the skin
High-energy rays that kill cancer cells, aimed from outside the body
Care that reduces pain and improves quality of life during the illness

Carcinoma starts in bone or soft tissue, sarcoma in skin or lining tissue
Carcinoma starts in blood-forming tissue, sarcoma in immune system cells
Carcinoma starts in lining tissue, sarcoma in blood-forming tissue

preguntas.pregunta: What does a reticulocyte count estimate, and what proportion of the red cells should reticulocytes normally be?
opciones: The rate of red cell production; about 1 to 2 percent of erythrocytes
The rate of platelet production; about 2 to 4 percent of formed elements
The share of immature neutrophils; about 2 to 8 percent of leukocytes
The share of red cells being hemolyzed; less than 1 percent of the count
preguntas.explicacion: A reticulocyte is an erythrocyte in its first day or two in the circulation, still carrying remnants of organelles. Reticulocytes should be about 1 to 2 percent of the erythrocyte count, and that share serves as a rough gauge of how fast red cells are being produced; abnormally low or high values point to a production problem. Immature neutrophils are called bands, a different measure.

Flutter is irregularly irregular and shows a sawtooth pattern
Flutter keeps its P waves, while fibrillation loses them
Flutter is a wide complex rhythm and fibrillation is narrow

Clean the head of the penis with a sterile wipe, leaving the foreskin in place
Wash the tip of the penis downward with soap and water, as for an infant

Most of them, 71 %, stayed under 1 %, and 15 % fell between 1 % and 3 %
Most of them exceeded 6 %, with emergency samples pulling the average up
Most of them clustered near 10 %, the figure reported for emergency rooms
preguntas.explicacion: In that survey 71 % of the laboratories had a hemolysis rate below 3 % and 15 % fell between 3 % and 6 %, with the highest values coming from emergency department specimens. opciones: Relabeling by laboratory, clinical staff or third parties is strongly discouraged; a new specimen is collected
Relabeling is acceptable if the nurse who drew the specimen confirms the patient's identity by telephone with the unit
Relabeling is acceptable when it is done by laboratory personnel and documented in the record system
Relabeling is acceptable for hematology tubes but never for specimens intended for blood bank testing
preguntas.explicacion: Laboratories are expected to have a clear procedure for unlabeled and mislabeled specimens, and relabeling, whoever does it, is strongly discouraged: once the link between patient and tube is lost, a telephone confirmation or a documented note cannot restore it. preguntas.pregunta: During a clean-catch collection, at what point should the patient start filling the cup?
opciones: After voiding a small amount into the toilet and stopping, then collecting until the cup is about half full
As soon as the stream begins, collecting the first portion until the cup is about half full
After voiding a small amount into the toilet, then collecting every drop until the bladder is empty
After the stream has ended, collecting the last portion that remains and filling the cup to the top
preguntas.explicacion: The patient voids a small amount into the toilet, stops the flow, holds the cup a few inches from the urethra and fills it to about half, then finishes voiding into the toilet. The first portion carries the most contaminating cells and bacteria, which is why it is discarded; collecting every drop is the rule for a timed collection and for semen, not for a midstream sample. About 15 to 30 mL is enough for analysis, so the cup is never filled to the top.

preguntas.pregunta: A subcutaneous heparin injection has just been delivered. What happens as the needle comes out?
opciones: Keep pinching until just before withdrawal, press gently, and do not massage
Release the pinch before injecting, then massage the site to spread the dose
Keep pinching until just before withdrawal, then massage to avoid a hematoma
Release the pinch before injecting, then hold firm pressure for five minutes
preguntas.explicacion: With heparin, and when an insulin pen is used, the skinfold is held throughout the injection and released immediately before the needle is withdrawn. The needle comes out quickly at the same angle it went in, and gentle pressure is applied with sterile gauze. preguntas.pregunta: Which control does OSHA suggest for a phlebotomist who sorts specimens at a bench for hours at a stretch?
opciones: Rotate tasks; provide an adjustable bench with knee room and a chair with a footrest
Provide a back belt and require two-person lifts for every full specimen rack
Limit sorting to 20 minutes per shift and assign the rest to housekeeping
Install anti-fatigue mats and require standing for the whole shift
preguntas.explicacion: The recognized controls for laboratory musculoskeletal hazards include automated specimen delivery systems to cut reaching and repetition, supportive chairs with footrests, adjustable workstations with enough knee clearance so the knees do not hit the bench, rotating tasks or limiting time on them, ergonomic computer stations for sitting and standing, anti-fatigue mats for standing stations, and handling devices for heavy carboys. Mats help where standing is unavoidable but do not justify standing all shift, and back belts are not among the listed controls.

preguntas.pregunta: Under CLIA, what is a waived test?

A test performed by a physician or midlevel practitioner during a patient visit
A test that a laboratory chooses not to perform and refers to an accredited laboratory
A test of moderate complexity that has been exempted from proficiency testing

About 4 grams of protein
About 14 grams of protein
About 21 grams of protein

preguntas.pregunta: A light blue citrate tube for a PT/INR comes back only about half full. What is the fill requirement for this tube, and why is a half-filled tube a problem?
opciones: Filling to at least 90% of the tube volume, to keep the 9:1 blood-to-citrate ratio
Filling to at least 50% of the tube volume, so that the 9:1 ratio is still within range
Filling to at least 90% of the tube volume, to keep the 1:9 blood-to-citrate ratio
Filling to the line only when the patient's hematocrit is above 55 percent
preguntas.explicacion: The tube has to be filled to within 90% of its full volume so that blood and sodium citrate stay in a 9 to 1 ratio; a half-filled tube breaks that ratio. The coagulopathies review adds that underfilling, like a hematocrit above 55%, raises the relative citrate level and disturbs the recalcification step of the assay. The ratio is nine parts blood to one of citrate, not the reverse.

Type I, in which the median antebrachial vein links both veins
Type III, in which the median cubital vein is unusually large
