preguntas.pregunta: A newborn's CRP is ordered to monitor for perinatal infection and the serum returns a hemolysis index of about 800 µmol/L. What does the laboratory do with the CRP?
opciones: Rejects it and asks for a repeat sample, since an index above about 622 µmol/L can underestimate CRP
Reports it, since specific proteins such as CRP are immune to hemolysis interference at any index
Reports it with a note, since only indices above 2,000 µmol/L are considered severe in newborns
Dilutes the serum to bring the index below 31 µmol/L and reports the CRP measured on the dilution
preguntas.explicacion: Specific proteins are less sensitive to hemolysis than many chemistry tests, but severe in vitro hemolysis can still interfere: a hemolysis index above 622 µmol/L may cause underestimation of CRP, and in that series 199 newborn CRP requests were rejected for severe hemolysis, the highest index being 1,997 µmol/L. Each rejected CRP became reliable after the blood sampling was repeated two to five hours later. The 31 µmol/L figure is merely the index equivalent of 0.5 g/L free haemoglobin, the threshold that defines a hemolysed sample.

Section 14, which also gives the shipping name and the UN number
Section 11, which also gives the toxicity figures and the symptoms

preguntas.pregunta: A urine collection bag is being applied to a male infant. Where does the bag go?

Only the tip of the penis is placed inside the bag and the adhesive strip is pressed onto the diaper

preguntas.pregunta: A patient arrives at the office laboratory out of breath after climbing several flights of stairs. What is recommended before the draw, and why?
opciones: Have the patient sit for at least 15 minutes, since posture changes alter biochemistry results
Draw immediately, because exertion raises the venous pressure and makes the veins easier to find
Have the patient lie down for two to three minutes and then draw with a butterfly set
Postpone the draw for 24 hours, the interval the chapter sets after physical activity
preguntas.explicacion: Patients in an office setting should stay seated for at least 15 minutes before the procedure, because statistically significant changes in several biochemistry parameters follow a change in position, and any unavoidable change should be recorded. preguntas.pregunta: A patient who smells strongly of alcohol refuses his draw and the nurse is unsure how impaired he is. What is directed?
opciones: Carry out the usual capacity assessment, since intoxication varies in degree
Draw anyway, because intoxication always removes the right to refuse care
Accept the refusal with no assessment, since the refusal is his to make
Wait for a court order before any decision about the draw is taken
preguntas.explicacion: Patients under the influence of alcohol or drugs may lack capacity, and where there is uncertainty about the level of intoxication, the typical assessment of capacity is performed. preguntas.pregunta: Pleural, peritoneal and synovial fluids have been aspirated for culture. How should they travel to the laboratory?
opciones: Promptly and at room temperature, which keeps the organisms viable
Promptly and refrigerated, which keeps the organisms viable in transit
Promptly and frozen, since the cell count is read from the thawed fluid
Whenever convenient, provided each container has been sealed and labeled
preguntas.explicacion: These fluids are aspirated aseptically into sterile containers, and their appearance, color, turbidity, viscosity and any clots are recorded. Portions go for cell count and differential, for protein and glucose, for culture and for cytology. preguntas.pregunta: Under which measure was the Institutional Review Board established in the United States?

The National Research Act, in 1984
The Belmont Report, issued in 1976
The Declaration of Helsinki revisions

preguntas.pregunta: Which superficial vein connects the cephalic and basilic veins in the cubital fossa?

The median antebrachial vein
The brachial vein
The dorsal venous arch

preguntas.pregunta: An older office building has two steps at its entrance. What does the law ask of the practice inside it?
opciones: Remove the barrier where doing so is readily achievable, and otherwise serve by other means
Remove the barrier only when the building is next altered or the lease comes up for renewal
Remove the barrier only if a patient files a written complaint about the entrance first
Leave the entrance as it stands, since buildings raised before the law are not reached by it

preguntas.pregunta: What does the allowed amount of a plan represent?
opciones: The most the plan will pay for a covered service, also called the negotiated rate
The most the patient will pay for a covered service before the plan pays its share
The most the patient will pay in a plan year before coverage of benefits reaches 100%
The total the provider charges for the service before any discount is applied to it
preguntas.explicacion: The allowed amount is the ceiling a plan will pay for a covered service, and the glossary also calls it the eligible expense, the payment allowance or the negotiated rate. What the patient pays first is the deductible; the yearly ceiling on patient spending is the out-of-pocket limit; and the provider's own charge is a separate figure, which is why a charge above the allowed amount can leave a balance.

preguntas.pregunta: At which blood glucose level is a patient considered to be hypoglycemic?
opciones: Below 70 mg/dL (3.9 mmol/L), which can already do harm
Below 100 mg/dL (5.6 mmol/L), the lower end of the fasting range
Below 55 mg/dL (3.1 mmol/L), and never above that figure
Below 40 mg/dL (2.2 mmol/L), when the patient loses consciousness
preguntas.explicacion: A blood sugar under 70 mg/dL, or 3.9 mmol/L, counts as low and can be harmful at or below that level. Symptoms may not appear until the glucose falls below 55 mg/dL, which is why the number matters and not only how the patient looks. Severe low blood sugar that ends in unconsciousness is what is called insulin shock.

80/120 mm Hg, diastolic first because it is the resting value of the two
120/80 mm, since the unit of the gauge is millimetres of the column
120 over 80 kPa, the pressure unit used on automated office devices
preguntas.explicacion: The systolic value goes first, then a slash, then the diastolic, and the unit is millimetres of mercury: 120/80 mm Hg. The gauge on the cuff reads in that unit, and the arm used and the patient's position belong in the record beside the numbers, since both change the value.

The one-inch border running around the edge, plus the center
The half of the drape furthest from the person who opened it
The four corners where the flaps were folded before opening

preguntas.pregunta: A clinician takes a telephone consult about a named patient from the phone in the hospital cafeteria. What is wrong with that?
opciones: The talk is allowed, but it has to happen away from the public
The talk is barred, since consults require written authorization
The talk is allowed only if the patient is on the line as well
The talk is barred, because phone lines are never encrypted
preguntas.explicacion: Consulting another provider is a permitted conversation; where it takes place is what matters. Such conversations are to be held away from the public and in private rooms, and a telephone consult from a cafeteria line, where others can hear, is the example given of how not to do it. preguntas.pregunta: When does the CDC say soap and water must be used rather than alcohol-based hand sanitizer?
opciones: When hands are visibly soiled, after using the restroom, or during C. difficile outbreaks
Before every aseptic task and after any contact with the patient's immediate surroundings
Whenever the sanitizer on hand contains less than 60 percent alcohol by volume
Whenever gloves have been worn for longer than the 20 seconds a hand rub takes
preguntas.explicacion: The CDC prefers alcohol-based hand sanitizer in most clinical situations unless hands are visibly soiled, and reserves soap and water for visibly soiled hands, before eating, after using the restroom, and during care of patients with suspected or confirmed infection in outbreaks of C. difficile and norovirus. StatPearls explains that spore-forming and non-enveloped organisms resist alcohol, so mechanical removal by washing is needed. Aseptic tasks and contact with surroundings are moments for hand hygiene by either method, not reasons to choose soap.

preguntas.pregunta: The superficial veins of the cubital fossa are classified into four types. Which pattern is the most common?

Type I, in which a dominant median antebrachial vein joins both veins (the N pattern)
Type III, in which the brachial cephalic vein is poorly developed or missing
Type IV, in which there is no communicating branch between cephalic and basilic
preguntas.explicacion: Type II, with the cephalic and basilic veins connected by the median cubital vein and also called type M, is the most common pattern, followed by type I, the N type with a dominant median antebrachial vein. preguntas.pregunta: How is a spot tested to decide whether it is non-blanching?
opciones: Brief pressure is applied, and the spot does not disappear
Brief pressure is applied, and the spot fades then returns
The skin is stretched, and the spot spreads sideways with it
The skin is cooled, and the spot pales under the cold pack
preguntas.explicacion: A non-blanching spot is one that stays visible after brief pressure is put on the area. That single manoeuvre separates bleeding into the skin, which does not pale, from simple redness of the skin, which does. Both petechiae and purpura are defined as non-blanching.

preguntas.pregunta: A cerebrospinal fluid specimen from a neurology ICU arrives in a urine cup instead of a sterile CSF tube. How does the emergency laboratory handle it?
opciones: A laboratory medicine specialist decides whether this precious specimen is rejected or accepted
The accessioning clerk rejects it automatically, as with any specimen in an improper container
It is accepted without review, because CSF can never be recollected from the same patient
It is transferred by the clerk into a sterile tube and processed as an ordinary specimen
preguntas.explicacion: Improper container is a standing rejection criterion, and sending CSF in a urine cup is described as a common mistake in the neurology ICU; but for precious specimens such as CSF, bone marrow or aspirates received in unsuitable tubes or under wrong transport conditions, the decision to reject or accept is reserved to the laboratory medicine specialists rather than made automatically at the desk.

opciones: A 1.5-inch needle, 22 to 25 gauge, because she weighs more than 200 lb
A 1-inch needle, 22 to 25 gauge, which is the choice below 130 lb
A 5/8-inch needle, 23 to 25 gauge, which is the subcutaneous choice
A 1-inch needle, 18 to 22 gauge, chosen for a thicker vaccine product

The standard chart is kept, and the values below the curve are simply noted
The chart is dropped, and only the measurements themselves are recorded
The chart for a younger age group is used, since growth runs behind schedule

It cannot be used for blood drawing in the paediatric population
It cannot be heparinized, so it is unsuitable for arterial blood samples
It requires more training than an evacuated tube system

preguntas.pregunta: A patient says the only thing taken that morning before a fasting draw was a cup of black coffee, no sugar. Under the guidance on fasting samples, is the specimen acceptable?
opciones: No: during the fasting period water is acceptable, but coffee and other drinks such as energy drinks are not allowed
Yes: black coffee without sugar adds no calories and is treated the same way as plain water during a fast
Yes, provided the coffee was taken more than 2 hours before the draw and the patient then drank plain water
No: coffee is allowed only together with the morning medicines, which this patient did not take
preguntas.explicacion: Morning sampling after a fast of at least 12 hours since the last solid meal is the recommended condition; water during the fasting period is acceptable, but other drinks, coffee and energy drinks included, are not allowed on the morning of the procedure, and alcohol is avoided for the 24 hours before. Non-fasting samples are accepted only for patients who cannot tolerate the fast, for emergencies and for parameters that fasting does not affect; fasting status is double-checked once identification is verified.

Draw from the right arm but use a smaller-gauge needle
Draw from the right hand only, never from the antecubital fossa
Draw from either arm, as long as the tourniquet stays under one minute

preguntas.pregunta: What is the difference between a copayment and coinsurance?
opciones: A copayment is a set dollar figure per service and coinsurance is a percentage of it
A copayment is a percentage of the service and coinsurance is a set dollar figure
A copayment is owed before the deductible and coinsurance replaces the deductible
A copayment is owed monthly for coverage and coinsurance is owed at each visit
preguntas.explicacion: A copayment is a fixed amount, $20 for instance, that the patient pays for a covered service. Coinsurance is a share expressed as a percentage of the allowed amount, 20% for instance, so the dollars change with the price of the service. Both are usually owed after the deductible is satisfied. The monthly amount owed for the coverage itself, used or not, is the premium.

preguntas.pregunta: A volunteer blood donation center decides gloves are not routinely needed for every draw. What must the employer still do?
opciones: Reevaluate the policy periodically, keep gloves available, and never discourage their use
Record every draw done without gloves in the sharps injury log kept for the year
Obtain a signed declination from each employee who draws without wearing gloves
Report the policy to the Assistant Secretary before the first donation session
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(3)(ix)(D) lets a volunteer blood donation center judge that routine gloving for every phlebotomy is unnecessary, but it attaches four duties: reevaluate that judgment periodically, make gloves available to anyone who wants them, do nothing to discourage their use, and require them when the employee has cuts or breaks in the skin, when hand contamination looks likely, and while the employee is being trained. preguntas.pregunta: How should paper records and prescription labels that contain PHI be disposed of?
opciones: Shredded or incinerated so that nobody can piece them back together
Placed in a red biohazard bag and treated as regulated waste
Handed to the person in charge of shredding to take home and destroy later
Kept in a locked cabinet indefinitely, since PHI may never be destroyed
preguntas.explicacion: Documents with PHI are shredded or incinerated so that no reconstruction is possible, computers, CDs and drives are completely erased before disposal, and the people assigned to destruction are chosen so that records are in fact destroyed rather than taken home; letting the shredding staff carry records home is exactly what that selection is meant to prevent. preguntas.pregunta: How much urine is needed for an accurate routine urinalysis, and where should the label go?

About 15 to 30 mL, with the label placed on the lid so the container stays see-through

preguntas.pregunta: After a needlestick, what does the CDC say about squeezing the wound or applying bleach to it?
opciones: Neither has evidence behind it, and caustic agents like bleach are not advised
Squeezing is recommended to expel contaminated blood; bleach is not advised
Bleach at a 1:10 dilution is recommended on the wound; squeezing is not
Both are recommended right away, before the wound is washed with soap and water
preguntas.explicacion: No scientific evidence shows that using antiseptics or squeezing the wound reduces the risk of transmitting a bloodborne pathogen, and a caustic agent such as bleach is not recommended. The recommended care is washing the needlestick with soap and water. WHO's annex on occupational exposure agrees: wash with soap and water, no alcohol or strong disinfectant, let the wound bleed freely, and do not dress it. The 1:10 bleach dilution is for surfaces after a spill, never for skin.

preguntas.pregunta: What does the jury have to be convinced of in a civil medical negligence case?
opciones: That the plaintiff's account is more plausible than the defendant's
That the plaintiff's account is proven beyond any reasonable doubt
That the plaintiff's account is supported by two expert witnesses
That the plaintiff's account is admitted by the treating clinician
preguntas.explicacion: Civil cases use a lower bar than criminal ones. The plaintiff must convince the jury by a preponderance of the evidence, meaning at least 51 percent: their argument and evidence must be more plausible as the proximate cause of the alleged injury than what the defense puts up. Proof beyond a reasonable doubt belongs to criminal prosecutions.

The nurse confirms the patient's name aloud at the door of the room
The room and bed numbers match the numbers printed on the requisition
The name on the wristband matches the name printed on the requisition
preguntas.explicacion: Step 1 is to use at least two unique patient-specific identifiers, and the procedure gives the patient's name and date of birth as the example of good practice. Any patient who forgot to fast, provided the omission is written on the requisition
Inpatients only, because their meals are already controlled by the ward
Patients on therapeutic drug monitoring, who must eat together with the dose

Whenever the employer is the one paying the premium for the employee's plan
Whenever the employee has already told the employer that the injury happened
Only when a court has ordered the practice to produce the medical record

On the strength of the dose and the route by which it is given
On the cost to the health plan and the risk of diversion in transit
On the length of time the drug has been approved for sale in the country

preguntas.pregunta: A tracing shows no build-up of the R wave across the chest leads. Which technical cause does the assistant check?

A paper speed that was set below 25 mm per second
A calibration mark that printed at half its usual height
A lead wire that was left looped across the patient's arm
preguntas.explicacion: The R wave should grow steadily from V1, the smallest, to V5, the largest. When that build-up is missing, the listed causes are an old anteroseptal infarct, hypertrophy of the left ventricle and an electrode that was placed inaccurately, which is the fixable one.

preguntas.pregunta: Which division of the nervous system controls the heart, the stomach and the intestines without conscious effort?
opciones: The autonomic division of the peripheral nervous system
The somatic division of the peripheral nervous system
The sensory division of the central nervous system
The reflex division of the central nervous system
preguntas.explicacion: The peripheral system splits in two. The somatic part serves the skin and skeletal muscles and handles conscious activity. The autonomic part connects the center to the visceral organs and works continuously without conscious effort, minding heart rate, breathing rate, blood pressure and body temperature.

Its staff members trained on paper charting, marked by the date of their training
Its patients seen during the last outage, marked by the unit that attended them
Its equipment serviced in the past year, marked by the date of the next service
preguntas.explicacion: Interfaces are the part that fails quietly. The organization keeps a comprehensive list of its system-to-system interfaces and reviews it regularly, every six months or yearly, noting which of them raise legal or regulatory duties to warn the other side, such as a state immunization registry or a prescription drug monitoring programme.

preguntas.pregunta: What is the wall of a capillary made of, and what is the capillary's job?
opciones: One endothelial layer on a basement membrane; exchange with tissue fluid
Three tunics with a thin muscular media; regulation of blood pressure
Endothelium plus a thin layer of muscle cells; the main site of diapedesis
Rings of smooth muscle called sphincters; control of flow into the bed
preguntas.explicacion: The capillary wall is an endothelial layer surrounded by a basement membrane, sometimes a single cell wrapped around itself, and its function is perfusion: exchanging gases and other substances between blood and interstitial fluid. Capillaries are the smallest and most numerous vessels, built for exchange. Three tunics describe arterioles; sphincters belong to the metarteriole.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient wants her records sent straight to a research app she uses. What does the Privacy Rule require of her request?
opciones: It must be in writing, signed by her, and name the recipient and where to send the copy
It must be approved by the privacy official, who decides whether the recipient is suitable
It must come with an authorization from the app developer accepting business associate duties
It must be limited to a summary, since only summaries may be directed outside the practice
preguntas.explicacion: Besides receiving copies herself, an individual may direct the covered entity to transmit her PHI to another person or entity she designates. preguntas.pregunta: During an intake interview, when is a closed or direct question the better tool?
opciones: When one specific detail has to be pinned down, such as whether medicines are taken as prescribed
When the patient is first invited to say, in their own words, exactly what brought them in today
When the patient's cultural background and what matters about it is being explored
When the patient is asked to put into words what the dizziness actually feels like
preguntas.explicacion: Closed questions collect a fact: taken as prescribed or not, allergic or not, pregnant or not. Open-ended ones invite the patient to elaborate and are what the interview opens with, what cultural background and beliefs are explored with, and how a symptom gets described. A closed answer of no or sometimes is then followed up with an open-ended request to tell more.

preguntas.pregunta: Which patients are most likely to show orthostatic hypotension?
opciones: Older adults: about 1 in 5 of those aged 60 and over are affected
Older adults: about 1 in 50 of those aged 60 and over are affected
Young adults, in whom the baroreceptor reflex has not yet fully matured
Adults aged 45 to 49, the group in which more than 25% are affected
preguntas.explicacion: Prevalence climbs steeply with age, largely through loss of baroreceptor sensitivity: roughly one in five community-dwelling adults aged 60 or older is affected, and the rate is higher still in long-term care. Population studies put it under 5% at ages 45 to 49 and above 25% at 85 and over.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient's venipuncture site keeps bleeding through the gauze after the draw. What is the most important first step?
opciones: Apply direct pressure over the site and keep it until the bleeding stops
Apply a tourniquet 2 to 3 inches above the site and note the time
Remove the soaked gauze, clean the wound, and apply fresh gauze
Raise the arm above the heart and peek every minute to check
preguntas.explicacion: Direct pressure is the most important step for external bleeding and stops most of it: press on the wound with a sterile bandage, clean cloth or, failing that, a hand, and maintain the pressure until the bleeding stops, without peeking. Raising the bleeding part can be added when possible, but checking every minute disturbs the clot. A soaked dressing is left in place with another on top, and a tourniquet is reserved for severe, life-threatening limb bleeding that continuous pressure has failed to control.

preguntas.pregunta: Why are veins preferred over arteries for a routine blood draw?
opciones: Veins run superficially, while arteries have thicker walls and more nerves, so puncturing them hurts more
Veins carry oxygenated blood, which is what most chemistry analysers are calibrated to measure
Arteries collapse under the vacuum of the tube, while veins tolerate the negative pressure
Arterial blood clots too quickly in a citrate tube to allow coagulation testing
preguntas.explicacion: Veins are preferred for efficiency and patient comfort because they run superficially, whereas arteries tend to have thicker walls and more associated nerves, making a puncture more painful; arterial sampling is reserved for arterial blood gases. The chapter says nothing about arteries collapsing or clotting faster, and thick walls are a property it credits to the median cubital vein.

preguntas.pregunta: What exactly is a platelet?
opciones: A fragment of megakaryocyte cytoplasm wrapped in plasma membrane
A small complete cell with a two-lobed nucleus, 8 to 10 µm wide
An immature erythrocyte that still contains remnants of organelles
A leukocyte that has left the circulation to phagocytize debris
preguntas.explicacion: A platelet is not a cell: it is a piece of the cytoplasm of a large marrow cell, the megakaryocyte, enclosed by a bit of plasma membrane, which is why the older name thrombocyte is misleading. Each megakaryocyte releases 2000 to 3000 platelets. The small two-lobed cell is the basophil, the immature red cell is the reticulocyte, and the emigrated phagocyte is the macrophage.

preguntas.pregunta: A practice writes down which staff member took which laptop out of the building and when it came back. Which specification does that log satisfy?

Maintenance records, a record of repairs made to doors, walls and locks in the office
Workstation use, which fixes what may be done at a given class of workstation
Facility security plan, which guards the premises and its equipment against theft
preguntas.explicacion: Accountability sits under device and media controls, and it is the addressable specification that asks for a record of the movements of hardware and electronic media and of who is responsible for them. preguntas.pregunta: A patient hands over a new insurance card at check-in. Which step protects the claim best?
opciones: Verifying coverage and benefits with the plan before the visit is billed
Filing the card in the paper chart and billing the plan listed last year
Asking the patient to state the group number aloud instead of copying it
Waiting for the remittance advice to reveal which plan is now primary
preguntas.explicacion: Verification of patient data prevents rejections, delays and denials: insurance eligibility belongs on the list of items to confirm before the claim goes out, along with the name, the age and the billing address. Billing last year's plan invites a denial for coverage that has ended, an oral group number adds an error, and learning it from the remittance advice means the denial already happened.

preguntas.pregunta: To save time, a phlebotomist prints and sticks labels on all the tubes at the nursing station before entering the patient's room. What is wrong with this practice?
opciones: Tube identification and labeling must be done in the presence of the patient to avoid misidentification
Labels printed in advance lose their adhesive and can peel off during centrifugation or refrigeration
Tubes must be labeled only after the draw is complete, and the label must be applied later at the accessioning desk
Pre-printed labels are acceptable only when the requisition is placed outside the transport bag
preguntas.explicacion: Both identifying the tube and applying its label are done with the patient present, so that the tube cannot be matched to the wrong person; before the draw the patient's identification data and the tube labels are double-checked against each other. Labeling away from the patient, whether before at the station or later at the accessioning desk, breaks that link. The transport bag pocket is a separate rule about the requisition, not about when to label.

opciones: Doctors, nurses, nurse practitioners and physician assistants may all serve
Only doctors of medicine and doctors of osteopathic medicine may serve
Only physicians who completed a family practice residency may serve
Any licensed health worker, a pharmacist or a dietitian included, may serve as one
preguntas.explicacion: Primary care providers include doctors, nurses, nurse practitioners and physician assistants. The primary care provider is the person a patient sees first for checkups and health problems and who helps manage overall health. opciones: The emergency department, at 6.81 %, ahead of intensive care at 5.93 %
Intensive care, at 6.81 %, ahead of the emergency department at 5.93 % of sera
The inpatient wards, whose draws are done with a straight needle
The outpatient clinics, whose samples travel longest before separation

preguntas.pregunta: What does the first S in PASS stand for when operating a portable fire extinguisher?
opciones: Squeeze the trigger, holding the extinguisher upright
Sweep the nozzle from side to side across the flames
Stand back 75 feet, the maximum travel distance
Shut the door behind you before discharging
preguntas.explicacion: PASS summarizes extinguisher operation: pull the pin, aim the nozzle at the base of the fire, squeeze the trigger while holding the extinguisher upright, and sweep from side to side to cover the fire with the spray. Seventy-five feet is the maximum travel distance to a Class A extinguisher under 29 CFR 1910.157, not a stand-off distance, and shutting doors is the confine step of RACE, done before anyone attempts to extinguish.

opciones: Use a formal form of address such as Mr. or Ms., and give your own name and role
Use the patient's first name to build rapport, then state your job title
Speak louder and more slowly, because most older adults have hearing loss
Address the accompanying family member first, to save the patient effort
preguntas.explicacion: Formal terms of address are the default with older patients, and familiar words like 'dear' can be taken as disrespect; staff may ask how the patient prefers to be addressed. preguntas.pregunta: After a needlestick, what does the standard say about testing the source patient's blood?
opciones: Test it as soon as feasible for HBV and HIV once consent is obtained, unless consent is not legally required
Test it only if the exposed employee first agrees to have his or her own baseline blood drawn
Test it without asking, because a patient's blood already drawn belongs to the laboratory
Do not test it; the standard bases follow-up on the employee's serology and vaccination status alone
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (f)(3)(ii) makes identification and documentation of the source individual part of the follow-up unless it is infeasible or barred by state or local law. Under (f)(3)(ii)(A) the source's blood is tested for HBV and HIV infectivity as soon as feasible after consent; if consent is refused, the employer documents that legally required consent could not be obtained, and where the law does not require consent, available blood is tested and the results recorded. preguntas.pregunta: A light blue sodium citrate tube has just been filled for a PT/INR. How should it be mixed?
opciones: Inverted gently 3 to 6 times immediately after the draw
Inverted gently 8 to 10 times immediately after the draw
Shaken vigorously for a few seconds so the anticoagulant mixes
Left upright for 10 to 15 minutes before any mixing
preguntas.explicacion: Gentle mixing means inverting the citrate tube 3 to 6 times right after the sample enters the tube; vigorous shaking can froth or hemolyse the sample and distort coagulation results. preguntas.pregunta: A pathology report calls a growth benign. What does that tell the patient?
opciones: It may keep growing, but it does not spread to other parts of the body
It has stopped growing, and it does not spread to other parts of the body
It is growing slowly, and it spreads only through the lymph system
It is not growing at all, and it will disappear without any treatment
preguntas.explicacion: Benign means not cancer. A benign tumor can still get larger, and its size may cause trouble by itself, but it does not invade nearby tissue or travel elsewhere. The opposite term is malignant: those cells grow in an uncontrolled way, invade nearby tissue and spread through the blood and lymph system.

preguntas.pregunta: An infant is found unresponsive and not breathing. How are chest compressions delivered?
opciones: With the two thumbs side by side over the sternum, below the nipple line
With the heel of one hand over the lower half of the sternum, as in a child
With two fingers over the upper third of the sternum, above the nipples
With both hands wrapped around the chest, squeezing from front and back
preguntas.explicacion: The rescuer's hands encircle the infant's chest and both thumbs press together on the sternum below the nipple line, to a depth of about 1½ inches (4 cm) at 100 to 120 per minute. Two fingers on the sternum just under the nipple line is the other accepted hand position. The heel of one hand is what a child of 1 year to puberty gets.

preguntas.pregunta: An order says a dose is due at a set hour. How far from that hour should the dose be given?
opciones: Within about half an hour, since a wider gap can alter the drug's bioavailability
Within about six hours, the widest interval an around-the-clock order would use
Within about four hours, the window written into a typical order given as needed
At any point in the shift, as long as the true time is charted in the record
preguntas.explicacion: The right time means administering the medication as close as possible to the hour the prescriber intended, and the guiding principle is not to stray from it by more than about half an hour, because a longer gap can shift bioavailability and other mechanisms. Drugs given by infusion must also run at the ordered rate. Four to six hours is the window inside an as-needed order, not a tolerance for timing.

preguntas.pregunta: If the mean arterial pressure stays below 60 mm Hg for an extended time, what is the result?
opciones: Ischemia, too little blood flow, usually with hypoxia
Hypervolemia, too much fluid retained by the kidneys
Hypertension, from an excess of endothelin release
Polycythemia, from a rise in the output of EPO
preguntas.explicacion: When MAP falls below 60 mm Hg for long, pressure is no longer enough to push blood through the tissues; the result is ischemia, insufficient blood flow, commonly accompanied by hypoxia, inadequate tissue oxygenation, to which neurons are especially sensitive. Hypervolemia and hypertension are excesses of volume and pressure, and polycythemia is an overproduction of red cells, a different condition.
preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 20.2 Blood Flow, Blood Pressure, and Resistance, Mean Arterial Pressure

preguntas.pregunta: What is the out-of-pocket maximum of a health plan?
opciones: The yearly cap on what the patient pays for covered in-network care; past it, the plan pays 100%
The most the patient pays per visit for covered services; the plan pays 100% of the rest
The most the patient pays in a plan year including premiums and out-of-network care
The 2026 Marketplace cap, $10,600 per individual, which applies only to premiums
preguntas.explicacion: HealthCare.gov describes the out-of-pocket maximum, or limit, as the ceiling on what the patient spends on covered services in a plan year, not per visit. Once deductibles, copayments and coinsurance for in-network care add up to that figure, the plan covers 100% of covered benefits for the rest of the year. The glossary lists what does not count toward it: monthly premiums, out-of-network care, services the plan does not cover, and charges above the allowed amount. preguntas.pregunta: Which three components must be present for a fire to ignite?
opciones: A fuel, an oxidizer like oxygen, and an ignition source
A fuel, a flammable liquid, and a compressed gas
Heat, smoke, and an electrical current from a wall outlet
Oxygen, nitrous oxide, and an electrocautery device
preguntas.explicacion: Three components are needed: a fuel source such as linens, flammable liquids or tissue; an oxidizer such as oxygen or nitrous oxide, which greatly increases combustibility; and an ignition source such as an open flame, electrostatic discharge, electrocautery, lasers or any energized device. The operating room is a high-risk setting because all three are usually present at once. preguntas.pregunta: Which structure is the heart's pacemaker, where is it, and how often does it fire on its own?
opciones: The SA node, in the upper posterior wall of the right atrium; 70 to 80 per minute
The AV node, in the lower right atrium within the septum; 70 to 80 per minute
The SA node, in the upper wall of the left atrium; about 100 per minute
The bundle of His, in the interventricular septum; up to 220 per minute
preguntas.explicacion: The sinoatrial node sits in the superior and posterior walls of the right atrium near the opening of the superior vena cava and is the pacemaker because it has the fastest inherent rate, firing 70 to 80 times per minute without neural input. The AV node sits lower in the right atrium and can pass at most about 220 impulses per minute, which sets the typical maximum heart rate.

Destroying all microbial life, including highly resistant bacterial endospores
Treating all blood and certain body fluids as if known to be infectious
Altering the way a task is performed so that exposure becomes less likely

preguntas.pregunta: A colleague keeps a jar of cotton balls soaking in alcohol and tears the cotton by hand as she goes. What is wrong with that?
opciones: Cotton torn by bare hands is contaminated and bacteria can grow in the jar
Alcohol evaporates from an open jar and is too weak to prepare the skin
Cotton fibres stick to the puncture site and cause the wound to keep oozing
Alcohol stored in an open jar has to be discarded at the end of the shift

preguntas.pregunta: A blood type is reported as A positive. What does the 'positive' refer to, and what share of Americans share that status?

The Rh D antigen is on the red cells; about 50 percent
Anti-D antibodies are in the plasma; about 85 percent
The A antigen is on the red cells; about 15 percent
preguntas.explicacion: The Rh group is separate from ABO, and only one Rh antigen, D, matters clinically; those who carry it, about 85 percent of Americans, are Rh positive, and the word positive or negative is added to the ABO letter. About 15 to 20 seconds
About 10 to 15 minutes
About 30 to 60 seconds

preguntas.pregunta: In the common pathway of coagulation, what is the job of thrombin?
opciones: Turns soluble fibrinogen into insoluble fibrin
Turns inactive prothrombin into its active form
Cross-links and stabilizes the fibrin clot
Degrades the fibrin once the vessel has healed
preguntas.explicacion: The common pathway has three moves: once factor X is active, prothrombinase converts prothrombin (factor II) into thrombin; thrombin then converts fibrinogen (factor I) into insoluble fibrin strands; and factor XIII stabilizes the fibrin clot. Activating prothrombin is the job of prothrombinase, not of thrombin, and breaking fibrin down later is the work of plasmin.

The plantar venous arch
The great saphenous vein
The small saphenous vein

preguntas.pregunta: A front desk moving to open access is told its single rule is to do today's work today. Which habit does that ask the staff to drop?
opciones: Sorting callers by clinical urgency, since demand is now sorted by clinician instead
Booking the follow-up visits a clinician asked for, since those slots are needed today
Offering a caller a later day, since under this model nobody may decline the same-day slot
Counting how many slots were free yesterday, since only the supply of time is measured
preguntas.explicacion: The model breaks with the traditional split between urgent and routine, which is what pushes routine care back. Instead of triaging callers by urgency, reception simply sorts the demand by clinician. Clinically necessary follow-ups are still booked ahead, patients may still choose a later day, and the practice has to measure both supply and demand as precisely as it can.

preguntas.pregunta: Under the bloodborne pathogens standard, protective equipment counts as appropriate only when it does what?

Carries the manufacturer's label with the biohazard symbol printed in orange-red
Is picked by the employee from the sizes the supplier keeps in stock at the site
Is worn over the uniform, which the standard also counts as protective clothing

A clot activator on the tube wall makes the blood clot so the serum can be poured off
Lithium heparin keeps the blood liquid and a gel separates the plasma on spinning
Sodium citrate binds calcium and the serum rises above the cells within an hour

preguntas.pregunta: A 60-year-old reports knee pain that worsens with activity and eases with rest, plus morning stiffness that clears in about twenty minutes. Which diagnosis fits?
opciones: Osteoarthritis, the most common form of arthritis
Osteoporosis, the most common form of arthritis
Rheumatoid arthritis, the most common form of arthritis
Osteomalacia, the most common form of arthritis
preguntas.explicacion: Osteoarthritis is a clinical diagnosis, and the picture is consistent: pain worse with activity and better with rest, age over 45, morning stiffness under thirty minutes, bony joint enlargement and limited range of motion. Osteoporosis is loss of bone mass, not a joint disease, and it usually causes no symptoms until something breaks.

One dose of HBIG plus the start of a third complete vaccine series
A single vaccine booster, then anti-HBs testing 1 to 2 months later
No further treatment, since two series show the worker is a documented responder

Press the plunger gently once the stopper has been removed from the tube
Pressing is acceptable for the last tube, once the tourniquet has been released

preguntas.pregunta: An unvaccinated phlebotomist is stuck by a needle used on an HBsAg-positive patient. According to the CDC, what is given and when?
opciones: HBIG and the first vaccine dose, as soon as possible and preferably within 24 hours, at separate sites
The vaccine series only, started within 7 days, since HBIG is reserved for known non-responders
HBIG only, repeated one month later, since starting the vaccine after exposure is too late
A 28-day antiviral course started within 72 hours, followed by the vaccine series
preguntas.explicacion: The CDC's table for unvaccinated or incompletely vaccinated clinicians exposed to an HBsAg-positive or unknown source calls for one dose of HBIG plus the hepatitis B vaccine, given as soon as possible, at a different anatomical site such as a separate limb, with the series completed on schedule and anti-HBs tested 1 to 2 months after the last dose. The older brochure says HBV post-exposure treatment should start preferably within 24 hours and no later than 7 days. An N95 respirator with eye protection, as for airborne cases
A chemical-resistant suit with a self-contained air supply

Read it for any excursion during transit and place it inside the storage unit

preguntas.pregunta: A patient reports taking high-dose vitamin C supplements. Which two dipstick pads are most likely to give a false-negative result?
opciones: Occult blood and glucose
Protein and bilirubin
pH and specific gravity
Ketones and urobilinogen

The blood pad detects the peroxidase activity of erythrocytes, hemoglobin and myoglobin, and the glucose pad turns positive once the filtered glucose exceeds what the tubules reabsorb. Protein, bilirubin, ketones and pH have other listed interferents, such as alkaline urine for protein or a stale specimen for bilirubin.

preguntas.pregunta: Which facility falls outside the CLIA definition of a laboratory?

A physician office that performs only waived tests on its own patients
A hospital laboratory accredited by a CMS-approved organization
A mobile unit that performs hematology testing on human specimens

A waived-testing office and a mobile unit that runs hematology tests both perform examinations and therefore need a certificate; a pure collection site does not.

preguntas.pregunta: In which forms is medication supplied for the vaginal route?
opciones: Foams, creams, tablets and suppositories that melt with the heat of the body
Foams, creams and coated tablets that are swallowed with a full glass of water
Powders for reconstitution and metered aerosols delivered through a spacer device
Ointments and skin patches that are pressed firmly in place for about ten seconds
preguntas.explicacion: Vaginal instillation is used mostly for hormone therapy and antifungal treatment, and the medication comes as foam, cream, tablet, or a suppository that melts at body heat. Privacy is part of the procedure, not an extra.

preguntas.pregunta: What does the standard require of the safety devices and sharps containers a draw station uses every day?
opciones: They are examined and maintained or replaced on a regular schedule so they keep working
They are examined only after an exposure incident has been reported and logged
They are replaced every three years, the period set for keeping training records
They are checked by the manufacturer at installation and then left in service
preguntas.explicacion: Engineering controls are the devices that take the hazard away from the worker: sharps disposal containers, self-sheathing needles, needleless systems. Paragraph (d)(2)(ii) says they have to be examined and either maintained or replaced on a regular schedule, so that they still do what they were bought to do. Waiting for an injury reverses that logic, and the three-year figure is the retention period for training records in (h)(2)(ii), not a replacement interval.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with diabetes is too drowsy to swallow and the glucose meter reads 42 mg/dL. Which emergency medicine is indicated?
opciones: Glucagon, given into the muscle or by the newer intranasal form
Glucose tablets, placed under the tongue until they dissolve there
Epinephrine, injected into the outer part of the thigh right away
Insulin, given subcutaneously to move the glucose into the cells
preguntas.explicacion: A conscious patient who can swallow gets a readily absorbed carbohydrate such as fruit juice; when the patient cannot take anything by mouth, glucagon is the answer, given intramuscularly or by the newer intranasal preparations. Once the patient is awake, a complex carbohydrate follows and the glucose is rechecked more often.

preguntas.pregunta: What is a hematoma, and which two technique errors cause it?
opciones: Blood pooled under the skin; a needle pushed beyond the vein lumen, or too little pressure during and after the draw
Pinpoint bleeding into the dermis; leaving the tourniquet on too long, or using a needle that is too small
Pooling of blood under the skin; shaking the tube after filling, or drawing the tubes out of sequence
Bleeding into the skin larger than 2 mm; drawing from the basilic vein, or using povidone iodine
preguntas.explicacion: A hematoma is the pooling of blood under the skin, and two errors are linked to it: deep insertion of the needle beyond the lumen of the vein, and failure to apply adequate pressure during and after the draw. The WHO adds a third, letting the patient bend the arm. Pinpoint dermal bleeding is petechiae, and spots larger than 2 mm are purpura in the petechiae chapter.

preguntas.pregunta: Two medical assistants are giving CPR to a 4-year-old child. Which compression-to-ventilation ratio do they use?
opciones: 15 compressions to 2 breaths, because two rescuers are working
30 compressions to 2 breaths, the ratio for a single rescuer
5 compressions to 1 breath, trading places after every cycle
10 compressions to 2 breaths, with 1 breath every 6 seconds
preguntas.explicacion: A child or infant worked by one rescuer gets 2 breaths after every 30 compressions; when two rescuers are present that changes to 2 breaths after every 15 compressions. The rate stays at 100 to 120 per minute either way. One breath every 6 seconds is the rate for rescue breathing in a patient who still has a pulse, not a compression ratio.

preguntas.pregunta: The flow into the tube is slow during a child's draw. Which measure does the WHO offer for the parent to do?
opciones: Rhythmically tighten and release the child's wrist to help the flow
Lower the child's arm below the level of the table for a minute
Press firmly above the elbow until the vein stands out clearly
Rub the puncture site briskly with dry gauze between the tubes
preguntas.explicacion: Where venipuncture proves difficult, the parent may be asked to tighten and release the child's wrist rhythmically so there is adequate blood flow, the child may be kept warm, warm cloths may be laid over the puncture area to dilate the vessels, and a transilluminator or pocket pen light may be used to show the dorsal hand veins and those of the antecubital fossa.

preguntas.pregunta: The laboratory notifies a phlebotomist that a specimen was rejected for a critically ill patient. Why must the recollection be arranged without delay?
opciones: Rejection forces a new sample request, prolongs turnaround and can delay diagnosis and treatment
Rejected specimens are discarded after 30 minutes, after which the original order is cancelled
The laboratory cannot issue any report for the patient until the replacement sample is received
A second rejection from the same unit automatically triggers an accreditation incident report
preguntas.explicacion: Sample rejection stops the analysis and generates a new request, which lengthens turnaround time and delays diagnosis and treatment of critical patients, with adverse outcomes described in the literature; that is the reason the task of contacting the patient or unit for recollection matters. preguntas.pregunta: How many culpability categories does the civil money penalty scheme for HIPAA violations use?
opciones: Four, running from not knowing up to willful neglect that was never corrected
Three, running from an honest mistake up to a deliberate sale of patient records
Two, one for covered entities and a separate one for their business associates
Six, one for each of the circumstances in which records may go to law enforcement
preguntas.explicacion: The HITECH Act set four categories of violation reflecting rising culpability, with four matching tiers of penalty amounts. preguntas.pregunta: The R waves on a strip are spaced unevenly, so the square method will not work. What is done instead?
opciones: Count the beats in a 10-second strip and multiply by 6
Count the beats in a 10-second strip and multiply by 4
Count the beats in a 10-second strip and multiply by 10
Count the small squares between two R waves and use 300
preguntas.explicacion: The square methods assume the beats are evenly spaced. When they are not, the count is taken over the whole ten-second strip and multiplied by six to reach a rate per minute. Dividing 300 by small squares mixes up the two grids and gives a figure far off the real rate.

preguntas.pregunta: Why does laying a patient flat bring them round after a faint?
opciones: Blood returns from the legs and the heart no longer pumps uphill
Blood leaves the legs and pools where the tourniquet had been
The vagus nerve is compressed and the heart rate rises at once
Cooling of the skin restores the vascular tone that had been lost
preguntas.explicacion: When the patient falls or is laid supine, circulating volume returns from the lower limbs and the heart no longer has to deliver blood against gravity, so consciousness comes back quickly. That is also why the person is asked to sit or lie down promptly as soon as the warning symptoms appear.

preguntas.pregunta: The forearm a patient offers shows a hot, red area diagnosed as cellulitis. Why is that site excluded for venipuncture?
opciones: Cellulitis or an abscess raises the risk of bacteria entering the blood directly
The inflamed skin blanches under pressure, which hides the vein from view
The swelling dilutes the specimen with tissue fluid, just as squeezing a finger does
Alcohol cannot be used on inflamed skin, so the site cannot be disinfected
preguntas.explicacion: Conditions such as cellulitis or an abscess can increase the risk of bacteria infiltrating the blood directly, so another site is chosen. Blanching is the feature that tells erythema from bleeding into the skin, tissue fluid dilution is the WHO's capillary warning about squeezing, and nothing in the material forbids alcohol on inflamed skin.

preguntas.pregunta: A clinic uses event-related shelf life for its sterile packs. What does that mean in practice?
opciones: A pack stays sterile until something compromises it, such as a tear, wetness or a broken seal
A pack stays sterile for thirty days from the cycle date, after which it is reprocessed
A pack stays sterile until the next biological indicator is run, regardless of its cycle date
A pack stays sterile only while it sits in a closed cabinet, and is reprocessed once moved
preguntas.explicacion: Event-related practice recognizes that contamination is caused by an event, not by the calendar: a tear in the packaging, packaging that gets wet, a broken seal. preguntas.pregunta: The son says, 'I'll sign the consent, she's forgetful.' No proxy or power-of-attorney paperwork exists. Who decides?
opciones: The patient remains responsible for her own choices; set clear boundaries with the family
The son may sign, because adult children are the default decision-makers for parents
A clinic staff member signs on the patient's behalf as a neutral third party
The draw is deferred until a court appoints a guardian for the patient
preguntas.explicacion: Adult children may want to step in for a parent with cognitive impairment, but that only a family member named as health care agent or proxy has legal authority in some circumstances; without it the patient makes her own choices, and the clinician sets boundaries. Court-appointed guardians are reserved for when the state hierarchy of surrogates fails.

Checking that the kit lot matches the lot of the control material
Writing the date of opening on the outside of the reagent vial

Shared equipment may be used freely, since the pathogen spreads by contact with the patient, not with objects
Wrap shared equipment in a protective cover that is changed at the end of the shift
Autoclave the equipment after each use, since disinfection does not reach contact pathogens
preguntas.explicacion: The CDC's Contact Precautions recommendations name blood pressure cuffs as the example: use disposable or dedicated patient-care equipment, and when common use for several patients cannot be avoided, clean and disinfect it before use on another patient. preguntas.pregunta: How should the puncture stroke itself be made in capillary sampling?
opciones: One quick, continuous and deliberate stroke, to get good flow and avoid repeating the puncture
Two short strokes in the same track, so that the second opens the capillary bed fully
A slow, controlled stroke that stops as soon as the first drop of blood appears
A rocking stroke across the fingerprint lines, which widens the opening without going deeper
preguntas.explicacion: The skin is punctured with one quick, continuous and deliberate stroke, to achieve a good flow of blood and to prevent the need to repeat the puncture. A second puncture would mean either reusing the lancet or the site, both of which are prohibited because of bacterial contamination and infection. Depth is controlled by lancet length, not by rocking.

preguntas.pregunta: An agitated inpatient calms down 20 minutes into a 4-hour restraint order. What should happen?

Keep the restraints on until the 4-hour order expires, as written
Keep the restraints on until the next scheduled face-to-face evaluation
Loosen one limb every 15 minutes until the order runs out
preguntas.explicacion: When the patient is no longer a danger to themselves or others, the restraints are removed at once; the time limit on the order is a maximum, not a prescribed duration. Restraint and seclusion are interventions of last resort, required to be the least restrictive measure, with no evidence that they are therapeutic or reduce aggression, and staff observe the patient regularly throughout.

Free, but only at the occupational health service the employer has contracted
At the employee's expense, reimbursed once the written opinion has arrived

Recapping every needle carefully with the cap held in the other hand
Storing used needles on the tray until the end of the drawing session
Rinsing the used needle before it goes into the puncture-resistant bin
preguntas.explicacion: Eliminating needle recapping and disposing of the sharp immediately into a puncture-resistant container is described as markedly reducing these injuries. Eating a light meal, reading in poor light, walking upstairs, yawning
Drinking water, sitting down slowly, wearing loose clothing, resting
Breathing slowly, lying flat for an hour, raising the legs, whistling

Only if the gloves were visibly soiled with blood
Before touching the next patient, which covers this case
At the end of the shift, because gloves replace hand hygiene

So the same manufacturer supplies the needles and holders in the tray

Alcohol rub, worked in until the hands are dry
Alcohol rub, followed by a second pair of gloves
Soap and water, dried with a shared cloth towel

preguntas.pregunta: A glucose specimen will not reach the laboratory for two days. What does the additive in the grey top tube provide?
opciones: It is antiglycolytic and preserves the glucose for up to five days
It is antiglycolytic and preserves the glucose for up to twelve hours
It activates clotting so the glucose stays with the separated serum
It inactivates thrombin so the glucose stays with the plasma fraction
preguntas.explicacion: The light grey tube holds sodium fluoride with potassium oxalate. The oxalate binds calcium and stops clotting, and the fluoride is the antiglycolytic agent credited with preserving glucose for as much as five days. Clot activation belongs to the red tube and thrombin inactivation to the heparin tubes.

preguntas.pregunta: What does a 'trough level' represent in antiepileptic drug monitoring?
opciones: The lowest drug concentration, typically just before the next dose is due
The highest drug concentration, shortly after the dose has been taken
The unbound, pharmacologically active fraction of the drug in blood
The average concentration across the whole dosing interval
preguntas.explicacion: The trough is the concentration at its lowest point, typically just before the next dose, a measurement that matters most for drugs with short half-lives because it shows the minimum level maintained between doses. Free levels are the unbound active fraction, measured when protein binding may be altered. The peak and the interval average are different quantities.

preguntas.pregunta: What makes a POLST or MOLST form different from a living will?
opciones: It records the wishes as medical orders that carry across care settings
It records the wishes as a sworn statement filed with the state registry
It records the wishes of the family rather than those of the patient
It records the wishes only for the hospital where it was first signed
preguntas.explicacion: On a POLST or MOLST the patient's preferences are written as medical orders, and in states that recognize the form those orders travel with the patient across health care settings, including the prehospital one. preguntas.pregunta: A group practice and each of its physicians are enrolling. Which NPI entity types apply?

Type 1 for the organization and Type 2 for each individual provider
Type 2 for both, since everyone in a group enrolls under the group number
Type 1 for both, since the number always belongs to a licensed human being

Entity Type 1 covers individual health care providers, sole proprietors included, and a sole proprietor applies with a Social Security Number rather than an employer identification number even if one exists. preguntas.pregunta: Why do the veins of the limbs have valves, and roughly what share of the blood volume is in the veins at any moment?
opciones: To stop backflow under low pressure and gravity; almost 70 percent
To stop backflow under low pressure and gravity; about 10 percent
To produce the pulse felt at the radial artery; almost 70 percent
To regulate flow into the capillary beds; about 5 percent
preguntas.explicacion: Veins are low-pressure vessels, so the larger ones, especially in the limbs, carry valves that keep blood moving toward the heart against the low pressure and the pull of gravity. Thinner, less rigid venous walls let veins hold more blood, almost 70 percent of the total volume, against about 10 percent in the systemic arteries and 5 percent in the systemic capillaries.

preguntas.pregunta: A man with new hypertension asks how much sodium a day the Dietary Guidelines allow for a healthy adult. What do you tell him?
opciones: Under 2,300 mg a day, and less than that for children under 14
Under 1,500 mg a day, and less than that for children under 14
Under 3,400 mg a day, which is what most adults already eat
Under 2,300 mg a day, but only for adults who already have hypertension
preguntas.explicacion: The guidelines cap sodium below 2,300 mg a day for the general population and set lower amounts for children under 14. preguntas.pregunta: A pulse of 48 beats per minute is documented as bradycardia. Which two word parts build that term?
opciones: A prefix meaning slow plus a root meaning heart
A prefix meaning fast plus a root meaning heart
A prefix meaning slow plus a root meaning artery
A prefix meaning half plus a root meaning muscle
preguntas.explicacion: Brady- means slow and tachy- means fast; cardi- and cardio- name the heart. So bradycardia is a slow heart and tachycardia a fast one. The root for artery is arterio-, and my- or myo- names muscle, which is why a heart attack is a myocardial infarction rather than an arterial one.

preguntas.pregunta: For adult CPR, what compression-to-breath ratio and compression rate are used?
opciones: 30 compressions to 2 breaths, at 100 to 120 compressions per minute
15 compressions to 2 breaths, at 60 to 80 compressions per minute
30 compressions to 5 breaths, at 100 to 120 compressions per minute
5 compressions to 1 breath, at 120 to 140 compressions per minute
preguntas.explicacion: Adult CPR runs in cycles of 30 chest compressions followed by 2 rescue breaths, repeated until the person recovers or help arrives, at a rate of 100 to 120 compressions per minute with pauses for breaths kept under 10 seconds. The heel of one hand goes in the center of the chest between the nipples with the other hand on top, elbows locked and shoulders over the hands. With two or more rescuers, compressors switch every 2 minutes or about 5 cycles to avoid fatigue, and an AED is used as soon as one is available.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient admits to a history of panic attacks during blood draws. Which two simple measures are described to lower anxiety and prepare for a possible reaction?
opciones: Counting down before the puncture, and having the patient lie down when the history is severe
Drawing without warning so the patient has no time to react, and using a smaller needle
Applying the tourniquet early so the draw is quicker, and keeping the patient standing
Postponing the draw until a family member is present, and skipping the identification questions
preguntas.explicacion: Simple steps such as counting down can significantly reduce anxiety and improve the conditions for the venipuncture, and a patient with a severe history of panic attacks during the procedure may be asked to lie down; identifying patients afraid of blood tests or with a history of vasovagal attacks in advance lets the team prepare for a possible faint. preguntas.pregunta: During a venipuncture the phlebotomist notices a tear in one glove. What does the standard require?
opciones: Replace it as soon as feasible; a single-use glove is never washed for reuse
Finish the draw, then wash the glove with soap and water so it can be reused
Cover the tear with tape until the procedure ends, then discard the glove
Replace it only if blood reached the skin; otherwise finish the draw and discard it
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(3)(ix)(A) requires disposable gloves to be replaced as soon as practical when contaminated, or as soon as feasible when torn, punctured or otherwise unable to act as a barrier. The trigger is the loss of the barrier, not whether blood has already reached the skin.

preguntas.pregunta: What are the four basic steps of food safety taught for the home kitchen?
opciones: Clean, separate, cook and chill
Clean, sanitize, cook and freeze
Wash, marinate, cook and reheat
Clean, separate, season and store
preguntas.explicacion: Handling, cooking and storing food safely is what keeps foodborne illness away, and the steps are four: clean hands, produce, counters and utensils; separate raw foods so germs do not travel between them; cook food hot and keep it hot, because heat kills germs; and chill fresh food in the refrigerator right away.

The prothrombin tube goes third and the thromboplastin tube tenth
Both are citrate tubes, but they follow the serum separator tube
The thromboplastin tube goes second, ahead of the prothrombin tube

preguntas.pregunta: How far should Steri-Strips extend past a staple line, and what is the patient told about them?

About 1.5 to 2 cm on each side, and to peel them off gently at the first follow-up visit
About 5 to 6 cm on each side, and to let them fall off on their own over one to three weeks
Only as far as the staple holes, and to soak them off in the bath after three or four days

preguntas.pregunta: How does the technique of an intramuscular injection differ from a subcutaneous one?
opciones: The skin is stabilized instead of pinched, and the needle enters at 90 degrees
The skin is pinched instead of stabilized, and the needle enters at 45 degrees
The skin is held taut and flat, and the needle enters at 5 to 15 degrees

preguntas.pregunta: A patient collecting a 24-hour urine for 5-HIAA asks which foods to avoid. Which list is correct?
opciones: Avocados, bananas, pineapples, walnuts and eggplants
Cooked meats, herbal tea and alcoholic beverages
Douching, tampons and sex in the 24 to 48 hours before
Coffee, energy drinks and lemon-flavoured water
preguntas.explicacion: For a 5-HIAA test the patient may be asked to avoid various foods, the examples given being avocados, bananas, pineapples, walnuts and eggplants. Other tests carry other restrictions: creatinine may call for fasting or avoiding cooked meats, cortisol for resting before the draw and avoiding eating, drinking or tooth-brushing for a period, and a fecal occult blood test for avoiding certain foods and medicines. The douching, tampon and intercourse restriction belongs to the Pap smear, not to a urine collection.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, How to Prepare for a Lab Test, section What types of lab tests require special preparation; StatPearls, "Urinalysis", section Interfering Factors

preguntas.pregunta: How many oxygen molecules can a single hemoglobin molecule carry, and what binds them?
opciones: Four, one on the iron ion of each of its four heme groups
Two, one on each alpha-beta pair of globin chains
Four, one bound directly to each of the four globin proteins
About 300 million, one for every hemoglobin in the cell
preguntas.explicacion: Hemoglobin consists of four folded globin chains, two alpha and two beta, each holding a heme group with an iron ion. Oxygen binds to the iron, not to the globin protein, so each hemoglobin carries up to four oxygen molecules. A single red cell holds about 300 million hemoglobin molecules, which is why one cell can carry about 1.2 billion oxygen molecules.
preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.3 Erythrocytes, Hemoglobin

preguntas.pregunta: A hospital's electronic system sends an event notification when a patient is admitted. Which three items must the message carry at a minimum?
opciones: The patient's name, the treating practitioner's name and the sending institution
The patient's name, the admitting diagnosis and the expected date of discharge
The patient's record number, the insurance plan and the treating practitioner
The patient's name, the reason for the visit and the telephone of the unit
preguntas.explicacion: Where a hospital runs a system that meets the adopted content exchange standard, its notification capacity has to be in use, and each message must include at least the name of the patient, the name of the practitioner treating him and the name of the institution sending it. Diagnosis and coverage are not part of that minimum.

preguntas.pregunta: The patient cable is hanging off the side of the table and the baseline will not settle. What is the mechanism?
opciones: The pull on the wires unsettles the contact at the electrode
The pull on the wires lowers the voltage the unit records
The pull on the wires draws room current into the tracing
The pull on the wires slows the paper leaving the writer
preguntas.explicacion: Tension on the lead wires is one of the six listed reasons for unstable electrode contact, and unstable contact is the prime suspect behind drift. The weight of a hanging wire tugs at the tab, which is why a towel is laid across the wires to take the pull off.

preguntas.pregunta: Which ethical principle is at work when a limited supply of a treatment is spread fairly across the patients who need it?
opciones: Distributing resources equitably across the patients
Preserving the patient's life and their autonomy
Avoiding acts known to expose a patient to harm
Placing a high value on the dignity of the person
preguntas.explicacion: Patient rights grow out of a short list of principles: valuing the dignity of the person, acting with goodwill toward the patient and in particular preserving life and autonomy, avoiding acts or omissions known to expose the patient to harm, and distributing resources equitably across patients. The last is the one that governs a scarce supply. A right to receive treatment is usually traced to goodwill, the sanctity of life and that same distributive fairness.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Rights and Ethics", Introduction; Issues of Concern: Medical Treatment

preguntas.pregunta: How does physician-patient privilege differ from doctor-patient confidentiality?
opciones: The privilege applies inside legal proceedings; confidentiality applies outside them
The privilege applies to written records; confidentiality applies to spoken exchanges
The privilege applies to federal cases; confidentiality applies to state-level cases
The privilege applies while treatment continues; confidentiality applies afterwards
preguntas.explicacion: The privilege protects communications between a clinician and a patient inside legal proceedings: it keeps the professional from testifying about the patient's medical information unless the patient waives it, and either side may assert it. Confidentiality protects records and information outside litigation, under state and federal statutes. The privilege comes from state statutes and varies.
preguntas.fuente: Cornell Law School LII, Wex: physician-patient privilege

preguntas.pregunta: A Medicaid patient also holds coverage through her husband's employer. Which plan does the practice bill first?
opciones: The employer plan, since Medicaid pays only the portion no third party owes
Medicaid, since a state program always pays ahead of a commercial plan
Whichever plan the patient names, since she may choose the order of payers
Both together, since the two share the bill in proportion to their benefits
preguntas.explicacion: Third party liability means a third party has a legal obligation to pay part or all of the cost of services given to a Medicaid beneficiary, and the examples named are other programs such as Medicare and any other health insurance the person holds. Where such an obligation exists Medicaid pays only its own portion, which is why the other coverage is billed first.
preguntas.fuente: CMS, Medicaid.gov: Eligibility, Third Party Liability

preguntas.pregunta: Which finding rules out ear irrigation for a cerumen impaction?
opciones: A history of tympanic membrane perforation or of previous ear surgery
A history of using cotton-tipped applicators to clean the ear canal
A cerumenolytic such as mineral oil having been instilled beforehand
Aural fullness and decreased hearing on the side to be irrigated
preguntas.explicacion: Otoscopy comes first, to confirm an intact eardrum and no ventilation tubes. Known perforation, tubes, previous surgery such as tympanomastoidectomy, discharge suggesting infection, or prior radiation to the area all rule it out, and those patients go to an otolaryngologist. Cotton swabs are a cause of impaction, and fullness is a reason to treat it.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Ear Irrigation", Contraindications

preguntas.pregunta: According to HealthCare.gov, who can serve as a patient's primary care provider?
opciones: An M.D. or D.O., a nurse practitioner, a clinical nurse specialist or a physician assistant, where state law allows
Only a physician holding a medical doctor (M.D.) degree, and never a doctor of osteopathic medicine (D.O.)
A physician or nurse practitioner only; physician assistants and clinical nurse specialists are excluded
Any of the four professionals, but only a physician may coordinate the patient's access to other services
preguntas.explicacion: HealthCare.gov's definition names four kinds of professional who can be a primary care provider: a physician, whether M.D. or D.O.; a nurse practitioner; a clinical nurse specialist; and a physician assistant, in each case as state law allows. All four share the same role in the definition: to provide, coordinate or help the patient reach a range of health care services. The D.O. is named alongside the M.D., no one of the four is excluded, and coordination is not reserved to the physician.
preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Primary care provider

preguntas.pregunta: A patient reports a latex allergy. Which items on a routine phlebotomy tray are likely to contain latex?
opciones: Gloves, tourniquets and elastic bandages or wraps
Gloves and alcohol swabs, but not the elastic band
Evacuated tubes and their stoppers, and the labels
Sharps containers and the plastic transport bags
preguntas.explicacion: Latex turns up throughout health care, most commonly in gloves, and the medical items listed alongside them include tourniquets and elastic bandages and wraps. A patient with this allergy needs latex-free substitutes for those items, and the whole team has to be told about the allergy.

preguntas.pregunta: A clotted EDTA tube is rejected. Under the CLIA test records standard, what must the laboratory's record system contain about that specimen?
opciones: Its condition and what was done with it, since it did not meet the acceptability criteria
Only the date of receipt, because no test was performed on the specimen
The name and title of the person who collected it and the reason the collection attempt failed
Only its positive identification, because the condition of a rejected specimen is not a record element
preguntas.explicacion: 42 CFR 493.1283(a)(3) requires the record system to include the condition and disposition of specimens that fail the laboratory's acceptability criteria, together with the positive identification of every specimen, the date and time of receipt, and the dates and identity of the personnel who ran each test. The collector's name is not a listed element, and rejected specimens are explicitly covered, not exempt.

preguntas.pregunta: A stage 3 pressure injury drains heavily and needs packing. Which dressing fits, and what must be avoided?
opciones: An alginate, which is highly absorptive and must not be put into a dry wound
A transparent film, which retains moisture and must not be put on fragile skin
A hydrogel, which adds moisture and must not be spread onto the surrounding skin
A dry gauze, which costs the least of these and must not be left in place beyond a day
preguntas.explicacion: Alginates and hydrofibers are nonadherent and highly absorptive, which suits heavily exuding wounds and packing of full-thickness injuries at stage 3 or 4. They are usually changed every 24 to 48 hours depending on how saturated they are, and they are kept out of dry wounds because there they can injure the wound bed.
preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, 20.5 Wound Dressings

preguntas.pregunta: A child with spina bifida is scheduled for a blood draw. Why is latex a particular concern?
opciones: The prevalence of latex hypersensitivity in spina bifida is 20% to 65%
The prevalence in spina bifida is 1% to 2%, the same as the general population
Spina bifida causes a type IV reaction to the cornstarch in gloves
Children with spina bifida are routinely allergic to bananas and kiwi
preguntas.explicacion: Patients with spina bifida are a recognized high-risk group, with reported prevalence of latex hypersensitivity between 20% and 65%, probably because of repeated corrective surgeries and procedures; patients with repeated catheterization are also at raised risk. One to two percent is the general-population figure, and the fruit link is a separate risk marker, not a rule.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Latex Allergy", section Epidemiology
