preguntas.pregunta: An e-mail marked urgent asks a receptionist to open an attachment and confirm her log-in. Which trained response does the guidance describe?
opciones: Hover over the link to read where it goes and check the sender by another route
Open the attachment only if the sender's address matches the practice's domain
Forward it to the whole staff so that everyone recognizes the message on sight
Reply to the same message asking the sender to confirm that it is legitimate
preguntas.explicacion: Malicious attachments and callers asking for log-in details are the usual first step of a ransomware attack. Users are trained to hover first and read the destination address, to weigh the sender, the urgency and the spelling, and, when in doubt, to confirm through a separate channel. Replying in the same thread confirms nothing, since the sender may be the attacker.
preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, SAFER Guide: Contingency Planning, Recommended Practice 2.4
preguntas.subtema: Ransomware prevention · CCMA 5 k191 · CMA III.E.1.e · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 7H k97 · NCMA 3.5

preguntas.pregunta: Which position is used for a routine office blood pressure?
opciones: Seated with the back supported, both feet flat on the floor and the legs uncrossed
Seated on the end of the table with the feet hanging and the back left unsupported
Lying supine with the arm at the side, which removes the effect of gravity entirely
Seated with the legs crossed at the ankle, which steadies the patient during inflation
preguntas.explicacion: The patient sits with the back against the chair, feet flat and legs uncrossed, and stays that way for at least five minutes before the cuff is inflated. Each departure has a price: an unsupported back and feet add about 6 mm Hg and crossed legs add 2 to 4 mm Hg to the systolic value.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Vital Sign Assessment", Clinical Significance: Blood Pressure
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k47 · CMA I.A.1.a · RMA III.E.2.b · NCMA 2B.6

preguntas.pregunta: A billing clerk asks a phlebotomist for a patient's full medical history to process a claim. Which HIPAA standard is at stake?
opciones: Minimum necessary: limit the PHI to what the payment purpose requires
Right of access: the clerk may see all records that the patient could see herself
Treatment exception: payment staff are exempt from all limits
De-identification: the clerk must receive only coded data
preguntas.explicacion: Payment is a permitted purpose, but it is not on the list of exceptions to the minimum necessary standard, so the covered entity must make reasonable efforts to limit what the clerk receives to what processing the claim requires. The treatment exception covers providers treating the patient, not billing. De-identified data would not serve payment, and the right of access belongs to the individual, not to workforce members. The same principle appears in guidance that access should match the employee's role, so a laboratory technologist sees laboratory records and not the whole history.
preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 164.502(b); StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Selective Access

preguntas.pregunta: Which tools are recommended for checking whether a patient really understood the risks, benefits and alternatives?
opciones: The teach-back or test/feedback method
A signed consent form and a staff witness
A formal psychiatric competency evaluation
A reading-level check of the consent form
preguntas.explicacion: Teach-back or the test/feedback method can be used to assess understanding, and open-ended questions and encouraging questions make the dialogue interactive. It also notes that the emphasis on a signature as proof of understanding is being questioned, and that a psychiatrist is consulted only when capacity is in doubt.

preguntas.pregunta: A scar is documented as being in the anterior carpal region. Which surface of the wrist does that describe?
opciones: The palm side, because anterior is defined from anatomical position
The back side, because anterior is defined from the resting hand
The thumb side, because anterior is defined from the midline
The little finger side, because anterior follows the ulnar edge
preguntas.explicacion: Every directional term is read as if the body were in anatomical position: standing upright, feet forward, arms out to the sides and palms facing forward. In that position the palm faces front, so an anterior carpal scar is on the palm side, and it keeps that name even when the hand is lying palm down on a table.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient lies tense on the table and the tracing is fuzzy. Besides reassurance, which step is suggested?
opciones: Tuck the hands under the buttocks and raise the knees
Fold the arms across the chest and cross the ankles
Have the patient sit up until the shivering has passed
Hold the arms down against the table during the run
preguntas.explicacion: Laying the hands on the stomach helps, and tucking them under the buttocks usually helps more; a pillow under the knees to raise the legs slightly is part of the same list. Crossing the legs is the opposite of what the position calls for, since the arms rest at the sides and the legs stay uncrossed.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 3.5.2 Muscle Tremor Interference

preguntas.pregunta: A sputum culture is scheduled. Which two instructions help the patient produce a usable specimen?
opciones: Drink plenty of fluids the night before, and collect first thing in the morning
Drink plenty of fluids the night before, and collect right after the evening meal
Fast completely for 12 hours, and then collect first thing in the morning
Take an over-the-counter cough suppressant, and collect first thing in the morning
preguntas.explicacion: Fluids the night before make the airways produce more phlegm and the sputum easier to raise, and the test is more accurate done first thing in the morning, before eating or drinking. A 12-hour fast is the preparation for bronchoscopy, not for a coughed specimen, and suppressing the cough would defeat the collection. The provider may tap the chest or offer a salty mist to help.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Sputum Gram stain (003765), How to Prepare for the Test; and MedlinePlus, Sputum Culture, Will I need to do anything to prepare for the test?

preguntas.pregunta: Who may obtain a copy of an employee's bloodborne pathogens medical record?
opciones: The employee, anyone with the employee's written consent, and OSHA or NIOSH
Any supervisor in the department where the exposure incident took place
The source patient, who is entitled to the results of the exposed worker
The employee's union representative, in the same way as training records
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (h)(1)(iii) keeps these records confidential and forbids disclosing them, inside or outside the workplace, without the employee's express written consent, unless the standard or another law requires it. Paragraph (h)(3)(iii) then names who does get them: the employee, anyone holding that written consent, the Director of NIOSH and the Assistant Secretary of Labor. Employee representatives appear one paragraph earlier, in (h)(3)(ii), and only for training records.

preguntas.pregunta: A serum sample from a patient with very high triglycerides is milky. Which analytes did the study by Calmarza and colleagues find clinically affected, and what can remove the interference?
opciones: Phosphorus, creatinine, total protein and calcium; ultracentrifugation of the sample
Potassium, LDH, AST and total bilirubin; dilution of the sample before analysis
Sodium, chloride and bicarbonate; refrigeration of the sample at 2 to 8 °C overnight
Glucose, urea and uric acid; filtering the sample through a serum separator gel
preguntas.explicacion: Lipemia from hypertriglyceridaemia produced clinically significant interference for phosphorus, creatinine, total protein and calcium, and those interferences could be reduced or removed by ultracentrifugation; a later study showed that high-speed centrifugation in a micro-centrifuge is a practical, cheaper alternative for several analytes. Potassium, LDH, AST and bilirubin are the hemolysis set, not the lipemia set.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Preanalytical phase - a continuous challenge for laboratory professionals" (Biochem Med 2012, PMC4062337), Preanalytical phase studies recently published

preguntas.pregunta: What did the Needlestick Safety and Prevention Act lead to?
opciones: A revision of the bloodborne pathogens standard, with a sharps injury log
A new federal agency dedicated to investigating percutaneous injuries
A requirement that every needlestick be reported to the state health board
A ban on all needle devices that are not fitted with a retracting sheath
preguntas.explicacion: The act became public law on November 6, 2000, and in 2001 the bloodborne pathogens standard was revised in response. Among other things the revised standard calls for engineering and work practice controls to remove or reduce exposure to blood and other potentially infectious material, and it requires employers to keep a sharps injury log recording percutaneous injuries from contaminated sharps.

preguntas.pregunta: Which three are the augmented unipolar limb leads?
opciones: aVR, aVL and aVF, taken from the four limb electrodes
I, II and III, taken from the four limb electrodes
V1, V2 and V3, taken from the four limb electrodes
II, III and aVF, taken from the four limb electrodes
preguntas.explicacion: The six limb leads split into two families that share the same four electrodes: the standard bipolar leads I, II and III, and the augmented unipolar leads aVR, aVL and aVF. V1 through V6 are the precordial leads and come from the six electrodes stuck on the chest wall.

preguntas.pregunta: Why is the ventrogluteal site preferred over the dorsogluteal one for an intramuscular injection?
opciones: The dorsogluteal site risks injuring the sciatic nerve and the superior gluteal artery
The dorsogluteal site holds so little muscle that it cannot take a full millilitre
The ventrogluteal site lies over a very vascular area, so the drug is absorbed faster
The ventrogluteal site is the only one that can be reached with the patient seated
preguntas.explicacion: Intramuscular medication can go into the deltoid, the dorsogluteal, the ventrogluteal, the rectus femoris or the vastus lateralis. The dorsogluteal site, the upper outer quadrant of the buttock, was the traditional choice, but it carries a risk of injury to the superior gluteal artery and the sciatic nerve. The ventrogluteal site targets the gluteus medius and avoids both, which is why it is the recommended one.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Medication Routes of Administration", Anatomy and Physiology: Parenteral Route

preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks for his records and refuses to say what he wants them for. How should the office respond?
opciones: Process the request, because a covered entity may not require a reason for wanting access
Hold the request until he states a purpose the office can record on its own access form
Deny the request, since a stated purpose is one of the elements of a valid access request
Refer him to the privacy official, who alone may waive the requirement to state a purpose
preguntas.explicacion: A covered entity may require that access requests be in writing and may use its own form, but only if that does not become a barrier or an unreasonable delay. OCR states plainly that the entity may not require the individual to give a reason, and that a rationale volunteered or already known is not a permitted ground for denying access.
preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Individuals Right under HIPAA to Access their Health Information: Requests for Access

preguntas.pregunta: Why is the midstream clean-catch technique used instead of simply voiding into a cup?
opciones: To keep germs from the penis or vagina out of the sample, so contaminants and formed particles are minimized
To obtain the most concentrated urine of the day, which shows the kidneys' ability to concentrate
To bypass the urethra entirely, which is the only way to get a sample free of periurethral flora
To capture the first portion of the stream, where epithelial cells and leukocytes are most numerous
preguntas.explicacion: The clean-catch method exists to stop organisms from the penis or vagina from entering the urine. A multicenter comparison found that first-voided samples carried more epithelial cells, red cells and leukocytes than midstream samples, so midstream urine was confirmed as the most appropriate sample. Concentration is the reason for a first-morning specimen, and bypassing the urethra describes suprapubic aspiration, not a voided sample.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, PMC3936984 Delanghe & Speeckaert, Preanalytical requirements of urinalysis (2014), Which sampling procedure is preferable?

preguntas.pregunta: Which practice protects the assistant's back during a transfer?
opciones: Staying close so the patient's weight rides near the assistant's center of gravity
Lifting with the assistant's own weight so the patient does not have to help at all
Standing at arm's length so that the patient has room to shift the feet freely
Letting the patient link both arms around the assistant's neck for extra security
preguntas.explicacion: Two rules do most of the work: let the patient use their own strength wherever they can, and keep them close so their weight stays near the helper's center of gravity. The patient should not be allowed to wrap their arms around the helper's head. Feet apart between the patient's shoulders and hips, weight shifting from the back foot to the front.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Care Transfer Techniques", Preparation: Special considerations
preguntas.subtema: NCMA 2A.6 · CCMA 3B4 k65

preguntas.pregunta: When the employer decides which jobs involve occupational exposure, how must protective equipment be treated?
opciones: Ignored: the determination is made as if no protective equipment were worn
Counted: a job is exposed only if PPE cannot fully block the anticipated contact
Counted: the determination lists the PPE provided and excludes tasks it covers
Deferred: PPE is assessed later, in the annual review of safer medical devices
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (c)(2)(ii) states that the exposure determination is made without regard to the use of personal protective equipment. The question is whether contact with blood or OPIM is reasonably anticipated in the job, not whether gloves or gowns would stop it. That is why the lists in (c)(2)(i) are built from job classifications and tasks. The annual review in (c)(1)(iv) looks at technology and safer devices; it does not substitute for the determination.
preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(c)(2)(i) and (c)(2)(ii), Exposure Determination

preguntas.pregunta: An uninsured patient and an insured patient need the same limited resource. What does the ethical framework require?
opciones: Fair distribution regardless of insurance status or social standing
Priority for the insured patient, because the cost is already covered
Priority for the uninsured patient, to correct the existing imbalance
A decision by the business manager, who is accountable for the budget
preguntas.explicacion: The principle of justice tells the practitioner to distribute medical resources fairly and equitably regardless of demographics, insurance status, socioeconomic status or mental disability. Applied at the bedside, that means rationing what good can be done evenly and equitably among the patients involved, rather than sorting them by who pays.

preguntas.pregunta: As the needle is advanced, a swelling rises quickly at the site. What has most likely happened?
opciones: The needle went beyond the lumen of the vein and blood is pooling under the skin
The vein has collapsed under the vacuum of the tube and blood is backing up into it
The tourniquet has occluded the artery and the limb is becoming congested
The alcohol was not dry, and the irritated skin is swelling around the needle
preguntas.explicacion: Inserting the needle beyond the lumen of the vein causes a hematoma, the pooling of blood under the skin. A hematoma can also form when adequate pressure is not applied during and after the draw. A collapsed vein is not described in these sources, and wet alcohol raises contamination risk, not swelling.

preguntas.pregunta: Which of these is one of the extra rights added to the traditional five rights of medication administration?
opciones: The right of the patient to refuse the medication that has been prescribed
The right of the patient to a generic substitution chosen by the pharmacist
The right of the patient to a second opinion before any injection is given
The right of the patient to a written copy of the prescriber's own signature
preguntas.explicacion: The five traditional rights are patient, drug, dose, route and time. Documentation is usually added as a sixth, and the literature stretches the list as far as ten with right history and assessment, right drug interactions, right to refuse, and right education and information. Others have proposed the right indication, the right patient response and legible orders. Adding rights on its own does not stop errors.

preguntas.pregunta: A laboratory measuring its rate of misidentified samples wants a benchmark to judge itself against. Which figure marks optimum performance in the published specifications?
opciones: Under 0.4 % of samples misidentified
Under 2 % of samples misidentified
Under 0.01 % of samples misidentified
Under 5 % of samples misidentified
preguntas.explicacion: The preliminary quality specifications drawn from laboratories in Europe, the United States and the Asia-Pacific region place three figures at the optimum level: fewer than 0.4 % of samples misidentified, an average time under 50 minutes to communicate a critical result, and more than 96 % of critical results communicated at all. preguntas.pregunta: A patient in a Medicare Advantage Plan asks whether joining it ends her monthly Part B bill.
opciones: No, she must keep Part B and go on paying that premium to stay in the plan
Yes, the plan takes the place of Part B and of the premium that goes with it
Yes, provided the plan she joined also includes prescription drug coverage
No, but the Part B premium is refunded to her each year by the plan itself
preguntas.explicacion: Premiums, deductibles, copayments and coinsurance under a Medicare Advantage Plan vary by plan and can change every year, and the condition Medicare states plainly is that the enrollee must have Part B and keep paying the Part B premium in order to stay in the plan. preguntas.pregunta: When several tubes are collected in one venipuncture, which tube is filled first?
opciones: The blood culture bottle
The light blue citrate tube
The non-additive tube
The grey fluoride tube
preguntas.explicacion: Tubes are filled in a fixed sequence so that the additive of one tube is not carried into the next. In the order the WHO reproduces from the United States laboratory standards consensus, the blood culture bottle is number 1. A tube with no additive comes second, the citrate tube third, then the clot activator and serum separator tubes, the heparin tubes, EDTA, the ACD tube, and the fluoride/oxalate tube last, in tenth place. Colour codes can differ between manufacturers, so the WHO tells you to check with the local laboratory.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks that appointment calls go to her work number rather than her home. What must the office do?
opciones: Accommodate the reasonable request for confidential communication at an alternative number
Refuse, because the number in the demographic record is the only one the office may dial
Require a signed authorization naming the workplace as a permitted disclosure location
Send the reminder by postcard instead, since written notice avoids the problem entirely
preguntas.explicacion: Health plans and covered providers must let individuals request that communications reach them by an alternative means or at an alternative location. The example the rule gives is a patient asking to be called at her office rather than her home, and a provider must accommodate a reasonable request. The parallel example for written mail is asking for a closed envelope instead of a postcard.

preguntas.pregunta: What does the contingency guidance expect of the power arrangements behind the record system?
opciones: An uninterrupted supply for at least ten minutes and a generator with fuel for two days
An uninterrupted supply for at least one hour and a generator with fuel for one day
A generator alone, tested each year, since the record system restarts by itself after a cut
A second electricity contract with another company, switched over by the building's staff
preguntas.explicacion: Two layers are described. A battery or flywheel supply carries the record system instantly for at least ten minutes, and it is tested regularly, optimally monthly. Behind it sits an on-site generator able to keep the functions critical to operations running, with two days of fuel held on site, tested monthly and kept where flooding is unlikely.

preguntas.pregunta: When must bloodborne pathogens training be given to an employee with occupational exposure?
opciones: At initial assignment to exposure tasks and at least once a year afterward
At initial assignment only, with a refresher when an exposure incident occurs
Within 10 working days of hire and again whenever the sharps log is updated
Once every three years, matching the retention period for the training records
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (g)(2)(ii) requires training at the time of initial assignment to tasks where exposure may occur and at least annually thereafter; (g)(2)(iv) adds that each annual session falls within one year of the previous one. An exposure incident triggers follow-up for the employee, not a training cycle. Ten working days is the vaccine deadline of (f)(2)(i), and three years is how long the training records are kept, not how often the training happens.

preguntas.pregunta: Beyond the rate, which characteristics does a complete pulse assessment describe?
opciones: Rhythm, volume, amplitude, rate of rise and symmetry between the two sides
Rhythm, skin colour at the site, capillary refill time and the limb temperature
Rhythm, the pressure needed to obliterate the beat and the width of the vessel
Rhythm, volume and the oxygen saturation read at the same finger during the count
preguntas.explicacion: Counting beats is only part of it. A full assessment covers rhythm, volume, amplitude, how fast the wave rises and whether the two sides match. Symmetry earns its place because unequal pulses can point to major vascular disease such as aortic dissection or coarctation of the aorta.

preguntas.pregunta: The clinician will need to look at a rash on the patient's shoulder by video. Which instruction does the setup guidance give her beforehand?
opciones: To wear loose clothing, so that she can show the part of the body in question
To sit with the window behind her, so that the strongest light falls on the camera
To hold the device in her hand and move it about as the clinician asks her to
To sit far enough back that her whole body stays inside the picture throughout
preguntas.explicacion: The advice on getting set up is to choose a spot with plenty of light and avoid sitting with the back towards a window, since that makes the face harder to see; to keep the camera steady and at eye level with head and shoulders in view; to wear loose clothing where the clinician needs to see skin or a particular part of the body; and to cut background noise and distractions.

preguntas.pregunta: An older patient on a diuretic gets dizzy when standing up quickly. What connects the two?
opciones: Blood pressure medicines, diuretics among them, are a common cause of the drop
Diuretics raise the pressure on standing, and the dizziness comes from that rise
Diuretics have no effect on posture, so another cause must explain the dizziness
Diuretics slow the pulse, and it is the slow rate that produces the dizziness
preguntas.explicacion: Feeling dizzy on standing up too quickly is the drop in pressure called orthostatic hypotension, and it is often related to medicines, particularly the drugs used for blood pressure. Diuretics can lower pressure, most often when the patient changes position too fast. Digoxin and beta blockers are the ones that slow the pulse.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Aging changes in vital signs

preguntas.pregunta: Which description of the subcutaneous injection sites is correct?
opciones: Outer upper arm, front of the thighs, upper back, upper gluteal area, abdomen
Ventrogluteal area, vastus lateralis and deltoid, chosen by age and body mass
Upper third of the forearm, outer upper arms, and the area between the scapulae
Deltoid alone, located three finger widths below the acromion process of the arm
preguntas.explicacion: The subcutaneous sites are the outer lateral aspect of the upper arm, the abdomen from below the costal margin to the iliac crest and more than two inches away from the umbilicus, the front of the upper thighs, the upper back and the upper ventral gluteal area. They are broad enough to allow rotation within the same site. Skin that is bruised, open, scarred or over a bony prominence is avoided, as is any area with poor blood flow.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks what a health savings account can be used for. Which answer is correct?
opciones: Untaxed dollars for qualified medical expenses, but generally not for premiums
Untaxed dollars for premiums, but generally not for deductibles or copayments
Employer dollars that are lost in full if they are not spent by the plan year end
Plan dollars that pay the provider directly once the out-of-pocket limit is reached
preguntas.explicacion: A health savings account lets a person set money aside before taxes and spend it on qualified medical costs such as deductibles, copayments and coinsurance; the funds generally may not go toward premiums, and only someone with an HSA-eligible plan may contribute. The use-it-or-lose-it design with an employer-set limit describes a flexible spending arrangement instead, and no savings account pays providers on the plan's behalf.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient's coagulation panel keeps coming back haemolysed. Which two features of the draw are singled out to protect it?
opciones: An atraumatic venipuncture and as little tourniquet time as possible
A large tube volume and as long a tourniquet time as the vein allows
A fasting patient and a puncture placed over the basilic vein instead
A second discard tube and a needle finer than twenty-three gauge
preguntas.explicacion: For coagulation work the puncture should be atraumatic and made without delay, and the tourniquet should stay on as briefly as possible, because both faults produce artifacts such as haemolysis. The gauge suggested runs from nineteen to twenty-two, with the wider end preferred for factor assays.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient's radial pulse is full on the right and barely detectable on the left. Why does the difference between sides matter by itself?
opciones: An uneven pulse can mark major vascular disease such as an aortic dissection
An uneven pulse is a normal variant found in roughly a tenth of all people
An uneven pulse only reflects which arm the patient uses for daily work
An uneven pulse appears whenever the rhythm is irregularly irregular
preguntas.explicacion: A full pulse assessment covers rate, rhythm, volume, amplitude, rate of rise and symmetry between the two sides. Symmetry earns its place because an uneven pulse may point to aortic dissection, large-vessel occlusive disease or coarctation of the aorta. That is why both sides are compared rather than one side measured and charted.

preguntas.pregunta: Does holding a professional licence mean a person may provide any service in that field?
opciones: No: each state's law and the licensing body set what the licence permits
Yes, as long as the employer's job description includes that service
Yes, once the institution has finished credentialing that professional
No: only the institution's privileges list decides, and state law does not
preguntas.explicacion: Every state has its own laws on medical practice, and simply holding a licence does not mean the holder may deliver whatever service they want: an advanced practice nurse cannot start prescribing on that basis alone, and a family physician cannot start inserting central lines. Credentialing checks the qualifications; privileging then authorizes a specific set of services after evaluating credentials and performance.

preguntas.pregunta: Where can a patient file a complaint about a violation of their health information privacy rights?
opciones: With the HHS Office for Civil Rights
With the state insurance oversight agency
With the hospital's patient advocate only
With the long-term care ombudsman office
preguntas.explicacion: The Office for Civil Rights of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services receives complaints from people who believe their health information privacy rights were violated or who were discriminated against in their medical care; it investigates, audits and may refer criminal matters to the Department of Justice. Patient advocates, state health departments, insurance oversight agencies and long-term care ombudsman offices help with other kinds of problems. A covered entity must also have its own complaint process and may not retaliate against anyone who files.

preguntas.pregunta: A receptionist with no clinical role suspects a child in the waiting room is being abused. May she report it?
opciones: Yes: every jurisdiction permits any person to report a suspicion
Yes, but only in the 17 states where all persons must report
No: reports from staff outside clinical roles are not accepted
No: the report has to come from the child's treating clinician
preguntas.explicacion: In all states, territories and the District of Columbia any person is permitted to report when they have reason to believe a child has been abused or neglected; those voluntary reporters are called permissive reporters. preguntas.pregunta: A 62-year-old patient with permanent kidney failure asks whether she can have Medicare. Who is the program for?
opciones: People age 65 or older, and some under 65 with a disability or kidney failure
People with low income, under the rules that each state writes for itself
Children in families that earn too much to qualify for the state plan
Workers whose employer purchases the coverage as a benefit of the job
preguntas.explicacion: Medicare is the government's health insurance program for people age 65 or older. Some people under 65 qualify as well: those with disabilities, permanent kidney failure or amyotrophic lateral sclerosis. It helps with the cost of care without covering every medical expense, and it has four parts: A for hospital insurance, B for medical services, C for Advantage plans and D for prescription drugs.

preguntas.pregunta: An electrode will not stay on a patient with a very hairy chest. What is the recommended fix?
opciones: Part the hair before applying it, and tape it down if needed
Shave the whole chest and apply a second electrode on top
Move the electrode one space lower where there is less hair
Use extra gel so that the electrode floats above the hair
preguntas.explicacion: Parting the hair first gives the adhesive a surface to grip, and on extremely hairy chests the electrodes may have to be taped down. Moving an electrode off its landmark is never the answer: even a small displacement of a chest electrode can change the pattern considerably.

preguntas.pregunta: How is the stream of water directed during an ear irrigation?
opciones: Superiorly and posteriorly in the canal, at low pressure, toward the eardrum
Inferiorly and anteriorly in the canal, at low pressure, away from the eardrum
Superiorly and posteriorly in the canal, at high pressure, to break the plug up
Straight along the axis of the canal, at high pressure, until the plug floats out
preguntas.explicacion: The catheter points up and back so the stream runs behind the wax and lifts it off the tympanic membrane, and it is aimed at the membrane rather than into the canal wall. Low pressure is what keeps it safe: force causes trauma, bleeding and pain. Lacerations, perforation and ossicular injury are the complications, rare as they are.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks whether the swollen bruise on the arm can be drained with a needle at home. What is the advice?
opciones: Do not drain it, and rest the bruised part rather than using it
Drain it only with a sterile lancet after cleaning the skin first
Drain it once the colour has turned bluish, but not before that
Do not drain it, but keep exercising the arm to disperse the blood
preguntas.explicacion: The instructions are explicit: a bruise is not drained with a needle, the painful part is rested rather than worked, and pain and swelling are not ignored. preguntas.pregunta: What backup arrangement does the contingency guidance describe for patient data?
opciones: A daily, complete, encrypted copy held off site and restored as a test regularly
A weekly complete copy kept on a second drive inside the same server cabinet
A monthly copy of the day's new entries stored with the software developer
A copy made each time the system is upgraded and kept until the next upgrade
preguntas.explicacion: The recommended arrangement is a daily off-site complete encrypted backup, with the most critical data copied as close to real time as possible. Restoring the whole system and the patient data is tested regularly, optimally monthly, and the media are kept physically apart from the working data, ideally air-gapped so that ransomware cannot reach them.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with cognitive impairment hears you but does not understand the instruction. What should you do?
opciones: Rephrase the statement, without speaking any faster or louder
Repeat it word for word until it finally registers with him
Speak much louder, since hearing is usually the underlying problem
Ask the caregiver to answer so the visit stays on schedule
preguntas.explicacion: When the patient can hear but does not understand, the clinician should try rephrasing rather than repeating, and should not speak too quickly or too loudly. preguntas.pregunta: A wrong medication is caught by the pharmacist before it reaches the patient. What is that called, and what should follow?
opciones: A near miss, and it deserves the same scrutiny as an event that caused harm
A near miss, and no report is needed at all because the patient was not harmed
An adverse event, and the patient must be told before the shift is over
A sentinel event, and the accrediting body must be notified immediately
preguntas.explicacion: A near miss is an error that could have harmed the patient but did not, because someone intervened or because of chance. It is identical to an adverse event except for the outcome, which is exactly why it should get the same scrutiny: it shows the weakness without the cost. An adverse event means the patient was actually injured.

preguntas.pregunta: Which habit is recommended to workers so that a used needle never becomes a hazard in the room?
opciones: Plan how the needle will be handled and discarded before the procedure starts
Recap the needle with one hand until a container can be brought to the room
Set the used needle on the tray until the tubes have been labeled correctly
Carry the needle to the container at the end of the round of draws
preguntas.explicacion: The advice to workers is a short list: avoid needles where a safe alternative exists, help evaluate and then use the safety devices provided, avoid recapping, plan safe handling and disposal before beginning any procedure with needles, dispose of them promptly in the proper container, report every injury promptly, point out hazards, and take part in training and hepatitis B vaccination. Leaving a used sharp on a tray or carrying it around are exactly the delays this list is meant to remove.

preguntas.pregunta: A combined nasal and throat swab is being collected for influenza. Which area does the throat swab deliberately miss?
opciones: The tongue, while the posterior pharynx and the tonsillar areas are swabbed
The tonsillar areas, while the posterior pharynx and the tongue are both swabbed
The posterior pharynx, while the tonsillar areas and the tongue are swabbed
The soft palate, while the posterior pharynx and the tongue are swabbed
preguntas.explicacion: For the throat half of a combined specimen, a second dry polyester swab goes into the mouth and collects from the posterior pharynx and the tonsillar areas, and the instruction is to avoid the tongue. preguntas.pregunta: A patient with diabetes becomes shaky, sweaty and confused while waiting, but can swallow and follow directions. What is offered?
opciones: Juice, a sugary drink or glucose tablets, and then the provider is told
An injection of glucagon into the muscle of the outer part of the thigh
A glass of water and a rest in a cool room until the shaking settles
No food or drink, because the glucose must be measured in the lab first
preguntas.explicacion: A patient who is awake and able to swallow is given fast sugar: juice or another sugary drink, food, or glucose tablets. Glucagon, a medicine that raises blood sugar, is the route when the patient cannot take sugar by mouth. If the signs do not improve after a snack with sugar, the patient goes to the emergency room and does not drive.

preguntas.pregunta: An older patient with hearing loss keeps asking you to repeat the fasting question. What should you do?
opciones: Face her at eye level and speak clearly in a normal tone, with less noise
Raise your voice and use a higher pitch so that the words carry across the room
Turn to the computer and type the questions for her in a large font

Sit the patient up against a wall and watch the pupils for any change
Shake the patient gently by the shoulder until some response is obtained

preguntas.pregunta: At what angle does the WHO guideline say the needle should enter the vein?

At 30 degrees or more, steepening the angle as the needle advances along the vein
At 90 degrees, straight down, as when piercing a tube stopper directly from above
At 30 degrees or less, with the thumb anchoring the vein just ABOVE the puncture site
preguntas.explicacion: Step 6 says to enter the vein swiftly at an angle of 30 degrees or less and then keep advancing the needle along the vein at whatever angle gives the easiest entry: the angle does not steepen. preguntas.pregunta: A 5-month-old infant who weighs 6 kg needs a capillary blood sample. Where is the lancet placed?

On the side of the middle or ring finger, across the print
On the posterior curve of the heel, where the tissue is deepest
On the great toe, which has more tissue over bone than the heel
preguntas.explicacion: The capillary site is chosen by age and weight: heel-prick from birth to about 6 months and roughly 3 to 10 kg, finger-prick over 6 months and above 10 kg. On the heel the lancet goes on the medial or lateral plantar surface. In a 3 kg baby the skin-to-bone distance is 3.32 mm there, only 2.33 mm at the posterior heel, which is to be avoided, and 2.19 mm at the toe.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient's veins are small and hard to see. Which measures can improve the chance of success before the puncture?

Applying an ice pack for up to 15 minutes each hour so the vein wall becomes firmer
Keeping the tourniquet in place for two to three minutes so the veins fill completely
Asking the patient to fast for 12 hours and avoid alcohol for 24 hours before the draw
preguntas.explicacion: Measures that help include ballotting or tapping the skin over the vein, followed by antiseptic preparation, and applying a warm compress or soaking the limb briefly in warm water, along with good positioning and lighting. The urine should have been carried to the laboratory after each void instead of being pooled at home
The container should have been kept at body temperature and delivered within 30 minutes of the last void

preguntas.pregunta: After deciding an impermissible disclosure was not a breach, what does the practice have to be able to show?

A signed statement from the patient agreeing that no harm was done
A letter from the Office for Civil Rights closing the matter without action
A note in the chart of every patient the practice treated on the same day

preguntas.pregunta: Pulse intensity is graded from 0 to 4+. What does a grade of 3+ mean?

A barely detectable pulse, felt only after the fingers press for several beats
A bounding pulse, clearly stronger than expected for that site and patient
A slightly diminished pulse, present but weaker than the other side of the body
preguntas.explicacion: The scale runs 0 for nothing palpable, 1+ barely detectable, 2+ slightly diminished, 3+ normal and easily felt, and 4+ bounding. preguntas.pregunta: A patient denies any latex allergy but says bananas and avocados make her mouth itch. How should that be handled?

Fruit allergies are unrelated to latex; proceed with the standard latex gloves
Only a chestnut allergy is linked with latex, so no precaution is needed here

preguntas.explicacion: Some people with latex allergy also react to foods whose proteins resemble those in latex, the latex-fruit syndrome; bananas, avocado and chestnuts are the most strongly linked, with kiwi, peaches, nectarines, celery and melons less so, and the association runs in both directions. Less than 30 seconds, the time needed to reposition the head
Up to 2 minutes, the interval at which compressors are rotated
Up to 1 minute, while the mouth is checked for a foreign object
preguntas.explicacion: Pauses in compressions are held under 10 seconds, because interruptions cost circulation and continuous CPR improves survival. Usually after 24 hours, and baths are preferred because the warm water loosens the tape
Usually after 7 days, and showers are preferred because soaking can reopen the wound
Usually after 72 hours, and either is fine as long as the dressing is left on throughout
preguntas.explicacion: The surgeon says when, but showering is usually fine after about a day. Showers beat baths because the wound is not left soaking, and soaking could reopen it or let it become infected. preguntas.pregunta: An ESR tube is filled only two thirds of the way. What effect does the short fill have on the reading?

Air bubbles are introduced and the measured value comes out lower
The citrate is diluted and the red cells stop stacking altogether
The plasma layer disappears and no reading at all can be taken

preguntas.pregunta: A patient's oral temperature is 36.4 °C at 7 am and 37.1 °C at 5 pm on the same day. What accounts for the difference?
opciones: Normal daily variation: the value is lowest early in the morning and peaks late in the afternoon
A change of site: an axillary reading runs about one full degree above an oral one in the same patient
The second half of the menstrual cycle, which lowers the recorded value by about one degree
An early low-grade fever, which is graded from a reading of 37.3 °C upward at any hour
preguntas.explicacion: Body temperature swings by roughly half a degree Celsius over 24 hours: lowest in the early morning, highest late in the day. Both readings sit inside the 36.5 to 37.5 °C band, so neither is a fever. Low-grade fever starts at 37.3 °C, the axilla reads lower than the mouth, and the luteal phase raises the value, it does not lower it.

preguntas.pregunta: A laboratory validating its own storage limits asks how long nasopharyngeal swabs in viral transport medium have been shown to hold up at room temperature.

As long as three days for one coronavirus target, and no longer for any other
As long as three weeks for every respiratory virus target that was studied
As long as twelve hours, which is the limit quoted for a dry swab instead

preguntas.pregunta: In a resting adult, what are the end diastolic volume of a ventricle and the stroke volume?
opciones: EDV about 130 mL; stroke volume 70 to 80 mL
EDV about 70 to 80 mL; stroke volume 130 mL
EDV about 130 mL; stroke volume 50 to 60 mL
EDV about 5 liters; stroke volume 130 mL
preguntas.explicacion: Just before ventricular contraction a resting adult's ventricle holds about 130 mL, the end diastolic volume or preload; each ventricle then ejects 70 to 80 mL, the stroke volume, leaving 50 to 60 mL behind as the end systolic volume. Both ventricles pump the same amount. Five liters is roughly what the heart moves in a minute, not what one ventricle holds.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient scheduled for fasting blood work asks the phlebotomist whether to skip the morning blood-pressure pill. What is the right guidance?
opciones: Take usual medicines unless the provider said to stop, and tell the provider of every medicine, vitamin and supplement
Skip all medicines on the morning of a fasting test, since swallowing any pill counts as breaking the fast
Take prescription medicines but stop vitamins and supplements, which are the only products that alter results
Take the pill only if it can be swallowed without water, because liquids are not allowed during the fast
preguntas.explicacion: Patients are told to ask their provider whether their usual prescription and over-the-counter medicines may be taken, and never to stop a medicine unless the provider says so; for some tests the provider will ask them to hold a drug, and the phlebotomist does not make that call. Vitamins and supplements are reported too, because some medicines raise or lower blood glucose and can change a result drawn too soon after a dose. Plain water is allowed throughout the fast.

preguntas.pregunta: For an infection to be classified as healthcare-associated (nosocomial), which condition must be met?
opciones: The patient was admitted for a reason other than that infection
The infection was acquired from a healthcare worker rather than from equipment
The infection appeared within 24 hours of admission to the facility
The infection is caused by a multidrug-resistant organism
preguntas.explicacion: Healthcare-associated infections are infections acquired in health-care facilities, and the defining condition is that the patient was admitted for some reason other than the infection. They are often linked to surgery or invasive procedures that give pathogens a portal of entry, and to contaminated equipment such as catheters and ventilators; in 2011 more than 720,000 occurred in U.S. hospitals, with surgical sites and pneumonia each about 22 percent. The source may be equipment, staff or the environment, the organism need not be resistant, and there is no 24-hour cutoff in the definition.

Reusing the tube holder risks a haemolysed specimen in the next tube
Filling several tubes risks losing the vacuum in the last of them
Filling several tubes risks carrying additive back into the syringe
preguntas.explicacion: Among the drawbacks listed for vacuum systems is that reuse of the needle holder creates a needle-stick risk during disassembly, which happens once the blood is already drawn. preguntas.pregunta: Blood soaks through the gauze being held on a bleeding wound. What should be done?
opciones: Lay another cloth over the first one and keep up the pressure
Lift the gauze to look at the wound and then press again harder
Replace the soaked gauze with dry gauze and press on the artery
Loosen the pressure for a moment so that a clot can start to form
preguntas.explicacion: A soaked dressing is not taken off: another one is placed on top and pressure continues until bleeding stops, and then the dressing is wrapped firmly in place. Peeking disturbs the wound and makes control harder. Bleeding that keeps seeping through calls for medical attention right away.

preguntas.pregunta: Which category of information is expressly excluded from the individual's right of access?
opciones: Psychotherapy notes kept separate from the rest of the patient's medical record
Laboratory results, which the patient obtains from the testing laboratory instead
Billing and payment records, which belong to the revenue cycle rather than the chart
Medical images such as X-rays, because they are not readily producible on paper
preguntas.explicacion: Two categories are excluded outright: psychotherapy notes, meaning a mental health provider's personal notes on a counseling session kept apart from the record, and information compiled in anticipation of or for use in a legal proceeding. The right of access is otherwise broad and expressly reaches billing and payment records, insurance information, laboratory results and medical images such as X-rays.

preguntas.pregunta: A barcode scanner at the accessioning desk misreads a patient identification label. What did the emergency laboratory identify as the cause of such misreads?
opciones: Incompatibility between the barcode print area size or symbology on the wristband or label and the scanner settings
Barcodes printed more than 30 minutes before collection, which fade beyond the reading threshold of the scanner
Labels printed with more than two identifiers, which overload the nine-digit internal code the scanner expects
Heat from the centrifuge, which distorts the code 39 bars so that the digits no longer match the record
preguntas.explicacion: Barcoding is recommended as an evidence-based best practice because it reduces identification errors in specimens and testing, yet the laboratory observed that scanners occasionally misread patient identification barcodes when the print area size or the symbology on the wristband or specimen label did not match the scanner settings. Its internal nine-digit code 39 barcode carries name, sex, age, tube and sample type, print and collection times, collection site, the tests, the ordering doctor and the phlebotomist.

preguntas.pregunta: The practice hires an outside company to process its claims. Under the Privacy Rule, what is that company?
opciones: A business associate, because it performs a function for the practice that uses patient information
A member of the practice workforce, because it handles the same records the front desk handles
A health care clearinghouse, because any outside company that touches claims fits that definition
An ordinary supplier outside the rule, since only entities that treat patients are regulated
preguntas.explicacion: A business associate is a person or organization outside the workforce that carries out functions or provides services for a covered entity involving the use or disclosure of individually identifiable health information. Claims processing, data analysis, utilization review and billing are named as such functions. Someone whose work never touches PHI is not a business associate.

preguntas.pregunta: Which two documents are the predominant health care advance directives?
opciones: The living will and the durable power of attorney for health care
The living will and the hospital's own general consent-to-treat form
The DNR order and the hospital's notice of privacy practices
The DNI order and the surrogate list written into state law
preguntas.explicacion: Several kinds of advance directive overlap, but the two that dominate are the living will, where the person writes down which treatments they want and which they refuse, and the durable power of attorney for health care, which names someone to speak for them. A DNR is a clinician's order, not a directive the patient writes, and the state surrogate list only operates when nobody was named.

preguntas.pregunta: An assistant has a lot of ground to cover with a patient. When should teach-back be used during the visit?
opciones: In chunks through the visit, checking each segment before the next
Once at the very end, so the whole plan can be repeated together
Once at the start, to find out what the patient already knows
Only when the patient looks confused during the explanation
preguntas.explicacion: The habit is called chunk and check: information is broken into small segments and each one is taught back before the next is started, rather than saving it all for the end. Used consistently it becomes routine and does not make the visit longer.

preguntas.pregunta: A used needle really has to come off its syringe. How is the one-hand scoop performed?
opciones: Leave the cap on a surface, guide the tip in with one hand, then secure it
Hold the cap in one hand and push the needle into it with the other hand
Pinch the cap between two fingers and twist the syringe until it is covered
Hold the cap with forceps and press the needle down onto a firm surface
preguntas.explicacion: The cap is left resting on a surface, or set against a firm upright surface with its opening facing the worker, and the used tip is guided into it with one hand only. The needle and syringe are then lifted vertically and the other hand fixes the cap once the tip is covered.

preguntas.pregunta: A 47-year-old with no risk factors asks whether colorectal screening applies to him yet. What is the recommendation?
opciones: Yes; screening is recommended from age 45, and carries an A grade from 50 to 75
No; screening is recommended only from age 50, and runs through age 75
Yes; screening is recommended from age 40, and carries an A grade from 45 to 75
No; screening starts at 45 only for adults who have a family history
preguntas.explicacion: Colorectal cancer screening is recommended for adults from 45 to 49 with a B grade and for all adults from 50 through 75 with an A grade, so a 47-year-old is inside the window. Grade B means the recommendation rests on somewhat less certainty of benefit than grade A, not that it is optional.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient's job ended last month and he kept his employer coverage under COBRA. What changed for him?
opciones: He now pays the full premium, including the employer's old share, plus a small fee
He now pays the same share of the premium he paid while he was still employed
He now pays no premium, and the plan bills the former employer for the coverage
He now pays a premium set by the Marketplace, based on his household income
preguntas.explicacion: COBRA is the federal law that lets a person keep employer coverage for a time after the job ends, after losing dependent status, or after another qualifying event. Whoever elects it pays 100% of the premium, the portion the employer used to cover included, plus a small administrative charge. Nothing shifts the cost back to the employer, and income-based premiums belong to Marketplace coverage instead.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient on omeprazole and a recent course of antibiotics is booked for a urea breath test. What has to happen first?
opciones: Stop antibiotics and bismuth for at least 4 weeks and the proton pump inhibitor for at least 2 weeks
Stop antibiotics and bismuth for at least 2 weeks and the proton pump inhibitor for at least 4 full weeks
Stop antibiotics and bismuth for at least 4 days and the proton pump inhibitor for at least 2 days
Only the antibiotic has to stop, for 4 weeks; acid suppressants do not interfere
preguntas.explicacion: Antibiotics and bismuth compounds are stopped at least 4 weeks ahead, and proton pump inhibitors and sucralfate at least 2 weeks ahead, because all of them suppress the urease activity the test measures and produce a false negative. Histamine-2 blockers are ideally held 24 to 48 hours beforehand. Plain antacids are allowed and do not interfere.

preguntas.pregunta: An adult arrives with fast, shallow breathing and no history of anxiety. How is this handled?
opciones: It is treated as an emergency rather than something to be managed at home
It is observed at home for 24 hours, since the pattern often settles on its own
It is managed with an inhaler alone, which settles the breathing once the dose is taken
It is recorded as hyperventilation, which is the term for fast and shallow breathing
preguntas.explicacion: Rapid shallow breathing is generally handled as a medical emergency unless anxiety is the only cause: asthma, a clot in the lung, pneumonia, heart failure and chronic lung disease all present this way. Hyperventilation is the term for breathing that is rapid and deep, which is why the depth is charted along with the rate.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient trying to lose weight asks why fat is watched so closely when some fat is necessary. What is true of dietary fat?
opciones: Gram for gram it carries twice the calories of protein or carbohydrate
Gram for gram it carries half the calories of protein or carbohydrate
Gram for gram it carries the same calories as protein or carbohydrate
Gram for gram it carries twice the calories that alcohol carries
preguntas.explicacion: Some fat belongs in the diet: it supplies energy, it helps the body absorb certain vitamins, and it shapes cholesterol levels. What makes it easy to overdo is density, since fat holds twice the calories that protein or carbohydrate holds for the same weight, so extra fat puts on weight quickly.

preguntas.pregunta: After cleaning the site, a phlebotomist palpates the vein once more with a gloved finger to confirm its position. What does the WHO require now?
opciones: Repeat the disinfection, because the cleaned site was touched
Proceed at once, since the glove was clean and the alcohol has dried
Wipe the fingerprint with dry gauze and proceed without delay
Apply povidone iodine over the alcohol before inserting the needle
preguntas.explicacion: Step 5 says not to touch the cleaned site and, in particular, not to place a finger over the vein to guide the exposed needle; if the site is touched, the disinfection is repeated. A clean glove does not change the rule. The same step prefers alcohol to povidone iodine, which can falsely raise potassium, phosphorus or uric acid results.

preguntas.pregunta: How is a GHS hazard pictogram drawn on a shipped chemical label?
opciones: A black symbol on a white background inside a red square frame set on a point
A black symbol on a fluorescent orange background with the legend BIOHAZARD
A red symbol on a white background inside a black diamond used for transport
A black symbol inside a red square frame that may be left empty as a design element
preguntas.explicacion: Pictograms on shipped containers consist of a red square frame set on a point with a black hazard symbol on a white background, wide enough to be clearly visible. An empty red frame with no symbol is not a pictogram and is not permitted on the label. The fluorescent orange label with the BIOHAZARD legend belongs to the bloodborne pathogens standard, and the diamond-shaped transport labels are required by the Department of Transportation for shipping, which the OSHA pictograms do not replace.

preguntas.pregunta: A new phlebotomist shakes a filled citrate tube hard to be sure the blood mixes. What is the consequence?
opciones: Frothing or hemolysis that makes the coagulation results inaccurate
Small clots in the tube, the result the review links to under-mixing
A rise in the citrate-to-blood ratio, as happens with a short draw
Loss of the vacuum, so the next tube in the sequence will not fill
preguntas.explicacion: Both the coagulopathies review and the prothrombin time chapter say the citrate tube is inverted gently and never shaken, because vigorous agitation causes frothing or hemolysis and the coagulation results become unreliable. Small clots are the opposite problem, inefficient mixing, in the tube collection review; the citrate ratio changes with underfilling, not with shaking.

preguntas.pregunta: A lab coat is soaked with blood after a difficult draw. How do the standard's laundry rules apply?
opciones: Bag it where it was used, without sorting or rinsing, in a container that prevents soak-through
Rinse it in the nearest sink first, then bag it, so the laundry service is not exposed
Take it home to wash separately, since the employer is not responsible for laundering
Sort it with other soiled coats at the laundry, where staff wear gloves and gowns
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(4)(iv)(A) requires contaminated laundry to be handled as little as possible and with minimal agitation, bagged or containerized at the location of use, and never sorted or rinsed there; when it is wet enough to soak through, the bag or container must prevent leakage to the outside. The employer, not the employee, cleans and launders required PPE at no cost under (d)(3)(iv), so taking the coat home is not an option, and the gloves worn by laundry staff under (d)(4)(iv)(B) do not permit sorting at the point of use.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient writes that she is leaving the practice for a clinician nearer her home. Does the office owe her a termination notice?
opciones: No, though a letter confirming her decision is wise and cuts the risk of a later claim
Yes, and the same thirty days of care and medication refills still have to be offered
Yes, and it has to travel by certified mail with a return receipt like any other notice
No, and no letter should go out either, since the record closes with her last visit
preguntas.explicacion: Where the patient is the one who has ended the relationship, the physician is not required to send a termination notice. Sending a letter that confirms her choice in writing is still the wise course, because it removes the ambiguity and reduces the risk of legal liability. The thirty days and the certified mail belong to a termination the practice itself initiates.

preguntas.pregunta: Which two arteries are normally used to palpate a pulse?
opciones: The radial artery at the wrist and the common carotid in the neck
The brachial artery in the upper arm and the femoral in the thigh
The median cubital vein at the elbow and the cephalic along the arm
The dorsalis pedis on the foot and the popliteal behind the knee
preguntas.explicacion: The pulse, the expansion and recoil of an artery, is normally palpated at the radial artery in the wrist or the common carotid artery in the neck, although any superficial artery will do; the temporal, facial, brachial, femoral, popliteal, posterior tibial and dorsalis pedis arteries are other sites. The median cubital and cephalic are veins, and the pulse is a property of arteries.

preguntas.pregunta: An older patient is being taught how to make the home safer after a near fall. Which change is advised?
opciones: Take up the loose throw rugs and secure any cords crossing the walking routes
Keep a low stepladder in the kitchen so high shelves stay within easy reach
Choose smooth leather soles, which slide less on carpet than rubber ones do
Move the bedroom upstairs so that the daily climb builds strength in the legs
preguntas.explicacion: Tripping hazards come out first: loose rugs, trailing cords, uneven flooring in doorways. Light the path from the bedroom to the bathroom, put rails by the tub and toilet and a non-slip mat inside. Shoes should be low-heeled with rubber soles, not leather. Standing on chairs or stepladders is out, and daily life is arranged to avoid stairs altogether.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Patient Instructions: Preventing falls — Home Setup

preguntas.pregunta: Life-sustaining treatment is given to a patient whose living will refused it. What claim may follow, and what defeats it?
opciones: Medical battery; the claim fails if the provider did not know of the living will
Medical battery; the claim fails only if a relative asked for the treatment
Negligence; the claim fails if the treatment turned out to help the patient
Breach of contract; the claim fails if the document was signed years earlier
preguntas.explicacion: A living will is an advance directive listing what the person wants if they can no longer give informed consent or refusal, commonly which life-sustaining measures may be used when there is no reasonable expectation of recovery. Administering life-sustaining treatment against it can expose the provider to a medical battery suit, but a provider unaware of the living will will not lose such a claim.

preguntas.pregunta: How should the lancet be oriented on the fingertip in a capillary puncture?
opciones: On the side of the ball of the finger, perpendicular to the fingerprint lines
On the centre of the fingertip pad, parallel to the fingerprint lines
On the side of the ball of the finger, parallel to the fingerprint lines
Over the tip of the finger next to the nail, perpendicular to the nail bed
preguntas.explicacion: The finger-prick goes on the side of the ball of the finger, perpendicular to the lines of the fingerprint. Heel-pricks go to the medial or lateral plantar surface. The puncture should be made with one quick, continuous and deliberate stroke so that flow is good and the puncture does not have to be repeated.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks for a change in how the office usually does things so that she can be seen. What is the limit on that duty?
opciones: The change is made unless it would fundamentally alter the nature of the service
The change is made unless another patient objects to the way it affects his visit
The change is made unless it costs the practice more than a routine visit is paid
The change is made unless the practice has already made one for her this year
preguntas.explicacion: Providers owe full and equal access, and with it reasonable modifications to policies, practices and procedures whenever they are needed to make the service fully available to a person with a disability. preguntas.pregunta: Where does the heart sit in the body?
opciones: In the mediastinum between the lungs, with the apex pointing to the left
In the mediastinum, with two thirds of its mass to the right of the midline
In the left pleural cavity behind the sternum, with the apex pointing right
In the pericardial cavity below the diaphragm, at the level of the third rib
preguntas.explicacion: The heart lies in the thoracic cavity, medially between the lungs in the mediastinum, inside its own pericardial sac; the base is at the level of the third costal cartilage and the apex lies just left of the sternum between the fourth and fifth ribs, with about two thirds of the mass to the left of the midline. That position matters when placing a stethoscope on the chest.

preguntas.pregunta: The superficial veins on the back of the hand arise from which structure, and where do they drain?
opciones: From the dorsal venous arch, into the cephalic and basilic veins
From the dorsal venous arch, into the radial and ulnar deep veins
From the deep palmar arch, into the cephalic and basilic veins
From the median cubital vein, into the dorsal venous arch below it
preguntas.explicacion: On the dorsum of the hand the superficial veins spring from the dorsal venous arch, which empties into the cephalic and the basilic veins, the two main superficial channels of the limb. The name of the insurance plan covering the visit
The colour of the identification bracelet in use
The number of the room where the draw took place

preguntas.pregunta: When must a provider with a direct treatment relationship give a new patient its notice of privacy practices?
opciones: No later than the first service delivery, with a good-faith effort to obtain acknowledgment
Within 60 days of the first visit, by mail to the patient's home address
Only when the patient asks for it, since posting the notice in the office is sufficient by itself
At the first visit, and the patient must sign it before any care may be provided
preguntas.explicacion: Section 164.520(c)(2) requires a covered provider with a direct treatment relationship to give the notice no later than the date of first service delivery, electronic service included, or as soon as practicable after an emergency; to make a good-faith effort to obtain a written acknowledgment of receipt and, if it fails, to document the attempt and the reason; and to have the notice available on site and posted prominently. The acknowledgment is sought, not made a condition of care. Sixty days is the window for a health plan without a website to distribute a materially revised notice.

preguntas.pregunta: Surgical caps or hoods and shoe covers are required by the standard in which situation?
opciones: When gross contamination can reasonably be anticipated, as in autopsies
When performing any vascular access procedure on an uncooperative patient
When splashes to the eyes, nose or mouth can reasonably be anticipated
When entering the room of a patient placed on Contact Precautions
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(3)(xii) reserves caps, hoods, shoe covers and boots for situations where gross contamination is reasonably anticipated, and gives autopsies and orthopaedic surgery as the examples. An uncooperative patient is the example the standard uses in (d)(3)(ix)(D)(4)(ii) for when a blood donation center must require gloves; splashes to the face trigger masks and eye protection under (d)(3)(x); and Contact Precautions call for gown and gloves under the CDC recommendations, not for head or shoe covering.

It ensures the tubes that need a full draw are filled while the tourniquet is still on
It gives the serum tubes 10 to 15 minutes to clot before the last tube is filled
It minimizes platelet clumping, which is the reason given for the capillary sequence
preguntas.explicacion: Step 8 states the purpose in one line: draw the tubes in the correct order to avoid cross-contamination of additives from one tube to the next. Hemolysed specimens, followed by clotted ones
Misidentified specimens, followed by lipemic ones
Improper containers, followed by delayed transport

It is below the 20 % benchmark set by the ASCP for samples drawn during intravenous placement
It is unusually high, since emergency departments typically report hemolysis in fewer than 3 % of samples
It matches the 13 to 14 % rate expected for any sample sent through a pneumatic tube system
preguntas.explicacion: Emergency department blood samples carry a hemolysis rate of 6 to 30 %, much higher than the 2 % benchmark of the American Society for Clinical Pathology; in the pneumatic tube study the ED rate was about 13.5 % against roughly 3 % elsewhere in the hospital, a difference the authors tie to drawing blood during IV placement rather than by straight stick. preguntas.pregunta: When preparing a lancing device for a fingerstick glucose test, what depth setting is advised?
opciones: No more than 2.0 mm, to minimize the risk of bone injury
No more than 3.0 mm, to minimize the risk of bone injury
At least 2.4 mm, to guarantee a drop large enough for the strip
The deepest setting on the first finger, then shallower on repeats
preguntas.explicacion: For a capillary glucose test the lancing device depth is set to no more than 2.0 mm to minimize the risk of bone injury; newer lancing devices cause less pain than older systems. One where the spacing changes in a repeating pattern
One where the spacing is even but the rate is above 100
One where the spacing is even but the QRS is over 120 ms

For 3 years from the date of the last entry
For 6 years from the date of the last entry
For the duration of employment plus 5 years

Reinstatement is automatic on the day the stated period of exclusion runs out
Reinstatement follows as soon as a state Medicaid agency enrols her once more
Reinstatement follows as soon as a practice checks the list and cannot find her

preguntas.pregunta: A CBC drawn in EDTA reports a very low platelet count, but the smear shows the platelets stuck together in clumps. What is this called, and what causes it?
opciones: Pseudothrombocytopenia, from in vitro platelet clumping caused by EDTA-dependent agglutinins
True thrombocytopenia, from platelet destruction that had already begun before the blood was drawn
Hemoconcentration, from a tourniquet left in place for more than one minute
Platelet satellitism, from the sodium fluoride in a grey tube drawn before the EDTA
preguntas.explicacion: Platelet clumping can occur when EDTA is the anticoagulant, producing pseudothrombocytopenia, a falsely low count due to in vitro aggregation from EDTA-dependent agglutinins. It is an artifact of the tube, not a disease of the patient. Platelet satellitism is a different smear finding, and hemoconcentration is the tourniquet effect described in the phlebotomy chapter.

An inclusion term, a list of the conditions for which that one code is used
An Excludes2 note, saying the condition is not included but may be coded too
A code also note, saying that two codes may be needed with no order given
preguntas.explicacion: An Includes note appears immediately under a three-character code title to define the category further or to illustrate its content. Inclusion terms are a different device: they are the list of conditions for which a particular code is used, they may be synonyms of the title, and they are not necessarily exhaustive, since the Index may add more.

preguntas.pregunta: Blood is flowing poorly from a heel-prick in a cold, fussy infant. Which measure improves flow?
opciones: Keep the child warm, swaddled, with only the puncture extremity exposed; warmth can raise flow up to sevenfold
Lower the heel below the level of the heart for two minutes so gravity fills the capillary bed
Squeeze the heel rhythmically at the puncture itself until a steady stream of blood appears
Switch to a 25-gauge butterfly on the dorsal hand, which the WHO prefers when a heel-prick fails
preguntas.explicacion: The child is kept warm by removing as few clothes as possible, swaddling an infant in a blanket and having a caregiver hold the infant with only the sampling extremity exposed; warmth may increase blood flow by as much as sevenfold, with warm cloths on the site. Squeezing causes haemolysis, and 25-gauge or thinner needles are to be avoided.

preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist is worried that tissue fluid from a difficult puncture could contaminate a coagulation specimen. What does the WHO table allow in that situation?
opciones: Collecting a non-additive tube before the light blue citrate tube
Collecting the light blue tube first and then a second one for the test
Collecting a purple EDTA tube before the light blue citrate tube
Collecting the citrate tube last, after all the additive tubes
preguntas.explicacion: Footnote d of Table 2.3 addresses this exact concern: if contamination by tissue fluids or thromboplastins is possible, a tube without additive can be drawn ahead of the additive tube. preguntas.pregunta: A sputum specimen for molecular bacterial testing is too thick to pipette and cannot be run today. Which pair of handling points applies?
opciones: Thin it with acetylcysteine or dithiothreitol; hold it at 4 to 8 °C for up to a week
Thin it with sterile saline; hold it at room temperature for up to a week
Thin it with acetylcysteine or dithiothreitol; freeze it at −20 °C the same day
Thin it with buffered glycerol; hold it at 4 to 8 °C for up to three days
preguntas.explicacion: Sputum is one of the viscous specimen types that jam automated pipetting, and the additives named for it are N-acetyl l-cysteine and dithiothreitol; homogenisation with inert beads in sterile buffer is the physical alternative. For storage the general guideline is 4 to 8 °C for up to seven days, with below −70 °C reserved for keeping it as long as twelve months.

preguntas.pregunta: While palpating for a venipuncture site you feel a vessel that pulses. Which set of features identifies an artery rather than a vein?
opciones: Thick wall, small rounded lumen, high pressure, no valves
Thin wall, large flattened lumen, low pressure, valves in the limbs
Thin wall, large lumen, high pressure, valves present in the limbs
Thick wall, small lumen, low pressure, valves present in the limbs
preguntas.explicacion: Arteries have thick walls, a rounded appearance, high pressure and no valves; veins have thin walls, irregular often collapsed lumens, low pressure and valves, mostly in the limbs and below the heart. The pulse itself is the expansion and recoil of an artery as blood is ejected from the heart, so a pulsing vessel is an artery.

preguntas.pregunta: How does a self-blunting phlebotomy needle protect the person drawing the blood?
opciones: A blunt cannula inside it is pushed past the tip before the needle leaves the vein
A spring pulls the needle back into the tube holder once the vein has been entered
A hinged shield snaps over the tip as the tube is pushed onto the holder
A blunt cap is screwed onto the tip once the needle has left the vein
preguntas.explicacion: In a self-blunting phlebotomy or winged-steel needle, a blunt cannula sits inside the needle and is advanced beyond the needle tip before the needle is withdrawn from the vein, so what comes out of the patient is no longer sharp. Retracting needles and hinged or sliding shields are separate designs on the same list, and each works at a different moment; the blunting one is the only one that acts while the needle is still in the vein.

No, an incident starts only once information has actually been reached or altered
No, unless the attempt is later shown to have exposed unsecured information
Yes, but only where the attempt interferes with how the information system runs
preguntas.explicacion: The definition is deliberately wide: attempted or successful unauthorized access, use, disclosure, modification or destruction of information, and also interference with system operations. opciones: It need not agree to the restriction, but once it agrees it is bound by what it accepted
It must agree to any restriction a patient requests about treatment, payment or operations
It may agree only if the patient pays the visit in full at the time of the appointment
It may not agree, because restrictions would conflict with the notice of privacy practices

preguntas.pregunta: A patient is asked to sign for a procedure while already medicated in the holding area. Why is that criticised?

Consent signed outside a clinic has to be witnessed by a second nurse
Consent is not valid unless the same clinician performs the procedure
Consent in writing takes the place of discussing risks and benefits

preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist has greeted the patient and is about to clean the skin for the puncture. Which moment for hand hygiene is that?

After contact with the patient nearby
After exposure to any body fluid
After leaving the patient's own room

preguntas.pregunta: When is a person falsely imprisoned?
opciones: When they are confined in an area bounded in every direction, without consent
When they are asked to remain in a room until the paperwork has been finished
When they are told they may face a lawsuit if they leave the building early
When they are kept waiting far longer than the appointment time they were given
preguntas.explicacion: False imprisonment is intentionally restraining someone inside a bounded area without their consent or legal authority, and an area counts as bounded only if movement is blocked in every direction; a reasonable and safe way out means it is not. Restraint can come from a locked door, force, failure to release or misuse of authority. A threat of future legal trouble is not enough.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient reports extreme pressure and severe pain in a large bruised area of the forearm. Why does that need urgent care?
