It may be a periosteal bruise, which heals only after several months
It may be thrombophlebitis, which resolves once the arm is elevated
It may be simple swelling, which settles with ice applied every hour
preguntas.explicacion: A feeling of extreme pressure in a bruised part, especially when the area is large or very painful, can mean compartment syndrome, in which rising pressure cuts the blood and oxygen supply to the tissues. Automatic acceptance of borderline samples and a monthly report to the medical director
A separate set of rejection criteria for the night shift and longer storage of rejects

preguntas.pregunta: The plan approved the preauthorization for a scheduled procedure. What has the office actually obtained?
opciones: A decision that the service is medically necessary, with payment still not promised
A decision that the service is medically necessary, and a guarantee it will be paid
A decision that the patient has met the deductible for the plan year in question
A decision that the provider may bill the patient if the plan denies the claim

preguntas.pregunta: A lumbar puncture yields three numbered sterile tubes. Which tube is routinely designated for microbiological culture and sensitivity?
opciones: Tube 2, with tube 1 going to chemistry and serology and tube 3 to cytology
Tube 1, with tube 2 going to chemistry and serology and tube 3 to cytology
Tube 3, with tube 1 going to chemistry and serology and tube 2 to cytology
Tube 1, with tube 2 going to cytology and tube 3 to chemistry and serology
preguntas.explicacion: Cerebrospinal fluid collected under strict asepsis, usually between L3-L4 or L4-L5, is distributed into three sterile tubes: the first for chemistry and serology, the second for culture and sensitivity, and the third for cytological examination. A paper chart opened under the patient's name and filed as a permanent record
A wait until the system returns, since a record cannot be opened without it

preguntas.pregunta: Which container is exempt from the biohazard labeling requirement of the standard?

A refrigerator that stores specimens of blood awaiting testing
A sharps container that is only one-quarter full
A bag of regulated waste that is going to an off-site incinerator
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (g)(1)(i)(F) exempts containers of blood, blood components or blood products that are labeled as to their contents and released for transfusion or other clinical use; (g)(1)(i)(G) also exempts individual containers placed inside a labeled container, and (g)(1)(i)(I) waste that has already been decontaminated. In 2 to 4 hours, the incubation time the plates need before organisms can be identified
In 48 to 72 hours, the incubation time the plates need before any organism can be identified
In about a week, the incubation time the plates need before organisms can be identified

A blood condition involving the cells named by the root
An enlargement of the structure named by the root
An abnormal softening of the tissue named by the root

preguntas.pregunta: A CBC report lists white cells at 7,000 per microliter. How do leukocytes differ from the other formed elements?
opciones: They are complete cells with a nucleus, some 5,000 to 10,000 per µL
They are anucleate biconcave discs, numbering about 5 million per µL
They are cell fragments, numbering 150,000 to 160,000 per µL
They are complete cells that never leave the vessels, unlike erythrocytes
preguntas.explicacion: Leukocytes are the only formed elements that are complete cells, with a nucleus and organelles, and they are far fewer than red cells, typically 5,000 to 10,000 per microliter, so 7,000 is within range. preguntas.pregunta: Which plasma protein is the most abundant and contributes most to the osmotic pressure of blood?
opciones: Albumin, about 54 percent of plasma protein
Fibrinogen, about 7 percent of plasma protein
Gamma globulin, the antibody fraction
Alpha globulin, which carries iron and lipids
preguntas.explicacion: There are three groups of plasma proteins. Albumin, made by the liver, is the largest share at about 54 percent (3.5 to 5.0 g/dL); it binds fatty acids and steroid hormones and is the main protein holding water inside the vessels, which helps keep blood volume and pressure. Globulins are second at about 38 percent, and the gamma fraction is the antibodies. Fibrinogen is about 7 percent and is needed for clotting.

preguntas.pregunta: A biopsy report reads carcinoma in situ. What do those last two words add?
opciones: The abnormal cells are still only where they first formed
The abnormal cells have reached one nearby lymph node only
The abnormal cells have already settled in a second organ
The abnormal cells are not cancer and will not spread at all
preguntas.explicacion: In situ means in its original place, so in a carcinoma in situ the abnormal cells are found only where they first formed and have not spread. About 45 percent
About 7 percent

preguntas.pregunta: A newborn is cyanotic, a 'blue baby'. Which congenital defect is the most common cause of cyanosis after birth?

Patent foramen ovale
Aortic coarctation
Patent ductus arteriosus

preguntas.explicacion: Priority Mail is the everyday parcel service: two to three days, tracking and up to $100 of insurance built into the price, free flat rate packaging and a 70 lb ceiling. Express is faster but is bought for speed, and First-Class carries no tracking of its own.

preguntas.pregunta: A child's phase V cannot be heard at all during a manual reading. What is used for the diastolic value?
opciones: Phase IV, the abrupt muffling, is used when the fifth sound cannot be detected
Phase III, the return of sharper sounds, is used as the nearest available marker
The reading is abandoned, since only the disappearance of sound can be recorded
Zero is recorded, because sound that continues to the end means no diastolic point
preguntas.explicacion: The recommendation in children is the same as in adults, phase V; but where that point cannot be found, phase IV is used instead. The same debate exists in pregnancy, and there too phase V is preferred, with phase IV kept for the patients in whom the fifth phase cannot be determined.

preguntas.pregunta: What do the letters H, I and L stand for in the serum indices that conventional laboratory analyzers measure, and how are the same problems detected at the point of care?
opciones: Hemoglobin, icterus and lipemia; at the point of care only by visual inspection of a centrifuged aliquot
Heparin, infusion and light; at the point of care by a built-in spectrophotometric check on every strip
Hemoglobin, icterus and lipemia; at the point of care by an automatic index reported with each result
Hematocrit, ionic strength and lactate; at the point of care by running a control before each sample
preguntas.explicacion: Conventional laboratories add a step that measures the serum index for hemoglobin (H), icterus (I) and lipemia (L), usually spectrophotometrically, because all three can make results inaccurate or incalculable, potassium being especially vulnerable. Point-of-care devices have no such index, so hemolysis, icterus and lipemia can be recognised there only by looking at a centrifuged aliquot; dilution may fix excess bilirubin and ultracentrifugation excess lipids.

Ask the child to state his own first and last names, then match the form
Read the name off the band tied to the cot rail, then match the form
Ask the nurse who admitted the child, then match her answer to the form

preguntas.pregunta: How are a child's height and weight recorded so that they can be interpreted?

As raw figures alone, since the chart is drawn only when a problem appears
As a percentage of the average value for children of that age and sex
As a single combined score, which the chart converts into an age equivalent

To accept any assignment the employer gives while the shift is under way

Into the muscle, using a longer needle whenever the ordered dose is a large one
Into a vein at home, since regular insulin can also be given by that same route
Under the skin, with a tuberculin syringe marked in milliliters and a long needle
preguntas.explicacion: Insulin is given subcutaneously in almost every case, with a plastic disposable syringe that holds 30, 50 or 100 units and carries a fine needle, as thin as 31 gauge, from about 3/16 of an inch for infants to half an inch or more for adults. preguntas.pregunta: During the HIV follow-up period after an exposure, what does the CDC advise the worker to avoid?
opciones: Donating blood, semen or organs and unprotected sex, mostly in the first 6 to 12 weeks
Patient care duties of any kind until the 6-month antibody test comes back negative
Close contact with household members until the 12-week antibody test is negative
Any other medication, since it would interfere with the antiretroviral regimen
preguntas.explicacion: The CDC brochure asks exposed workers, especially during the first 6 to 12 weeks when most infected persons show signs of infection, to follow HIV prevention recommendations: no donation of blood, semen or organs, no sexual intercourse or consistent condom use, and consideration of not breastfeeding. WHO's annex adds no blood or organ donation for up to 6 months. Neither source restricts patient care or household contact, and the CDC asks workers to tell the treating provider about other medications, not to stop them.

An automatic release of records to any provider who asks, without further authorization

Whether the calibration sticker is still inside its expiry period

preguntas.pregunta: A patient who hurried in and is visibly anxious has a regular strip at 108 with upright P waves in I and II. Which reading fits?
opciones: A sinus rhythm sped up by stress, one of the physiologic triggers
A rhythm from the AV node, since any rate past 100 starts there
An artifact of movement, which doubles the complexes counted
A recording error, since the paper ran at 50 mm per second
preguntas.explicacion: Sinus tachycardia is the same tracing as normal sinus rhythm with a rate above 100, and its physiologic causes are catecholamine-driven: exercise, stress, pain and anxiety. Those cases usually need no cardiac treatment, but the strip still goes to the provider to read.

preguntas.pregunta: How many sections does a GHS-format Safety Data Sheet have, and which of them does OSHA not enforce?
opciones: 16 sections; OSHA does not enforce sections 12 through 15
16 sections; OSHA does not enforce sections 9 through 11 and 16
12 sections; OSHA does not enforce the last two, transport and regulatory
8 sections, one per required pictogram; all are enforced by OSHA
preguntas.explicacion: A safety data sheet under the Hazard Communication standard has 16 numbered sections in a fixed order. Sections 12 through 15, ecological information, disposal, transport and regulatory information, must be present to match the GHS, but OSHA does not enforce their content because other agencies handle those matters. Sections 9 through 11 and 16 hold technical data such as physical properties, reactivity, toxicology and the date of preparation, and they are enforced. Eight is the number of pictograms OSHA requires, not of SDS sections.

preguntas.pregunta: What has to be true for consent to be valid?
opciones: Enough mental capacity, and no coercion, fraud or mistake behind it
A signature on the practice's own form, witnessed by a staff member
A relative present at the time the person agrees to the procedure
A note in the record showing the person was told the likely outcome
preguntas.explicacion: Consent means the person voluntarily and willingly agrees to what is proposed. The person consenting must have sufficient mental capacity, and the agreement must be free of coercion, fraud or error. It divides into express consent, given directly in speech or writing, and implied consent, inferred from actions, signs, facts or even silence.

preguntas.pregunta: The label of a lisinopril and hydrochlorothiazide tablet carries a boxed warning. What does that warning cover?

Lactic acidosis: reported cases have ended in death, hypothermia, bradycardia
Severe cutaneous reactions: the drug is stopped if the rash keeps spreading
Head and neck angioedema: reported more often in Black patients on this class
preguntas.explicacion: The box on this label is short and single-minded: drugs acting on the renin-angiotensin system injure and can kill the developing fetus, so treatment stops as soon as pregnancy is known. Lactic acidosis is the boxed warning of metformin and severe cutaneous reactions belong to the amoxicillin label. preguntas.pregunta: What are essential health benefits?
opciones: Ten categories of service that plans must cover under the health care law
Ten categories of service that plans may add to lower the monthly premium
The list of covered prescription drugs that each plan updates every year
The preventive screenings that plans must provide without any cost sharing
preguntas.explicacion: Essential health benefits are the ten categories of service the health care law requires plans to cover, among them doctors' services, inpatient and outpatient hospital care, prescription drugs, pregnancy and childbirth, and mental health care. Dental coverage must be offered for children; for adults it is optional. The covered drug list is the formulary, and free preventive care is one protection among several, not the whole set of categories.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient breathes in clusters of deep, even breaths separated by pauses, with no build-up or fading within each cluster. Which pattern is charted?
opciones: Biot respiration, clusters of deep breaths broken by spells of apnea
Cheyne-Stokes respiration, breaths that swell and fade before a pause
Kussmaul respiration, deep and rapid breathing that never pauses at all
Paradoxical ventilation, the chest wall drawing in during inspiration
preguntas.explicacion: The pause is shared by two patterns, and the shape of the breaths between pauses tells them apart: Cheyne-Stokes grows and fades in a crescendo, while Biot keeps the same depth from breath to breath. Biot respiration follows damage to the pons from stroke, trauma or herniation, and also appears with opioid toxicity.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Abnormal Respirations", Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A7 k50 · CMA I.A.1.f · RMA III.E.3 Respiration d · NCMA 2B.7

preguntas.pregunta: A patient in the lobby coughs forcefully after swallowing a piece of food and can still speak. What is the correct response?
opciones: Stay with the patient and let the coughing go on, watching it weaken
Deliver five firm back blows between the shoulder blades without waiting
Begin cycles of five abdominal thrusts before the airway closes completely
Sweep a finger through the mouth to hook out the piece of food lodged there
preguntas.explicacion: First aid for choking is not started while the person is coughing forcefully and able to speak: a strong cough often expels the object by itself. The rescuer stays ready to act if the cough weakens or speech is lost. A blind finger sweep can push the object further down toward the larynx and is avoided in every age group.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Abdominal thrusts", First Aid

preguntas.pregunta: A patient keeps chatting while the cuff deflates. What does that do to the reading?
opciones: It raises both numbers by roughly 10 mm Hg, so the reading is repeated in silence
It raises both numbers by roughly 2 mm Hg, which is inside the tolerance of the gauge
It lowers both numbers, because talking relaxes the patient and the vessels widen
It has no effect on an automated device, which is deaf to what the patient says
preguntas.explicacion: Talking or actively listening during the measurement adds about 10 mm Hg to both values, which is why the instruction is that nobody speaks while the cuff is deflating. preguntas.pregunta: A trough level is ordered for a patient on an antiepileptic drug. When is the sample drawn?
opciones: At the lowest point of the dosing interval, just before the next dose
At the highest point of the dosing interval, just after the next dose
Halfway between two doses, when the concentration is most stable
At the same hour each morning, independently of the dose times
preguntas.explicacion: A trough is the concentration of the drug in blood at its lowest point, which falls just before the next dose is due; it matters most for drugs with short half-lives. preguntas.pregunta: Under the Security Rule, what does the word integrity mean?
opciones: Data has not been altered or destroyed in a manner that was not authorized
Data is accessible and usable on demand by a person who is authorized
Data is not made available or disclosed to unauthorized persons or processes
Data is stored on equipment the practice owns rather than on a vendor's servers
preguntas.explicacion: The rule promotes three objectives and defines each one. Confidentiality means data is not made available or disclosed to unauthorized persons or processes, which supports the Privacy Rule's limits on use and disclosure. Integrity means it has not been altered or destroyed in an unauthorized manner. Availability means it is accessible and usable on demand by an authorized person.

preguntas.pregunta: A biller is uneasy because a Medicare claim has still not paid twenty-two days after it was sent. What do the benchmarks for time to payment say?
opciones: Medicare pays in 18 to 30 days, so this claim is still inside the payment benchmark
Medicare pays in 12 to 20 days, so this claim is already past the payment benchmark
Medicare pays in 55 to 75 days, so this claim is nowhere near the payment benchmark
Medicare pays in 2 to 5 days, so this claim is far beyond the payment benchmark
preguntas.explicacion: Time to payment is benchmarked payer by payer: 12 to 20 days for private insurance, 18 to 30 for Medicare, and 55 to 75 for the Bureau of Workers' Compensation. Twenty-two days therefore sits comfortably inside the Medicare span. What stretches the wait is billing errors, wrong demographic data, missing or incomplete documentation, and paper rather than electronic submission.

opciones: Five titles, and administrative simplification sits in Title II
Five titles, and administrative simplification sits in Title I
Three titles, and administrative simplification sits in Title III
Seven titles, and administrative simplification sits in Title IV
preguntas.explicacion: The 1996 statute, also known as the Kennedy-Kassebaum Act, has five titles. Title I protects insurance coverage for workers changing or losing jobs. preguntas.pregunta: Which foods are patients told to avoid before a guaiac-based fecal occult blood test?
opciones: Red meat, cantaloupe, raw broccoli, turnip, radish and horseradish
Beets, blackberries, rhubarb, carrots and other strongly colored foods
Onions, garlic and asparagus, which change the odor of the specimen
Cranberry juice and a high-protein diet, which acidify the specimen
preguntas.explicacion: Red meat carries heme with peroxidase activity, and raw produce such as turnip, broccoli, horseradish, radish and cantaloupe is rich in plant peroxidases; either can turn a guaiac card falsely positive, and about 3 days of avoidance is advised. The axilla, which is shielded by the arm and follows the core value closely
The tympanic membrane, which is convenient but not advised as a primary site
The temporal artery, whose skin sensor is the least invasive of the options

After the light blue tube, before the lavender

Right after a non-additive discard tube

preguntas.pregunta: A patient takes 1,000 mg of vitamin C daily and is about to do a guaiac stool test. What effect should be expected if she continues?

A false-positive result, because ascorbic acid has peroxidase activity
An unchanged result, because only vitamin C above 2,000 mg a day interferes
A false-negative result, because ascorbic acid stops intestinal bleeding for 3 days
preguntas.explicacion: Vitamin C is a reducing agent that interferes with the oxidation the guaiac reaction depends on, so it hides blood that is really there. Patients are told to avoid more than 250 mg a day from supplements, juice or fruit, and high amounts for the 3 days before the test can cause a false negative; 1 to 2 grams daily has produced false negatives in studies. Coverage reaching back up to six months before the month of application

preguntas.pregunta: Why does a therapeutic drug level have to be drawn at the scheduled time rather than whenever the patient arrives?
opciones: The useful range is narrow: too high is harmful and too low does not work
The tube additive breaks down if the specimen is collected off schedule
The laboratory only runs drug levels in fixed batches during the day
A late sample would need a larger volume to reach the same sensitivity
preguntas.explicacion: For most medicines a certain level in the blood is needed for the proper effect: some are harmful if the level climbs too high and useless if it falls too low, so monitoring keeps the drug inside its therapeutic range. The published ranges assume a set moment in the dosing interval, such as 12 hours after the dose, which is why the clock, not the workload, sets the draw time.

preguntas.pregunta: How high is the cuff inflated for a manual reading, and how fast is it let down?
opciones: To 30 mm Hg above where the radial pulse disappears, then down at 2 to 3 mm Hg a second
To 30 mm Hg above the last recorded systolic value, then down at 10 mm Hg a second
To 200 mm Hg in every adult, then down at 2 to 3 mm Hg a second while listening
To 20 mm Hg above where the radial pulse disappears, then down as fast as the valve allows
preguntas.explicacion: The radial pulse is palpated while the cuff fills, and inflation continues to about 30 mm Hg past the point where that pulse vanishes. preguntas.pregunta: How often should a practice take stock of what it holds, and what does it weigh when deciding how much to order?

Weekly and after each order, weighing the price offered and the delivery times

preguntas.pregunta: When taking a manual blood pressure, where is the stethoscope placed, and which artery is being heard?
opciones: In the antecubital fossa, listening over the brachial artery
At the wrist, listening over the radial artery
At the neck, listening over the common carotid artery
In the antecubital fossa, listening over the median cubital vein
preguntas.explicacion: The cuff goes around the arm at heart level, and the stethoscope is placed on the antecubital region while the cuff deflates, to hear the Korotkoff sounds as blood returns through the brachial artery; the first sound marks the systolic pressure and the last the diastolic. The radial and carotid arteries are pulse sites, not where the cuff is read.

preguntas.pregunta: A wound culture is being taken. From where in the wound is the swab taken?
opciones: From a square centimeter of viable tissue at or near the center, never from pus or slough
From the thickest pocket of pus, where the organisms are present in the largest numbers
From the eschar at the edge, where the oldest tissue holds the longest-standing organisms
From the skin just outside the margin, where exudate collects and dries against the dressing
preguntas.explicacion: The specimen has to come from the cleanest tissue available, so a square centimeter of viable tissue at or near the center of the wound is chosen, and pus, slough, eschar and necrotic material are avoided; exudate is never collected from the skin. The swab is rotated over that area for five seconds with enough pressure to express fluid, and moistened with saline first if the bed is dry.

They are the reference standard against which body mass index is judged
They have replaced waist circumference as the measure of central fat
They are taken with a tape rather than calipers at eight standard sites

preguntas.pregunta: Which three types of muscle tissue does the body contain, and which of them is both striated and involuntary?
opciones: Skeletal, smooth and cardiac; cardiac is striated and involuntary
Skeletal, smooth and cardiac; smooth is striated and involuntary
Skeletal, smooth and cardiac; skeletal is striated and involuntary
Striated, spindle and rectangular; spindle is striated and involuntary
preguntas.explicacion: Skeletal muscle attaches to bone, is striated and is under voluntary control. Smooth muscle lines the hollow organs, is not striated and works involuntarily under the autonomic nervous system. Superficial, the depth once called a first-degree burn
Full thickness, the depth once called a third-degree burn
Superficial with inhalation injury, since blisters mean smoke

preguntas.pregunta: In what order do the three steps of hemostasis occur after a vessel is punctured?
opciones: Vascular spasm, platelet plug, coagulation
Platelet plug, vascular spasm, coagulation
Coagulation, fibrinolysis, platelet plug
Vascular spasm, coagulation, fibrinolysis
preguntas.explicacion: Hemostasis is the sealing of a ruptured vessel, in three steps: first the smooth muscle of the vessel wall contracts (vascular spasm), then platelets stick to the exposed collagen and to each other (platelet plug), and finally a fibrin clot forms (coagulation). Fibrinolysis is not one of the three; it is the later breakdown of the clot as the vessel heals. Failure of any step leads to hemorrhage.

Over the middle of the cuff, so the sound reaches it through the inflated bladder

preguntas.pregunta: A patient in the waiting room starts a nosebleed. How is it managed?
opciones: Sitting up and leaning forward, pinching the soft part for 10 full minutes
Sitting up and tilting the head back, pinching the bridge for 5 minutes
Lying down flat with a cold pack on the neck and the nostrils packed
Sitting up and blowing the nose gently every minute to clear the clots
preguntas.explicacion: The patient sits, leans forward so blood is not swallowed, breathes through the mouth, and squeezes the soft part of the nose shut between thumb and finger for a full 10 minutes without checking early. preguntas.pregunta: Which pattern is the hallmark of atrial fibrillation?

Regularly irregular narrow complexes with no clear P waves
Irregularly irregular wide complexes with clear P waves
Regular narrow complexes with a P wave before each of them

opciones: Hemophilia A, roughly 80 percent of cases
Hemophilia B, roughly 20 percent of cases
Hemophilia C, the rare autosomal form
Thrombocytopenia, a shortage of platelets
preguntas.explicacion: Hemophilia is a group of inherited disorders in which one or more clotting factors are not produced in functional amounts. Hemophilia A, a deficiency of factor VIII, accounts for about 80 percent of cases; hemophilia B, a deficiency of factor IX, about 20 percent. Both are X-linked and typically passed from carrier mothers to sons. Hemophilia C is a rare autosomal defect of factor XI.
preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.5 Hemostasis, Disorders of Clotting

preguntas.pregunta: The rapid HIV test on the source patient will not be back for hours. What do the WHO and CDC guidance say about starting PEP?
opciones: Start it without waiting for results; stop it later if the source proves negative
Wait for the result, since PEP is only prescribed once the source is confirmed positive
Start it only if the worker's own baseline test is negative and the 72-hour window has closed
Skip it and rely on follow-up testing at 6 weeks, 12 weeks and 6 months
preguntas.explicacion: Health workers should not wait for test results before taking or administering PEP, and prophylaxis can be stopped if the source turns out to be negative. The CDC says the same for the exposed person's own rapid test: if results are unavailable and PEP is indicated, give the first dose immediately and stop later if the person has HIV or the source is found not to. The 72-hour window is the deadline to start, not a period to wait out, and follow-up testing complements PEP rather than replacing it.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010), Annex G, Antiretroviral drugs for PEP; CDC, Clinical Guidance for PEP, Exposure to HIV is a medical emergency

preguntas.pregunta: A patient revokes his consent to share his substance use disorder records. What about what was already sent?
opciones: The revocation does not undo disclosures already acted on in reliance
The revocation obliges the recipient to return or destroy the records
The revocation is only valid if it is given before the expiration event
The revocation must be approved by the program before it takes effect
preguntas.explicacion: The consent form has to tell the patient how to revoke it in writing, and that the right to revoke does not reach back over what the program or another lawful holder has already done in reliance on the consent. The program does not get to approve or refuse the revocation, and revoking is not tied to the expiration date the form carries.

preguntas.pregunta: Within the metric system, which way does the decimal point move when a larger unit is converted into a smaller one?
opciones: To the right, because the unit is getting smaller
To the left, because the unit is getting smaller
It stays put, since only the unit's name changes
It moves both ways, depending on the drug ordered
preguntas.explicacion: The metric system is organized in units of ten, so a conversion inside it only moves the decimal point: to the right when going to a smaller unit, and to the left when going to a larger one. Grams to milligrams is a move to the right by three places; milligrams to grams is the same move to the left. The prefixes run kilo, hecto, deca, the base unit, deci, centi and milli.
preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, ch. 5.4: Metric Equivalencies

preguntas.pregunta: Which risk does the boxed warning of an extended-release metformin product describe?
opciones: Lactic acidosis, with malaise, myalgia, breathing trouble, drowsiness and belly pain
Hypoglycemia deep enough to bring on seizures, coma and death if a meal is missed
Fetal toxicity, so that the drug has to stop as soon as a pregnancy is detected
Anaphylactic reactions, occasionally fatal, of the kind seen with beta-lactam drugs
preguntas.explicacion: The box on this label describes metformin-associated lactic acidosis reported after marketing, which has ended in death, hypothermia, hypotension and resistant bradyarrhythmias. It lists the risk factors, among them kidney impairment, age 65 or over, contrast studies, surgery and heavy alcohol use, and it directs that the drug be stopped and hemodialysis started promptly when acidosis is suspected.
preguntas.fuente: DailyMed, GLUMETZA (metformin hydrochloride) extended-release tablets, Boxed Warning

preguntas.pregunta: What can cause alternating-current interference on a tracing?
opciones: Loops in the lead wires, or poor electrode contact
A cold patient, or a nerve disorder of the arms and legs
A pillow under the head, or crossed legs on the table
Scaly skin, or an electrode placed over breast tissue
preguntas.explicacion: Interference from the current in the walls is common in clinics and hospitals, and it traces back either to poor contact at an electrode or to equipment near the room. Wires are pulled straight when they are attached because a loop in a lead wire also invites it.

opciones: A man's gown top comes off; a woman's stays draped over her chest
A woman's gown top comes off; a man's stays draped over his chest
Both gowns come off, and a sheet is drawn up over the shoulders
Both gowns stay closed, and the electrodes go on top of them
preguntas.explicacion: A male patient takes the top of the gown off so the chest is exposed. A female patient slips her arms out but keeps the gown over her chest, and after the chest electrodes are on, the gown is carefully re-draped over her while the tracing is recorded.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient's adult daughter is helping with his care and asks about the medication list. What does the Privacy Rule permit?
opciones: Sharing what is directly relevant to her involvement in his care, on his informal permission
Sharing the entire record with her, since a relative helping with care stands in for the patient
Withholding the list unless she is appointed as his personal representative by a court
Sharing only after she signs an authorization form on the patient's behalf at the front desk
preguntas.explicacion: A covered entity may rely on informal permission to give family, relatives, friends or others the patient identifies the information directly relevant to that person's involvement in the care or payment for care. That is narrower than a personal representative, who stands in the patient's shoes for all purposes. The same provision lets a pharmacist hand filled prescriptions to someone acting for the patient.

preguntas.pregunta: A primary care clinician sends a focused question to a specialist and receives the answer two days later. Which telehealth service is that?
opciones: An electronic consultation, which is one of the asynchronous arrangements
A facilitated virtual visit, where an assistant gathers the objective data
A teletriage visit, used to sort symptoms quickly in an urgent setting
A remote critical care consultation, which guides a team at the bedside
preguntas.explicacion: Asynchronous telemedicine, the store-and-forward method, gathers history, images and diagnostic data and sends them to a specialist to interpret later. Electronic consultations, where a primary care clinician asks a specialist a focused question, belong here, along with portal messaging, teledermatology, remote reading of images and digital intake questionnaires.

preguntas.pregunta: A basic metabolic panel was drawn after the skin was prepared with povidone iodine. Which results does the WHO warn may be falsely raised?
opciones: Potassium, phosphorus and uric acid
Sodium, chloride and bicarbonate
Glucose, BUN and creatinine
Albumin, bilirubin and total protein
preguntas.explicacion: The note to Step 5 explains why alcohol is preferred over povidone iodine: blood contaminated with iodine may show falsely increased potassium, phosphorus or uric acid. The other groups are real components of the metabolic panels (electrolytes, kidney waste products, liver proteins), but the WHO does not link them to iodine contamination.

preguntas.pregunta: Which two mechanisms does the WHO describe in some vacuum-tube systems for dealing with the used needle?
opciones: One retracts the needle into the barrel and snaps shut; another releases it into the sharps container
One shears the needle from the hub with a small blade; another bends it so it cannot be used a second time
One recaps the needle automatically; another sterilizes it in place for reuse on the same patient
One dissolves the needle in disinfectant; another seals it inside the last tube that was filled
preguntas.explicacion: Section 3.1.1 says some systems have a mechanism that, once the needle has been used, retracts it into the barrel and snaps it shut, while others have a quick-release mechanism that dislodges the used needle straight into the sharps container. Shearing or breaking contaminated needles is prohibited by OSHA, and no source describes automatic recapping, dissolving or sealing a needle in a tube.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 3.1.1, Vacuum extraction systems

preguntas.pregunta: Which sutures are taken out first when an incision line is being cleared?
opciones: Every second one, with the wound reassessed before any of the rest come out
Every one at once, since leaving some in place delays the closure of the skin
The two at the ends first, since they carry the most tension along the line
The ones nearest any redness first, since those are the ones most likely to infect
preguntas.explicacion: Alternate sutures are removed first, then the wound is judged again: if the edges are well approximated the rest can follow, and if there is doubt the remainder wait several days. Removing them all too early risks dehiscence. Steri-Strips may be applied before removal to lower that risk, and the line is watched for separation throughout.
preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, 20.10 Checklist for Intermittent Suture Removal

preguntas.pregunta: From what age is body mass index calculated in children, and how often?
opciones: From the age of 2, and once a year as part of the growth assessment
From the age of 5, and once a year as part of the growth assessment
From birth, and at every well-child visit alongside length and weight
From the age of 2, but only when the weight has crossed a percentile line
preguntas.explicacion: The index can be worked out from the age of 2, once height and weight are both being measured in the usual way, and an annual assessment using the growth charts is recommended from that age. Tracking it over time is what makes it useful, for monitoring growth and development and for dosing medicines.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, About Body Mass Index (BMI)
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A6 k58 · CMA I.A.1.h · RMA III.E.4.e · NCMA 2B.3

preguntas.pregunta: A staff member e-mails a lab result to the wrong patient. How does the Breach Notification Rule treat that event at the outset?
opciones: As a breach, unless a risk assessment shows a low probability that the information was compromised
As a breach only after the Office for Civil Rights investigates and reaches that conclusion
As an incidental disclosure, since a misdirected message cannot reasonably be prevented
As a security incident rather than a breach, because e-mail systems are technical safeguards
preguntas.explicacion: An impermissible use or disclosure under the Privacy Rule is presumed to be a breach. The presumption falls only if the covered entity or business associate demonstrates a low probability that the PHI was compromised, using a risk assessment. Entities may also skip the assessment altogether and simply notify.
preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Breach Notification Rule: Definition of Breach

preguntas.pregunta: Every complex in lead I comes out inverted. What is checked first?
opciones: The arm electrodes, which are almost certainly reversed
The leg electrodes, which are almost certainly reversed
The chest electrodes, which are almost certainly reversed
The clip connectors, which are almost certainly loose
preguntas.explicacion: Inverted complexes throughout lead I point to the two arm wires having been swapped, a common error that the technician does not always catch. Reversed leads can even produce something that looks like electrical interference, so the hook-up is verified before blaming the room or the machine.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 3.5.5.2 Lead Patterns

preguntas.pregunta: What does that code say about a certified professional's knowledge over time?
opciones: That learning continues and that the person keeps up with current research
That the original training is sufficient until the credential is renewed
That new techniques are learned only through the employer's own program
That research is followed only when the employer pays for the coursework
preguntas.explicacion: One of the six duties is to keep learning, applying and advancing scientific and practical knowledge and skills, and to stay current with the latest research and how it is used in practice. Nothing ties that duty to who pays or who provides the course, and the very purpose of renewing the credential is to show that the holder stays current.
preguntas.fuente: NHA Candidate Handbook (2026), Code of Ethics; and Maintaining your Certification

preguntas.pregunta: By what mechanism does the EDTA in a purple top tube keep the blood from clotting?
opciones: It binds the calcium in the sample so the coagulation cascade cannot proceed
It inhibits the formation of thrombin, as the heparin in a green tube does
It activates clotting on contact so the cells can be spun away from the serum
It blocks the breakdown of glucose, which also keeps the cells from clumping
preguntas.explicacion: EDTA works by chelating the calcium ions in the blood, and the WHO table describes the same action as forming calcium salts to remove calcium. Because the blood never clots, the liquid left after spinning is plasma. Thrombin inhibition is how heparin works, contact activation is the plain red tube, and blocking glycolysis is the sodium fluoride of the grey tube.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Laboratory Tube Collection", section Definition/Introduction, Lavender; and WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010), Table 2.3

preguntas.pregunta: The practice's billing vendor suffers a breach of unsecured PHI. What does the vendor owe the practice?
opciones: Notice without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 days from discovering the breach
Notice within 30 days, together with the individual notices already mailed on its own
No more than its yearly report to the Secretary, which the practice can look up
Notice only once the practice asks, since the duty to notify patients rests with the practice
preguntas.explicacion: A business associate that suffers a breach must notify the covered entity without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 days from discovery, and should identify each affected individual and supply what the entity needs for its own notices. The covered entity remains ultimately responsible for notifying the individuals, although it may delegate that task to the business associate when that makes more sense.
preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Breach Notification Rule: Business Associate Notice

preguntas.pregunta: The tracing shows a wandering baseline in leads I and II. Which correction comes first?
opciones: Clean the sites again with alcohol and dry them with gauze
Straighten the lead wires so that no loops are left in them
Ask the patient to hold a breath while the strip is recorded
Switch the machine off and on so the self test runs again
preguntas.explicacion: Leads I and II both take their signal from the arm electrodes, so the sites those leads share are the place to look. Poor skin preparation heads the list of causes, and the remedy given for it is more alcohol to clean and gauze to dry before the electrode goes back on.

Silver chloride electrodes, iodine, cotton and cloth tape
Carbon electrodes, alcohol, gauze and adhesive bandages
Silver chloride electrodes, saline, gauze and elastic wrap
preguntas.explicacion: The tray holds silver chloride electrodes with their clip connectors, alcohol and gauze for the skin, table paper, paper tape, a wax cosmetic pencil for the chest marks and scissors. Iodine and saline belong to other procedures and do not go into this one.

preguntas.pregunta: While a practice works down its backlog it is told to apply max packing. What does that mean in the appointment book?
opciones: Handling any upcoming preventive or screening need at whatever visit brings the patient in
Booking the patient's next preventive and screening visits before she leaves the office
Replacing one-to-one visits for a chronic condition with a single group visit
Using the telephone and e-mail for concerns that do not really need a visit at all
preguntas.explicacion: Max packing reduces the demand for future visits by dealing with preventive and screening needs whenever the patient is already there, whatever the reason for that visit. Group visits for patients who share a chronic condition, and using phone and e-mail for concerns that need no visit, are two other tactics the same section lists for reducing demand.

preguntas.pregunta: A chemical splashes into a patient's eye at the front desk. What is done?
opciones: Flush the eye with running water for at least 15 minutes and get help
Cover both eyes with a dry pad and send the patient to the hospital
Rinse the eye for 30 seconds and then check the vision with a chart
Hold the eyelid open and wipe the chemical away with sterile gauze
preguntas.explicacion: A chemical in the eye is flushed with water immediately and the irrigation keeps going for at least 15 minutes under running water, and medical help is sought right away. Household remedies, ointments and salves are not put on a chemical burn, and a blister or dead skin is left alone.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient says her video appointments freeze constantly. Which barrier does HHS name as the biggest one for telehealth?
opciones: Lack of access to internet service with enough bandwidth for video
Lack of a telephone line at the address where the patient normally lives
Lack of a signed consent form covering the use of video technology
Lack of a printer at home for the visit summary the clinician sends
preguntas.explicacion: The single biggest barrier named is a lack of access to internet service with enough bandwidth for video. The suggestions offered are that the patient may qualify for federal support through the Lifeline program, that many fast food restaurants have free Wi-Fi reaching the parking lot, and that most public libraries provide high-speed internet and often private rooms.

preguntas.pregunta: What distinguishes atherosclerosis from arteriosclerosis?
opciones: Atherosclerosis is plaque in the wall, one specific type of arteriosclerosis
Arteriosclerosis is the plaque buildup; atherosclerosis is generalized loss of compliance
Atherosclerosis affects the veins of the legs; arteriosclerosis affects the arteries
Arteriosclerosis is a congenital narrowing of the aorta; atherosclerosis is acquired
preguntas.explicacion: Arteriosclerosis is the general loss of arterial compliance, the hardening of the arteries, which raises pressure and resistance and drives hypertension and coronary disease. Atherosclerosis is the more specific buildup of plaque, triglycerides, cholesterol, leukocytes and calcium trapped in a damaged wall, and is one type of arteriosclerosis. A congenital narrowing of the aorta is coarctation.
preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 20.2 Blood Flow, Blood Pressure, and Resistance, Cardiovascular System: Arteriosclerosis

preguntas.pregunta: For a susceptible worker, the CDC puts the risk of HBV infection from a single needlestick with HBV-positive blood at which figure?
opciones: 6 to 30 percent, depending on the source's HBeAg status
0.3 percent, the same figure the CDC gives for HIV
About 1.8 percent, the same as for hepatitis C
Under 0.1 percent, since most workers are vaccinated
preguntas.explicacion: A susceptible person stuck or cut with HBV-infected blood faces a 6 to 30 percent chance of infection, and where in that range depends on the source's hepatitis B e antigen status: HBsAg-positive individuals who are also HBeAg-positive carry more virus and transmit more readily. Workers who were vaccinated and developed immunity are at virtually no risk, which is why the question specifies a susceptible worker. There is no known risk from intact skin. The 0.3 and 1.8 percent figures are for HIV and HCV.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient's peak flow reading falls at 65% of her personal best. Which zone is that?
opciones: The yellow zone, which runs from 50% to 80% of personal best
The green zone, which runs from 50% to 80% of personal best
The yellow zone, which runs from 30% to 50% of personal best
The green zone, which runs from 65% to 100% of personal best
preguntas.explicacion: The meter is marked in three zones after a traffic light. Green covers 80% to 100% of personal best, and with no symptoms the patient carries on as before. Yellow runs from 50% to 80% and is where the written action plan starts, beginning with the bronchodilator. The zones only work alongside the symptoms, not instead of them.

preguntas.pregunta: A lavender EDTA tube for a CBC arrives with a visible red-cell clot. Which handling error is the most likely cause according to the rejection study?
opciones: Poor mixing after collection and leaving the tube lying horizontally instead of upright
Centrifuging the tube too soon, before the anticoagulant had time to dissolve
Transporting the tube in a padded holder, which stops the additive from circulating
Filling the tube above its nominal volume so that the EDTA was diluted by excess blood
preguntas.explicacion: Visible clots in anticoagulated tubes, whether red-cell clots in whole blood or fibrin in plasma, are attributed mainly to poor mixing after the draw and to tubes left horizontal rather than vertical; manufacturers and CLSI ask for gentle inversion several times to bring blood and additive into contact. Anticoagulated tubes are not centrifuged for a CBC, and racks or padded holders are the recommended way to carry tubes.

preguntas.pregunta: A non-blanching spot at the puncture site measures about four millimetres. What is it called?
opciones: Purpura, because it is larger than two millimetres
Petechia, because it is smaller than ten millimetres
Erythema, because it sits over an inflamed puncture
Ecchymosis, because it is smaller than ten millimetres
preguntas.explicacion: The dividing line is two millimetres: a non-blanching spot below that size is a petechia and one above it is purpura. A very large bruised area of bleeding under the skin is called an ecchymosis, and redness that fades under pressure is erythema, not bleeding at all.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Petechiae", section Introduction; and MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Bleeding into the skin

preguntas.pregunta: Over four hours a patient's pulse and respiratory rate climb steadily, though every value is still inside the usual range. How is that read?
opciones: As possible early deterioration, since the trend carries more than one value
As normal, since a value inside the reference range is by definition normal
As measurement error, since real change would cross the range boundaries
As anxiety, the usual reason for a rise while the readings stay in range
preguntas.explicacion: Vital signs are compared with the patient's own earlier values, not only with a reference range. Trends over time carry more meaning than isolated measurements in evolving infection, bleeding, respiratory failure or shock, and even modest progressive change can be early physiologic deterioration while every reading still sits inside the traditional range.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Vital Sign Assessment", Clinical Interpretation of Vital Signs

preguntas.pregunta: A shipment of a hazardous disinfectant arrives at a laboratory with a label but no safety data sheet. What must the employer do?
opciones: Obtain one from the manufacturer or importer as soon as possible
Return the shipment unopened, since the sheet travels with the label
Write one from the label, which carries the same hazard information
Wait for the next shipment, which must include the updated sheet
preguntas.explicacion: Manufacturers and importers have to provide a safety data sheet with the first shipment and with the first shipment after the sheet is updated, either with the containers or beforehand. When a shipment labeled as a hazardous chemical arrives without one, the duty falls on the distributor or employer to obtain it from the manufacturer or importer as soon as possible, and they must also supply one on request. A label alone is not a substitute: it carries a fraction of what the sheet holds.

In the floor, deep to the brachialis and supinator muscles below
Beside the brachial artery, between the two heads of pronator teres
Under the biceps tendon, which shields it from the skin above it

preguntas.pregunta: A light blue citrate tube for PT and aPTT arrives filled to about two-thirds of its nominal volume. Applying the acceptance criteria of the emergency laboratory, what is done?
opciones: It is rejected: under-filled citrate tubes below 80 % of target volume fail acceptance because the blood-to-anticoagulant ratio is wrong
It is accepted for both tests, because prothrombin time remains reliable at 67 % fill and aPTT is only slightly affected
It is accepted for the prothrombin time only, and the aPTT is cancelled with a note asking for a properly filled tube
It is topped up with blood from the lavender tube of the same patient to restore the nominal volume before testing
preguntas.explicacion: Insufficient volume gives an inadequate blood-to-anticoagulant ratio, and in citrate tubes that lengthens PT, aPTT and thrombin time and lowers fibrinogen; a clinically significant bias appears below 89 % of fill for aPTT and 78 % for fibrinogen, so the laboratory rejects any citrate tube under 80 % of target. Prothrombin time alone stays fairly reliable down to 67 %, but that does not rescue a tube ordered for both tests, and blood is never moved between tubes.

Past the injury, taking in the joint above it but leaving the one below
Only over the injury itself, so the joints can still be moved and checked

Hematoma formation and prolonged tourniquet time

preguntas.pregunta: A patient scheduled for fasting morning blood work says she had only black coffee and water since dinner 13 hours ago. Is the fasting acceptable?

No; the fast must be at least 24 hours, the same interval set for alcohol

Proceed, but skip the fasting sample and draw only at 2 hours
Proceed with a 100-g load instead, to compensate for the meal

preguntas.pregunta: Both arteries and veins have three tunics. Which tunic is normally the thickest in an artery, and which in a vein?
opciones: Tunica media in arteries; tunica externa in veins
Tunica externa in arteries; tunica media in veins
Tunica intima in arteries; tunica media in veins
Tunica media in both, since both carry blood under pressure
preguntas.explicacion: The layers from inside out are tunica intima, tunica media and tunica externa. The media, rich in smooth muscle and elastic fibers, is normally the thickest layer in arteries, while in veins the media is thinner than the externa, which is the thickest layer there. Veins have less smooth muscle and connective tissue overall, which is why their walls are thinner than those of arteries.

preguntas.pregunta: How long does the vascular spasm that follows a vessel injury usually last, and what triggers it?

A matter of seconds, the time the extrinsic pathway needs
A few minutes, the time the intrinsic pathway needs

Level with Schedule V, because both are dispensed without limits

preguntas.pregunta: The process by which leukocytes squeeze between the cells of a vessel wall to enter the tissues is called what?

Chemotaxis
Phagocytosis
Hemopoiesis
preguntas.explicacion: The exit of white cells through the wall of capillaries and other small vessels is called emigration or diapedesis, from roots meaning to leap through. Chemotaxis is the movement of leukocytes toward chemical signals once they are in the tissue; phagocytosis is the engulfing of pathogens or debris; and hemopoiesis is the production of the formed elements in the marrow.

preguntas.pregunta: An 82-year-old with a urinary infection has a temperature of 37.2 °C (99 °F). Why is that value not reassuring?
opciones: Thermoregulation blunts with age, so a serious infection may raise the value only slightly
Older adults run a higher baseline, so 37.2 °C means the temperature has actually dropped
Urinary infections are the one group of infections that never raise body temperature
The reading is only reassuring once a second value taken an hour later agrees with it
preguntas.explicacion: Baseline core temperature tends to fall with age and the response to infection is blunted, so an older adult may never mount a high fever even when seriously ill. A modest rise above that person's own baseline can be clinically important, which is why the other vital signs and the clinical picture are weighed alongside it.

A purple top tube with EDTA, which also removes calcium, filled completely
A red top clot activator tube, spun so the serum can be tested
A light grey fluoride/oxalate tube, which also requires a full draw
preguntas.explicacion: The WHO table lists the light blue coagulation tube for tests such as protime and prothrombin time. EDTA works the same way on calcium, but the table assigns it to haematology and cross-match, not coagulation; the red top carries a clot activator and gives serum, which a clotting test cannot use; and the grey fluoride/oxalate tube, which also needs a full draw, is the glucose tube.

preguntas.pregunta: A provider orders a routine urinalysis for a patient coming in tomorrow. Which specimen should the medical assistant ask the patient to bring, and why?
opciones: The first void of the morning, because urine that collected overnight is more concentrated
A random specimen collected two hours after breakfast, because food raises the analyte levels
A 24-hour collection, because a single void cannot be dipped reliably for protein or glucose
A specimen collected after drinking a liter of water, because dilute urine is easier to read
preguntas.explicacion: First-void or morning urine is considered the best specimen for routine testing: the urine that accumulates in the bladder overnight is more concentrated, which reflects the kidneys' ability to concentrate and lets the strip detect trace substances that a dilute sample would miss. Random, postprandial and 24-hour collections exist, but each is ordered for a specific purpose, not for the routine dipstick.

Premiums, deductibles and the charges for services a plan does not cover

The strength of the grip, the turgor of the skin and breath sounds
The oral temperature, the pain score and the pattern of breathing
The last recorded weight, the fluid intake and the urine output

preguntas.pregunta: A chart note lists tonsillitis as the reason for the visit. What does the ending of that term tell you?

That the structure named by the root has been removed
That the structure named by the root has been cut into
That the structure named by the root is drooping down

preguntas.pregunta: An emergency patient is typed AB positive. Which blood types could he theoretically receive, and why?
opciones: Any type, since his plasma carries neither anti-A nor anti-B
Only AB+, since both antigens must match the donor exactly
Only O−, since that is the type of the universal donor
Any Rh− type, since Rh+ cells would sensitize the patient
preguntas.explicacion: The AB positive patient is the universal recipient: with both A and B antigens on his own cells he makes neither anti-A nor anti-B, and as an Rh positive person he can take Rh positive or Rh negative blood. A tube filled to its line, which leaves the anticoagulant in excess
A tube inverted six times, which shears the fibrin strands apart
A tube kept at room temperature, which activates factor VII early

Cycles of five back blows and then five chest thrusts, until the object is out

Keep the cup in an inside coat pocket so the specimen stays at body temperature during transport

The lot number of the gloves worn and the brand of disinfectant on the counter
The names of all patients drawn that shift and the time each was seen
preguntas.explicacion: NIOSH lists what to gather: the date and time of the exposure, the procedure or action being performed, specific details such as profession, department or unit, shift and whether the injured person was the device user, and the specific type of device with brand and model when known. These details feed the sharps injury log, which records the device type and brand, the work area and how the incident occurred, including depth of injury and whether a safety feature was activated. preguntas.pregunta: An eye drop has just been instilled. What is the patient told to do next?
opciones: Close the eye two to three minutes and tip the head down, without blinking hard
Blink several times quickly so that the drop spreads over the surface of the eye
Close the eye ten to fifteen minutes, the time an emergency eye flush station runs
Keep the eye open and look up for five minutes, as is done after an ear instillation
preguntas.explicacion: The lower lid is pulled down to form a pocket, and the drop is released into it with the dropper held close but touching nothing. The eye then stays closed for two to three minutes with the head tipped down as if looking at the floor, without blinking or squeezing; gentle pressure over the tear duct helps, and any excess is wiped away. The fifteen minutes belong to an eye flush and the five minutes to ear drops.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient bleeds about 5 mL onto a countertop. Which hypochlorite dilution does the guideline give for decontaminating that surface?

1:50, which delivers roughly 1,000 ppm of available chlorine at day zero
1:5, which delivers the concentration used against Clostridioides difficile spores
preguntas.explicacion: For a small spill of blood or other potentially infectious material, under about 10 mL, a 1:100 dilution of 5.25 to 6.15 percent sodium hypochlorite is used on the nonporous surface, which works out to 525 to 615 ppm of available chlorine. Wait for the remittance advice, which every payer owes within thirty days
Send the whole batch again on paper so the payer cannot say it never arrived

preguntas.explicacion: Among the remedies for slow payment are gathering demographic data accurately, billing accurately, cross-checking entries before submission, confirming that the claims sent were actually received and processed, and setting reminders to follow up on every claim within twenty-one days of submission. Without unreasonable delay and within thirty days, by telephone call to each patient
Within sixty days of the end of the calendar year, in a single written summary

preguntas.pregunta: A processor holds a separated serum tube up to the light and records it as clear. Below roughly what free haemoglobin concentration will hemolysis escape the naked eye?
opciones: About 0.2 to 0.3 g/L, below which separated serum still looks normal
About 0.5 to 0.6 g/L, the level taken as significant interference at the bench
About 1.0 to 1.5 g/L, the level at which potassium begins to climb
About 0.05 to 0.1 g/L, roughly the detection limit of the analyser
preguntas.explicacion: Once the serum has been separated, hemolysis becomes visible at a free haemoglobin of about 0.2 to 0.3 g/L, while the concentration accepted as clinically significant interference is 0.5 g/L. It stands as a firm requirement of 150 g daily for three days
It was replaced by a 24-hour fast in place of the eight-hour one
It applies now only to patients who are already taking insulin
preguntas.explicacion: Individuals were traditionally advised to take at least 150 g of carbohydrate a day for three days beforehand to avoid false-positive results. Updated evidence suggests that unrestricted carbohydrate intake in the preceding days does not significantly change the outcome in most clinical situations, so the preparation may not be necessary for all. The eight-hour fast stands.

Its tip goes into a dry sterile tube and the applicator stick is left long for handling
Its tip is rolled onto a glass slide, air dried, and sent with the applicator attached
Its tip goes into a tube of normal saline and the applicator stick is snapped off

A digital intake questionnaire the patient completes before the appointment
A continuous glucose monitor transmitting readings to the clinician's dashboard
A secure portal message asking for a refill that the office answers next week

preguntas.pregunta: A CBC on a man reports 5.4 million red cells per microliter. How does that compare with the reference values?
opciones: It matches the typical male value; women average about 4.8 million
It is high; men average about 4.8 million and women about 5.4 million
It is high; the reference count is 5,000 to 10,000 per microliter
It is normal only if reticulocytes are under 25 percent of the count
preguntas.explicacion: Men have about 5.4 million erythrocytes per microliter and women about 4.8 million, so this count is typical for a man. The 5,000 to 10,000 per microliter range is the leukocyte count. Reticulocytes should be about 1 to 2 percent of the red cells; the 25 percent figure is the share of all the body's cells that are erythrocytes, not a reticulocyte limit.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient taking metformin alone asks whether the tablets can drop the blood sugar too low. What is correct?
opciones: They do not, because metformin does not make the pancreas secrete extra insulin
They do, because metformin shuts the potassium channels of the pancreatic beta cells
They do, because metformin drives glucose and potassium into the cells like insulin
They do, but only once the daily dose passes 2000 mg taken in divided doses
preguntas.explicacion: Metformin works on the liver and the muscle: it activates hepatic AMP-activated protein kinase, damps gluconeogenesis and lipogenesis, and improves the uptake of glucose driven by insulin. Because it never asks the beta cell for more insulin, monotherapy does not produce hypoglycemia. Closing the beta cell's potassium channels is how a sulfonylurea works, and that is the class where hypoglycemia is the main worry.

Yes: a covered entity may set any condition it discloses in its notice
Yes, if the marketing company has signed a business associate agreement
No, unless the patient pays out of pocket and in full, which removes the restriction
preguntas.explicacion: Section 164.508(b)(4) prohibits conditioning treatment, payment, enrollment or eligibility for benefits on the individual signing an authorization. Marketing requires an authorization of its own under 164.508(a)(3), and a business associate agreement covers services performed for the covered entity, not marketing by an outside company.

preguntas.pregunta: After the tourniquet is released, a patient's forearm shows a scatter of red dots about 1 mm across that do not fade when pressed. What are they called?
opciones: Petechiae
Purpura
Ecchymosis
Erythema
preguntas.explicacion: Petechiae are pinpoint non-blanching spots under 2 mm affecting skin and mucous membranes, caused by bleeding into the dermis; a non-blanching spot over 2 mm is purpura. preguntas.pregunta: How does a patient establish a personal best peak flow?
opciones: Recording readings 2 to 4 times a day for 2 weeks while feeling well
Recording readings 2 to 4 times a day for 2 weeks during an exacerbation
Taking the highest of three readings on the day the meter is handed over
Using the value predicted for the patient's height, age and sex instead
preguntas.explicacion: The personal best is the highest value recorded in a diary over two weeks of readings taken two to four times a day, ideally while the patient feels well; it can come out above or below the predicted value. preguntas.pregunta: In a neonatal unit many samples are icteric. Why does this make visual screening for hemolysis even less dependable?
opciones: The high bilirubin colours the serum and leads to underestimation of hemolysis by eye
Bilirubin binds free hemoglobin, so the hemolysis index reads falsely low on the analyzer
Icteric serum cannot be centrifuged fully, so the red cells stay suspended in the sample
Bilirubin makes the serum turbid, which is mistaken for lipemia rather than hemolysis
preguntas.explicacion: In neonatal samples, where elevated bilirubin is common, the ability to detect hemolysis by visual inspection is further biased towards underestimating it; this is one more argument for automated, objective assessment of hemolysis, lipemia and icterus. To a depth equal to the distance from the nostril to the outer corner of the eyelid

preguntas.explicacion: The proportions of hemolysed specimens were 13.6 % by pneumatic tube and 13.1 % hand-carried, with no statistical difference, and the result held for gross and mild hemolysis separately. Because other hospitals have seen large increases after installing a system, and features such as speed, distance and packing differ, the authors encourage each facility to consider whether its own transport method contributes to hemolysis rather than generalising.

A flammable liquid such as a solvent
A gas under pressure in a cylinder

preguntas.pregunta: Bleeding from a small puncture stops within minutes, before any fibrin has formed. Which step of hemostasis is doing the work, and which plasma glycoprotein stabilizes it?
opciones: The platelet plug, stabilized by von Willebrand factor
The fibrin mesh, which factor XIII cross-links and stabilizes
The vascular spasm, which serotonin from platelets maintains
Fibrinolysis, which plasmin made from plasminogen carries out
preguntas.explicacion: In the second step of hemostasis, platelets meet the exposed collagen, become spiked and sticky and clump together, helped by a plasma glycoprotein called von Willebrand factor that stabilizes the growing plug. The plug can temporarily seal a small opening and buys time for coagulation. Factor XIII stabilizes fibrin, serotonin keeps the vessel constricted, and plasmin dissolves the finished clot.

Take one reading a day, at the hour the patient happens to be free that day
Take at least two readings 10 minutes apart, at a different hour each day
Take a reading only on days the patient feels unwell, and log those values
preguntas.explicacion: Self-measured monitoring works best with a routine: the same hour every day, at least two readings a minute or two apart, and every value written in a log. preguntas.pregunta: A patient with dementia signed a consent form last month. What does that tell the team about today's decision?

It stands until a court holds a hearing and rules the patient incapacitated
It stands as long as the same clinician is the one obtaining consent today
It stands, because a dementia diagnosis makes the finding permanent anyway
preguntas.explicacion: A capacity assessment is valid only for the time, place and situation in which it was made: it is a snapshot, not a status. preguntas.pregunta: A patient's blood pressure is recorded as 120/80. What does each number represent?
opciones: 120 is systolic, during ventricular contraction; 80 is diastolic, during relaxation
120 is diastolic, during ventricular relaxation; 80 is systolic, during contraction
120 is the pulse pressure in the aorta; 80 is the mean arterial pressure in the arteries
120 is the pressure inside the aorta; 80 is the pressure inside the venae cavae
preguntas.explicacion: A blood pressure of 120/80 is a normal adult value written as systolic over diastolic: the higher number, around 120 mm Hg, is the arterial pressure produced by ventricular contraction, and the lower, about 80 mm Hg, is the pressure during ventricular relaxation. Injected as briskly as possible so the tube fills before it can clot
Poured down the inner wall of the tube after the needle is removed
Injected only after the needle has been recapped for the transfer

At least monthly, and in every load that contains implantable objects
At least weekly, and in every load, including loads of routine reusable instruments
At least daily, and in the first load after any repair to the machine

A special swab picks up cells or pus; for a deeper wound the drainage is squeezed onto a glass slide
The wound is irrigated with sterile saline and the runoff is caught in a sterile container
A dry dressing is left on the wound overnight and then sent to the laboratory in a sealed bag

The needle may go to general waste once its safety feature is activated; the gloves go to the sharps container instead
Every item from a blood draw, gloves included, goes to the sharps container

From the shoulders to the hips, left open behind for ventilation
From the neck to the ankles, with the ties left loose at the neck
From the chest to the knees, over the uniform but under the badge
preguntas.explicacion: In the donning sequence the gown goes on first, outside the patient room, and it has to cover the body from neck to knees and the arms to the wrists, and wrap around the back, with the neck and waist ties fastened if the gown has them. preguntas.pregunta: A physician asks to add a test to a serum sample collected the previous day and kept refrigerated. What decides whether the laboratory can honour the add-on?

Whether the request reaches the laboratory within 30 days of the original oral order for the panel
Whether the original requisition already listed the panel to which the new test belongs
Whether the sample can be recentrifuged, since a second spin restores the quality of the serum
preguntas.explicacion: Add-on acceptability rests on stability data: studies such as the one that measured common biochemical analytes in serum separator tubes with and without gel under various storage conditions exist precisely to define the time and temperature within which a stored sample can be retested. The 30-day rule concerns written authorisation of oral orders, the original panel does not fix what may be added, and recentrifugation does not restore an analyte that has already changed.

Skip it, since addressable means the specification is offered to entities as an option
Adopt it anyway, since addressable and required specifications carry identical obligations
Ask OCR for a written waiver before the standard containing it can be treated as met
preguntas.explicacion: Every standard must be met, but the specifications inside them are labelled required or addressable. 2 cm proximal, tight enough to abolish the radial pulse for the duration of the draw
15 to 20 cm proximal, loose enough that the veins remain flat until the fist is made
5 to 10 cm distal, tight enough to engorge the veins without obstructing the arterial flow
preguntas.explicacion: For a peripheral line the tourniquet goes roughly 5 to 10 cm proximal to the intended site, tight enough to engorge the veins but not so tight that arterial flow is blocked, since engorgement is what makes the vein easy to identify and cannulate. preguntas.pregunta: A tube of blood shatters on the floor of the draw room. How must the broken glass be picked up?
opciones: With mechanical means such as a brush and dust pan, tongs or forceps, never by hand
With gloved hands, since gloves are the barrier the standard requires for contaminated items
With paper towels soaked in disinfectant, so the glass is decontaminated as it is lifted
With a reusable sharps container held open, so the pieces can be swept directly into it
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(4)(ii)(D) is explicit: broken glassware that may be contaminated is not picked up directly with the hands, gloved or not, but cleaned up by mechanical means such as a brush and dust pan, tongs or forceps. WHO's blood spillage annex describes the same sequence, tongs or pan and brush for the glass, which then goes into a sharps container, followed by absorbing the fluid, cleaning with detergent and applying 0.5 percent hypochlorite. preguntas.pregunta: Why does the CDC describe an HIV exposure as a medical emergency?
opciones: Infection often takes hold within 24 to 36 hours, so PEP works best when begun within hours
Antibodies appear within 24 to 36 hours, so a rapid test must be done before any PEP
PEP is only effective if started before the source patient's viral load is known
The exposed worker becomes infectious to others within 24 to 36 hours
preguntas.explicacion: Infection with HIV takes hold fast, usually 24 to 36 hours after exposure, which is why patients are evaluated rapidly and the first dose is given immediately when rapid test results are unavailable and PEP is indicated. The older CDC brochure makes the same point: treatment should start preferably within hours rather than days, since animal studies suggest less benefit after 24 to 36 hours. Antibody appearance and infectiousness take much longer, which is why follow-up testing runs for months.

An alginate, usually changed every twenty-four to forty-eight hours
A transparent film, usually left over wounds with no exudate at all
A dry sterile gauze, usually changed at least once every twenty-four hours
preguntas.explicacion: Hydrocolloids act as an occlusive barrier against contaminants, hold a moist environment and bring about autolytic debridement, and the thicker ones take up moderate drainage. Pinpoint non-blanching spots smaller than 2 mm
Pooling of blood under the skin with swelling
Lightheadedness, sweating and a brief loss of consciousness

preguntas.pregunta: What does wearing two pairs of gloves do for a worker who suffers a sharps injury?
opciones: It cuts the volume of blood transferred, without stopping the puncture
It stops the needle from reaching the skin when the gauge is small
It removes the need to wash hands once the outer pair comes off
It counts as an engineering control under the bloodborne standard
preguntas.explicacion: Double gloving may reduce the volume of blood that gets through during a sharps injury, but it does not stop the needle from puncturing the skin, so it is a way of lessening an exposure and not of preventing one. preguntas.pregunta: Which set of features defines a normal sinus rhythm?
opciones: Regular, with a P wave before every QRS and a rate of 60 to 100
Regular, with a P wave after every QRS and a rate of 60 to 100
Irregular, with a P wave before each QRS and a rate of 60 to 100
Regular, with no P waves at all and a rate of 60 to 100
preguntas.explicacion: The criteria are a regular rhythm with one P wave ahead of each QRS complex, a P wave that is upright in leads I and II and biphasic in V1, a P wave no taller than 2.5 mm in leads II and III, and a rate between 60 and 100 beats per minute.

No food for 8 hours, but light meals are allowed up to the test
No food for 12 to 16 hours and no exercise for 24 hours before
No dairy for 3 days, then a normal breakfast on the morning of the test

preguntas.pregunta: A patient is blood type A. Which antigen is on the red cells and which antibody circulates in the plasma?
opciones: A antigen on the red cells; anti-B antibodies in the plasma
A antigen on the red cells; anti-A antibodies in the plasma
B antigen on the red cells; anti-A antibodies in the plasma
Neither antigen; both anti-A and anti-B in the plasma
preguntas.explicacion: ABO typing looks at two glycoprotein antigens, A and B. Type A cells carry the A antigen, and because people are exposed to A and B antigens in food and microbes early in life, a type A person has naturally formed anti-B antibodies. Type B has the B antigen with anti-A, type AB has both antigens and neither antibody, and type O has no antigens but both antibodies.

preguntas.pregunta: A preterm infant on oxygen has a moderately hemolysed serum sample with an LDH ordered for monitoring. What approach did the neonatal laboratory and the surveyed neonatologists favour?
opciones: Report the approximate LDH with a comment that moderate hemolysis affects it, rather than rejecting it outright
Reject the LDH and every other analyte on the sample, since LDH is the analyte most sensitive to hemolysis
Correct the LDH with a formula based on the hemolysis index and report the adjusted value without a comment
Report the LDH only after a repeat heel sample, since a moderate index in a newborn always means in vivo hemolysis
preguntas.explicacion: LDH is a basic monitoring test in premature babies receiving supplementary oxygen and is very sensitive to hemolysis, so the laboratory may be slightly more permissive in them: raise the hemolysis borderline a little and report the approximate LDH with a note that moderate hemolysis affects it. Correction formulas, by contrast, have been shown to be unreliable.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with dementia looks lost when asked, 'Have you eaten, taken your pills, or had any coffee since midnight?' How should the questioning be reworked?

Switch to open-ended questions so that he can tell the story in his own words
Put every question to the caregiver, since he cannot answer reliably
