preguntas.pregunta: Which pattern of freezing does cryosurgery aim for, and how is a benign lesion margin judged?
opciones: Rapid freezing then slow thawing, with the white halo reaching 1 to 2 mm past the border
Slow freezing then rapid thawing, with the white halo reaching 1 to 2 mm past the border
Rapid freezing then slow thawing, with the white halo reaching 10 mm past the border
Slow freezing then rapid thawing, with the white halo reaching exactly to the border
preguntas.explicacion: Ice crystals form between and then inside the cells, and thawing damages them again as water rushes back in, so the ideal is fast freezing followed by slow thawing. A benign lesion is frozen until the white halo extends 1 to 2 mm beyond its border, usually for five to ten seconds, and thawing is complete when the original color returns and no frost remains.

preguntas.pregunta: Which vessels are the main site of resistance and of blood pressure regulation, and how wide are they?
opciones: Arterioles, with lumens of about 30 μm or less
Capillaries, with lumens of only 5 to 10 μm
Venules, with lumens of from 8 to 100 μm
Elastic arteries, more than 10 mm in diameter
preguntas.explicacion: Arterioles, with lumens averaging 30 micrometers or less, are called resistance vessels because they slow blood flow and cause the sharpest drop in pressure; their constriction and dilation are the main way blood flow is distributed and pressure is regulated. Capillaries are narrower but far more numerous, and their total cross-sectional area is greater, so they are not the main site of resistance.

preguntas.pregunta: How deep are adult chest compressions, and how soon can permanent brain damage begin once blood flow stops?
opciones: About 2 inches (5 cm); damage can begin in as little as 4 minutes
About 1 inch (2.5 cm); damage can begin after 10 minutes
About 3 inches (7.5 cm); damage can begin after 2 minutes
About 2 inches (5 cm); damage can begin only after 15 minutes
preguntas.explicacion: Compressions press the adult chest down about 2 inches, 5 centimeters, fast and hard with no pausing, letting the chest rise completely between compressions. Time is the reason CPR cannot wait: permanent brain damage or death can occur in as little as 4 minutes after blood flow stops, and death can follow 4 to 6 minutes after that, so CPR continues until heartbeat and breathing return or trained help takes over. If the person has normal breathing, coughing or movement, compressions are not started.

About 1½ inches (4 cm), the depth used on the chest of an infant
About 3 inches (7.5 cm), going deeper when the patient is obese
About 1 inch (2.5 cm), just enough to move the sternum downward
preguntas.explicacion: The adult target is roughly 2 inches, or 5 centimeters, pressing hard but avoiding excessive force, and letting the chest recoil completely each time. preguntas.pregunta: A patient is told the disease is in complete remission. What does that phrase mean?
opciones: Every sign and symptom has gone, though cancer may still be present
Every sign and symptom has gone, so the cancer is considered cured
Some of the signs and symptoms have gone and the others have not
The signs have gone but the tests still show the disease clearly
preguntas.explicacion: Remission is a decrease in, or the disappearance of, the signs and symptoms of cancer. Abducted 30 to 45 degrees from the midline, knees extended, raised one at a time
Abducted 15 to 20 degrees from the midline, knees flexed, lowered before the drape
preguntas.explicacion: The legs go out about 30 to 45 degrees from midline with the knees bent and the foot of the bed lowered or removed. Both legs move at the same time, up and down together, because moving one alone twists the spine and strains muscle. Padding under the legs keeps the supports from compressing nerves where they rest.

preguntas.pregunta: The provider is about to examine the abdomen of a patient with cramping. In what order are the four methods used?
opciones: Inspection, auscultation, percussion and palpation
Inspection, palpation, percussion and auscultation
Auscultation, then inspection, palpation and percussion
Inspection, percussion, palpation and auscultation
preguntas.explicacion: The abdomen breaks the usual pattern. Listening comes second, before any hand presses on the wall, because pressing can stir up or quiet the bowel and change what is heard. The chest is the sequence most people memorize instead: inspection, palpation, percussion, auscultation. Getting the two mixed up is the classic error.

preguntas.pregunta: Whole blood for a PCR assay cannot be extracted until next week. Which storage plan follows the recommendations?
opciones: Separate the plasma or serum from the red cells and store it at −20 °C or colder
Freeze the whole blood tube at −20 °C or colder until the extraction can be done
Keep the whole blood tube at 2 to 8 °C, where it stays stable indefinitely for DNA
Keep the whole blood tube at room temperature, since cold storage lyses the white cells
preguntas.explicacion: Whole blood is not stored below 0 °C: when a frozen sample thaws, heme is released, and heme inhibits the polymerase and quenches the fluorophores used to detect the product. If extraction cannot happen within an acceptable time the erythrocytes are removed and the plasma or serum is frozen at −20 °C or colder. There is no absolute limit for whole blood at room temperature or 2 to 8 °C, but prolonged storage there raises the risk of hemolysis and of nucleic acid degradation from white cell lysis.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Taking a step back from testing: Preanalytical considerations in molecular infectious disease diagnostics" (Clin Biochem 2023, PMC9729171), section 4.1 Time, temperature and freeze-thaw cycles

preguntas.pregunta: A patient reports heartburn and regurgitation after meals. Which structure normally prevents that, and what is the diagnosis?

The lower esophageal sphincter; the diagnosis is peptic ulcer disease
The pyloric sphincter; the diagnosis is gastroesophageal reflux disease
The upper esophageal sphincter; the diagnosis is irritable bowel syndrome
preguntas.explicacion: Heartburn, regurgitation and noncardiac chest pain are the usual complaints in gastroesophageal reflux disease, and with those typical symptoms the diagnosis can be made presumptively. What normally holds the contents down is the lower esophageal sphincter, a physiological sphincter three to five centimeters long whose high resting tone keeps stomach contents out of the esophagus.

opciones: The heparin tubes, the EDTA tube and the citrate tube
The clot activator tube and the serum separator tube alone
The clot activator tube, the citrate tube and the EDTA tube
The serum separator tube and the light green separator tube

Up to 1 mL in adults, and up to 0.5 mL in infants and children
0.1 mL at any age, the same volume used for a tuberculin test

Klebsiella species, responsible for the majority of these infections
Staphylococcus aureus, responsible for the majority of these infections
Neisseria gonorrhoeae, responsible for the majority of these infections
preguntas.explicacion: Frequency, urgency, dysuria and suprapubic discomfort are the typical symptoms of an uncomplicated urinary tract infection, and Escherichia coli causes most of them, with Klebsiella next and Proteus, Enterobacter and Enterococcus behind. About 2 to 6 minutes for the rub; at least 20 seconds for the wash
About 10 seconds for the rub; at least 60 seconds for the wash
About 30 seconds for the rub; at least 30 seconds for the wash

preguntas.pregunta: What separates proximate cause from cause-in-fact in a negligence claim?
opciones: Proximate cause asks whether the harm was a foreseeable consequence
Proximate cause asks whether the defendant intended the harm to happen
Proximate cause asks whether the plaintiff suffered any monetary loss
Proximate cause asks whether a statute was broken before the harm began
preguntas.explicacion: Negligence needs both a factual link and a legal one. Proximate cause is the test the law adds on top: it usually turns on foreseeability, so throwing a rock off a balcony without looking is the proximate cause of the injury below because the harm was foreseeable. Conduct by the plaintiff or an intervening third party can break that link.

preguntas.pregunta: Which statement about restraint or seclusion orders is correct under the CMS patient-rights condition?
opciones: They may never be written as standing or as-needed (PRN) orders
They may be written PRN for patients with a history of falls
They may be renewed indefinitely without a new assessment
They may be issued by any staff member trained in restraint use
preguntas.explicacion: Restraint or seclusion may be used only to ensure the immediate physical safety of the patient, staff or others, never for coercion, discipline, convenience or retaliation, only when less restrictive measures have failed, and under the order of a physician or other licensed practitioner responsible for the patient. Orders must never be written as standing orders or on an as-needed basis. For violent behavior each order is limited to 4 hours for adults, 2 hours for ages 9 to 17 and 1 hour under 9, up to 24 hours in total, with a face-to-face evaluation within 1 hour, and the intervention ends as soon as possible.

Draw quickly while he stands, so that he can walk the dizziness off afterwards
Ask him to watch the needle closely so that he stays alert throughout
Postpone the draw until he returns with a signed consent form

preguntas.pregunta: Why are iron tests usually done in the morning, often after a 12-hour fast?

Blood iron peaks around 4 p.m., so the morning gives a trough value
Blood iron is stable in serum for only two hours after waking
Blood iron falls once the 24-hour glycogen stores have been used up

preguntas.pregunta: An 80-year-old with a serious infection has a pulse of 76 beats per minute. Why does that not rule out the infection?
opciones: The rise in rate is blunted in older adults, so tachycardia may never appear
The rate in older adults is read against a resting band that starts at 50 per minute
The rate falls rather than rises during infection once a patient passes 75 years
The rate is unreliable at the wrist in older adults and only counts at the carotid
preguntas.explicacion: Older adults often show a blunted rise in heart rate under stress because the response to adrenergic drive is reduced, and drugs such as beta blockers and some calcium channel blockers flatten it further. Tachycardia can therefore be missing in serious infection or blood loss, so a normal-looking rate is not reassurance on its own.

So the patient stays warm and does not shiver
So the wires do not pick up current from the room
So the chest marks are not rubbed off the skin

preguntas.pregunta: Blood for serological testing is drawn at a rural clinic in midsummer and sent by car to the laboratory. Which two handling points apply to that specimen?
opciones: Let the blood clot before processing, and protect the sample from extreme temperatures during transport
Centrifuge the tube immediately after the draw, and keep the sample frozen at −20 °C during transport
Mix the tube by five inversions to prevent clotting, and keep the sample at 37 °C during transport
Let the blood clot before processing, and keep the sample on wet ice during the whole transport
preguntas.explicacion: For serological testing the blood is allowed to clot before it is processed, the specimen goes into properly labelled containers, and during transport it is protected from extreme temperatures; serum for prompt serology is then stored at 2 to 8 °C, and only long-term storage or delayed transport calls for freezing at −20 °C or lower. Spinning before the clot has formed is what produces fibrin in the serum, and wet ice is the transport rule for other specimen types.

To the state health department, which requires reports of all device failures
To the Ryan White notification system for emergency response personnel

opciones: Bring it within 30 minutes, carried in an inside coat pocket so it stays at body temperature
Bring it within 30 minutes, carried in an insulated bag with a cold pack so that it stays chilled
Bring it within 6 hours, carried in an inside coat pocket so it stays at body temperature

preguntas.pregunta: In the cubital fossa, where does the brachial artery run relative to the biceps tendon, and where is the median nerve?
opciones: The artery just medial to the tendon; the median nerve most medial of all
The artery just lateral to the tendon; the median nerve most lateral of all
The artery deep to the median cubital vein in the roof; the nerve lateral
The artery only at the apex of the fossa; the radial nerve most medial
preguntas.explicacion: The contents of the fossa run from lateral to medial: the radial nerve near the brachioradialis, the biceps tendon, the brachial artery just medial to that tendon, and the median nerve, the most medial structure, usually passing between the two heads of pronator teres. To the individual asking for access, and to any provider who requests records for treatment

preguntas.pregunta: What decides whether a procedure calls for sterile gloves rather than clean exam gloves?

Whether the patient is on transmission-based precautions during the visit that day
Whether the procedure will last long enough for the practitioner's hands to perspire

Record it and tell the patient it shows sinus tachycardia
Repeat it at half the paper speed to slow the tracing down
Repeat it with the limb electrodes moved up to the thighs
preguntas.explicacion: The tracing is obtained by the technician and interpreted by the clinician, so the finding goes to the provider rather than to the patient. Changing the paper speed would make the recording unreadable against the standard grid, and moving the limb electrodes is a remedy for tremor, not for a fast rate.

preguntas.pregunta: What should a patient do just before coughing a sputum specimen into the container?
opciones: Rinse the mouth with plain water for 10 to 15 seconds and spit the saliva out
Rinse the mouth with an antiseptic mouthwash and spit the rinse out completely
Eat a light breakfast so the cough reflex is stronger and the sputum comes up
Hold the breath for 10 to 15 seconds, which loosens secretions from the airway
preguntas.explicacion: Rinsing with clear water for 10 to 15 seconds clears contaminants from the mouth, and the saliva is expelled before the patient takes three deep breaths and coughs at about two-minute intervals until sputum comes up. A deep-cough sample is best taken early in the morning before eating or drinking. Antiseptic mouthwash is the thing specifically avoided before a throat swab.

preguntas.pregunta: Serum for hepatitis serology will not reach the reference laboratory for another six days. How should it be stored in the meantime?
opciones: Frozen at −20 °C or lower, the rule for long-term storage or delayed transport
Refrigerated at 2 to 8 °C, the rule for serum awaiting prompt serological testing
At room temperature away from extremes, the rule for specimens while in transit
Frozen at −70 °C, the rule for specimens that must keep the virus intact for culture
preguntas.explicacion: Serum meant for prompt serological testing waits at 2 to 8 °C, but when transport is delayed or storage will be long the specimen is frozen at −20 °C or lower. Protection from temperature extremes applies while the sample travels, and −70 °C is the transport temperature for viral culture specimens, so each distractor is a real instruction attached to the wrong situation. The blood must also have clotted before the serum is processed.

Thymol reads as no albumin; mercury salts read as leukocyte esterase
Thymol reads as nitrite; mercury salts read as no bilirubin present

The radial, felt at the wrist just above the base of the infant's thumb
The carotid, felt beside the airway as it is in an adult resuscitation
The dorsalis pedis, felt on the top of the foot beside the tendon there

Buy whichever device the largest hospital in the region already uses

preguntas.pregunta: Which four tissue types make up every organ in the body?
opciones: Epithelial, connective, muscle and nervous tissue
Epithelial, glandular, cartilage and nervous tissue
Connective, muscle, adipose and vascular tissue
Epithelial, connective, muscle and lymphoid tissue
preguntas.explicacion: Four tissue types cover every job. Epithelium sheets the outer surfaces, lines cavities and passageways and forms glands; connective tissue binds and supports; muscle is excitable and shortens to give movement; nervous tissue is excitable and carries signals. Adipose, cartilage and blood are specialized kinds of connective tissue.

preguntas.pregunta: Which elements of the informed consent discussion have to appear in the record?
opciones: The nature of the procedure, its risks and benefits, the alternatives with theirs, and understanding
The nature of the procedure, its cost, the name of the assistant present, and the patient's signature
The nature of the procedure, its expected duration, the recovery time, and the follow-up date set
The nature of the procedure, the surgeon's experience with it, the anesthetic, and the tetanus status
preguntas.explicacion: Documentation has to carry the nature of the procedure or intervention, its risks and benefits, the reasonable alternatives, the risks and benefits of those alternatives, and an assessment of whether the patient understood all of it. Consent has moved from collecting a signature to a process built on clear communication, with the patient competent and free of coercion.

preguntas.pregunta: What is a health care proxy, in the strict sense of the term?
opciones: The agent named in a health care declaration to decide for the principal
The written document itself, listing the treatments the person refuses
The relative the state's law puts first when nobody has been named
The clinician who signs the orders once the person becomes incapacitated
preguntas.explicacion: The proxy is the agent named in a health care declaration to make medical decisions for the person who signed it, once that person cannot decide for themselves. preguntas.pregunta: On a rapid pregnancy cassette, what does the built-in control line tell the operator?
opciones: That the device worked and enough sample migrated through the strip; not whether the result is right
That the whole testing process, from sample application to interpretation, was performed correctly
That the result is positive, because a control line only develops in the presence of the analyte
That the kit lot has passed the manufacturer's quality control and is within its expiration date
preguntas.explicacion: Internal, procedural or built-in controls check that the test itself is functioning: the sample volume was adequate, the fluid moved through the strip, and any electronic functions worked. They do not prove the operator handled the whole process correctly; that is what an external control, run like a patient sample, is for. A missing control line means an invalid test, whatever the result window shows.

preguntas.pregunta: On a normal ECG tracing, what does the P wave represent?
opciones: Depolarization of the atria
Depolarization of the ventricles
Repolarization of the ventricles
Repolarization of the atria
preguntas.explicacion: The ECG has three prominent features: the small P wave is atrial depolarization, and the atria start contracting about 25 ms after it begins; the large QRS complex is ventricular depolarization; and the T wave is ventricular repolarization. Atrial repolarization does occur during the QRS complex, which masks it, but that is not what the P wave shows.

preguntas.pregunta: The contents of a delivery do not match the packing list and a temperature excursion is suspected. What happens to those doses?
opciones: They are labelled not for use, kept apart in the storage unit, and the maker is called
They are put into stock and used first, so that no dose is wasted before it expires
They are returned to the carrier at once, since the office never took delivery of them
They are discarded on the spot and the loss is recorded in the inventory account
preguntas.explicacion: A discrepancy or a suspected excursion is reported to the manufacturer immediately. Meanwhile the doses are marked so nobody uses them, and they stay in the proper storage unit but separated from the rest until somebody decides whether they are still viable. Publicly funded stock also means a call to the state or local immunization programme.

preguntas.pregunta: What usually separates a misdemeanor from a felony?
opciones: A misdemeanor is typically punishable by less than 12 months in jail
A misdemeanor is typically punishable by a fine and never by any jail
A misdemeanor is tried in a civil court and a felony in a criminal one
A misdemeanor is charged by the state and a felony only by the federal
preguntas.explicacion: Both are offenses punishable under criminal law. A misdemeanor is typically punishable by less than 12 months in jail, with community service, probation and fines among the usual sentences; the more serious felonies carry stiffer penalties, including jail beyond a year. Many states grade both into lettered classes, while others sentence crime by crime.

preguntas.pregunta: Why is the date of the last menstrual period recorded at intake for a pregnant patient?
opciones: It dates the pregnancy: 7 days and 9 months are added to give the expected date
It dates the pregnancy: 14 days and 9 months are added to give the expected date
It confirms the pregnancy, since no other method can establish that a patient is pregnant
It sets the dose of prenatal vitamins, which is calculated from the cycle length
preguntas.explicacion: Adding 7 days and then 9 months to the first day of the last period, 280 days in all, gives an estimated date of delivery. The method assumes a regular 28-day cycle with ovulation on day 14, and the patient has to be sure of the date. First-trimester ultrasonography is the most accurate way to confirm or revise it.

preguntas.pregunta: How long is an exposed worker followed with HIV antibody testing after an occupational exposure?
opciones: Baseline, then periodically for at least 6 months, for example at 6 weeks, 12 weeks and 6 months
Baseline and one repeat at 7 days, when the 28-day PEP course is one quarter done
Baseline and one repeat at 1 to 2 months, the schedule used after the hepatitis B series
Baseline only, since a negative rapid test rules out infection from that exposure
preguntas.explicacion: HIV antibody is tested as soon as possible after exposure and periodically for at least 6 months, typically at 6 weeks, 12 weeks and 6 months; WHO's annex uses baseline, 6 to 12 weeks and 6 months. Workers on PEP also have blood counts and kidney and liver tests before and 2 weeks after starting. The 1-to-2-month test is the anti-HBs check after hepatitis B vaccination, and a baseline test only shows the worker's status at the time of exposure.

preguntas.pregunta: For which of these exposures do the CDC and WHO guidance say HIV post-exposure prophylaxis is NOT indicated?
opciones: A few drops of blood on intact skin
A splash of blood into the eye
A needlestick with a hollow-bore needle
Blood contact with a fresh abrasion on the hand
preguntas.explicacion: Exposure of intact skin to potentially infectious fluids is one of the situations where PEP for HIV and hepatitis B is not indicated, together with fluids not known to transmit HIV such as faeces, saliva, urine or sweat. The CDC adds that a small amount of blood on intact skin probably poses no risk and that no such transmission has been documented, and its PEP guidance lists mucous membranes, non-intact skin and perforated skin as the routes that warrant consideration. Eye splashes, hollow-bore needlesticks and abrasions are all on that list.

preguntas.pregunta: What is the difference between a living will and a health care power of attorney?
opciones: The living will states the choices; the power of attorney names who decides
The living will names who decides; the power of attorney states the choices
The living will works while the patient can still speak; the power does not
The living will is a medical order; the power of attorney is a legal document
preguntas.explicacion: A living will is a written statement of the person's own wishes, such as whether they want resuscitation or intubation, and it designates nobody. A health care power of attorney grants a named agent the power to make medical decisions on the person's behalf, and that agent may use the living will to guide those decisions. Intra- is between and inter- is within
Intra- is within and inter- is beneath
Intra- is beyond and inter- is between

Yes, but only if she travels to a clinic in a rural area that acts as the originating site
No, Medicare stopped covering telehealth when the public health emergency was declared over

preguntas.pregunta: A patient wearing a fentanyl patch asks whether a heating pad may be placed over it for back pain. What is the answer?
opciones: No: heat over a patch speeds the release of the drug and has caused fatal overdoses
Yes: heat brings vasodilation, which is why it is applied over patches of every kind
Yes, as long as the previous patch is left in place while the new one is being applied
No: heat loosens the adhesive, so the patch has to be pressed down for ten seconds
preguntas.explicacion: Heat is sometimes used with an inunction rubbed into the skin, because vasodilation improves the blood flow and the absorption. Tell the patient firmly that it will not hurt at all this time
Proceed as quickly as possible before the anxiety builds further
Ask a colleague to hold the arm firmly while you perform the draw

preguntas.pregunta: A colleague leaves a needle inserted in a medication vial's septum between doses. Why does the CDC object?
opciones: It opens a direct route for microorganisms into the vial and its contents
It counts as recapping, which the bloodborne pathogens standard prohibits
It exposes the drug to light and reduces its potency within minutes
It is acceptable in a clean medication area away from patient treatment
preguntas.explicacion: A needle is never left inserted in a vial septum for multiple uses, because it creates a direct route for microorganisms to enter the vial and contaminate the fluid; vials whose sterility is compromised or questionable are discarded. preguntas.pregunta: An order for a child calls for four different specimen types by skin puncture. What is the best approach?
opciones: Consider venipuncture, which may give more accurate results when more than two specimens are needed
Collect all four by skin puncture, starting with blood bank so the largest volume comes first
Collect two by heel-prick and two by finger-prick, so that no single site is over-punctured
Collect all four from one puncture, squeezing gently between specimens to keep the flow going
preguntas.explicacion: If more than two specimens are needed by skin puncture, venepuncture may provide more accurate laboratory results. preguntas.pregunta: With an antimicrobial scrub agent, how long is the surgical hand antisepsis, and what does going past ten minutes add?
opciones: About 2 to 6 minutes, and going past ten adds no benefit while irritating the skin
About 2 to 6 minutes, and going past ten adds residual activity that lasts the case
About 8 to 12 minutes, and going past ten adds no benefit while irritating the skin
About 30 to 60 seconds, and going past ten adds a measurable drop in resident flora

preguntas.pregunta: A red top tube is sent to the laboratory for a prothrombin time. Why will it be rejected?
opciones: Coagulation tests need plasma; serum has lost its clotting factors
Coagulation tests need serum; the red tube gives plasma instead
The red tube clots too slowly, beyond the 60 minutes the test allows
The clot activator in the red tube binds the calcium the test measures
preguntas.explicacion: Coagulation testing is done on plasma, never on serum, because the clotting factors are removed when serum forms. The correct specimen is a light blue tube with 3.2% sodium citrate, which chelates calcium and holds the sample in stasis until calcium chloride is added in the laboratory. The clot activator does not bind calcium; it does the opposite, it lets the blood clot.

preguntas.pregunta: A self-sheathing needle is an example of which type of control under the standard?
opciones: An engineering control, which isolates or removes the hazard from the workplace
A work practice control, which changes the way a task is performed
Personal protective equipment, which is used when exposure remains after controls
An administrative control, such as the annual review of the Exposure Control Plan
preguntas.explicacion: The definitions in paragraph (b) list self-sheathing needles, sharps disposal containers and sharps with engineered injury protections as engineering controls: devices that isolate or remove the bloodborne pathogens hazard. A work practice control alters how the task is done; the example the standard gives is banning two-handed recapping. PPE is specialized clothing or equipment worn by the employee. NIOSH's hierarchy of controls places elimination and substitution first, then work practices and administrative controls, then engineering controls, and PPE last.

opciones: The Wong-Baker FACES scale, built for children who are nonverbal in acute settings
The numeric rating scale, which most children can manage from the age of four
The McGill Pain Questionnaire, whose 78 descriptors cover sensory and affective terms
The Short Form Health Survey 36, which measures quality of life across many domains
preguntas.explicacion: The FACES scale was designed for children who cannot put pain into words in an acute setting, and it can be adapted for adults with communication difficulties. Whether the clinician judges that she is mature enough during the encounter
Whether a parent can be reached by telephone before the visit starts
preguntas.explicacion: Minors under 18 usually cannot consent, and the parent gives permission instead. The openings are emancipation — marriage, active military duty, or living apart and managing one's own money — and the services a state lets minors seek alone, such as contraception, care for a sexually transmitted infection, or prenatal care. Paying for a visit does not emancipate anyone, and the mature minor doctrine exists in very few states.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Emancipated Minor", Issues of Concern

preguntas.pregunta: Which patient right is guaranteed by federal law, as opposed to a facility's own bill of rights?
opciones: The right to a copy of one's medical records and to keep them private
The right to receive any treatment the patient requests, regardless of medical necessity
The right to free care in any hospital that accepts Medicare
The right to choose which staff member performs each procedure
preguntas.explicacion: Some patient rights are guaranteed by federal law, notably the right to get a copy of one's medical records and to have them kept private and secure; many states add protections, and insurers, medical organizations and facilities publish their own non-enforceable bills of rights. Other common rights are respectful treatment, freedom from discrimination, the right to refuse treatment and informed consent. The CMS condition adds that the right to make informed decisions is not a mechanism to demand treatment that is medically unnecessary.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Health Topic: Patient Rights, Summary; 42 CFR 482.13(b)(2)

preguntas.pregunta: Which statement about a wandering baseline is correct?
opciones: It is not caused by the machine but by unstable contact
It is caused by the machine when the paper speed drifts
It is caused by the machine picking up nearby equipment
It is not caused by contact but by the patient breathing
preguntas.explicacion: Drift is the problem technicians meet most often, and the instrument is not to blame for it. The prime suspect is unstable contact between the electrode and the skin, so the fix has to happen before the recording starts: clean skin, fresh electrodes and a firm attachment.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient on warfarin comes in for routine monitoring. Which test and tube are expected?
opciones: A PT/INR in a light blue tube with 3.2% sodium citrate
A PTT test in a light blue tube with 3.2% sodium citrate
A PT/INR in a lavender tube with EDTA
A CBC with differential in a lavender tube with EDTA
preguntas.explicacion: The PT/INR is used most often to check how well warfarin (Coumadin) is preventing clots, with the INR letting providers compare results from different laboratories, and the specimen goes in a light blue tube with 3.2% sodium citrate. The PTT is the test linked to monitoring heparin, and EDTA is the hematology anticoagulant.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks orally for an electronic copy of their current hospital records. What is required?
opciones: The records in the form requested, if readily producible, within a reasonable time
A written and notarized request before any copy of the record can be released
A paper copy only, since electronic release is limited to other treating providers
A copy of everything except the current admission, which stays open until discharge
preguntas.explicacion: The right of access covers current records, on an oral or a written request, in the form and format asked for when that is readily producible — including electronic format when the records are kept electronically — and otherwise in readable hard copy or another agreed format, within a reasonable time. The hospital must not frustrate that right.

preguntas.pregunta: The dismissed patient never signed for the certified letter and appears at the desk two months later asking to be booked. What is the guidance?
opciones: Hand her a copy of the letter or say it was mailed, and that care ended on its date
Book her, because a return receipt nobody signed leaves the notice without effect
Start the thirty days again from today, since she has only now learned of the decision
Send a second certified letter and keep seeing her until that new period runs out
preguntas.explicacion: The situation is anticipated: the patient does not sign the return receipt and then contacts the office or turns up after the period in the letter has run. She should be given a copy of the letter, or told by telephone that a letter was sent, and politely told that care ended on the date it named. Nothing in the guidance restarts the clock because the receipt came back unsigned.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, Terminating the Therapeutic Relationship, Utilize standardized notification procedures
preguntas.subtema: Missed appointments and dismissal · CMAA 4F k60 · CCMA 5A k170 · CMA III.H.1.e · RMA II.B.2.b · NCMA 4.9

preguntas.pregunta: A patient's hands are cold and the oximeter will not settle on a value. Why?
opciones: The device needs pulsating blood, and cold and poor perfusion flatten that signal
The device needs a warm sensor, and the cold skin cools the light emitter itself
The device needs venous blood, and cold shifts the reading toward the arterial side
The device needs a still finger, and the cold makes the patient's hand tremble
preguntas.explicacion: The reading depends on a pulsating vascular bed, so anything that flattens the pulse wave defeats it: severe hypotension, cold extremities, Raynaud disease and excessive movement. Readings are also less accurate at cold temperatures, and a skin temperature near 33 °C (91.4 °F) is given as the level needed for reliable values.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Pulse Oximetry", Interfering Factors
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k51 · CMA I.A.1.e · RMA III.E.3 Blood Oxygen Saturation · NCMA 2B.6

preguntas.pregunta: How is the standard of care described when a malpractice claim is judged?
opciones: The care a reasonable clinician of similar training would give in like cases
The care described in the manufacturer's instructions for the device used
The care the best specialist in the state would have given the same patient
The care the patient expected after reading the practice's own brochures
preguntas.explicacion: The defendant's actions are measured against the standard of care for that diagnosis and situation: the reasonable and ordinary care, skill and diligence that clinicians in good standing, with the same general line of practice, ordinarily exercise in like cases. National boards have flattened much of the old regional variation, though access in rural or underserved areas is the occasional exception.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Expert Witness", Introduction: Standard of Care

preguntas.pregunta: A patient loses consciousness during a draw. Which set of findings fits a vasovagal episode while it is happening?
opciones: Slow pulse, low blood pressure, pallor and heavy sweating
Fast pulse, high blood pressure, flushing and dry warm skin
Slow pulse, high blood pressure, flushing and heavy sweating
Fast pulse, low blood pressure, pallor and a bitten tongue
preguntas.explicacion: During the event the patient is typically bradycardic and hypotensive, pale and diaphoretic, and consciousness returns without help. A bitten tongue points instead towards a seizure, which is why it is looked for afterwards along with any sign of injury from a fall.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Vasovagal Episode", section History and Physical
preguntas.subtema: Complications: syncope · CPT D3 3K k68 · PBT II.I · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.12

preguntas.pregunta: How many readings are needed before hypertension is diagnosed?
opciones: Three or more measurements taken at separate visits, when that is feasible
Two measurements taken one minute apart during a single office visit
One measurement, provided the cuff was the right size and the arm supported
Three measurements taken during one visit, five minutes apart from each other
preguntas.explicacion: Where it can be done, three or more readings at separate visits are used to confirm the diagnosis. Taking two or three at one sitting is good practice for a single visit's value, but it does not settle the diagnosis. White-coat and masked hypertension are common, so home or ambulatory monitoring may be considered too.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Blood Pressure Measurement", Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k47 · CMA I.A.1.a · RMA III.E.2.e · NCMA 2B.7

preguntas.pregunta: A bedridden patient is repositioned every couple of hours. What is that meant to prevent?
opciones: Pressure injuries, foot drop and contractures, while keeping the body in alignment
Orthostatic hypotension, which appears when a patient stands after lying flat
Aspiration during tube feeding, which is the reason the head of the bed goes up
Compartment syndrome of the leg, which follows long periods in leg supports
preguntas.explicacion: Turning a patient who cannot turn themselves keeps the body in alignment and heads off pressure injuries, foot drop and contractures, with pillows, rolls and blankets used as supports. Care is taken not to leave a patient lying on an arm, which can cause a neurological injury. Raising the head of the bed is what guards against aspiration.
preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 13: Repositioning Patients
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A1 · NCMA 2A.5 · RMA III.F.2

preguntas.pregunta: The WHO pre-draw interview asks specifically about allergies to which three items?
opciones: Latex, povidone iodine and tape
Latex, alcohol and chlorhexidine
Bananas, avocado and kiwi
Vinyl, silicone and neoprene
preguntas.explicacion: The Annex C interview asks whether the patient is allergic to anything and tells the health worker to ask specifically about latex, povidone iodine and tape. Bananas, avocado and kiwi are the fruits of the latex-fruit syndrome, a reason to probe further rather than the question itself, and vinyl, silicone and neoprene are the latex alternatives used once an allergy is known.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Annex C, Please sit down and make yourself comfortable
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2L k48 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E1 k128 · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.3

preguntas.pregunta: A patient who cut himself badly is pale and clammy. Besides controlling the bleeding, what position does first aid recommend?
opciones: Lay him flat, raise the feet about 12 inches, and cover him with a blanket
Sit him upright with the head between the knees to improve breathing
Lay him on his side in the recovery position with the legs straight
Stand him up and walk him slowly to keep blood circulating
preguntas.explicacion: Pallor, clammy skin, a rapid pulse, dizziness and confusion are signs of shock from blood loss. For severe bleeding the guidance is to get help, keep the injured part still, lay the person flat, raise the feet about 12 inches, 30 centimeters, and cover them with a coat or blanket, avoiding movement if a head, neck, back or leg injury is possible. Lying down also reduces the chance of fainting by improving blood flow to the brain. The recovery position is for someone who is breathing after CPR, not for shock.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Bleeding, Symptoms and First Aid
preguntas.subtema: Shock position · CPT D1 1M k37 · CMA I.B.9.a · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2A.10

preguntas.pregunta: Which patient is a sliding transfer board intended for?
opciones: One with paraplegia, who has upper-body strength but poor balance in the legs
One with quadriplegia, who lacks postural support and upper extremity strength
One who already transfers by standing and pivoting from the bed to the chair
One who cannot follow commands and must be guided through each step verbally
preguntas.explicacion: The board bridges the gap between two surfaces for someone whose arms work but whose legs will not hold them: paraplegia, lower-limb amputation, poor balance or leg strength. It does not suit a patient with quadriplegia, who lacks the trunk control and arm strength to use it, nor someone who already stands and pivots, nor a patient who cannot follow commands.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Care Transfer Techniques", Clinical Significance: Slide Board Transfers
preguntas.subtema: NCMA 2A.5 · RMA III.H.3.a

preguntas.pregunta: What safety advantage do retractable lancets offer?
opciones: They retract and prevent needle-stick injuries
They allow many samples from one puncture
They eliminate transfer of blood into tubes
They can be heparinized for arterial blood
preguntas.explicacion: In the classification of blood-drawing devices, lancets appear among the passive safety-engineered devices with a single entry: retractable, they prevent needle-stick injuries. The other features belong to other rows of the same table: multiple samples from one venepuncture and no blood transfer are advantages of vacuum-tube systems, and heparinized use for arterial blood is listed for the hypodermic needle and syringe.

preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist wants to keep the tube holder and pulls the used needle off it with a gloved hand. Which rule does this break?
opciones: Under OSHA, contaminated needles are removed only by a mechanical device or one-handed technique, when no alternative is feasible
Under OSHA, contaminated needles may be removed by hand as long as clean gloves are worn and the tube holder is disinfected afterwards
The WHO allows removal by hand provided the needle is dropped into a sharps container that is within arm's reach
Removal by hand is permitted when the holder is reused on the same patient within two minutes
preguntas.explicacion: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(2)(vii) prohibits bending, recapping or removing contaminated needles unless the employer can show no alternative is feasible or a specific medical procedure requires it, and then only with a mechanical device or a one-handed technique; shearing or breaking is always prohibited. WHO Annex E says an exposed used needle is never disassembled with bare hands, and Chapter 3 prefers discarding barrel and needle together.
preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(2)(vii)(A)-(B); and WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010), Annex E

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with heart failure breathes in cycles that build up, fade away and then pause before starting again. Which pattern is charted?
opciones: Cheyne-Stokes respiration, a crescendo and decrescendo cycle with apneic gaps
Kussmaul respiration, deep and rapid breaths that keep an even depth throughout
Hyperventilation, rapid deep breathing that carries the carbon dioxide too low
Obstructive sleep apnea, in which snoring and shallow breaths alternate in sleep
preguntas.explicacion: Breathing that swells, fades and then stops for a moment before the next cycle is Cheyne-Stokes respiration. It is seen in heart failure and with raised intracranial pressure, and it carries a poor prognosis. The pattern is described in the chart along with the rate, because the rate alone would miss it.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Abnormal Respirations", Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A7 k50 · CMA I.A.1.f · RMA III.E.3 Respiration d · NCMA 2B.7

preguntas.pregunta: After a needle has been re-sheathed with the scoop technique on a work surface, what is the next step?
opciones: Disinfect the surface, so no blood is left behind on it
Rinse the surface with water and dry it with a paper towel
Cover the surface with fresh paper until the session ends
Leave the surface as it is until the end of the working shift
preguntas.explicacion: The manoeuvre is carried out close to a sharps container and the needle is discarded immediately afterwards. Because the cap was resting on the surface, that surface is then cleaned with disinfectant so that no blood is left on it. An exposed used needle is never taken apart by hand.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Annex E, One-hand scoop technique

preguntas.pregunta: Why does the technique call for repeating height, length and head circumference twice?
opciones: So two readings agree within 0.2 cm, and the average of the closest two is recorded
So the second reading can replace the first, which is treated as a practice attempt
So the larger of the two readings is charted, since the smaller one loses posture
So each reading can be taken by a different person and compared for agreement
preguntas.explicacion: Each of these measurements is taken twice and the two have to fall within 0.2 cm or 0.25 inches of one another; the average of the two closest values is what goes in the record. Head and waist circumferences vary more than height and weight and are the ones most prone to measurement error.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Anthropometric Measurement", Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A6 k58 · CMA I.A.1.h · RMA III.E.4.d · NCMA 2B.3

preguntas.pregunta: What does the light green PST contain, and what kind of sample does it provide?
opciones: Lithium heparin plus a gel separator; plasma for chemistries
Sodium heparin without gel; plasma for lithium and ammonia levels
A clot activator plus a gel separator; serum for chemistries
Potassium oxalate plus sodium fluoride; plasma for glucose
preguntas.explicacion: Table 2.3 describes the PST as a light green tube with lithium heparin anticoagulant and a gel separator, whose gel separates the plasma at the bottom of the tube; its use is chemistries. The dark green tube holds sodium or lithium heparin without gel, the serum separator tube has gel but no anticoagulant and gives serum, and oxalate with fluoride is the grey glucose tube.

preguntas.pregunta: Why might a clinician listen to the heart while palpating a peripheral pulse at the same time?
opciones: To see whether every ventricular contraction produces a beat that can be felt
To confirm that the stethoscope and the palpating fingers agree on the rhythm term
To measure the delay between the heart sound and the wave arriving at the wrist
To decide which of the two sides of the body carries the stronger pulse volume
preguntas.explicacion: Doing both at once answers a specific question: does each contraction of the ventricle reach the periphery as a palpable beat? Contractions that do not produce a felt beat will be missed by counting at the wrist alone, which is why the two are compared when the finding is in doubt.

preguntas.pregunta: Staff verify a returning patient online by asking for her date of birth and her mother's maiden name. What does the FTC say about that choice?
opciones: Those details are not reliable authenticators, because they are so easily obtained
Those details are the two identifiers the safety goal asks for before a procedure
Those details satisfy the rule, because they were collected on the intake form
Those details may be used once the patient has signed the privacy acknowledgment
preguntas.explicacion: For existing accounts the program may include reasonable procedures to confirm who it is dealing with, watch transactions and check the validity of address changes, and for online authentication the guidance points to multi-factor techniques with passwords, PINs, smart cards, tokens and biometrics. A Social Security number, date of birth, mother's maiden name or mailing address is not.

opciones: Third, after the blood culture bottle and a non-additive tube
First, before the blood culture bottle and any other tube
Second, right after the blood culture bottle and before any plain tube
Fourth, after the culture bottle, the plain tube and the red clot activator
preguntas.explicacion: Table 2.3 places the blood culture bottle first, a non-additive tube second and the light blue sodium citrate tube third. The red clot activator tube follows in fourth place. preguntas.pregunta: An assistant's certification lapsed last year but she still signs her name with the initials. What is that?
opciones: Unethical, and a misrepresentation of a credential she no longer holds
Acceptable, as long as she is working toward reinstating the credential
Acceptable, because the exam she passed years ago cannot be undone
Unethical, but permitted while the reinstatement application is pending
preguntas.explicacion: Publicly displaying the certification title, or using the initials after one's name, once the credential has expired is treated as unethical and as a misrepresentation. preguntas.pregunta: Before booking an imaging study, staff contact the insurer for its decision on medical necessity. What limits does that decision carry?
opciones: It is not a promise that the plan will pay the cost of the service
It removes the need for a referral from the patient's primary care doctor
It fixes the amount the patient will owe once the study has been performed
It obliges the imaging center to accept the amount the plan decides to pay
preguntas.explicacion: Preauthorization is the insurer's decision that a service, treatment plan, prescription drug or item of durable medical equipment is medically necessary. preguntas.pregunta: A dialysis patient's arm carries a fistula with a palpable vibration under the fingertips. What does that vibration mean, and what is avoided on that arm?
opciones: A thrill, meaning the fistula is patent; draws, venous access and cuff readings are avoided
A thrill, meaning the fistula has clotted; draws and cuff readings may go ahead as usual
A pulsation, meaning the fistula is patent; only intravenous fluids are avoided on that arm
A pulsation, meaning steal syndrome has begun; the arm is used only for capillary sampling
preguntas.explicacion: Laying the fingertips lightly over a fistula picks up a thrill, a vibration that means the fistula is open, and a thrill is distinguished from a merely pulsating fistula. To protect veins for dialysis, peripheral access, blood draws and blood pressure readings are kept off that side.

preguntas.pregunta: Which needle is recommended for venipuncture in a paediatric patient, and which gauge is avoided?
opciones: A 23-gauge winged steel needle (butterfly) with extension tubing; avoid 25 gauge or thinner because of haemolysis
A 21-gauge straight multisample needle on a tube holder; avoid 23 gauge because it collapses small veins
A 25-gauge winged steel needle (butterfly), which the WHO prefers because it is the least painful in children
A 23-gauge hypodermic needle on an auto-disable syringe; avoid butterflies because of air in the tubing
preguntas.explicacion: For paediatric venepuncture the needle is a winged steel needle, preferably 23 gauge, with an extension tube; gauges of 25 or more of 25 or more are avoided because they may be associated with an increased risk of haemolysis. The butterfly is used with a syringe or an evacuated tube with an adaptor. Auto-disable syringes are designed for injection and are not appropriate for phlebotomy.

preguntas.pregunta: How does the viscosity of blood compare with that of water, and what does that viscosity affect?
opciones: Roughly five times that of water; it raises resistance to flow
Roughly twice that of water; it raises resistance to flow
Roughly five times that of water; it lowers resistance to flow
Roughly the same as water, since plasma is 92 percent water
preguntas.explicacion: Blood is viscous and sticky, with a viscosity about five times that of water, owing to the plasma proteins and the formed elements. Viscosity is resistance to flow, and it has a dramatic effect on blood pressure and flow: honey resists flow more than water, and blood behaves the same way relative to water. Plasma being mostly water does not make whole blood flow like water.
preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.1 An Overview of Blood, Characteristics of Blood

preguntas.pregunta: A patient about to give a sputum culture mentions he is on an antibiotic. What is the correct response?
opciones: Record it and tell the provider, since antibiotics can affect bacterial growth in the culture
Tell him to skip today's dose, since antibiotics can affect the bacterial growth in the culture
Ignore it, since antibiotics reach the bloodstream and not the airway secretions
Postpone the collection for 4 weeks, the interval used before a urea breath test
preguntas.explicacion: Antibiotics can suppress the growth the culture depends on, so the medication is documented and reported; the patient is told not to stop anything unless the provider says so. That is the same rule as in urine culture, where recent antibiotics can produce a false negative. The four-week hold belongs to the urea breath test for Helicobacter pylori.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Sputum Culture, Will I need to do anything to prepare for the test?; and MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Urine culture (003751), Considerations

preguntas.pregunta: Which instruction protects a patient's fingers after a cast is put on the arm?
opciones: Keep rings off that hand until the provider says it is safe to wear them
Keep rings on that hand so that any swelling can be judged against them
Keep the arm below heart level so that the fingers stay warm and pink
Keep the fingers still inside the cast until the follow-up visit is over
preguntas.explicacion: Swelling works its way down the limb and a ring can become a tourniquet on a finger or toe, so rings come off until the provider says otherwise. The limb is rested and propped above the level of the heart, and ice helps in the first days. Swelling, redness, numbness, a cast that feels too tight or too loose, or a bad smell are all reasons to call.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Patient Instructions: Closed reduction of a fractured bone - aftercare — Self-care at Home

preguntas.pregunta: Why does the cardiac impulse pause for about 100 milliseconds at the AV node?
opciones: So the atria complete their contraction before the ventricles begin
So the ventricles finish contracting before the atria start to refill
So the SA node can reset itself before the next sinus rhythm begins
So the Purkinje fibers reach the apex ahead of the two bundle branches
preguntas.explicacion: The AV node's small cells and less efficient junctions slow the impulse, so it takes about 100 ms to cross the node, and this pause is critical: it lets the atrial muscle finish contracting and pumping blood into the ventricles before the ventricles themselves are stimulated. The cardiac skeleton blocks any other route from atria to ventricles, so the AV node is the only gateway.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient has followed a strict low-carbohydrate diet for a week before an OGTT. Why is that a problem?

The test requires 3 days of fasting so that glycogen stores are emptied first
The test requires a low-carbohydrate diet only on the day before, not for a week
The test requires the same diet the patient will follow after diagnosis
preguntas.explicacion: For at least three days before the OGTT the patient must eat an unrestricted diet containing 150 g or more of carbohydrate per day, keep normal activity and avoid unusual or vigorous exercise; a week of carbohydrate restriction invalidates the conditions of the test. Drinking plain water during the fasting hours
Taking a medicine the provider said to continue
Brushing teeth within 30 minutes of the draw
preguntas.explicacion: Besides not eating or drinking anything but plain water, there are three things not to do while fasting: chew gum, smoke, or exercise. Air bubbles that lower the blood gas values, and loss of vacuum in the evacuated tube
preguntas.explicacion: Draws from indwelling catheters or during IV starts are more prone to hemolysis than venipuncture, which the study links to flow through the narrow tube, and samples contaminated by intravenous infusion were 2.2 % of that laboratory's rejections. preguntas.pregunta: A patient in the waiting room falls to the floor with jerking of all four limbs. What should the assistant do first?
opciones: Clear the area of furniture and sharp objects and cushion the head
Hold the arms and legs still so that the patient does not get hurt
Slide a padded tongue blade between the teeth to protect the tongue
Lift the patient onto the exam table where the jerking can be watched
preguntas.explicacion: The whole goal during a convulsion is to keep the patient from being injured: furniture and sharp objects are moved away, the head is cushioned, and tight clothing is loosened, especially at the neck. Cold skin holds less gel, so the electrodes come loose
Cold raises the heart rate, so the rate reads too high
Cold slows the paper, so the squares stand for less time
preguntas.explicacion: Any movement changes what is recorded, and shivering counts as movement, so being relaxed and warm is part of the preparation. Keeping the room temperature right is listed alongside removing metal objects and identifying the electrode sites before the patient lies down.

preguntas.pregunta: An intradermal injection is about to be given. How is the needle held and inserted?
opciones: Bevel up, almost flat on the skin, entering at an angle of 5 to 15 degrees
Bevel up, held like a dart, entering at an angle of 45 to 90 degrees
Bevel down, almost flat on the skin, entering at 5 to 15 degrees
Bevel down, held like a dart, entering straight in at 90 degrees
preguntas.explicacion: The syringe is held between thumb and forefinger with the bevel up and the needle almost flat against the skin, entering at 5 to 15 degrees, and it advances no more than an eighth of an inch, just far enough to cover the bevel. Bevel up lets the needle pierce smoothly and puts the medication into the dermis. The dart grip and the 45 to 90 degree range belong to subcutaneous and intramuscular injections.

preguntas.pregunta: What distance separates direct droplet transmission from airborne transmission in the microbiology definition?
opciones: About one meter: droplets travel a meter or less; airborne goes farther
About three meters: droplets travel three meters or less
About six feet: droplets travel six feet or less; airborne travels farther
There is no distance; the difference is whether a mask was worn
preguntas.explicacion: When a person coughs or sneezes, droplets of mucus that may carry pathogens are ejected; direct droplet transmission covers distances of one meter or less and is treated as a form of contact transmission, while transmission over more than one meter is called airborne and is classed as vehicle transmission through the air. Fine droplets can stay suspended, travel far, and dry into droplet nuclei; tuberculosis is the classic airborne example, needing as few as 10 organisms to infect. The 3 to 6 feet figure is the clinical rule of thumb for Droplet Precautions, a different framework.

preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist stuck by a used needle agrees to have her blood drawn but refuses HIV testing that day. What does the standard require of the sample?
opciones: Keep it at least 90 days so the employee may still choose to have it tested for HIV
Test it for HIV anyway, since consent to the blood draw covers the serologic testing
Discard it, since HIV testing requires a fresh sample drawn after consent is given
Keep it 30 days, the period in which the written opinion has to be provided
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (f)(3)(iii)(B) separates the two consents. If the employee agrees to baseline collection but not, at that moment, to HIV serology, the sample is preserved for at least 90 days; should she decide within those 90 days to have it tested, the test is run as soon as feasible. Testing without her consent is not allowed, and throwing the sample away would defeat the purpose of the rule. The written opinion has its own deadline, 15 days, and is unrelated to the storage period.

preguntas.pregunta: An older patient cannot swallow a tablet. Which alternative oral forms of the same drug might be available?
opciones: A suspension or solution, a chewable tablet, or a tablet that dissolves in the mouth
A suppository, a transdermal patch, or an aerosol delivered through a spacer device
An extended-release tablet, a filter needle preparation, or a multi-dose vial product
A sublingual tablet only, since no other form suits a patient who cannot swallow
preguntas.explicacion: One drug is often supplied in several forms for the same route: acetaminophen alone comes as a tablet, a chewable tablet, a capsule, a suspension or solution, an extended-release tablet and an orally disintegrating tablet. Amoxicillin comes as a capsule, a tablet, a chewable tablet and a suspension. The FDA's list of accepted dosage form terms runs from aerosol and elixir through lotion, ointment, patch and suppository.

preguntas.pregunta: A hospital brings in safety-engineered devices and its injury rate does not fall. Which two problems have been reported in that situation?
opciones: Trouble working the safety mechanism, and needles still discarded improperly
Shortage of sharps containers, and gloves supplied in only one size
Poor lighting at the bedside, and tubes filled in the wrong order
Late reporting of injuries, and no written exposure control plan
preguntas.explicacion: Safety-engineered devices are widely used, but the fall in injuries has not always followed. In one study the rate went from 1.9 to 2.2 per 100 healthcare workers after implementation, and the factors reported most often were difficulty operating the safety mechanism and needles that continued to be disposed of improperly. Both are training and work-practice problems, which is why buying a device is only one part of a prevention program.

preguntas.pregunta: Which practice is named by OCR as a reasonable safeguard a health care office can adopt?
opciones: Speaking quietly when discussing a condition with relatives in a public area of the office
Guaranteeing that no visitor can ever overhear or glimpse any patient information at all
Requiring every workforce member to obtain the patient's consent before each chart entry
Sending all internal messages about patients through unencrypted e-mail to speed up care
preguntas.explicacion: The Privacy Rule expects appropriate administrative, technical and physical safeguards, but OCR says outright that they are not expected to guarantee privacy against every possible risk. A photograph or an X-ray documenting the suspected injury
Proof that abuse or neglect occurred, on the balance of evidence
A second staff member willing to sign the report as a witness

preguntas.pregunta: A trainee asks how much blood a commercial citrate tube should receive. What is the answer?
opciones: A line printed on the tube marks the volume of blood to be drawn
The vacuum stops the flow well before the tube can be overfilled
The colour of the stopper sets the volume for every manufacturer
The laboratory calculates it from the patient's haematocrit result
preguntas.explicacion: Blood for these assays is collected into commercially prepared tubes that already hold their trisodium citrate, and each carries a line showing the volume of blood that should go in. preguntas.pregunta: What does the Z-track method for an intramuscular injection involve?
opciones: Pulling the skin about an inch to one side, injecting, and waiting ten seconds
Pulling the skin about an inch to one side, injecting, and withdrawing at once
Pinching the skin into a fold, injecting, and letting go before the needle exits
Holding the skin taut and flat, injecting, and pressing the site for ten seconds
preguntas.explicacion: The non-dominant hand displaces the skin downward or to one side by about an inch, some two centimetres, and the needle goes in at 90 degrees while that pull is held. Once the medication is in, the needle stays in place ten seconds before coming out in a smooth motion and the skin is released, so the tissue closes over a zigzag path. That keeps the medication in the muscle instead of leaking into subcutaneous tissue.

Security awareness and training, the administrative standard for teaching staff the policies
Contingency planning, the administrative standard for keeping care going during a system failure
Evaluation, the administrative standard for periodically testing how well the policies work

Refilled tubes carry the wrong stopper colour and confuse the sequence

A Td or Tdap booster every 5 years
A Td or Tdap booster every 20 years
No further booster once a Tdap dose is on record

Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae
Staphylococcus aureus and Streptococcus pneumoniae

Placing the cuff over clothing can shift the reading by as much as 5 mm Hg
Placing the cuff over clothing is acceptable when the fabric is thin and smooth
Placing the cuff over clothing lowers the reading only, so a normal value is safe
preguntas.explicacion: A cuff over clothing can alter the result by up to 50 mm Hg, the largest of the quantified technique errors. preguntas.pregunta: Which findings warn that an abdominal surgical wound may be about to dehisce?
opciones: Redness at the wound margins, increasing drainage, growing pain and a broken suture
Pale flat wound margins, decreasing drainage, easing pain and a suture that has loosened
Blanching margins, clear serous drainage, itching and a suture that has begun to dissolve
Firm raised margins, no drainage, tightness across the line and a suture that has darkened
preguntas.explicacion: Dehiscence is the separation of the edges of a surgical wound, partial or full. The warning signs are redness around the margins, drainage that keeps increasing from the incision and pain that keeps growing; a broken suture can mean minor dehiscence or that it is about to happen. preguntas.pregunta: A week after a venipuncture the small clot at the site has disappeared. Which enzyme broke down its fibrin, and from what precursor was it made?
opciones: Plasmin, from plasminogen
Thrombin, from prothrombin
Fibrin, from fibrinogen
Heparin, from basophils
preguntas.explicacion: The gradual removal of a clot is called fibrinolysis: the inactive plasma protein plasminogen is converted into active plasmin, which slowly breaks down the fibrin, while bradykinin dilates the vessel again. Thrombin is the enzyme that builds fibrin, not the one that removes it; fibrin is the clot material itself; and heparin is an anticoagulant from basophils that opposes prothrombin.

preguntas.pregunta: What is seen on the tracing in a third-degree block?

P waves and QRS complexes at one shared but slow rate
P waves that lengthen the PR until a QRS is dropped
P waves that disappear while the QRS stays regular

preguntas.pregunta: A patient on atorvastatin reports diffuse muscle aches with no injury. Which reaction of this class does that fit?
opciones: Myopathy, which is dose dependent and reverses once the statin is discontinued
Rhabdomyolysis, the reaction reported most often in patients taking this class
Necrotizing myopathy, whose weakness clears a day or two after the drug stops
Cognitive dysfunction, the commonest reaction and a reason to change agents
preguntas.explicacion: Statins are generally well tolerated; the reactions seen most are myopathy, hepatotoxicity and new diabetes. Myopathy is dose dependent and shows as diffuse myalgias or otherwise unexplained tenderness or weakness that reverses when the drug is stopped. Rhabdomyolysis is the gravest complication but is rare, immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy persists for months, and cognitive change is rare.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Statin Medications", Adverse Effects

preguntas.pregunta: A vegetarian patient asks what counts as one ounce-equivalent in the Protein Foods Group. Which of these does?
opciones: One tablespoon of peanut butter
One tablespoon of sunflower seeds
One cup of cooked beans or lentils
One cup of tofu cut into cubes
preguntas.explicacion: An ounce-equivalent of protein is an ounce of lean meat, poultry or seafood, one egg, a quarter cup of cooked beans, or a tablespoon of peanut butter. Beans, peas and lentils count either here or in the vegetable group. A whole cup of beans is four ounce-equivalents, not one.

preguntas.pregunta: A ward asks why the laboratory presses so hard on hemolysis when redrawing a tube takes two minutes. What consequences does the literature attach to it?
opciones: Delayed decisions, a longer stay in the department, and extra needle sticks
Loss of the quality control run and a forced recalibration of the analyser
A mandatory report of the quality failure to the accrediting organisation
A penalty against the laboratory's proficiency testing performance that year
preguntas.explicacion: A hemolysed sample usually means a repeat specimen has to be drawn and tested. Those repeats delay treatment and clinical decision making, lengthen the patient's stay in the emergency department, and leave the patient dissatisfied after being stuck more than once. The cost lands on the patient, not on the analyser, which is why the collection step gets the attention.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient files a written grievance about the quality of care. What must the hospital give back?
opciones: Written notice naming the contact person, the steps taken, the result and the date
Written notice that the complaint was received and then forwarded to the state agency
Verbal notice from the department manager once the review has been completed
Written notice of the outcome only if the grievance is found to have merit
preguntas.explicacion: A hospital must run a process for resolving grievances promptly and tell each patient whom to contact to file one. Resolving it means giving the patient written notice of the decision, with the name of the hospital contact person, the steps taken to investigate, the results and the date the process closed. The governing body owns the process.

preguntas.pregunta: The chest electrodes are being placed on a patient. Where does V1 go?
opciones: At the fourth intercostal space, right of the sternal border
At the fifth intercostal space, right of the sternal border
At the fourth intercostal space, left of the sternal border
At the fifth intercostal space, in the mid-clavicular line
preguntas.explicacion: V1 sits in the fourth intercostal space just to the right of the sternum, and V2 goes in the same space on the left side. The two spots are found by walking the fingers down from the sternal angle, and they are marked before the skin is cleaned so the location is not lost.

preguntas.pregunta: Blood cultures, a prothrombin time and a complete blood count are ordered on one venipuncture. Which specimen is collected third?
opciones: The purple EDTA tube for the complete blood count
The light blue citrate tube for the prothrombin time
The blood culture bottle for the microbiology order
A non-additive tube drawn ahead of the citrate tube
preguntas.explicacion: Of the three, the culture bottle sits at position 1, the citrate tube at position 3 and EDTA at position 8, so the EDTA tube is the third one filled. A non-additive tube does hold position 2, but the footnote reserves it for when tissue fluid or thromboplastin contamination is a concern.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient has been prescribed eardrops. Which set of instructions is correct?
opciones: Warm the bottle in the hand a minute or two, lie with that ear up, stay five minutes
Warm the bottle under hot tap water, lie with that ear down, stay for two minutes
Use the drops cold from the refrigerator, sit upright, and stay still for ten minutes
Warm the bottle in the hand, lie with that ear up, and get up as soon as it is done
preguntas.explicacion: The bottle is held in the hand for one or two minutes to warm the solution, a suspension is shaken, and the ear canal is cleaned and dried with a sterile applicator first. The patient lies with the affected ear uppermost, the ordered number of drops goes in without the dropper touching anything, and that position is kept for five minutes. A cotton wick may be used and is replaced at least every 24 hours.

preguntas.pregunta: Which peripheral pulse is described as the hardest to palpate, especially for a less experienced clinician?
opciones: The posterior tibial, found immediately behind the medial malleolus
The popliteal, found in the popliteal fossa slightly lateral to the midline
The femoral, found just below the inguinal ligament toward the pubic symphysis
The brachial, found between the medial epicondyle and the tendon of the biceps
preguntas.explicacion: The posterior tibial pulse sits just behind the bony bump on the inner ankle and is considered the most difficult of the peripheral pulses to feel. The popliteal is also sought less often, but the one singled out for difficulty is the posterior tibial, which matters when its absence is being used as a finding.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Peripheral Pulse", Physical Examination Technique

preguntas.pregunta: A neuron may hold more than a thousand of one organelle, while a bone cell holds only a couple hundred. Which organelle is it, and why the difference?
opciones: The mitochondrion, because a neuron needs far more ATP than a bone cell
The lysosome, because a neuron digests far more debris than a bone cell
The nucleus, because a neuron stores far more genetic material than a bone cell
The Golgi apparatus, because a neuron exports far more protein than a bone cell
preguntas.explicacion: Mitochondria convert the energy held in nutrients such as glucose into ATP, along an inner membrane folded into cristae. Cells that spend a lot of energy carry a lot of them: muscle cells are packed with them for contraction and neurons need them to run their sodium and potassium pumps, while a bone cell is far less active.
preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 3.2 The Cytoplasm and Cellular Organelles, Organelles for Energy Production

preguntas.pregunta: Which feature must appear on a valid HIPAA authorization form?
opciones: An expiration and a statement of the right to revoke it in writing, all in plain language
A witness signature from a workforce member who watched the patient sign the document
A cost estimate of the copies, since the fee has to be agreed before the release is signed
A clause making treatment conditional on the patient granting the authorization requested
preguntas.explicacion: Authorizations must be written in specific terms and in plain language, and must state the information involved, who discloses it, who receives it, when it expires, and the right to revoke it in writing. A covered entity may not condition treatment, payment, enrollment or benefits on the patient signing one, except in limited circumstances the rule spells out.
preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Privacy Rule: Authorization

preguntas.pregunta: Which body mass index range is classified as overweight in adults aged 20 and older?
opciones: 25 to 29.9, with obesity beginning at 30
25 to 29.9, with obesity beginning at 35
24 to 28.9, with obesity beginning at 29
27 to 31.9, with obesity beginning at 32
preguntas.explicacion: The adult table runs 18.5 to 24.9 for healthy weight, 25 to 29.9 for overweight, and 30 or higher for obesity, with 40 and above marked as severe obesity. Body mass index estimates overweight and obesity from weight and height together; it is not a direct measurement of body fat.

preguntas.pregunta: What distinguishes an electronic health record from an electronic medical record?
opciones: The EHR is built to be shared with other organizations involved in the patient's care
The EHR is the version the patient keeps at home, while the EMR belongs to the practice
The EHR holds only billing and demographic data, while the EMR holds the clinical notes
The EHR is a scanned copy of the paper chart, while the EMR is entered directly by staff
preguntas.explicacion: An EMR is the digital version of the paper chart in one clinician's office: it tracks data over time, flags who is due for screening and supports quality work inside that practice, but the information does not travel easily beyond it. An EHR is designed to reach past the organization that collected the data, so the record follows the patient to the specialist, the hospital or the next state.

preguntas.pregunta: A clean-catch urine for culture cannot reach the microbiology laboratory for about 6 hours. What keeps the culture result valid?
opciones: Refrigerating it or placing it in a boric acid preservative tube, either of which holds it for up to 24 hours
Keeping it at room temperature, which is acceptable for up to 24 hours as long as the cup stays capped
Freezing it, since freezing stops bacterial growth more completely than refrigeration does
Adding a formaldehyde preservative, the additive that best protects bacteria for later culture
preguntas.explicacion: Urine for culture must be plated within 2 hours unless it is refrigerated or placed in a preservative; both boric acid and refrigeration hold the specimen adequately for up to 24 hours. Urine left at room temperature for more than 4 hours shows overgrowth of both pathogens and contaminants. Formaldehyde is used to preserve cells and causes false-positive strip reactions, and freezing is not an accepted substitute for refrigeration.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Urine Culture", Specimen Requirements and Procedure; and PMC, PMC4771218 LaRocco et al., Effectiveness of Preanalytic Practices on Urine Cultures (2016), Summary of findings
