preguntas.pregunta: A handwritten order reads QD. Which misreading put that abbreviation on the Do Not Use list?
opciones: It is read as QID, four times daily, instead of every day
It is read as QOD, every other day, instead of every day
It is read as QHS, nightly at bedtime, instead of every day
It is read as PRN, only as needed, instead of every day
preguntas.explicacion: QD means every day, but the period after the q, or the tail of a handwritten q, is taken for the letter i, and the order becomes QID, four doses a day. The recommended practice is to write daily. QOD has its own entry on the list, where the poorly written o is the problem.

preguntas.pregunta: What does a health plan's "network" consist of?
opciones: The providers, facilities and suppliers under contract with the insurer
The list of prescription drugs the plan covers, also called its drug list
The providers the patient may see without a referral from the primary care doctor
The services that count toward the out-of-pocket limit, including out-of-network care
preguntas.explicacion: HealthCare.gov defines the network as the set of facilities, providers and suppliers that have a contract with the insurer or plan to deliver health care services. Being in the network is a matter of contract, not of whether a referral is needed: in many HMOs even in-network specialists require one. The glossary's entry on the out-of-pocket limit shows the other side of the coin: care received out of network does not count toward that limit. The list of covered drugs is the formulary, a separate entry.

preguntas.pregunta: A temperature is charted as 38.2 °C with no other detail. What is missing?
opciones: The route used, since each site carries its own average and its own fever cut-off
The thermometer model, since each manufacturer calibrates its device differently
The room temperature, since a warm room lifts every reading by a fixed amount
The patient's baseline, since a value has no meaning until a baseline is on file
preguntas.explicacion: The same patient reads differently at the armpit, the mouth, the ear and the rectum, and the thresholds for calling a value a fever follow the site. A number without its route cannot be graded or compared with the last one, which is why the route is written beside the value and the hour it was taken.

preguntas.pregunta: Which natural anticoagulant is released by basophils, opposes prothrombin, and is also given as a drug to surgical patients at risk of clots?
opciones: Heparin
Protein C
Thrombin
Plasmin
preguntas.explicacion: Several plasma anticoagulants keep clotting confined to the injury: the protein C system, TFPI, antithrombin and heparin. Heparin comes from basophils, is short-acting, opposes prothrombin and also sits on the cells lining the vessels; a pharmaceutical form is given, for example, to surgical patients at risk of clots. Thrombin builds fibrin and plasmin dissolves it; neither is an anticoagulant.
preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.5 Hemostasis, Plasma Anticoagulants

preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist working alone finds an unresponsive adult who is not breathing. What is the first step?
opciones: Call 911 (or the local emergency number), get an AED if one is known to be nearby, then start CPR
Give 2 rescue breaths, then check the pulse for 10 seconds before calling
Start compressions for 2 minutes, then leave to look for an AED anywhere in the building
Place the person in the recovery position and monitor breathing until help arrives
preguntas.explicacion: After checking responsiveness by tapping and shouting, a lone rescuer calls 911 or the local emergency number as soon as the person is found unresponsive, retrieves an AED only if one is known to be nearby, and then begins CPR with 30 compressions and 2 breaths; the rescuer should not leave the person to search for an AED whose location is unknown. With help available, one person calls while another starts CPR. The recovery position is for a person who has started breathing again, and pulse checks are left to health professionals.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: CPR - adult and child after onset of puberty, First Aid and When to Contact a Medical Professional

preguntas.pregunta: How much authority does an appointed health care proxy have?
opciones: The same authority to request or refuse care the patient would have had
Authority limited to the treatments the living will names one by one
Authority limited to comfort care and to consenting for routine tests
Authority to demand any treatment at all, since the patient cannot speak now
preguntas.explicacion: The proxy or surrogate holds the same power to request or refuse treatment the patient would have held if they could still decide and speak. That authority is not confined to whatever the living will happened to list, and it is not narrowed to comfort measures. What it does not include is demanding care that is not medically indicated: the right to refuse is broader than the right to demand.

preguntas.pregunta: An inpatient with a known latex allergy is admitted for several days of blood work. Which measure applies?
opciones: Post a sign on the door, note the allergy in the chart, and remove latex items from the room
Use powdered latex gloves, which release fewer allergenic proteins onto the skin
Keep the latex gloves in the room but double-glove with vinyl over them
Notify only the surgical team, since gloves matter most in the operating room
preguntas.explicacion: Hospital patients with latex allergy should ask for a sign on the door and notes in the chart, for latex gloves and other latex items to be removed from the room, and for pharmacy and dietary staff to be told so they do not handle medicines or food with latex gloves. Cornstarch powder on latex gloves is a leading source of inhaled allergen, the opposite of a safeguard.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient is placed supine with the arms out on boards. How far may the arms be abducted?
opciones: Less than 90 degrees, which keeps the humerus from pressing on the axilla
Up to 120 degrees, as long as a pad is placed underneath each elbow
As far as the boards reach, provided the palms are turned toward the floor
Exactly 90 degrees, the angle at which the ulnar nerve is under least strain
preguntas.explicacion: Abduction is held under 90 degrees so that the humerus does not press into the axilla and injure the brachial plexus. The forearms rest neutral or supinated, palms toward the body, which keeps pressure off the ulnar nerve; malpositioning of the arm in this position is the commonest source of ulnar injury. A draw sheet tucked under the torso holds an adducted arm.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Anatomy, Patient Positioning", Structure and Function: Supine Position

preguntas.pregunta: A patient who doubled his fiber in one week complains of gas, bloating and cramps. What should he be told?
opciones: Build fiber up slowly over a few weeks and drink plenty of fluid
Build fiber up slowly over a few weeks and cut back on fluid
Stop the fiber, since these symptoms mean he cannot tolerate it
Switch entirely to fiber supplements, which do not cause symptoms
preguntas.explicacion: A large jump in fiber over a short time brings gas, bloating and abdominal cramps, and the complaint usually settles once the gut bacteria adjust. Adding fiber gradually rather than all at once reduces the gas and diarrhea, and fluid is what carries fiber through the digestive tract, so about eight glasses a day are advised.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Fiber — Side Effects; and Recommendations

preguntas.pregunta: A seated patient becomes pale and sweaty and says he is about to faint. What should happen right away?
opciones: He should sit or lie down quickly with the legs elevated, and stay horizontal afterwards
He should stand up and walk slowly to a couch, since the movement restores the venous return
He should be given a sugary drink, since hypoglycemia is the most common cause
He should keep still and upright while the last tube finishes filling
preguntas.explicacion: Patients should sit or lie down quickly during an acute episode, with their legs elevated, to help recovery from reflex postural hypotension, and should be kept horizontal afterwards and prevented from standing too soon; any injury from a fall needs immediate attention. Standing up is the opposite of the advice, and hypoglycemia is listed as a mimic of syncope, not its usual cause.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Syncope", section Treatment / Management

preguntas.pregunta: A provider gives a verbal order during a procedure. What does the record have to show afterwards?
opciones: That the order was dated, timed and authenticated promptly by a responsible practitioner
That the order was witnessed by two members of staff before it was carried out
That the order was entered as a standing order approved by the medical staff earlier
That the order was repeated back and then filed in the practice correspondence log
preguntas.explicacion: All orders, verbal ones included, must be dated, timed and authenticated promptly by the ordering practitioner, or by another practitioner responsible for the patient where State scope of practice law, facility policy and medical staff rules allow it. Preprinted and electronic standing orders are a separate mechanism with its own approval and review requirements.

preguntas.pregunta: Which structural feature separates bacteria from the fungi and protozoa?
opciones: Bacteria are prokaryotes, so their genetic material has no true nucleus
Bacteria are eukaryotes, so their genetic material has no true nucleus
Bacteria are acellular, so their genetic material sits outside any cell
Bacteria are multicellular, so their genetic material is shared between cells
preguntas.explicacion: Bacteria and archaea are prokaryotes: their DNA is not housed in a true nucleus, and most bacterial cell walls contain peptidoglycan. Fungi and protozoa belong to the eukaryotes, whose defining feature is that the cell does have a nucleus. Viruses are in neither camp, because they are not made of cells at all.
preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Microbiology, 1.3 Types of Microorganisms, Prokaryotic Microorganisms

preguntas.pregunta: When must soap and water be used for hand hygiene rather than an alcohol-based rub?
opciones: When the hands are visibly soiled, and when the patient has Clostridioides difficile
When the hands are visibly soiled, and when the patient is on droplet precautions
When gloves are about to be worn, and when the patient has Clostridioides difficile
When entering a room, and when the previous patient was on contact precautions
preguntas.explicacion: Alcohol-based rub is used until dry for most moments of hand hygiene, but two situations send the practitioner to the sink: hands that are visibly soiled and a patient with C. difficile. Hand hygiene is also one of the infection control measures planned before a procedure, alongside environmental control, the choice of gloves, the aseptic field and sequencing from clean to dirty.

preguntas.pregunta: What is placed under the patient's arm before the draw begins?
opciones: A clean paper or towel
A warm compress pack
A rolled cloth tourniquet
A sterile drape with a window
preguntas.explicacion: Preparing the patient includes making the person comfortable, supine where that is possible, and laying a clean paper or towel under the arm that is going to be used. Warming the limb is a measure kept for veins that are hard to find, not a routine part of setting the patient up.

preguntas.pregunta: A laboratory rejects a sample as haemolysed. Which collection practices are recognized causes of haemolysis?
opciones: Pressing the syringe plunger, shaking the tube, and a short draw in the grey tube
Leaving the tourniquet on for more than one minute, and drawing the tubes in the wrong sequence
Using a 21 G needle in an adult, and inverting the citrate tube three to six times
Preparing the skin with povidone iodine, and labeling the tubes away from the patient
preguntas.explicacion: Pressing the plunger raises the risk of haemolysis, Table 2.3 warns that a short draw in the fluoride tube may cause haemolysis, and vigorous shaking or overmixing of the tube produces haemolysis. A long tourniquet causes hemoconcentration, the wrong sequence causes additive carry-over, iodine raises potassium, and three to six gentle inversions is the correct handling of the citrate tube.

preguntas.pregunta: Under CLIA, laboratory tests are sorted into how many complexity categories, and which are they?
opciones: Three: waived, moderate complexity and high complexity
Two: waived and nonwaived, with no further split
Four: waived, PPM, moderate and high complexity
Three: home use, point-of-care and laboratory
preguntas.explicacion: The regulation grades every test system as waived, moderate complexity or high complexity, from the least to the most demanding. Moderate and high together are called nonwaived testing. Provider-performed microscopy is a subcategory inside moderate complexity, not a fourth category, and point-of-care describes where a test is run, not how it is classified.

preguntas.pregunta: Which three elements must valid informed consent for a research study include?
opciones: Disclosure of information, competency to decide, and a voluntary decision
Disclosure of information, a witness signature, and an approved study budget
Competency to decide, a voluntary decision, and payment for participation
Competency to decide, a signed waiver, and a copy filed with the sponsor
preguntas.explicacion: Valid research consent rests on three major elements: disclosure of information, competency of the patient or surrogate to make a decision, and the voluntary nature of that decision. preguntas.pregunta: A trainee steadies the vein by pressing a thumb on the skin just ABOVE the intended puncture point. What is the correct anchoring technique?

Place the thumb above the site but press down harder, so that the vein cannot roll sideways
Use the index finger over the vein itself to guide the shaft of the needle
Skip anchoring; ask the patient to make a fist, which fixes the vein in place
preguntas.explicacion: Step 6 of the WHO procedure anchors the vein by holding the arm and placing a thumb below the venipuncture site; the free hand then uses the thumb to pull the skin down and slightly away from the draw site so it is taut. preguntas.pregunta: A caller with no regular provider has a painful ear infection that began last night. Where should the front desk steer her first?
opciones: To an urgent care center, since the problem needs prompt care but is not emergency severe
To the hospital emergency department, where a sudden illness is always evaluated first
To an ambulatory surgical center, the outpatient site that handles same-day procedures
To a skilled nursing facility, where licensed nurses treat and observe a condition daily
preguntas.explicacion: Urgent care is meant for a problem serious enough that a person would want care without delay, yet not so severe that the emergency room is required. Emergency services mean evaluating an emergency condition and treating it so it does not worsen. For someone with no primary care provider, urgent care usually saves time and money over the emergency room.

Statins are safe throughout pregnancy but are stopped during lactation for the infant
Statins are ruled out in pregnancy but may be resumed as soon as lactation begins
preguntas.explicacion: Statins are discontinued for most patients who become pregnant, and the FDA asks clinicians to weigh the need in the few at very high cardiovascular risk, such as homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia or established cardiovascular disease. The number of years the practice has operated without a previous incident
Whether the workforce member involved had completed the yearly privacy training
Whether the patient complained to the practice about the disclosure afterwards

The sharps injury log, the training record and the employee medical record

preguntas.explicacion: Covered employers record each recordable injury and illness on the OSHA Form 300 log, prepare a Form 301 incident report with details of each case, and at the end of the year prepare the Form 300A summary and post it in a visible place. Run the scheduling module so that the day's appointments can still be moved

It is the category for tests cleared by the FDA for home use
It refers to a laboratory licensed by a state whose rules are stricter than CLIA

preguntas.pregunta: How often does OSHA require an employer's written Exposure Control Plan to be reviewed and updated?
opciones: At least once a year, and whenever the tasks, procedures or positions with occupational exposure change
Within 10 working days of each new hire with occupational exposure, and otherwise every three years
Once a year together with the annual employee training, and at no other time even if tasks change
Every time an exposure incident is reported, and kept for the duration of employment plus 30 years
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (c)(1)(iv) sets two triggers: a review at least every year, plus a review whenever new or changed tasks, procedures or job positions alter who is exposed and how. The other periods belong to other rules of the same standard: 10 working days is the deadline for offering the hepatitis B vaccine, three years is how long training records are kept, and employment plus 30 years is the retention of medical records. It carries over until a judge rules that the patient has recovered
It carries over for the whole admission, once it is in the record
It removes the need to explain the draw, but not to ask permission
preguntas.explicacion: An assessment of capacity is valid only within the time, place and situation in which it took place; it is a snapshot and cannot be carried across to another moment. The date the requisition was printed by the ordering office

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with diabetes has a pulse that is very hard to locate in one leg. What may this suggest?

Dehydration, which empties the vessel and flattens the wave that reaches the leg
A bounding circulation, which spreads the wave and makes any single beat harder to feel
An irregular rhythm, in which the beats are too widely spaced for the fingers to catch
preguntas.explicacion: A pulse that is hard to find can mean the artery is blocked, and those blockages are common in people with diabetes or with arteries hardened by high cholesterol. preguntas.pregunta: One draw yields a filled culture bottle and a filled citrate tube. How many mixing movements does each receive?

Three to six for the culture bottle and eight to ten for the citrate tube
Eight to ten for both containers, since both hold an anticoagulant
Three to six for both containers, since both are drawn before serum tubes
preguntas.explicacion: Once filled, the culture bottle is mixed eight to ten times, while the citrate tube is inverted three to six times straight after the blood goes in. Vigorous shaking is avoided in both cases, since it can froth or haemolyse the sample and spoil the clotting results.

opciones: No: while fasting for a blood test the patient should also not chew gum, smoke or exercise, so the provider is told
Yes: only food and caloric drinks break a fast; sugar-free gum and tobacco are permitted before a lipid panel

preguntas.pregunta: A patient who moved to a high-altitude city three months ago now has a hematocrit above the sea-level reference range. Which mechanism explains it?
opciones: Kidney cells sensed low oxygen and secreted EPO, raising red cell output
The liver secreted thrombopoietin, raising platelet and red cell output
The spleen released its stored third of the platelets and red cells
Reticulocytes were held in the marrow, so more mature cells circulated
preguntas.explicacion: Interstitial fibroblasts in the kidney secrete erythropoietin when oxygen is low, which steps up erythrocyte production until oxygen delivery is restored; people living at high elevations therefore keep a higher hematocrit than those at sea level, and altitude is a recognized cause of a high hematocrit. The head is tilted forward, the tongue depressed, and the swab rolled along the inner surface of both cheeks

Noise, ionizing radiation, chemical vapors and aerosols from biological specimens
Long shifts, night work, understaffing and fatigue from emergency procedures
Latex exposure, glove powder, hand lotions and frequent handwashing
preguntas.explicacion: Static postures while sitting or standing for long periods, repetitive movements when sorting samples or using the computer, forceful exertions, awkward postures and contact stress are the ergonomic risk factors, and carpal tunnel syndrome, tendonitis, tenosynovitis and back pain the resulting musculoskeletal disorders. preguntas.pregunta: How is the radial pulse located at the wrist?

Two fingers are laid on the underside of the wrist, below the base of the little finger
The thumb is laid over the front of the wrist, in line with the middle finger tendon
Two fingers are laid on the back of the wrist, between the two prominent tendons

preguntas.pregunta: Which pair of vital signs is expected to rise together with a fever?
opciones: Heart rate and respiratory rate, because the febrile state raises oxygen demand
Heart rate and blood pressure, because the vessels constrict to conserve body heat
Respiratory rate and oxygen saturation, because ventilation clears the extra heat
Blood pressure and oxygen saturation, because cardiac output rises with the fever
preguntas.explicacion: Producing a fever is expensive: a rise of one degree Celsius takes 10% to 12.5% more metabolic work. Oxygen demand climbs, and heart rate and respiratory rate climb with it. That is why a fast pulse in a febrile patient is expected rather than surprising, and why a fast pulse may also signal infection or dehydration.

preguntas.pregunta: A blood gas report shows a pH of 7.40. Where does this fall relative to the normal range for blood?
opciones: Right at the average; normal is 7.35 to 7.45
Slightly acidic; normal is 7.45 to 7.55
At the low end; normal runs 7.40 to 7.50
Slightly alkaline; normal is 7.0, like pure water
preguntas.explicacion: Blood pH averages about 7.4, with a healthy range of 7.35 to 7.45, so a reading of 7.40 sits in the middle of normal. Blood is somewhat more alkaline than pure water, whose pH is 7.0, and it carries many buffers that keep the value steady. A range starting at 7.45 or 7.40 would wrongly turn a normal reading into a low one.

preguntas.pregunta: What defines a premature ventricular complex on the tracing?
opciones: An early QRS over 120 ms, usually with no P wave before it
An early QRS under 120 ms, usually with no P wave before it
An early QRS over 120 ms, always with a P wave before it
A late QRS over 120 ms, usually with two P waves before it
preguntas.explicacion: The beat arises in the ventricles, so it comes early, its shape is abnormal and it lasts longer than 120 ms. A large T wave of the opposite polarity typically follows it, and no P wave precedes it, because the impulse did not travel down from the atria.

In the buccal space between the cheek and the lower molars, with lips parted
On the middle of the tongue, held down by the patient with gentle pressure
Under the tip of the tongue, kept away from the frenulum and the lower teeth

Only the patient's Social Security number or medical record number, not the name
Only the result itself, regardless of whether a name is attached
Only electronic storage; a printed result with a name attached is not PHI under the rule

preguntas.pregunta: Which HIPAA violation carries a criminal penalty of up to $100,000 and up to 5 years in prison?
opciones: Obtaining or disclosing identifiable health information under false pretenses
Knowingly obtaining or disclosing identifiable health information
Selling identifiable health information for commercial advantage or malicious harm
Failing to correct a violation due to willful neglect within the required period
preguntas.explicacion: The criminal provisions have three tiers: knowingly obtaining or disclosing individually identifiable health information, up to $50,000 and 1 year; doing so under false pretenses, up to $100,000 and 5 years; and doing so with intent to sell, transfer or use it for commercial advantage, personal gain or malicious harm, up to $250,000 and 10 years. preguntas.pregunta: A febrile patient in early septic shock has pulses that feel unusually strong and full. How does that fit the picture?
opciones: Distributive shock can give bounding pulses early, from widened vessels
Bounding pulses rule shock out, since every form of shock weakens them
Bounding pulses with fever come from fluid moving out into the tissues
Bounding pulses point to hypovolemia, where vessels clamp down early
preguntas.explicacion: Pulse quality helps separate the kinds of shock. Hypovolemic shock gives weak or absent peripheral pulses, because there is little volume and the vessels constrict to compensate. preguntas.pregunta: A purple EDTA tube arrives in the laboratory with several small clots inside. Which collection error is associated with this finding?

The tube was inverted too many times in the figure-of-8 pattern
The tube was filled after the grey fluoride tube
The tube was drawn through a butterfly without a discard

Outpatients should avoid heavy physical activity in the hour before

The reading runs about 10 mm Hg low, since the arm below the heart empties faster

Arteries have thinner walls and fewer nerves associated with them
Arteries carry a higher volume of blood at a much lower pressure

preguntas.pregunta: A patient starting a 24-hour urine collection at 7 a.m. asks what to do with the urine he passes at 7 a.m. on the first day. What is the correct instruction?
opciones: Void into the toilet and discard it; collect every void after that, including the 7 a.m. void the next morning
Collect it as the first specimen of the period, and stop with the last void before 7 a.m. the next morning
Void into the toilet and discard it, and also discard the 7 a.m. void of the next morning to keep exactly 24 hours
Collect it as a separate first-morning specimen for urinalysis, and start the timed collection with the next void

The patient's whole blood, to look for clumping of the donor cells
preguntas.explicacion: Blood typing has two steps. In ABO typing the sample's cells are mixed with anti-A and anti-B antibodies and watched for clumping. In back typing the serum, the liquid part without cells, is mixed with cells known to be type A and type B; since type A people have anti-B, type B have anti-A and type O have both, the serum reaction confirms the type. Rh typing is a similar but separate test.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia 003345 Blood typing, How the Test is Performed

preguntas.pregunta: A practice works out that it holds no covered accounts at all this year. What does the FTC advise it to do about the Red Flags Rule?
opciones: Repeat the risk assessment periodically, since a change in the business can create them
Write the program anyway, since every medical office holds covered accounts in practice
Send the Commission a statement recording that the Rule does not reach the practice
Destroy the identification documents on file, which are no longer needed for the Rule
preguntas.explicacion: A financial institution or creditor has to work out whether it holds covered accounts, looking at both existing and new ones, and only then does a written program become compulsory. If it holds none it needs no written program, but business models and services change, and accounts may arrive through a change in structure, process or organization, so the assessment is repeated periodically.

preguntas.pregunta: What is the National Provider Identifier?
opciones: A 10-digit number that identifies a covered provider and carries no other data
A 10-digit number that identifies a covered provider and encodes the specialty
A 9-digit number the payer assigns to each provider it contracts with
A number that replaces the provider's state license in clinical records
preguntas.explicacion: The National Provider Identifier is a HIPAA administrative simplification standard: a unique identification number for covered health care providers, ten positions long, numeric and intelligence-free, so the digits reveal nothing about the state where the provider lives or the specialty practiced. Payers do not assign it, and it replaces legacy identifiers in standard transactions rather than licenses in the record.
preguntas.fuente: CMS, National Provider Identifier Standard (NPI)

preguntas.pregunta: How is sinus bradycardia defined?
opciones: A sinus rhythm running at fewer than 60 beats per minute
A sinus rhythm running at fewer than 40 beats per minute
A sinus rhythm running at fewer than 80 beats per minute
Any irregular rhythm slower than 60 beats per minute
preguntas.explicacion: The depolarization still starts in the sinus node and the tracing still meets the criteria for sinus rhythm; only the rate is below 60. Most of these patients have no symptoms. There is a growing push to move the cut-off down to 50, since many healthy people rest between 50 and 60, but the accepted figure is still 60.

preguntas.pregunta: Before a transcription vendor may start receiving electronic protected health information, what must the practice have in place?
opciones: A written business associate agreement obligating the vendor to safeguard the information
A signed authorization from every patient whose dictation the vendor is going to transcribe
A notice of privacy practices addressed to the vendor and acknowledged by its privacy official
An accounting of disclosures listing each record the vendor is expected to receive that year
preguntas.explicacion: Under the Security Rule a covered entity may let a business associate create, receive, maintain or transmit ePHI on its behalf only after obtaining satisfactory assurances through a contract or other written arrangement. The agreement also binds the business associate to require the same of any subcontractor and to report security incidents, including breaches, back to the practice.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks that results never be left as a message on his home phone, only mailed to his address. How is that request treated?
opciones: As a right: patients may say how information reaches them
As a courtesy the clinic may grant if its system allows it
As a restriction that needs the privacy officer's approval
As impossible, since results go out the way the system sends
preguntas.explicacion: The list of patient rights includes stating how one's information is to be handled and communicated to others; the example given is a patient who wants any message from the pharmacy or the hospital mailed to his home rather than left on his telephone. It sits beside the right to ask that disclosures be restricted and the right to receive an accounting of the disclosures that were made.

preguntas.pregunta: In lead V6 the ventricular complex shows a deep downstroke instead of the usual tall upright wave. What is suggested?
opciones: Record from a position further to the left, out at V7
Record from a position further to the right, back at V1
Drop V6 one intercostal space and run the tracing again
Raise the standardization and run the tracing again
preguntas.explicacion: V6 is expected to write a tall upward wave. When a deep S appears there instead, the guidance is to move out to the left and take V7, hunting for a pattern whose main deflection points up. Moving an electrode down a space is not part of that advice.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 3.5.5.2 Lead Patterns

preguntas.pregunta: You are choosing a vein in the antecubital area. Which vein is the most common venipuncture site, and what does it connect?
opciones: The median cubital vein, linking the cephalic and basilic veins
The basilic vein, linking the median antebrachial and axillary veins
The cephalic vein, running superficially along the biceps brachii
The brachial vein, formed where the radial and ulnar veins join
preguntas.explicacion: Venous blood is drawn more often from the median cubital vein than from any other vein; it branches from the basilic vein in the antecubital region and crosses at an angle to join the cephalic vein, forming a V, and it lies very superficially in the roof of the cubital fossa, where it is easy to reach. The brachial vein is deep, formed by the radial and ulnar veins.
preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 20.5 Circulatory Pathways, Veins Draining the Upper Limbs and Table 20.14; and StatPearls, "Anatomy, Shoulder and Upper Limb, Cubital Fossa" (2023), section Blood Supply and Lymphatics

preguntas.pregunta: The clerk asks which of the panels she books usually need a fast. Which grouping is named among the common tests that do?
opciones: Blood glucose, a lipid panel and a basic metabolic panel
Blood glucose, a complete blood count and a coagulation panel
A lipid panel, a troponin test and a complete blood count
A basic metabolic panel, a troponin test and a strep screen
preguntas.explicacion: The tests said usually to require fasting are blood glucose tests, cholesterol level tests, that is the lipid panel, and the basic metabolic panel. Liver function tests and a renal function panel may also call for a fast in some cases. A blood count is part of a routine checkup, and troponin is a blood enzyme test used after a suspected heart attack.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Fasting for a Blood Test, What types of blood tests require fasting?; and MedlinePlus, What You Need to Know About Blood Testing, What are the different types of blood tests?

preguntas.pregunta: Which medication instruction is written the way the toolkit recommends?
opciones: "Take 1 pill in the morning and 1 pill at bedtime"
"Take twice daily", leaving the timing to the patient
"Take 1 pill every 12 hours around the clock as needed"
"Take as directed by the prescribing clinician"
preguntas.explicacion: Precise wording removes the guesswork: naming the standard time periods, morning, noon, evening and bedtime, tells the patient exactly when to take the dose, while "twice daily" invites errors when nobody knows the doses have to be spread out. The label should also carry a plain description of what the medicine is for.
preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit, Tool 16: Prevent errors
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4F facilitate compliance · CMA I.D pharmacology · 2027 I.D · NCMA B.21

preguntas.pregunta: Which opening question invites a patient to lay out their own concerns?
opciones: "What is the main reason you are seeking care today?"
"Has this pain been present for more than three days?"
"Would you rather have the lab drawn before the visit?"
"Did the last provider already start you on a medicine?"
preguntas.explicacion: The first question posed is usually open-ended, inviting the patient to share what brought them in and showing that someone is listening without judgment. The other three are focused questions: they gather a specific detail with a yes-or-no answer and belong later in the encounter.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Interview Techniques", Issues of Concern

preguntas.pregunta: A methotrexate level is being sent to the laboratory. Under which transport condition will the specimen be accepted?
opciones: Carried on ice and protected from light
Carried at room temperature in a gel tube
Carried frozen at –20 °C in an EDTA tube
Carried at 37 °C in a heated transport block
preguntas.explicacion: Blood samples for methotrexate measurement are accepted only if they were carried on ice and in the dark; specimens transported otherwise are rejected. The same passage assigns EDTA whole blood to cyclosporine monitoring and bans gel tubes for drug levels, so the distractors combine real rules from neighbouring drugs with conditions the source never gives for methotrexate.

preguntas.pregunta: A pregnant patient is due for group B strep screening. Which specimen is collected, and when?
opciones: A swab of the vagina plus the rectum, usually between 36 and 38 weeks of pregnancy
A cervical swab taken with a speculum, usually between 36 and 38 weeks of pregnancy
A swab of the vagina plus the rectum, usually between 12 and 14 weeks of pregnancy
A clean-catch urine specimen only, usually between 36 and 38 weeks of pregnancy
preguntas.explicacion: Group B strep lives in the vagina and rectum, so screening uses a swab of both sites, and the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists puts the timing at 36 to 38 weeks; a patient who goes into labor earlier may be tested then. A urine test is the other option offered, not the only one. A positive result means antibiotics during labor to protect the baby.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Group B Strep Test, What happens during a group B strep test? and Why do I need a group B strep test?

preguntas.pregunta: In addition to anchoring the vein, what does the WHO's Step 6 ask the patient to do so the veins stand out?
opciones: Form a fist
Pump the hand
Lower the arm
Hold a breath
preguntas.explicacion: Step 6 lists three actions in sequence: anchor the vein with a thumb below the site, ask the patient to make a fist so the veins are more prominent, and enter the vein swiftly at 30 degrees or less. Pumping the hand, dangling the arm and breath-holding are not part of the WHO procedure; the warm compress and tapping are the only other vein-raising measures in the material.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 6: Take blood

preguntas.pregunta: What do the two ends of the numeric rating scale for pain stand for?
opciones: Zero is no pain at all and ten is the worst pain the patient can imagine
Zero is mild pain and ten is the point at which analgesia becomes mandatory
Zero is no pain at all and five is the worst pain the patient can imagine
One is the least pain measurable and ten is the average pain of childbirth
preguntas.explicacion: The scale runs from 0, no pain, to 10, the worst possible pain. It is quick and widely used but crude, and the number is worth more when the patient is asked to explain it: a 1 usually means a bump or a bruise, while a 10 is compared to childbirth or passing a kidney stone. A high number alone does not decide the treatment.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Pain Assessment", Introduction
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k53 · CMA I.A.1.g · RMA III.E.1.a · NCMA 2B.6

preguntas.pregunta: A CBC reports a low mean corpuscular volume (MCV). How are the patient's red cells described?
opciones: Microcytic, smaller than normal
Macrocytic, larger than normal
Normocytic, of normal size
Polycythemic, too numerous
preguntas.explicacion: The MCV is a common test that measures red cell size, used in the morphological approach to anemia: normal-sized cells are normocytic, smaller cells microcytic and larger cells macrocytic. A low MCV therefore means microcytic cells. Polycythemia is not a size term; it is an overproduction of red cells.
preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.3 Erythrocytes, Disorders of Erythrocytes

preguntas.pregunta: How is lead aVR produced from the limb electrodes?
opciones: The right arm is the positive one and the others a common ground
The left arm is the positive one and the others a common ground
The right leg is the positive one and the others a common ground
The right arm and the left leg are paired against each other
preguntas.explicacion: The augmented leads take one limb as the positive pole and use the remaining limb electrodes together as a common ground: the right arm for aVR, the left arm for aVL and the left leg for aVF. Pairing two electrodes against each other is how leads I to III work.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 3.5.5.2 Lead Patterns

preguntas.pregunta: Which groups of laboratory parameters can be distorted by venous stasis from a prolonged tourniquet?
opciones: Biochemistry and coagulation factors
Blood cultures and HLA tissue typing
Glucose only, once fluoride is added
Hematology counts only, in the EDTA tube
preguntas.explicacion: In recommending venous illumination devices over prolonged tourniquet use, the chapter says venous stasis from a long application can negatively affect several parameters, naming biochemistry and coagulation factors. The coagulopathies review agrees, asking for minimal tourniquet time to avoid artifacts in clotting tests. Cultures and HLA typing are not among the parameters the chapter lists.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Preparation (venous illumination devices)

preguntas.pregunta: A patient develops a rash where the electrode patches were. How is that handled?
opciones: It usually clears when the patches come off and needs no care
It usually clears once an antihistamine cream has been applied
It means the test cannot be repeated on that patient again
It means the gel was left on too long and must be reported
preguntas.explicacion: Skin sensitivity to the adhesive gel is the one complication of a test that is otherwise safe and non-invasive. It settles as soon as the patches are taken off and in most cases needs no treatment at all, although a known allergy to the adhesive is noted as a relative contraindication.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Electrocardiogram", Complications

preguntas.pregunta: Interference on a tracing has blurred the P waves in every lead. What follows?
opciones: The strip is run again: the P wave has to be plainly visible
The strip is kept: only the QRS complexes have to be visible
The strip is kept and the interference is noted on the log
The strip is run again only if the QRS is blurred as well
preguntas.explicacion: One of the minimum standards is a complex clearly drawn with the P wave in plain view, with no noise obscuring or wiping it out. Because the tracing is reviewed before the patient leaves, a strip below the standard is repeated rather than filed.

preguntas.pregunta: Before handing a batch of samples to the courier, what final check does the WHO procedure place immediately before dispatch?
opciones: Rechecking the labels on the tubes against the forms
Recentrifuging any tube whose serum looks cloudy
Re-verifying the patient's fasting status by telephone
Recording the tourniquet time for each tube on the form
preguntas.explicacion: After the draw, hand hygiene and waste disposal, the WHO sequence has the phlebotomist recheck the labels on the tubes and the forms before dispatch, then inform the patient that the procedure is over and check the puncture site. Patient-sample matching, that is labelling, and the transportation conditions are two of the factors WHO lists as influencing laboratory results during collection and transport, alongside needle gauge, insertion site and the correct tubes.

preguntas.pregunta: Under the Medicare conditions of participation, how long must a hospital keep its medical records?
opciones: At least five years, in their original or legally reproduced form
At least seven years, matching the rule for orders and certifications
At least ten years, matching the rule for Medicare Advantage organizations
For the duration of care plus thirty years, matching the OSHA employee rule
preguntas.explicacion: The medical record service condition requires records to be accurately written, promptly completed, properly filed and retained, and accessible, and sets a floor of five years in original or legally reproduced form. The seven, ten and thirty year periods belong to other rules: documentation of ordered and certified services, Medicare Advantage contracts, and OSHA employee medical records.

preguntas.pregunta: Which term describes a disease whose cause is unknown, and which describes one that is present at birth?
opciones: Idiopathic for the unknown cause; congenital for present at birth
Congenital for the unknown cause; idiopathic for present at birth
Hereditary for the unknown cause; idiopathic for present at birth
Acute for the unknown cause; hereditary for present at birth
preguntas.explicacion: Idiopathic describes a disease of unknown cause. Congenital means a condition or trait present at birth, which may be genetic or not. Hereditary is narrower: genetic information passed from parent to child through sperm and egg cells. Acute is about the pace, signs that begin and worsen quickly.
preguntas.fuente: NCI Dictionary of Cancer Terms, idiopathic and congenital

preguntas.pregunta: A menstruating patient asks when in the month to do a breast self-exam.
opciones: About three to five days after her period starts, at the same time each month
About three to five days before her period starts, at the same time each month
On the first day of her period, when the tissue is at its most tender
Halfway between two periods, which is when the tissue is most nodular
preguntas.explicacion: Three to five days after the period begins the breasts are least tender and least lumpy, which makes changes easier to notice; the point is to repeat it on the same schedule every month. After menopause, the same day of each month is used instead. Experts do not agree on whether the practice finds cancers or saves lives.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Patient Instructions: Breast self-exam — Information
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B3 k64 · CMA I.A.5.a · NCMA 2B.21

preguntas.pregunta: A clinic decides that stopper colour alone will tell staff in what sequence to fill tubes. What problem remains?
opciones: The sequence still has to be followed; colour by itself does not enforce it
Stopper colours are identical between manufacturers, so the risk is covered
Colour tells the phlebotomist how many inversions each tube will need
Colour identifies the additive, so carry-over between tubes cannot happen
preguntas.explicacion: Colour coding makes the tubes easy to tell apart, but an incorrect collection still follows when the sequence is not respected, which is why training matters. Colour codes can also differ from one laboratory to another, so they should be checked locally rather than assumed.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Laboratory Tube Collection", section Issues of Concern; and WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010), Table 2.3, footnote b

preguntas.pregunta: How long is the strip captured by a standard resting recording?
opciones: Ten seconds, taken once the patient is lying down and relaxed
Three minutes, taken once the patient is lying down and relaxed
Sixty seconds, taken once the patient is lying down and relaxed
Ten minutes, taken once the patient is lying down and relaxed
preguntas.explicacion: Everything else in the preparation leads up to a ten-second recording, which is why the patient must be settled before it starts. That same ten seconds is what makes the count-and-multiply method work when the rhythm is too irregular for the square methods.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Electrocardiogram", Preparation
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F3 k147 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(i) · RMA III.F.6.a.i · NCMA 2D.9

preguntas.pregunta: A patient spills hot coffee on the hand and the skin is unbroken and red. What is the first aid?
opciones: Cool running water or a cool bath for at least 5 to 30 minutes
An ice water bath for at least 5 minutes, then a snug bandage
A layer of butter or ointment at once, then a dry sterile gauze
A cold pack held on the skin for 20 minutes with firm pressure
preguntas.explicacion: Cool water, not ice water, is run over the burn or the part is soaked for 5 to 30 minutes; a clean, cold, wet towel eases the pain. Afterward the area is covered with a dry sterile bandage and protected from pressure and friction. Butter, oil, ice, creams and household remedies do not go on a burn.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Burns", First Aid: Minor burns
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B10 k78 · CMA I.B.9.b · 2027 I.B.8.b · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2B.12 EKB 15

preguntas.pregunta: A clinic phones the laboratory three times in one week because reports reached the wrong provider. Under CLIA, what must the laboratory already have in place for this?
opciones: A system that documents each complaint and identifies problems caused by a breakdown in communication
A system that stores each ordering provider's credentials and verifies them before a report is released
A policy requiring every printed result to be read back by telephone before the report is mailed out
A file of each analyst's competency assessment, reviewed whenever a client questions a reported value
preguntas.explicacion: Two separate standards apply. One obliges the laboratory to document all complaints and problems reported to it, and to investigate when appropriate. The other obliges it to have a system that identifies and documents problems arising from a breakdown in communication between the laboratory and the authorized person who orders or receives results. The quality assessment step then asks whether the fix worked.
preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.B Quality Improvement · NCMA Law and Ethics 12 comply with CLIA

preguntas.pregunta: Which right does a hospitalized patient have over the plan of care?
opciones: To be informed of their status, take part in planning, and refuse treatment
To be informed of their status and to demand any treatment they have read about
To take part in planning only when a family representative is at the bedside
To refuse treatment only after a second physician has documented agreement
preguntas.explicacion: The patient, or their representative where state law allows one, has the right to make informed decisions: to be told their health status, to be involved in care planning and treatment, and to request or refuse treatment. That right explicitly does not become a way to demand services judged medically unnecessary or inappropriate, and no second signature is needed to refuse.
preguntas.subtema: Patient rights · CCMA k215 · CMA E.1.d · RMA I.C.1.e · NCMA EKB 29 · CMAA 3D k32

preguntas.pregunta: A 15-year-old comes for a lipid panel with her mother, who agrees to the draw. Which term describes what the mother gives?
opciones: Informed permission
Informed consent
Pediatric assent
Implied consent
preguntas.explicacion: Children, typically under 18, cannot give informed consent; parents or legal guardians permit the intervention instead, and that process is called informed permission. Assent is what the child may add, valuable when reasonable. The exception to the rule is the legally emancipated minor, who consents alone.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Informed Consent", section Issues of Concern, Children
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2G k43 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7B k216 · CMA E.3.c (both outlines) · RMA I.C.1.a · NCMA 4.7

preguntas.pregunta: A child's tympanogram is flat, with no identifiable peak. What does that suggest?
opciones: Fluid in the middle ear, or a perforation of the tympanic membrane
Normal middle ear function, with the peak simply falling off the scale
Negative middle ear pressure from eustachian tube dysfunction
A sensorineural loss, since the cochlea cannot return the probe tone
preguntas.explicacion: A flat tracing is called type B and usually means middle ear fluid or a perforated eardrum; an ear canal volume above 1.5 cubic centimeters points to a perforation or a ventilation tube. Type A is normal, with the peak between -100 and +100 decapascals. Type C peaks below -100 decapascals and indicates negative pressure with eustachian tube dysfunction.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Hearing Loss Assessment in Children", Evaluation: Tympanometry
preguntas.subtema: CMA I.C.10.d(11)(c) · NCMA 2B.10

preguntas.pregunta: A patient in acute kidney failure has produced no urine at all. Which term names that finding, and how is it built?
opciones: Anuria: a prefix meaning without plus an ending meaning in the urine
Dysuria: a prefix meaning without plus an ending meaning in the urine
Polyuria: a prefix meaning without plus an ending meaning in the urine
Nocturia: a prefix meaning without plus an ending meaning in the urine
preguntas.explicacion: The prefix a- or an- means without or lacking, and the ending -uria means in the urine, so anuria is the absence of urine. The distractors reuse the same ending with other prefixes: dys- is difficult or abnormal, and poly- is many or excessive, which is why polyuria is a large output rather than none.

cardi/o for the heart, aden/o for a vessel, hepat/o for a vein
coron/o for the heart, arthr/o for a vessel, nephr/o for a vein
my/o for the heart, thromb/o for a vessel, splen/o for a vein
preguntas.explicacion: Cardi- and coron- both name the heart, angi- and vasculo- name a blood vessel, and phleb- and ven- name a vein. The roots in the wrong answers belong elsewhere: aden- is a gland, hepat- the liver, arthr- a joint, nephr- the kidney, thromb- a clot and splen- the spleen.

preguntas.pregunta: In an adult finger-prick, why is a 2.2 mm lancet the longest typically used?
opciones: Because the puncture depth should not go beyond 2.4 mm, and pressure makes the puncture deeper than the lancet
Because the puncture depth should not go beyond 2.2 mm, and the lancet must match that limit exactly
Because the skin-to-bone distance on the side of an adult finger averages 2.33 mm
Because lancets longer than 2.2 mm are made only as surgical blades, which the WHO prohibits
preguntas.explicacion: The lancet chosen is slightly shorter than the estimated depth needed, because pressure compresses the skin and the puncture ends up slightly deeper than the lancet length. Since a finger-prick should not go beyond 2.4 mm, a 2.2 mm lancet is the longest typically used. The 2.33 mm figure is the posterior heel of a 3 kg baby, and surgical blades are prohibited for any skin puncture.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 7.1.2 and 7.2.1

preguntas.pregunta: Breast cancer has spread to the lung. Which cells does the pathologist find in the lung tumor?
opciones: Breast cancer cells, because a metastasis keeps the type of the primary tumor
Lung cancer cells, because a metastasis takes the type of the organ it reaches
A mix of both, because a metastasis blends the primary and the new tissue
Neither, because a metastasis is made of scar tissue rather than tumor cells
preguntas.explicacion: Metastasis is the spread of cancer cells from the place where they first formed to another part of the body: the cells break away from the primary tumor, travel through the blood or the lymph system and start a new tumor. The new growth is the same type of cancer as the original, so breast cancer in the lung is still breast cancer.

preguntas.pregunta: A lead wire on the machine is found with frayed insulation. What is done?
opciones: The unit is left unused and the problem is reported at once
The unit is used and the wire is taped up for the rest of the day
The back of the unit is opened so the wire can be replaced
The unit is used for the limb leads until a repair is arranged
preguntas.explicacion: The unit is grounded, so a shock is highly unlikely, but the rule is firm: if a short happens or frayed wiring turns up, the equipment is not used. The cover and the back are never removed by the technician, and the damage is reported straight away.

opciones: Blood-contaminated devices have been implicated in hepatitis B outbreaks
Shared devices lose their calibration and read the glucose far too low
Shared devices carry latex particles from one patient's skin to the next
Shared devices void the manufacturer's warranty on the meter and lancets
preguntas.explicacion: Reusable finger-prick devices and point-of-care instruments such as glucose meters, once contaminated with blood, have been linked to outbreaks of hepatitis B. The rule that follows is plain: common-use items are visibly clean before they touch a patient, and single-use items are not reused.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient is found unresponsive at the bottom of a staircase and a neck injury is suspected. How is the airway opened?
opciones: By pushing the jaw forward without tilting the head or turning the neck
By tilting the head back and lifting the chin with two fingers
By turning the head to one side so that the tongue falls forward
By placing a folded towel under the shoulders to extend the neck
preguntas.explicacion: When a cervical spine injury cannot be ruled out, the jaw is thrust forward and the head is left alone, and the mouth is not allowed to close. The head tilt-chin lift is the standard maneuver only when no spinal injury is suspected. A patient with a possible spinal injury is moved by two people so head and neck do not twist.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks whether electricity will be passed through the body. What is the answer?
opciones: No: the test is painless and no current is sent through
Yes: a small current goes through and may feel like a tingle
Yes: a current is sent only while the chest leads record
No: but the patches themselves can give a mild shock
preguntas.explicacion: The machine listens rather than stimulates: the test is painless and nothing is sent through the body. The electrodes may feel cold when they are first applied, and in rare cases a rash or irritation appears where the patches were, which is worth saying in advance.

preguntas.pregunta: The label on a drum of laboratory reagent is smeared and hard to read. What does the Hazard Communication standard require of the laboratory?
opciones: Labels on incoming containers must not be removed or defaced
Labels may be replaced with the in-house number of the reagent
Labels may be taken off once the sheet is filed in the binder
Labels must be covered with tape until the drum is emptied out
preguntas.explicacion: Laboratories are covered by the Hazard Communication standard in a reduced way, and the first of those duties is that labels on incoming containers of hazardous chemicals are not removed or defaced. The others are keeping the safety data sheets that arrive with shipments and making them readily accessible during each work shift, and giving employees the information and training of paragraph (h). Filing the sheet does not release the container from carrying its own warning.

preguntas.pregunta: How many essential vitamins does the body require, and how are they grouped?
opciones: Thirteen, grouped as fat-soluble and water-soluble
Thirteen, grouped as animal-source and plant-source
Nine, grouped as fat-soluble and water-soluble
Twenty, grouped as essential and conditionally essential
preguntas.explicacion: Thirteen vitamins are essential, meaning the body cannot work properly without them, and they split into two groups by how they dissolve: fat-soluble and water-soluble. Nine is the count of the water-soluble group alone. A few vitamin-like nutrients, choline and carnitine, are also needed but are not counted among the thirteen.

preguntas.pregunta: What separates sterilization from every other level of processing used on patient-care items?
opciones: It destroys or eliminates every form of microbial life, bacterial spores included
It wipes out many or all pathogens on an object but leaves bacterial spores alive
It takes visible soil off an object with water plus a detergent or enzymatic product
It lowers the count enough that the object is safe to handle, use or throw away
preguntas.explicacion: Sterilization is meant as an absolute: nothing microbial survives it, spores included. Disinfection stops short of that, since it is not sporicidal. Cleaning only lifts the visible soil off, and decontamination is what makes a used item safe for staff to handle. They are consecutive steps, not synonyms, and only one of them is absolute.

preguntas.pregunta: A urine specimen for culture is collected into a container with boric acid preservative, and the ward also wants a dipstick from the same cup. What should be expected?
opciones: The dipstick leukocyte reagent may be less sensitive and the initial pH altered, though the bacteria are preserved
The dipstick glucose and urobilinogen may read falsely positive, though the bacteria are preserved for culture
The dipstick leukocyte esterase may read falsely negative, and the culture will fail to grow at any concentration
The dipstick albumin may read falsely positive, and the bacteria will be killed within the first hour of storage
preguntas.explicacion: Boric acid is the preservative commonly used to keep bacteria alive in urine, but it can reduce the sensitivity of the leukocyte reagent on the dipstick and change the initial pH, and in excessive concentration it can even prevent bacterial growth in the sample sent for culture. False-positive glucose and urobilinogen are the formaldehyde pattern, a false-negative leukocyte esterase belongs to mercury salts, and thymol gives false-positive albumin.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Urinalysis", section Interfering Factors (Preservatives)

preguntas.pregunta: A patient needs HLA tissue typing (ACD tube), a CBC and a plasma glucose. Following the WHO table, which tube is filled second?
opciones: The pale yellow ACD tube for HLA typing
The purple EDTA haematology tube for the CBC
The light grey sodium fluoride tube
The dark green sodium heparin tube
preguntas.explicacion: Table 2.3 puts EDTA at position 8, the pale yellow ACD tube for HLA typing, paternity and DNA studies at position 9, and the grey oxalate/fluoride glucose tube at position 10. The purple tube therefore goes first, the ACD tube second and the grey tube last. No heparin tube is ordered here, and it would sit at position 6 in any case.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient who has just received an opioid analgesic becomes very drowsy and breathes slowly. Which class effect is this?
opciones: Respiratory depression, one of the effects opioid receptors produce everywhere
Serotonin syndrome, which follows any single opioid dose within a few minutes
Hyperalgesia from opioids, which shows up with the first dose in most patients
Anticholinergic toxicity, seen as dry mouth, retention and slowed breathing
preguntas.explicacion: Opioid receptors sit inside and outside the nervous system, so the class produces a wide spread of effects: dysphoria or euphoria, sedation, respiratory depression, constipation, bradycardia, nausea, vomiting, itching and pinpoint pupils. Tolerance and hyperalgesia come from long-term use, not from a first dose, and serotonin syndrome needs a serotonergic opioid combined with another serotonergic drug.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Opioid Analgesics", Adverse Effects

preguntas.pregunta: Besides confirming that a vein is suitable, what practical decision does the WHO say locating the vein helps the phlebotomist make?
opciones: The correct size of needle to use
Whether a tourniquet is needed
How many tubes one puncture yields
Which antiseptic to apply
preguntas.explicacion: Step 3 says that the vein should be visible without the tourniquet and that locating it will help in determining the correct needle size; Chapter 3 repeats that the gauge is chosen to fit comfortably into the most prominent vein. The antiseptic is fixed at 70% alcohol for routine draws, and the WHO does not tie the number of tubes to the vein found.

preguntas.pregunta: Setting prions aside, which organisms sit at the top of the resistance scale to chemical germicides?
opciones: Bacterial spores, above coccidia, mycobacteria, small nonlipid viruses, fungi and vegetative bacteria
Mycobacteria, above bacterial spores, coccidia, fungi, vegetative bacteria and small nonlipid viruses
Lipid viruses, above vegetative bacteria, fungi, mycobacteria, coccidia and the bacterial spores
Vegetative bacteria, above fungi, small nonlipid viruses, mycobacteria, coccidia and lipid viruses
preguntas.explicacion: Bacterial spores hold the highest innate resistance of all, and the ladder descends from them through coccidia, mycobacteria, small nonlipid viruses, fungi, vegetative bacteria and finally lipid or medium-sized viruses such as herpes and HIV. Each group resists for its own reason: the spore coat and cortex act as a barrier, and mycobacteria have a waxy wall.

preguntas.pregunta: A resting strip on a young competitive athlete is regular at 52 per minute with normal P waves. How does the material read that?
opciones: As sinus bradycardia, common in athletes and during sleep
As sinus arrhythmia, common in athletes and during sleep
As a junctional rhythm, common in athletes while resting
As a first-degree block, common in athletes while resting
preguntas.explicacion: A slow sinus rhythm turns up as an incidental finding in many healthy adults, and it is described as common in athletes and during sleep, where the vagal tone that slows the sinus node is higher. Every criterion of sinus rhythm still holds except the rate.

preguntas.pregunta: An 84-year-old patient with thin, fragile skin has just finished a recording. How are the electrodes taken off?
opciones: The wires come off first, then each electrode by its tab
The electrodes come off first, then the wires from the tabs
The wires and the electrodes come away together in one pull
The wires stay attached until all the copies have printed
preguntas.explicacion: The lead wires are lifted off the electrodes first, and only then is each electrode removed by pulling gently on its tab; they are thrown away after that single use. The step is done carefully because it can hurt and injure the skin, above all in older patients.

preguntas.pregunta: An ESR is ordered along with a CBC. Which tube is used for the ESR specimen, and can it be shared with other tests?
opciones: It goes in a black-top ESR tube with 3.2% citrate or a lavender EDTA tube, and is not shared with other tests
It goes in the same lavender EDTA tube as the CBC, and the leftover blood is used for the sedimentation
It goes in a light blue citrate tube filled to 90%, and it can be shared with any PT ordered on the same draw
It goes in a plain red tube, and the serum is transferred to the Westergren tube in the laboratory
preguntas.explicacion: Blood is usually collected in a black-top ESR vacuum tube containing 3.2% sodium citrate; whole blood in a lavender EDTA tube is also acceptable, and the sample must stay in its own ESR-designated tube because of the volume the test needs, so it cannot be shared. The test is run on anticoagulated whole blood, never on serum.

preguntas.pregunta: Which combination of vital signs makes up Cushing's triad?
opciones: Irregular respirations, high blood pressure and a slow pulse
Irregular respirations, low blood pressure and a fast pulse
Rapid shallow respirations, high blood pressure and a fast pulse
Rapid deep respirations, low blood pressure and a slow pulse
preguntas.explicacion: The triad is irregular breathing, hypertension and bradycardia, and it is the body's answer to rising intracranial pressure. It signals that herniation of the brain is near and calls for immediate action, which is why the three values are read together and not one at a time.

preguntas.pregunta: How quickly must an employer report a work-related fatality, and a work-related inpatient hospitalization, to OSHA?
opciones: A fatality within 8 hours; a hospitalization within 24 hours
A fatality within 24 hours; a hospitalization within 8 hours
Both within 72 hours, by telephone to the area office
Both within 60 days, on the OSHA 300A summary
preguntas.explicacion: Under the recordkeeping rule updated in 2015, as summarized in OSHA's Hospitals eTool, employers report every work-related fatality within 8 hours of learning of it, and every work-related inpatient hospitalization, amputation or loss of an eye within 24 hours. Reports can be made by phone to the nearest area office, to the 24-hour OSHA hotline at 1-800-321-6742, or through the online serious event form. The 300A summary is an annual posting, not a reporting channel, and 60 days is the HIPAA breach notification limit.

preguntas.pregunta: Which of these is counted as a fall risk factor in an older adult, defined by a specific number?
opciones: Polypharmacy, which is defined as taking more than four medications
Polypharmacy, which is defined as taking more than two medications
Age, which starts to count as a risk factor from 65 years upward
Body weight, which counts as a risk factor from 30 kilograms upward
preguntas.explicacion: The risk list is headed by a history of falls, impaired balance and reduced muscle strength, and it includes polypharmacy, meaning more than four medications, or the use of psychoactive drugs. Age counts as a risk factor from 80 years upward, not 65. Every added risk factor roughly doubles the one-year risk, from 8% with none to as much as 78% with four.

The operations in their work area where hazardous chemicals are present
The measures they can take to protect themselves from those chemicals
The requirements of the Hazard Communication standard itself

preguntas.pregunta: A patient is about to be moved from the bed onto a stretcher. How is the stretcher set up?
opciones: Brought against the bed slightly lower than it, with its own brakes locked
Brought against the bed slightly higher than it, with its own brakes locked
Set at a 45-degree angle to the bed, with the brakes deliberately released
Left at the foot of the bed until the slider board is under the patient
preguntas.explicacion: The bed is raised or lowered to a safe working height, its brakes go on and the rails come down; the stretcher then comes alongside a little lower than the bed and its brakes are set too, so the patient slides slightly downhill. preguntas.pregunta: A patient in the waiting room stands up clutching the throat with both hands and cannot speak. What does this show?
opciones: The universal sign of a blocked airway, which calls for immediate first aid
The first sign of a heart attack, which calls for rest and for chewed aspirin
A panic attack with hyperventilation, which calls for slow, coached breathing
A seizure that begins with a cry, which calls for protecting the head
preguntas.explicacion: Grabbing the neck with both hands is the universal choking sign. Sudden respiratory distress with coughing, gagging or stridor, an inability to speak or cry, and cyanosis point to a foreign body in the airway and call for action, because severe hypoxia leads to loss of consciousness within minutes.

Once, since $1,736 is a yearly deductible in the way the Part B deductible is
Twice, but at $283 each time, which is the figure the yearly deductible uses
Not at all, since days one to sixty of an inpatient stay carry no charge
preguntas.explicacion: The 2026 Part A deductible is $1,736 for each inpatient benefit period before Original Medicare begins to pay, and there is no limit on how many benefit periods a person may have in one year, so the deductible can fall due more than once. preguntas.pregunta: A housekeeper handles regulated waste bags twice a week, while every phlebotomist is exposed daily. How does the exposure determination list them?
opciones: Phlebotomists as a classification where all are exposed; the housekeeper with the task
Both as classifications where all employees are exposed, with no list of tasks needed
Only the phlebotomists, because the housekeeper wears gloves for that one task
Both by name in the medical record, which is where exposed workers are recorded
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (c)(2)(i) asks for three lists: job classifications in which every employee has occupational exposure, job classifications in which only some do, and the tasks or groups of related tasks that expose the people in that second group. preguntas.pregunta: A patient's chart notes a central venous line. According to the WHO, who may draw specimens from it, and what caveat applies?

Any phlebotomist trained in vacuum systems; the results are equivalent to those of a peripheral draw
No one; central lines may never be used for laboratory specimens under any protocol
Only laboratory technicians; they must draw a non-additive discard tube first
preguntas.explicacion: Step 3 says nursing staff and physicians may access central venous lines for specimens following protocols, but that specimens from central lines carry a risk of contamination or erroneous laboratory results. preguntas.pregunta: A red top tube with no anticoagulant has been filled. How long may the specimen need before it is spun?

Usually two to three minutes, and in some specimens up to ten minutes
Usually thirty seconds, the same contact time asked of an alcohol swab
Usually twenty-four hours, the interval allowed for a coagulation test
preguntas.explicacion: The red top carries no anticoagulant: contact with the tube wall sets off clotting, and the specimen is normally left ten to fifteen minutes before centrifugation, although clotting time varies and can reach a full hour. preguntas.pregunta: Which practice is consistent with HIPAA security guidance for email communication with patients?
opciones: Encrypt all emails, keep the patient's name out of the subject line, and send the minimum information
Use a personal commercial email account so the message is not stored on the institution's servers
Put the patient's name in the subject line so the message is easy to locate later
Attach the full record whenever a patient asks a question, to avoid follow-up messages
preguntas.explicacion: Institutions should set email rules: the patient's name is left out of the subject line, the address is verified, only the bare minimum of information is transmitted, a standard disclaimer closes every message, all emails are encrypted, and staff never use personal or commercial accounts for patient communication, only the system the institution provides. Similar rules govern faxes, which sit in a secure area with a cover sheet explaining what to do if the fax is misdirected. Sending a whole record in reply to a question violates the minimum necessary principle.

preguntas.pregunta: In the WHO blood spill procedure, which disinfectant is applied after the area has been cleaned with water and detergent?
opciones: Sodium hypochlorite 0.5 percent, a 1:10 bleach dilution prepared daily
Sodium hypochlorite 5.25 percent, used undiluted straight from the bottle
70 percent alcohol, the same solution used to prepare the skin
Sodium hypochlorite 0.05 percent, a 1:100 dilution, kept for a week
preguntas.explicacion: After the glass is removed with tongs, the fluid absorbed with paper towels and the area wiped with water and detergent until visibly clean, the spill area is saturated again with sodium hypochlorite 0.5 percent, which is 10,000 parts per million of available chlorine, made as a 1:10 dilution of 5.25 percent household bleach and prepared fresh each day. Undiluted bleach is not the instruction, 70 percent alcohol is WHO's skin antiseptic, and a solution kept for a week defeats the daily preparation rule. Gloves come off last, followed by handwashing and an incident record.

preguntas.pregunta: Before a fingerstick glucose, an assistant swabs the fingertip with alcohol and lances it while the skin is still wet. Why does the guidance advise against this?
opciones: Residual alcohol can dilute the drop or cause hemolysis, so the site must dry completely first
Alcohol left on the skin makes the meter read falsely high, because ethanol is measured as glucose
Alcohol is not recommended at all; the guidance calls for washing with cold water and no antiseptic
Wet alcohol stings on puncture, which is the only concern, so the result itself is not affected
preguntas.explicacion: The site is washed and dried thoroughly, using warm water to improve blood flow. Alcohol swabs are not routinely required, but if one is used the skin must be allowed to dry completely before lancing, because residual alcohol can dilute the sample or hemolyze it and affect the reading. Discomfort is not the point; sample integrity is. Cold water is not what the procedure describes.

preguntas.pregunta: Documentation reaches the billing team four or five days after each visit. Against the benchmark for the lag from service to charge entry, where does that practice stand?
opciones: Above the benchmark, which is two days or fewer from the date of service
Below the benchmark, which is seven days or fewer from the date of service
At the benchmark, which is five days or fewer from the date of service
Above the benchmark, which is twenty-one days from the date of service
preguntas.explicacion: The lag from care to charge is benchmarked at two days or less. preguntas.pregunta: Hydrochlorothiazide is prescribed for primary hypertension. Which statement matches the approved use of this class?

It is approved for hypertension only once a loop diuretic has failed at a full dose
It is approved for edema only, so any use in hypertension is entirely off-label
It is approved for hypertension only in patients who also have chronic kidney disease
preguntas.explicacion: Hydrochlorothiazide and chlorthalidone are approved for primary hypertension and are used either on their own or alongside other antihypertensives to lift the response in severe cases. Section 2, which also gives the signal word and the hazard statements
Section 15, which also gives the regulations that apply to the product
Section 16, which also gives the date the sheet was last revised

preguntas.pregunta: A cleaning solution splashes onto a patient's arm and burns the skin. How is the area flushed?
opciones: With cool running water for 15 minutes or more, after dry powder is brushed off
With cool running water for 30 seconds, and then a neutralizing rinse
With warm soapy water for 5 minutes, scrubbing until the pain settles
With a wet compress held in place, so that the chemical is not spread
preguntas.explicacion: Any dry chemical is brushed off first, and clothing and jewelry come off; then the skin is flushed with cool running water for 15 minutes or longer. opciones: Place it in a second container that prevents leakage and is labeled or color-coded
Wipe the tube with disinfectant and transport it in the usual rack with a new label
Discard the specimen as regulated waste and request a new draw from the patient
Place it in a puncture-resistant container, which is required for every leaking tube

Puncture resistance is added by (d)(2)(xiii)(C) only when the specimen could puncture the primary container, not for every leak. That it store every recorded visit for six years so the practice can produce it later

Only the notes written by the clinician who owns the practice where the record is kept
Only the data elements a health plan needs to adjudicate a claim for the encounter
Only the documents the patient has personally uploaded through the practice portal

opciones: The revised Face, Legs, Activity, Cry, Consolability tool for young children
The Behavioral Pain Scale, built for adults who are sedated or unconscious
The Nonverbal Pain Scale, built for intubated adults in intensive care units
The visual analogue scale, on which a mark is placed along a printed line
preguntas.explicacion: Observational tools take the place of self-report in patients who cannot speak for themselves. The tourniquet is still mandatory, applied about 3 inches above the site
A tighter tourniquet is used, because large veins collapse under vacuum
The tourniquet is applied only after the first tube has been filled
