preguntas.pregunta: A patient hands in a sputum cup holding a few milliliters of clear, watery fluid from the mouth. What should the medical assistant do?
opciones: Ask for a new specimen coughed up deeply, because thin, clear material is rejected
Send it as it is, because any material from the mouth still carries airway organisms
Add sterile saline to the cup and send it, because the volume is what was too small
Refrigerate it and send it the next morning, when a fresh specimen can be added to it
preguntas.explicacion: Sputum is what comes up from the air passages on a deep cough, not spit. 1 kilogram equals 1.2 pounds
1 kilogram equals 16 pounds
1 kilogram equals 10 pounds

preguntas.pregunta: A 6-month-old was at the 75th percentile for weight, moved to the 25th at 9 months and lower at 12 months. Why does that worry the provider?
opciones: The measurements are no longer tracking one curve, which matters more than any single value
The 25th percentile is below the normal range, so a single value there is the concern
Weight percentiles are expected to climb steadily, so any fall at all is abnormal
The child has crossed into the band that defines undernutrition on the charts
preguntas.explicacion: What raises concern on a chart is a measurement that stops following its own line, or one that stays below the 10th or above the 90th percentile for the age. preguntas.pregunta: A bystander with no duty to act stops to help at a roadside crash. What does the Good Samaritan rule say about that?
opciones: Taking charge assumes a duty to use reasonable care from then on
Taking charge carries no duty at all, since the help was voluntary
Taking charge creates liability only if payment was later accepted
Taking charge is barred unless the helper is licensed in that state
preguntas.explicacion: Under the rule, someone who provides services for another, whether free or for pay, assumes a duty to use reasonable care, and can be held liable if their negligence injures the person helped or a foreseeable third party. preguntas.pregunta: Which four elements must a patient prove to win a medical malpractice suit?
opciones: Duty, breach of duty (negligence), causation and damages
Assault, battery, negligence and abandonment
Intent, foreseeability, restitution and injunction
Duty, consent, documentation and insurance coverage
preguntas.explicacion: A simple mistake is not malpractice by itself. The plaintiff must establish four elements: a duty to the patient, meaning the clinician was responsible for that patient's care; a breach of that duty, the negligence, measured against the standard of care; causation, that the act or omission produced the bad outcome; and damages, the loss for which compensation is sought. The tort pathway states it the same way, duty, breach, proximate cause, damages. Assault, battery and abandonment are separate torts, and restitution and injunctions are remedies.

preguntas.pregunta: Which grains naturally contain the gluten that a patient with celiac disease must avoid?

preguntas.pregunta: Which feature separates a hypertensive emergency from a hypertensive urgency?

Acute organ damage is absent in the emergency and present in the urgency
The emergency is defined by a systolic reading above 140 mm Hg
The urgency is defined by a diastolic reading above 120 mm Hg
preguntas.explicacion: A hypertensive crisis is a severe, sudden rise in blood pressure. It counts as an emergency when acute hypertension-mediated organ damage comes with it, and as an urgency when it does not. Numbers such as 180 over 120 are conventions rather than firm lines, and how fast the pressure rose can matter more than how high it is.

preguntas.pregunta: A sling is being applied after a splint. How should the arm sit inside it?
opciones: Elbow at about a right angle, with the hand higher than the elbow
Elbow at about a right angle, with the hand lower than the elbow
Elbow fully extended, with the whole forearm resting along the cloth
Elbow at about a right angle, with the wrist left outside the cloth
preguntas.explicacion: The elbow goes at the point of the triangle and the wrist along the middle of its lower edge, and the sling is adjusted so the hand rides above the elbow, which limits swelling, with the elbow bent to roughly ninety degrees. The knot is tied at the side of the neck and padded. The splint always goes on before the sling.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: How to make a sling — First Aid
preguntas.subtema: CMA I.C.2.d · NCMA 2B.13 · RMA III.H.3.a.iv

preguntas.pregunta: What should a patient be taught to do when a cough or a sneeze is coming on?
opciones: Cover the mouth and nose with a tissue or the inside of the elbow
Cover the mouth and nose with the palm of the hand, then wash it
Turn the head to one side and cough without covering the mouth at all
Cover the mouth only, since the nose does not release germs when coughing
preguntas.explicacion: Germs travel from person to person by several routes, and respiratory droplets are one of them. Both mouth and nose are covered, with a tissue or with the inside of the elbow, and hand washing follows any cough, sneeze or nose blowing so nothing is carried onward on the hands.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Germs and Hygiene — How can I protect myself and others from germs?

preguntas.pregunta: An Rh negative mother delivered a healthy Rh positive first baby and received no RhoGAM. What is the concern for a second Rh positive pregnancy?
opciones: Her anti-Rh antibodies could cross the placenta and destroy the fetus's red cells
Her anti-A and anti-B antibodies could cross the placenta if the baby is type AB
The first baby's Rh+ cells remain in her blood and agglutinate her own cells
A second Rh+ fetus would sensitize her only if it were also ABO incompatible
preguntas.explicacion: A first pregnancy is usually safe because fetal cells rarely cross the placenta, but at birth the Rh negative parent can be exposed to the baby's Rh positive cells and begin making anti-Rh antibodies. In a later Rh positive pregnancy those antibodies can cross the placenta and hemolyze fetal red cells, causing hemolytic disease of the newborn, which ranges from mild anemia to fetal death.
preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.6 Blood Typing, Rh Blood Groups

preguntas.pregunta: A patient's spouse comes to the front desk, with other patients waiting behind him, and asks why the patient is here today.
opciones: Ask the patient whether he objects, and talk away from the desk
Answer at the desk, since a spouse needs no written authorization
Refuse any contact until the spouse produces a signed authorization
Send the spouse to the laboratory, which released the result
preguntas.explicacion: Two rules meet here. Information may be shared with a spouse, parent, guardian or other caregiver involved in the person's care without a formal written agreement, but when other people are present the patient is asked first whether there is any objection. And the conversation itself does not belong at a counter or in a hallway: anything specific waits until the patient is in a private room, with only what is relevant said out loud.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Clinical Significance: HIPAA and Communication With Patients
preguntas.subtema: At the front desk · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k213 · CMA II.E.2 · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k35

preguntas.pregunta: How does the American Diabetes Association define 'fasting' for a fasting plasma glucose?
opciones: No caloric intake at all for at least 8 hours
No food or drink, including water, for 12 hours
No solid food for 8 hours; sweetened drinks allowed
No caloric intake at all for at least 24 hours
preguntas.explicacion: The ADA diagnostic criteria define fasting as no caloric intake for at least 8 hours, with a fasting plasma glucose of 126 mg/dL (7.0 mmol/L) or higher meeting the threshold for diabetes. Water carries no calories and is allowed; sweetened drinks do carry calories. Twelve hours is the general recommendation for morning sampling, and 24 hours is the alcohol-free window.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Blood Glucose Monitoring", section Diagnostic Criteria
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2K k46 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E1 k125 · RMA III.C.4.e · NCMA 2C.2

preguntas.pregunta: A newborn's lips and fingertips look blue and the note reads cyanosis. Which color does that word part name?
opciones: Blue, from the color prefix cyano-
Red, from the color prefix erythro-
White, from the color prefix leuko-
Black, from the color prefix melano-
preguntas.explicacion: The color word parts run through much of the vocabulary: cyano- is blue, erythro- red, leuko- white, melano- black, xantho- yellow and chloro- green. That is why red cells are erythrocytes, white cells leukocytes and the skin pigment melanin, and why blue skin is recorded as cyanosis.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix A: Word Parts and What They Mean, Color
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k11 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.a) · RMA I.B.1.a · CMAA 1 k9 · NCMA 1.2

preguntas.pregunta: Which content is the notice of privacy practices required to include?
opciones: The individual's rights, how to exercise them, and whom to contact to make a complaint
The fee schedule for copies of records and the practice's policy on missed appointments
A list of every workforce member authorized to open the electronic health record system
The names of the business associates that handle claims and transcription for the practice
preguntas.explicacion: The notice must be in plain language and describe how the entity may use and disclose PHI, the individual's rights and how to exercise them including how to complain, the entity's legal duties including its obligation to protect privacy, and whom to contact for more information. It must carry an effective date, and it must be revised and redistributed promptly when privacy practices change materially.
preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Notice of Privacy Practices for Protected Health Information: Content of the Notice
preguntas.subtema: Notice content · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA III.E.1 · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 5D k64 · NCMA 4.3

preguntas.pregunta: A hospital hires per diem and contract phlebotomists for a busy season. How does the bloodborne pathogens standard treat them?
opciones: They are covered, and the plan must describe how the standard is met for them
They are covered after ninety days, the period allowed for a new hire's training
They are covered by the staffing agency's plan alone, never by the host facility
They fall outside the standard, since the exposure determination lists job titles
preguntas.explicacion: The model plan states plainly that part-time, temporary, contract and per diem employees fall under the bloodborne pathogens standard, and that the written plan should say how the requirements will be met for them. Nothing in paragraph (c) sets a waiting period: training comes at the time of initial assignment under (g)(2)(ii)(A), and the hepatitis B vaccine within ten working days of that assignment under (f)(2)(i). The exposure determination is a list of job classifications and tasks, so it does not exclude anyone by employment status.
preguntas.fuente: OSHA 3186, Model Exposure Control Plan, Employee Exposure Determination (note); OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(c)(2)(i)

preguntas.pregunta: How many characters can an ICD-10-CM code have?
opciones: Three to seven, with all categories being three characters long
Three to five, with the sixth and seventh reserved for inpatient use
Five exactly, in the same way procedure codes carry five digits
Seven exactly, since the seventh character is required on every code
preguntas.explicacion: In the tabular list all categories have three characters; subcategories have four or five, and codes may run to three, four, five, six or seven characters, each level of subdivision adding specificity. A three-character category with no further subdivision is itself a code. The seventh character is required only where the category calls for it, and five digits describe Level I procedure codes instead.
preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026, Section I.A.2

preguntas.pregunta: What happens to the respiratory rate over the first two years of life?
opciones: It drops from a median near 44 at birth to about 26 during the second year
It drops from a median near 60 at birth to about 40 during the second year
It holds near 30 through the whole period and only falls once the child walks
It climbs from a median near 20 at birth to about 30 during the second year
preguntas.explicacion: Children breathe faster than adults, and the rate falls as they grow: the median goes from around 44 breaths a minute at birth to about 26 in the second year of life. That is why a count that would be alarming in an adult may be ordinary in an infant, and why the value is read against the child's age.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Physiology, Respiratory Rate", Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A7 k50 · CMA I.A.1.h · RMA III.E.3 Respiration d · NCMA 2B.6

preguntas.pregunta: A nurse tells the phlebotomist that the patient in bed 12 is the one who needs the draw. Under the Joint Commission International patient identification goal, why is that not enough?
opciones: The room number or location cannot be used as an identifier; at least two identifiers such as name and birth date are needed
Only the bar-coded wristband counts as an identifier, so the nurse's statement must be confirmed by scanning it
The location is acceptable as one identifier, provided a second identifier such as the ordering physician's name is added
Two staff members must independently confirm the bed number before a specimen can be collected
preguntas.explicacion: The first international patient safety goal requires at least two ways of identifying the patient, for example name, identification number, birth date or a bar-coded wristband, and it excludes the room number or location outright. The wristband is one valid option, not the only one; the physician's name identifies the order, not the patient; and a second witness does not turn a location into an identifier.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Managing the pre- and post-analytical phases of the total testing process" (Ann Lab Med 2012, PMC3255486), section 3.1, IPSG 1
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 k89 · PBT III.B · CCMA 3E k124 · NCMA 2C.14 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.a

preguntas.pregunta: Which range is accepted as the normal body temperature of a resting adult?
opciones: 36.5 to 37.5 °C (97.7 to 99.5 °F), around an average of 37.0 °C (98.6 °F)
36.0 to 37.0 °C (96.8 to 98.6 °F), around an average of 36.5 °C (97.7 °F)
37.0 to 38.0 °C (98.6 to 100.4 °F), around an average of 37.5 °C (99.5 °F)
35.5 to 36.5 °C (95.9 to 97.7 °F), around an average of 36.0 °C (96.8 °F)
preguntas.explicacion: The figure everyone quotes, 37.0 °C or 98.6 °F, is an average and not a fixed value: the accepted reference band runs from 36.5 to 37.5 °C (97.7 to 99.5 °F). The hypothalamus holds core temperature inside that narrow band. A single reading at either edge is normal, so it is compared with the patient's own baseline.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Vital Sign Assessment", Clinical Significance: Temperature
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k52 · CMA I.A.1.d · RMA III.E.3 Temperature c · NCMA 2B.6

preguntas.pregunta: What do front-line staff need for a service recovery program to work?
opciones: Authority to settle complaints without prior approval
A script to read out to every dissatisfied patient
A manager present at each complaint conversation
A written record signed by the patient afterward
preguntas.explicacion: Complaints usually land on front-line staff, who often lack the resources to repair a system problem. What they need is clarity about how far their authority reaches without a manager's approval, defined courses of action for the most frequent complaints, minimal red tape, and named backup for the hard cases.
preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, CAHPS Ambulatory Care Improvement Guide, Section 6.P Service Recovery Programs
preguntas.subtema: Service recovery · CCMA 6J k207 · CMAA 2B k16 · NCMA EKB 22

preguntas.pregunta: A trainee scrubs for ten minutes before a sterile procedure, believing longer is safer. What is the effect?
opciones: No added benefit, and more risk of irritating the skin
A longer lasting effect on the resident skin flora
The same effect as a rub, which needs no drying time
A shorter effect, since the antiseptic is rinsed away
preguntas.explicacion: The usual scrub with an antimicrobial agent runs about two to six minutes, following the manufacturer and the institution. Scrub times of ten minutes or more add nothing and raise the risk of skin irritation, and irritated skin is harder to keep clean. Some institutions use shorter staged techniques or an alcohol-based formulation instead, applied as the manufacturer directs and left to dry completely before sterile gloves go on.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Hand Hygiene in Clinical Practice", Technique or Treatment: Surgical Hand Antisepsis

preguntas.pregunta: A patient is switched from a brand-name tablet to its approved generic. What must the generic match?
opciones: The active ingredient, the strength, form and route, and it must be bioequivalent
The active and the inactive ingredients as well, colour and shape of the tablet
The price the brand is sold at, because the FDA sets what a generic may charge
The clinical trials of the brand, which the generic maker has to run over again
preguntas.explicacion: An approved generic works the same way and carries the same benefits and risks as the brand. The applicant has to show that the active ingredient is the same, that strength, dosage form and route of administration match, that manufacturing meets the same standards, that the label is the same apart from certain exceptions, and that the product is bioequivalent. The FDA reviews before approval and inspects the plants.
preguntas.fuente: FDA, Generic Drug Facts: Generic medicines work the same as brand-name medicines
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1C k24 · CMA 2027 I.D.1.f · NCMA 1.4

preguntas.pregunta: What is a provisional certification, and how long does it last?
opciones: A placeholder for those not yet eligible, valid for twelve months
A placeholder for those not yet eligible, valid for twenty-four months
A temporary credential for candidates who failed once, valid for a year
A temporary credential granted while a background check is completed
preguntas.explicacion: A provisional certification is a placeholder that lets someone sit the exam close to finishing training even though the eligibility requirements — a high school diploma, a GED or an equivalent — are not met yet. It expires twelve months after the examination date, and if it lapses before the person converts it, the exam has to be taken again. Recertification and reinstatement do not apply to it.
preguntas.fuente: NHA Candidate Handbook (2026), Converting Provisional Certification to Full Certification
preguntas.subtema: Professional development · CCMA 7C · NCMA 4.6 · CMAA 3G k47

preguntas.pregunta: An unexpected outage has kept the record system down for a day and a half. What does the guidance ask the organization to do afterwards?
opciones: Review it in depth with root-cause or failure modes analysis, as a group
Report it to the certifying body that tested the record system's software
Repeat the yearly downtime drill within the month that follows the outage
Rebuild the disaster recovery plan from scratch before the system restarts
preguntas.explicacion: Unexpected downtimes lasting more than 24 hours are treated as learning material. The organization convenes clinicians and technical staff together to look at the event and how it was handled, identify possible root causes with a structured method, and decide what would prevent or soften the next one.
preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, SAFER Guide: Contingency Planning, Recommended Practice 3.3

preguntas.pregunta: A patient is diagnosed with polycythemia. What is the main drawback of the condition?
opciones: Higher blood viscosity, so the heart circulates blood with more effort
Too little oxygen delivered directly to the tissues by the red cells
Loss of the plasma buffers that keep the pH between 7.35 and 7.45
A hematocrit that falls below the 36 percent lower limit
preguntas.explicacion: Polycythemia is an overproduction of red cells, and its primary problem is not a failure to deliver oxygen but the increased viscosity of the blood, which makes it harder for the heart to move it. The hematocrit rises, not falls, in polycythemia, and the plasma buffers are unrelated. Viscosity is the property that makes honey flow more slowly than water.
preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.3 Erythrocytes, Hemoglobin; and 18.1 An Overview of Blood, Characteristics of Blood

preguntas.pregunta: Which statement matches what the Dietary Guidelines say about grains in a healthy pattern?
opciones: At least half of the grains eaten should be whole grains
At least a quarter of the grains eaten should be whole grains
Whole grains should replace refined grains completely
Grains are counted in cups, like fruits and vegetables
preguntas.explicacion: Among the core elements of a healthy pattern, grains carry the instruction that at least half of them be whole grain. Refined grains are not forbidden, so a complete swap overstates the rule. Grains are measured in ounce-equivalents; cups are the unit for fruits, vegetables and dairy.

preguntas.pregunta: Two isolation gowns carry different fluid barrier levels. What do those levels come from?
opciones: A four-level standard for medical gowns, from the lowest barrier up
The number of layers of fabric the manufacturer sewed together
The quality level that also grades gloves for micro-perforation
The hazardous materials scale that runs from level A down to D
preguntas.explicacion: Medical gowns are graded against a published standard for medical gowns that sets four levels of fluid barrier protection, and separate guidance sets gown standards for handling hazardous drugs. Choosing well means matching the level to the setting, sterile gowns for surgery and non-sterile ones for contact exposure. The acceptable quality level is a glove measure, and levels A through D are the hazardous materials scale, where level A is the most protective.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Personal Protective Equipment", Issues of Concern: Types of PPE

preguntas.pregunta: After filling three tubes at the bedside, a phlebotomist carries them to the nurses' station and labels them there. Which requirement was broken?
opciones: NPSG.01.01.01 EP 2: label specimen containers in the presence of the patient
NPSG.01.01.01 EP 1: use at least two identifiers when collecting any specimens
NPSG.02.03.01: report critical results within the established time frame
NPSG.07.01.01: follow the current CDC or WHO hand hygiene guidelines
preguntas.explicacion: Goal 1 has two elements of performance. EP 1 is about the identifiers themselves; EP 2 says that containers for blood and other specimens are labelled in the presence of the patient. Walking unlabelled tubes away from the bedside defeats EP 2 even if the identification at the bedside was perfect. StatPearls makes the same point: identify and label the tubes with the patient present.

preguntas.pregunta: Why must the fluid used for ear irrigation be at body temperature?
opciones: Fluid that is too cold or too hot provokes dizziness through the semicircular canal
Fluid that is too cold or too hot hardens the cerumen and blocks the canal further
Fluid at body temperature dissolves keratin, which is what cerumen is made of
Fluid at body temperature keeps the tympanic membrane from becoming translucent
preguntas.explicacion: The lateral semicircular canal lies close to the ear canal, so water off body temperature sets off vertigo and nystagmus. Warm water drives nystagmus toward the same side and cold water toward the opposite side, remembered as cold-opposite, warm-same. Transient vertigo, hearing loss or tinnitus after irrigation usually trace back to the temperature.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Ear Irrigation", Anatomy and Physiology
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B9 k76 · CMA I.C.2.b · NCMA 2B.17

preguntas.pregunta: A trainee argues that a mislabelled tube is just paperwork, since the analyser will still give a correct number. Which published figures answer that?
opciones: Half of transfusion deaths trace to identification, and 1 in 18 such errors harms
A tenth of transfusion deaths trace to identification, and 1 in 100 such errors harms
Half of transfusion deaths trace to identification, but no such error has harmed
A quarter of transfusion deaths trace to labelling, and 1 in 3 such errors harms
preguntas.explicacion: Of all the steps before the analysis, collection is arguably the most critical, because an identification error sends the right number to the wrong person. Up to 50 % of transfusion-related deaths follow an identification error, mislabelled blood specimens can end in a haemolytic transfusion reaction, and as many as one in eighteen identification errors leads to patient harm.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Managing the pre- and post-analytical phases of the total testing process" (Ann Lab Med 2012, PMC3255486), section 3.1

preguntas.pregunta: A chart holds an advance directive that mentions CPR. Is that the same as a DNR order?
opciones: No: a directive is a legal document, and a DNR is a medical order
No: a directive covers intubation, while a DNR covers only medication
Yes: any written mention of CPR in the chart operates as a DNR order
Yes: once the directive is scanned in, the code status changes to DNR
preguntas.explicacion: Advance directives are legal documents, not medical orders, so a directive that mentions resuscitation is not equivalent to a do-not-resuscitate or do-not-intubate order. The team has to draw the patient's preference out specifically and turn it into an order signed by the provider. On a MOLST or POLST form those same wishes are already written as orders.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Do Not Resuscitate", Function
preguntas.subtema: Medical directives · CCMA 7D k217 · CMA E.8.a-b (E.7.a from 2027) · RMA I.C.7 · NCMA 4.2

preguntas.pregunta: Under NPSG.01.01.01, which of the following may never be used as a patient identifier?
opciones: The room number or bed location
The telephone number on file
An assigned identification number
Any other person-specific identifier
preguntas.explicacion: The rationale for the goal lists what counts: the individual's name, an assigned identification number, a telephone number, or some other identifier that belongs to that person. EP 1 adds the one exclusion that examiners like to test: the patient's room number or physical location is not an identifier, because it belongs to the bed, not to the person.

preguntas.pregunta: Why are 3 separate stool specimens recommended for an ova and parasite examination?
opciones: Parasites are not shed in the stool every day, so several samples raise the chance of finding them
Each specimen is examined for a different infection: amebiasis, giardiasis or strongyloidiasis
The first specimen is used for culture, the second for the smear and the third for molecular testing
The specimens are pooled to reach the 8 to 10 mL that the microscope smear requires
preguntas.explicacion: Parasites and their eggs may be absent from the stool on a given day, so collecting several specimens over a few days makes the examination more sensitive; three different specimens are the usual recommendation. In the laboratory a small smear of each is placed on a slide and examined under the microscope, and molecular tests may be added. The 8 to 10 mL figure is the volume of each sputum specimen for tuberculosis.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Stool ova and parasites exam (003756), Why the Test is Performed; and MedlinePlus, Lab Tests: Ova and Parasite Test, What happens during an ova and parasite test?

preguntas.pregunta: Tourniquets have been found contaminated with methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus. By which two routes does that happen?
opciones: Poor hand hygiene by the phlebotomist and reuse of a contaminated band
Poor hand hygiene by the patient and storage of the band in a closed tray
Reuse of a contaminated band and application over a sleeve rather than skin
Poor hand hygiene by the phlebotomist and washing the band between patients
preguntas.explicacion: Up to a quarter of tourniquets have been found carrying this organism, and the two causes named are the phlebotomist's lack of hand hygiene and the reuse of bands that are already contaminated. That is why a disposable band is preferred and why gloves go on before the band.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.1.4, Avoidance of contaminated phlebotomy equipment

preguntas.pregunta: Which mechanism is described for winged steel needles that carry a safety feature?
opciones: A needle-locking mechanism that also prevents the set being reused
A blunting mechanism that dulls the tip once the last tube is filled
A colour change in the tubing that shows the set has been used once
A hinged shield activated by pressing the wings against each other
preguntas.explicacion: Winged steel needles with a passive or an active safety feature use a needle-locking mechanism that cuts the risk of a stick and stops reuse, and they make the transfer of blood safer when a syringe is used. Joined to vacuum tubes, they still need the first tube to be additive-free or discarded.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Annex C, Table C.1, Winged steel needles with safety mechanism

preguntas.pregunta: What share of needlestick injuries did older studies blame on recapping, and what does current hospital surveillance show?
opciones: Between 10% and 25% then; about 5% in the surveillance hospitals now
Between 40% and 60% then; about 20% in the surveillance hospitals now
About 5% then; between 10% and 25% in the surveillance hospitals now
Between 10% and 25% then; none at all since the standard prohibited it
preguntas.explicacion: Older studies traced ten to twenty-five percent of needlestick injuries to recapping a used needle. Recapping by hand has been discouraged for years and is prohibited by the bloodborne pathogens standard unless no alternative exists, yet it still causes about five percent of the injuries counted in surveillance hospitals. The share fell; it did not disappear, and that is the point of the rule.

preguntas.pregunta: During a child's venipuncture, why does the second adult grasp the child's wrist palm-up?
opciones: It anchors the shoulder, and the firm grasp acts as a tourniquet
It keeps the fingers open so the veins of the hand stay visible
It warms the forearm, which lifts the flow of blood sevenfold
It frees the elbow, which the phlebotomist then holds instead
preguntas.explicacion: The immobiliser reaches across the child and grasps the wrist palm-up: reaching across anchors the child's shoulder and stops twisting or rocking, while the firm grasp on the wrist gives the phlebotomist a tourniquet. The immobiliser's other, outstretched hand holds the elbow. Keeping the child warm is a separate measure that may raise the flow.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), section 6.2.2, Preparation

preguntas.pregunta: Tests are ordered to learn how far a cancer has spread from where it started. What is that process called?
opciones: Staging, which is done to plan the best treatment
Screening, which is done to plan the best treatment
Remission, which is done to plan the best treatment
Grading, which is done to plan the best treatment
preguntas.explicacion: Staging is performing exams and tests to learn the extent of a cancer in the body, above all whether it has left the place where it formed, and the stage drives the treatment plan. Screening is different: it checks for disease in someone with no symptoms at all, as with mammograms, colonoscopy and the Pap and HPV tests.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient says he has no advance directive and does not want one. What may the practice do about his care?
opciones: Nothing may change: care cannot be conditioned on having a directive
Care may be limited to what the state surrogate hierarchy authorizes
Care may go ahead once a relative signs a directive on his behalf
Care may be delayed until the community education material is given
preguntas.explicacion: Providers may not condition the provision of care, or otherwise discriminate, on whether or not a person has executed an advance directive. The state hierarchy of surrogates matters only when a patient can no longer decide, community education is an obligation the provider owes the public, and nobody else may execute a directive for a competent adult.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with early dementia clearly explains what the draw is for and why she agrees to it. Who consents?
opciones: She does; a diagnosis alone does not remove the right to give informed consent
Her daughter must, because a dementia diagnosis removes decision-making capacity
A psychiatrist must certify her competency before any venipuncture is done
No one needs to; consent is waived because the test is low risk
preguntas.explicacion: Cognitive impairment, mental illness or severe illness do not by themselves revoke the right to consent as long as the person can understand, evaluate and communicate a decision. A psychiatrist is asked to evaluate only when decision-making ability is questioned or unclear, and the waiver exception applies when the patient voluntarily waives, not because the test is minor.

preguntas.pregunta: What did the Needlestick Safety and Prevention Act of 2000 require?
opciones: Revising the OSHA standard to add safer devices, annual device review, employee input and a sharps injury log
Creating the bloodborne pathogens standard itself, with the hepatitis B vaccine offer and exposure control plans
Replacing the OSHA standard with the CDC's Standard Precautions for every healthcare employer
Requiring every employer to keep the OSHA 300 log, a form that had not existed before 2000
preguntas.explicacion: Public Law 106-430, signed November 6, 2000, ordered changes to the existing 1991 bloodborne pathogens standard: adding safer medical devices such as sharps with engineered injury protections and needleless systems to the definition of engineering controls, requiring the Exposure Control Plan review to reflect new technology and document annual consideration of safer devices, soliciting input from non-managerial direct-care employees, and establishing the sharps injury log. OSHA revised the standard in 2001; Congress found the existing OSHA 200 log insufficient rather than creating it.

preguntas.pregunta: A nurse changes the needle but reuses the syringe to give medication to a second patient. According to the CDC, this practice is which of these?
opciones: Unsafe: a syringe is contaminated after one use, even with a new needle
Safe, since the needle is the only part that touches the patient
Safe if the second dose is injected through IV tubing rather than into tissue
Unsafe only if the first patient has a known bloodborne infection
preguntas.explicacion: The CDC's rule is One Needle, One Syringe, Only One Time. Once used, both the syringe and the needle are contaminated and must be discarded; medication must not be given from the same syringe to more than one patient even when the needle is changed or the injection is given through a length of IV tubing. Reusing a syringe for more than one patient is one of the practices the CDC lists as having caused outbreaks of viral, bacterial and fungal infection, and the rule does not depend on the first patient's known status.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Injection Safety: Preventing Unsafe Injection Practices, Basic safe injection practices

preguntas.pregunta: After the explanation a patient nods and holds out his arm, then says 'Wait, I don't want this.' The needle has not touched him. Per WHO step 2?
opciones: Stop; the patient may refuse the test at any time before the blood is taken
Proceed, because verbal consent was already given when he offered the arm
Proceed if the ordering clinician confirms by telephone that the test is needed
Ask him to sign a refusal form first; until then the consent still stands
preguntas.explicacion: Step 2 says to discuss the test, obtain verbal consent, and remember that the patient has the right to refuse at any time before the blood sampling, which is why the WHO insists that the patient understand the procedure. An earlier nod does not lock the patient in, a clinician's wish does not override the refusal, and no paperwork is a precondition for stopping.

opciones: 16 to 18 G; collection for transfusion needs a larger gauge than blood drawing
21 to 22 G; the standard adult phlebotomy needles are used for donation as well
19 to 20 G; the intermediate sizes are set aside for donor collection only
23 G; a small needle protects the donor's vein during a long collection
preguntas.explicacion: Table 3.1 ticks 16 to 18 G for adults in the blood donation column, and Section 3.1.1 explains that blood collection for transfusion requires a larger gauge than the one used for drawing blood samples. The 21 and 22 G needles are the adult phlebotomy sizes, 19 to 20 G is marked not applicable, and 23 G is the small-vein and butterfly size.

preguntas.pregunta: What is characteristic of a high deductible health plan?
opciones: The monthly premium is usually lower and the patient pays more before coverage starts
The monthly premium is usually higher and the patient owes no cost sharing afterward
The monthly premium is set aside pre-tax and can be spent on any medical expense
The monthly premium is waived for the plan year once the deductible has been met
preguntas.explicacion: A high deductible health plan carries a bigger deductible than a traditional plan; in exchange, the monthly payment is usually smaller, so more of the early cost falls on the patient. It is commonly paired with a health savings account, which is the piece that holds untaxed dollars for qualified expenses. Meeting the deductible starts the plan's share of payment; it never suspends the premium, which is owed whether or not care is used.

preguntas.pregunta: Which urine specimen is best for a urine hCG pregnancy test, and why?
opciones: The first void of the morning, because it is the most concentrated and holds enough hormone
The first void of the morning, because overnight urine is the most dilute of the whole day
A specimen taken 2 hours after a large drink, because dilution reduces false-positive results
A midstream clean-catch taken at any hour, because the hormone level does not vary at all
preguntas.explicacion: Human chorionic gonadotropin is produced during pregnancy and detected in urine. The first specimen of the day is usually best because it is the most concentrated and therefore carries enough hormone to be picked up. The patient voids into a sterile cup, or with a home kit dips the strip or passes it through the stream, following the package directions.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient has missed six scheduled appointments in a row. Before the practice ends the relationship, what does the ethical guidance expect?
opciones: Efforts to repair the relationship, all of them documented in the record
An immediate dismissal letter, since repeated no-shows end the relationship by themselves
A referral to the health plan, which decides whether the patient may be dismissed
A written waiver from the patient releasing the practice from any further duty of care
preguntas.explicacion: Before dismissing a patient the clinician should weigh whether every effort has been made to improve the relationship: discussing the patient's needs and expectations, setting reasonable goals together, and trying to reconcile unrealistic expectations. All those efforts should be documented. Repeated noncompliance with treatment and with previously agreed follow-up appointments is among the reasons a patient may lawfully be dismissed.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, Patient Abandonment, Issues of Concern

preguntas.pregunta: A laptop holding the appointment schedule is stolen from a car. Notification is required only if the information was unsecured. What makes it secured?
opciones: Encryption or destruction as specified in the Secretary's guidance
A password on the operating system that the thief would have to guess
Storage on a device the practice had listed in its inventory of equipment
A remote lock the practice can apply to the device after it goes missing
preguntas.explicacion: Notifications are owed only where the breach involved unsecured PHI, meaning information that has not been rendered unusable, unreadable or indecipherable to unauthorized persons through a technology or methodology the Secretary specifies in guidance. That guidance names encryption and destruction. Entities that secure information as it describes are relieved of notifying after a breach of it.

preguntas.pregunta: A tube arrives labelled with the patient's full name and the room number only. Why does it fail the labelling checklist item used by CAP-accredited laboratories?
opciones: Primary specimen containers must carry at least two identifiers, and a room number is not an identifier
Primary specimen containers must carry the name plus a bar code; a handwritten room number is not machine-readable
Primary specimen containers must carry three identifiers when the specimen is collected on an inpatient unit
Primary specimen containers must carry the name and the collector's initials; the room number is merely optional
preguntas.explicacion: The CAP Laboratory General Checklist requires the collector to positively identify the patient before collection using at least two identifiers (GEN.40490) and requires primary specimen containers to be labelled with at least two identifiers (GEN.40491); the parallel Joint Commission International goal excludes the room number or location as an identifier outright. A name plus a location therefore leaves the tube one identifier short.

preguntas.pregunta: The patient is lying comfortably and the tray is ready. In WHO step 2, what is placed under the arm at this point?
opciones: A clean paper or towel
A warm moist cloth
A leak-proof plastic bag
A rolled-up tourniquet
preguntas.explicacion: Step 2 makes the patient comfortable in a supine position where that is possible and then places a clean paper or towel under the arm. Warm cloths over the puncture area are a paediatric measure for dilating vessels, leak-proof bags are for transporting the samples, and the tourniquet goes four to five finger widths above the site at the next step.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient is surprised that she owes nothing for a screening the office carried out. Why is that, under Part B?
opciones: Most preventive services cost nothing when the provider accepts assignment
Preventive services are paid for under Part A rather than under Part B
The yearly Part B deductible is waived for every service she is given
A Medigap policy pays for preventive services in full for every enrollee
preguntas.explicacion: Part B helps cover two kinds of service: those that are medically necessary, meaning they meet accepted standards of practice to diagnose or treat a condition, and preventive ones meant to stop illness or catch it early. The patient pays nothing for most preventive services when they come from a provider who accepts assignment.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient having a severe allergic reaction is short of breath and hoarse. Which action is wrong?
opciones: Giving the patient an antihistamine tablet with a little water
Injecting the emergency epinephrine the patient carries in a bag
Calling the emergency number while another person stays with them
Laying the patient flat and raising the feet about 12 inches (30 cm)
preguntas.explicacion: Nothing goes into the mouth of someone who is having trouble breathing, so an oral tablet is out. A hoarse or whispered voice, or coarse sounds on breathing in, warns of dangerous throat swelling. Injectable or intranasal epinephrine is used at the start of the reaction, without waiting to see whether it worsens, and help is called.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks whether an extended-release tablet can be cut in half to make it easier to swallow. What is the answer?
opciones: No: an extended-release tablet is swallowed whole, never split, chewed or crushed
Yes: splitting is allowed as long as both halves are taken within the same hour
Yes: splitting is allowed because the coating on the tablet controls the release
No: but the tablet may be crushed and stirred into food if it is not chewed first
preguntas.explicacion: Extended-release tablets are swallowed whole; they are not split, chewed, crushed or dissolved, because the form is what spreads the release out over hours. A patient who cannot swallow a tablet may have other forms available instead. An orally disintegrating tablet is a different form altogether, made to dissolve quickly in the mouth, and a chewable tablet is meant to be chewed.

preguntas.pregunta: A provider orders a colonoscopy and a barium enema. Which ending marks the study in which the colon is looked at directly?
opciones: -scopy, the ending that means examining
-graphy, the ending that means recording
-metry, the ending that means measuring
-centesis, the ending that means puncture
preguntas.explicacion: Diagnostic endings say how the information is obtained. The pair -scope and -scopy is for looking at a structure; -gram, -graph and -graphy are for recording an image or a tracing; -meter and -metry are for measuring; and -centesis is a surgical puncture that removes fluid. Only the first involves a direct look.

opciones: Whether new roles are needed, such as a telehealth coordinator and an IT lead
Whether the clinicians will accept a reduced fee for every virtual encounter
Whether the practice will stop offering in-person visits once telehealth begins
Whether the vendor will take over the front desk duties during virtual visits
preguntas.explicacion: The factors to consider before offering telehealth include whether additional staff or new roles are needed, such as a telehealth coordinator and an IT lead; how existing roles change, front desk personnel and patient intake among them; whether staff are ready and committed; how the team will be prepared and trained; and whether the platform is easy to use and integrates with the electronic health record.

preguntas.pregunta: Trace a drop of blood returning from the arm. From the right atrium it passes through which valve, and into which chamber?
opciones: The tricuspid valve, into the right ventricle
The mitral valve, into the left ventricle
The pulmonary valve, into the pulmonary trunk
The bicuspid valve, into the right ventricle
preguntas.explicacion: Systemic blood enters the right atrium from the venae cavae, passes the right atrioventricular (tricuspid) valve into the right ventricle, is pumped through the pulmonary valve into the pulmonary trunk to the lungs, returns to the left atrium, crosses the mitral (bicuspid) valve into the left ventricle and leaves through the aortic valve. The bicuspid valve is on the left side only.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with untreated diabetes is passing very large amounts of urine, charted as polyuria. Which two word parts build that term?
opciones: A prefix meaning many or excessive plus an ending meaning in the urine
A prefix meaning few or little plus an ending meaning in the urine
A prefix meaning without plus an ending meaning in the urine
A prefix meaning many or excessive plus a root meaning kidney
preguntas.explicacion: Poly- means many or excessive and -uria means in the urine, so the term says there is a great deal of it. preguntas.pregunta: Which technique describes a deep nasal swab?
opciones: Insert less than one inch until resistance at the turbinates, rotate several times, repeat in the other nostril
Insert less than one inch until resistance at the turbinates, hold still 10 seconds, and use a new swab per nostril
Insert to the depth of the ear opening, rotate several times, then repeat in the other nostril
Insert less than one inch and withdraw at once, then place the swab tip into a dry sterile tube
preguntas.explicacion: With the head tilted back 70 degrees, the swab is gently rotated as it goes in, stopping under an inch when resistance is met at the turbinates. It is rotated several times against the nasal wall and the same swab is then used in the other nostril. The tip goes into a viral transport tube and the applicator stick is cut off. The ear-opening depth belongs to the nasopharyngeal swab.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient describes retrosternal pressure spreading to the jaw and left arm, with sweating and nausea. Which findings confirm the suspected diagnosis?
opciones: Electrocardiographic changes together with a rise in cardiac troponin
Electrocardiographic changes together with a rise in blood urea nitrogen
A chest radiograph together with a rise in the white blood cell count
A rise in cardiac troponin together with a fall in the hemoglobin level
preguntas.explicacion: Myocardial infarction is death of heart muscle from a prolonged lack of oxygen, most often from plaque rupture with clot on top. The discomfort is diffuse pressure or tightness behind the sternum that can travel to shoulders, arms, neck, jaw or upper abdomen. History and examination alone may not settle it: the diagnosis combines the story with the ECG and a high-sensitivity troponin.

Enter the Monday reading in the blank rows and initial each of them
Enter the average of the readings before and after the gap
Enter the acceptable range midpoint and note that the site was closed

opciones: ICD-10, HCPCS, CPT, dental procedure codes and national drug codes

preguntas.pregunta: A patient is transferred without the gurney being stabilized first. What kind of error is that?
opciones: An error of omission, an adverse event caused by an action not taken
An error of commission, an adverse event caused by a direct action
A latent error, since the equipment itself was never checked properly
A never event, since a fall from a gurney should be impossible anyway
preguntas.explicacion: Medical errors split into omission and commission. Errors of omission cause harm through something not done — not strapping a patient into a wheelchair, not stabilizing a gurney before a transfer — while errors of commission follow from a direct act by a team member. preguntas.pregunta: A coworker says a patient with dementia "is not competent to sign." What is accurate about that word?
opciones: Competence is a legal finding a judge makes; the bedside call is capacity
Competence is the bedside finding; capacity is what a court declares later
Competence and capacity are one finding, made by any licensed staff member
Competence is presumed lost once a dementia diagnosis appears in the chart
preguntas.explicacion: Competence is about being able to take part in legal proceedings. It is presumed, and disproving it takes a hearing with evidence before a judge; clinicians never make that call. What the clinical team assesses is capacity: whether this patient can make this decision, now, in this situation. A dementia diagnosis does not by itself remove capacity.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Competency and Capacity", Issues of Concern: Relevant Definitions
preguntas.subtema: Competency vs capacity · CCMA 7B k216 · CMA E.3.c · RMA I.C.3 · NCMA 4.7

preguntas.pregunta: A vacuum-tube system is being used on a small child. What adjustment does the WHO device table call for, and why?
opciones: A smaller tube with reduced vacuum (1 to 5 ml), to reduce haemolysis
A larger tube with full vacuum, so the sample is collected before the vein collapses
A butterfly set with a discard tube, to remove the air from the tubing
A 16 to 18 G needle, so the tube fills before the tourniquet limit is reached
preguntas.explicacion: Table C.1 says that with vacuum systems a smaller tube with reduced vacuum should be used for paediatric patients, and for retractable evacuated systems specifies a 1 to 5 ml tube with lower vacuum to reduce haemolysis. The discard tube is the butterfly rule for air in the tubing, and 16 to 18 G is the blood donation gauge in Table 3.1, far too large for a child.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Annex C, Table C.1, Vacuum-tube systems and Manually retractable evacuated tube systems
preguntas.subtema: Device selection · CPT D3 k55 3D · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 3E4 k134 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.4

preguntas.pregunta: A 7-year-old girl's body mass index is at the 88th percentile for her age and sex. How is that read?
opciones: Overweight: the band runs from the 85th to below the 95th percentile
Obesity: the band starts once the 85th percentile has been reached
Healthy weight: the band runs from the 5th to below the 95th percentile
Overweight: the band runs from the 75th to below the 90th percentile
preguntas.explicacion: Children from 2 through 19 are compared with others of the same age and sex rather than with fixed adult numbers. A percentile of 88 means the value equals or exceeds that of 88% of the reference group, and the overweight band runs from the 85th to below the 95th. Obesity starts at the 95th percentile.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, BMI Frequently Asked Questions
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A6 k58 · CMA I.A.1.h · RMA III.E.4.e · NCMA 2B.3

preguntas.pregunta: Before a hospital adopts a new safety needle across its draw stations, what must the product evaluation show?
opciones: That the feature works reliably, staff accept it, and patient care does not suffer
That the device costs no more than the one it replaces over a full year
That the manufacturer has registered and listed it with the federal agency
That the injury rate has already fallen in the department that will use it
preguntas.explicacion: Devices with safety features should be evaluated on three points before they are adopted: the safety feature works effectively and reliably, the device is acceptable to the worker who will use it, and it does not harm patient care. The recommended process adds training in the new device, clear written criteria, on-site follow-up for informal feedback, and monitoring after implementation. Registration and listing are what the manufacturer owes the device regulator, not what the evaluation measures.
preguntas.fuente: NIOSH, Alert 2000-108, Recommendations: Selecting and Evaluating Needle Devices with Safety Features
preguntas.subtema: Evaluating a new device · CPT D1 1A k12 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k123 · CMA I.B.4.e · RMA III.A.2.e · NCMA 2A.8

preguntas.pregunta: Is a resting tracing recorded on a patient with cognitive impairment?
opciones: Yes: nobody is automatically excluded from the test
No: the patient cannot follow the instructions given
Yes, but only if a relative holds the arms still for it
No, unless a provider stays in the room during the run
preguntas.explicacion: The eligibility rules say plainly that there are no automatic exclusions and that patients with cognitive impairment should have the recording done. What is asked of every patient still applies: relax, breathe normally and stay still without talking.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 3.1 Eligibility Criteria
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F1 k150 k151 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(i) · RMA III.F.6.a.i · NCMA 2D.1 2D.2

preguntas.pregunta: A patient scheduled for a fasting glucose says he skipped breakfast but had a coffee with sugar an hour ago. What should the phlebotomist do?
opciones: He has broken the fast; tell the provider, since the test may need rescheduling
Coffee does not count as food, so the draw may proceed as a fasting sample
Proceed and mark the sample 'non-fasting' only if he also ate solid food
Wait one more hour so the sugar clears, then draw it as a fasting sample
preguntas.explicacion: Fasting means no food or drink except plain water; juice, coffee, soda and other beverages get into the bloodstream and affect results, and a patient who eats or drinks before the test should tell the provider because the test may have to be rescheduled. A fasting glucose needs at least 8 hours without caloric intake, not one more hour.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Fasting for a Blood Test, sections Can I drink anything besides water, and What if I make a mistake
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2K k46 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E1 k125 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.e · NCMA 2C.2

preguntas.pregunta: A chemistry panel gives results the clinician cannot explain, and the tube was set down without being inverted. What does the table warn about?
opciones: Blood not thoroughly mixed with its additive can give erroneous results
Blood not mixed with its additive loses the vacuum it was drawn under
Blood left unmixed separates into serum before it reaches the laboratory
Blood left unmixed cools too quickly and the additive stops working at all
preguntas.explicacion: The footnote to the order-of-draw table asks for additive tubes to be inverted gently and warns that erroneous results may follow when the blood is not thoroughly mixed with the additive. The movement described elsewhere is a figure-of-8, and it is done as soon as the tube comes off the needle.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.3, footnote c
preguntas.subtema: Tube inversions · CPT D3 3N k9 k59 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E7 k135 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.6

preguntas.pregunta: The sharps container in a drawing station is full to the top, so a phlebotomist sets the used needle on the tray to dispose of it later. Which risks are being ignored?
opciones: Injuries happen when sharps containers are overfilled and when used needles are not placed in them immediately
The needle should have been recapped with two hands and left on the tray until a container was available
The needle should have gone into the regulated-waste bag, since bags are acceptable whenever containers are full
There is no added risk once the safety feature is activated, so the delay is acceptable
preguntas.explicacion: Used needles are placed immediately into an approved sharps container located near the point of use; injuries also occur when needles end up in regular waste bags or when sharps containers are overfilled or mishandled. Routine recapping is no longer recommended because manipulating a used needle raises the risk of puncture, and the WHO requires the container to be within arm's reach and clearly visible.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Needlestick", section Issues of Concern (recapping and disposal); and WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010), Section 3.1.1
preguntas.subtema: Sharps disposal · CPT D1 1G k30 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C8 k108 · CMA I.B.4.e · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.8

preguntas.pregunta: A child arrives with one leg in a cast and the parent asks for the usual growth measurements. What does the technique call for?
opciones: The numbers taken now may mislead, so they are not forced in this state
The numbers are taken anyway and the weight of the cast subtracted later
The numbers are contraindicated in any child with a limb deformity
The numbers are taken and plotted on a chart drawn for injured children
preguntas.explicacion: Body measurements are noninvasive and carry no true contraindication, but there are states in which the figure will not mean what it appears to mean: acute illness, a limb deformity, a cast. A height or a weight taken then can be falsely reassuring or falsely alarming, so the measurement is better postponed than plotted.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Anthropometric Measurement", Contraindications
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A6 k58 · CMA I.A.1.h · RMA III.E.4.b · NCMA 2B.3

preguntas.pregunta: Several tubes are needed from one venipuncture. Which system does the WHO's Step 7 say to use, and what if it is not available?
opciones: Evacuated tubes with a needle and tube holder; otherwise a syringe or a winged needle set
A syringe, because it lets the phlebotomist control the pressure; otherwise evacuated tubes
A winged needle set attached to a syringe; otherwise a hypodermic needle and syringe
Evacuated tubes only; if they are not available the draw is postponed
preguntas.explicacion: Step 7 says that when multiple tubes are needed, evacuated tubes with a needle and tube holder are used because the tubes fill directly, and that a syringe or winged needle set is the alternative when that system is unavailable. Chapter 3 gives the reasons: closed vacuum systems reduce direct exposure to blood and make multiple samples from one puncture easier.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 7: Fill the laboratory sample tubes
preguntas.subtema: Collection methods · CPT D3 3A k54 · PBT II.F II.J · CCMA 3E7 k134 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.4

preguntas.pregunta: A patient has intermittent cough, wheezing and shortness of breath that come and go with allergens and colds. Which test confirms the suspected diagnosis?
opciones: Spirometry showing variable expiratory airflow obstruction
Spirometry showing a fixed and irreversible airflow obstruction
A chest radiograph showing a lobar area of consolidation
A sputum culture growing a typical respiratory pathogen
preguntas.explicacion: The hallmark symptoms of asthma are cough, wheezing and shortness of breath, but they are too nonspecific on their own, so the diagnosis needs consistent symptoms plus variable expiratory airflow obstruction documented on spirometry. Obstruction that does not vary points toward COPD, and consolidation or a positive culture toward pneumonia.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Asthma", Introduction
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k39 · CMA I.C.6.h(5) (2027 I.C.6.g(5)) · RMA I.A.2.a · CMAA 1 k10 · NCMA 1.10

preguntas.pregunta: How is ice applied to a freshly sprained ankle?
opciones: Wrapped in cloth, never placed straight onto the skin, with the joint raised
Placed straight onto the skin so that the cold reaches the joint faster
Alternated with a hot pack every few minutes to keep the tissue warm
Held under an elastic wrap tight enough to stop the swelling completely
preguntas.explicacion: Ice goes on right away to hold down swelling, always wrapped in cloth and never directly against the skin. The area is then wrapped firmly but not tightly to limit movement, and the swollen joint is kept raised above the level of the heart, even during sleep, with the joint rested for several days.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Sprains", First Aid
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B10 k78 · CMA I.B.9.o · 2027 I.B.8.o · RMA III.H.1.b III.I.1.b · NCMA 2B.13 EKB 14

preguntas.pregunta: What obligation does a court-appointed guardian owe the ward?
opciones: A fiduciary duty to act in the ward's best interests, not to follow their wishes
A fiduciary duty to follow the ward's stated wishes on every personal decision
A duty to consult the ward's relatives before any medical decision is taken
A duty to seek court approval before consenting to any routine medical care
preguntas.explicacion: Guardians are legal representatives appointed by a court for people who cannot care for themselves, and the person they act for is the ward. They owe a fiduciary duty to act in the ward's best interests, and they have no duty to respect the ward's wishes. They control finances, property and care, and they need court authorization for large or extraordinary expenditures.
preguntas.fuente: Cornell Law School LII, Wex: guardian
preguntas.subtema: Legal guardianship · CCMA k218 · CMA E.3.c · NCMA 4.7

preguntas.pregunta: How should the reasons for taking a blood sample be recorded in a service?
opciones: Clearly defined in a written protocol or in documented instructions
Agreed verbally between the phlebotomist and the ordering clinician
Written on the tube label at the moment the specimen is collected
Left to the judgement of whoever is drawing blood on that shift
preguntas.explicacion: The guidance asks that the indications for blood sampling be clearly defined, either in a written protocol or in documented instructions such as a laboratory form. Written standard operating procedures for each step also appear among the elements of quality assurance.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.2

preguntas.pregunta: Which containers does the equipment list accept for collecting the blood itself?
opciones: Glass or plastic tubes with rubber caps, vacuum tubes, or screw-capped glass
Vacuum tubes only, since caps of any other kind cannot hold a vacuum
Glass tubes with screw caps only, because plastic reacts with additives
Plastic tubes with rubber caps only, since glass may break in transport
preguntas.explicacion: Blood may be collected into sterile glass or plastic tubes with rubber caps, into vacuum-extraction tubes, or into glass tubes with screw caps, and which of them is used depends on what has been agreed with the laboratory. Large volumes call instead for a sterile glass or collapsible pack.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 1

preguntas.pregunta: A worker is transferred to a worse shift a week after complaining to OSHA. What can she do, and by when?
opciones: File a whistleblower complaint within 30 days of the retaliation
File a whistleblower complaint within 30 days of the original hazard
File a whistleblower complaint within 180 days of the retaliation
File a grievance with the employer, which OSHA reviews on appeal
preguntas.explicacion: It is illegal for an employer to fire, demote, transfer or otherwise retaliate against a worker for complaining to the agency. A worker who believes that happened may file a whistleblower complaint within 30 days of the retaliation — the clock runs from the retaliation itself, not from the hazard that prompted the original complaint, which can be reported confidentially.
preguntas.fuente: OSHA, Worker Rights and Protections
preguntas.subtema: Reportable violations · CCMA 7F · NCMA 4.11 · CMAA 3E k44

preguntas.pregunta: Which practices make up standard precautions, the framework applied at every patient encounter?
opciones: Hand hygiene, protective equipment, cough etiquette, placement and safe sharps
Isolation rooms, contact tracing, daily temperature checks and visitor logs
Sterile gloves, sterile fields, surgical scrub and sterile drapes for each draw
Testing every patient on admission and treating those who test positive
preguntas.explicacion: Standard precautions are the baseline for every encounter, before anything is known about the patient: hand hygiene whether or not gloves were worn, both before and after contact with a patient or with body fluids; appropriate protective equipment, including gown, gloves and eye protection where fluid exposure is possible; respiratory and cough etiquette; patient placement that takes single rooms and routes of transmission into account; and safe handling of needles and instruments.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Personal Protective Equipment", Issues of Concern: Standard Precautions
preguntas.subtema: Standard precautions · CPT D1 1J k11 · PBT VI.G.4.b · CCMA 3C1 k100 · CMA I.B.4 · RMA III.A.2.d · NCMA 2A.1

preguntas.pregunta: A patient due for a drug level asks whether to skip the morning dose so the result comes out low. What is the right answer?
opciones: No: doses are not stopped or changed without talking to the provider first
Yes: the dose is always held on the morning of a therapeutic drug level
Yes, if the level is a trough, since a trough must be drawn off therapy
No, but the dose may be delayed two hours without a new order
preguntas.explicacion: Patients must not stop or change their medicines before a drug level without speaking to the provider; the provider is the one who says whether the times of any doses need to change. Depending on the drug, the test is scheduled before or after the regular dose, which is exactly why an unannounced skipped dose ruins the result. A trough is drawn on therapy, just before the next dose.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Therapeutic drug levels (003430), How to Prepare for the Test; MedlinePlus, Therapeutic Drug Monitoring, Will I need to do anything to prepare for the test?
preguntas.subtema: Drug level preparation · CPT D2 k45 · PBT II.D patient preparation · CCMA 3E k139 · RMA III.C.4.e · NCMA 2C.2 pre-test conditions

preguntas.pregunta: The system comes back after a six-hour outage. What does the contingency guidance expect next?
opciones: A process that gets what was written on paper entered and reconciled into the record
A fresh risk analysis of the whole practice before any user logs back into the system
A breach report to the Secretary describing the outage and the paper forms used
Destruction of the paper forms, so that two versions of the visit never coexist
preguntas.explicacion: Alongside stocking paper forms, the guidance requires a process ensuring the information recorded on paper during the downtime is entered into the EHR and reconciled once the system is back, for instance by entering orders as coded data and scanning documents whose contents are not otherwise keyed in. Separate practices cover training and testing staff on downtime and recovery.
preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, SAFER Guide: Contingency Planning, Recommended Practice 1.3
preguntas.subtema: Downtime recovery · CCMA 5 k191 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.4.g · CMAA 7 k101 · NCMA 3.5

preguntas.pregunta: Which organelle is the site where the cell builds its proteins?
opciones: The ribosome, which reads messenger RNA to assemble a protein
The lysosome, which reads messenger RNA to assemble a protein
The peroxisome, which reads messenger RNA to assemble a protein
The centrosome, which reads messenger RNA to assemble a protein
preguntas.explicacion: A ribosome is the organelle where proteins are made: two ribosomal RNA subunits wrap around messenger RNA and translation begins. Ribosomes stud the rough endoplasmic reticulum, which is what makes it look bumpy. Lysosomes and peroxisomes are enzyme-filled sacs that break things down rather than build them.
preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 3.2 The Cytoplasm and Cellular Organelles, The Endoplasmic Reticulum
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k35 · CMA I.C.6.c (2027 I.C.6.b) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1

preguntas.pregunta: An inpatient carries a schizophrenia diagnosis and is being asked to agree to a draw. What follows?
opciones: The diagnosis by itself does not remove the right to give informed consent
A surrogate signs for any patient who carries a psychiatric diagnosis
Consent is waived, because the admission paperwork already covers draws
The nearest relative decides once a psychiatric diagnosis is on the record
preguntas.explicacion: Cognitive impairment, mental illness and severe medical conditions do not on their own revoke the right to give informed consent, so long as the person can understand, evaluate and communicate a decision. Research shows that carrying a diagnosis such as schizophrenia does not preclude capacity, so a full assessment is made for each patient.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Informed Consent", section Issues of Concern, Patients with Impaired Decision-Making Capacity; and StatPearls, "Refusal of Care", section Issues of Concern, Psychiatric Patients
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2F 2G k43 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7B k216 · CMA E.3.c (both outlines) · NCMA 4.7

preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks how to take a sublingual nitroglycerin tablet when an angina attack begins. What do you tell them?
opciones: Sit down, put it under the tongue and let it dissolve; do not chew, crush or swallow it
Sit down, chew the tablet well and swallow it with water so that it starts working faster
Lie down, crush the tablet between the teeth and hold the powder against the inner cheek
Sit down and swallow the tablet whole, then take a second one after ten minutes have passed
preguntas.explicacion: The instruction is to sit down and take one dose as the attack starts. The tablet goes under the tongue, or between cheek and gum, and is left to dissolve; it is never chewed, crushed or swallowed. Burning or tingling is normal and says nothing about whether it is working. If the pain does not ease, emergency help is called, and further doses come five minutes apart when the prescriber has ordered them.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Nitroglycerin Sublingual: How should this medicine be used?
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B5 k69 · CMA I.D.2.c(3) · RMA III.G.4.d(v) · NCMA 1.9

preguntas.pregunta: Smoke starts pouring from a centrifuge in the processing room while two patients sit in the waiting area. Under the RACE sequence, what is the first action?
opciones: Rescue or remove everyone in immediate danger
Activate the alarm system and call the operator
Confine the fire by closing the doors
Extinguish it with the nearest CO2 unit
preguntas.explicacion: RACE orders the response to a fire: R, rescue or remove all occupants from danger; A, activate the alarm system; C, confine the fire by closing doors; E, evacuate or extinguish. In healthcare the first step matters most because patients may be unable to move on their own. Extinguishing comes last and only for a fire that can be handled with a portable unit; the PASS rule, pull, aim, squeeze, sweep, governs how the extinguisher is used once that point is reached.
preguntas.fuente: OSHA, Laboratory Safety Guidance (OSHA 3404), Fire safety, the RACE rule; StatPearls, "OSHA Fire Safety", Issues of Concern
preguntas.subtema: RACE · CPT D1 1A 1L k24 · PBT VI.G.2 · CMA I.B.8.c · RMA II.B.7.c · NCMA 2A.9 · CMAA 3A k45

preguntas.pregunta: Two staff members are running a resuscitation in the office. How often should they trade the compressor role?
opciones: Every 2 minutes, or sooner if the one compressing gets tired
Every 10 minutes, or when the monitor shows a shockable rhythm
Every 30 seconds, after each set of 30 compressions and 2 breaths
Only when the defibrillator announces that everyone must stand clear
preguntas.explicacion: Compressors rotate every 2 minutes, or earlier if fatigue sets in, because tired hands lose rate and depth. Two minutes is also about five cycles of 30 compressions and 2 breaths. Rotation is one of the quality items of a high-performance team, along with proper depth, full recoil and avoiding excessive ventilation.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Advanced Cardiac Life Support (ACLS)", Recognition and Initial Management of Cardiac Arrest
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k83 · CMA I.B.9.c · 2027 I.B.8.c · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2A.10 EKB 15

preguntas.pregunta: A prosecutor subpoenas a patient's substance use disorder records for a case against that patient. What is needed?
opciones: A court order, and the subpoena as well, before anything is released
The subpoena on its own, since a court has already signed the document
The program director's approval, recorded in the disclosure log
Written notice to the patient, after which the records may be sent
preguntas.explicacion: Records, or testimony relaying what they contain, may not be used in civil, administrative, criminal or legislative proceedings against the patient without specific written consent or a court order. That order only comes after notice and an opportunity to be heard, and it has to be accompanied by a subpoena or similar legal mandate compelling disclosure before anything is released.
preguntas.subtema: Sharing information · CCMA 7E k220 · CMA E.4.c(1) · RMA I.C.1.b · NCMA 4.3

preguntas.pregunta: Under the medical record condition of participation, when may an original medical record leave the hospital?
opciones: Only in accordance with Federal or State law, a court order or a subpoena
Whenever another treating facility asks for it to continue the patient's care
Whenever the patient signs the practice release form at the records window
Whenever the medical record service keeps a photocopy of the file it releases
preguntas.explicacion: The confidentiality standard requires a procedure ensuring records stay confidential, allows information or copies to go only to authorized individuals, and obliges the facility to keep unauthorized people from reaching or altering them. Release of the original record is narrower still: it happens only in accordance with Federal or State laws, court orders or subpoenas.
preguntas.subtema: Release of records · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.4.f · CMAA 7A k39 · NCMA 4.4

preguntas.pregunta: A patient whose record is kept in the EHR asks for an electronic copy. What does the Privacy Rule require?
opciones: An electronic copy in the form asked for if readily producible, or an agreed readable format
A paper printout, since hard copy is always an acceptable substitute for an electronic request
New software purchased by the practice so that every requested file format can be produced
An electronic copy only when the patient accepts the security risk of unencrypted transfer
preguntas.explicacion: Where PHI is kept electronically and the individual asks for electronic access, the entity must provide it in the requested form and format if readily producible, and otherwise in an agreed alternative readable electronic format. No entity has to buy new software for every possible request, but each must be able to produce some electronic copy. Only if the individual turns down every electronic format offered may the request be satisfied with a readable hard copy.
preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Individuals Right under HIPAA to Access their Health Information: Form and Format
