preguntas.pregunta: A clinic stores some test kits and patient samples on an open shelf rather than in the refrigerator. Which range is typically kept for a room used for testing and storage?
opciones: 15 to 30 °C, that is 59 to 86 °F
2 to 8 °C, that is 36 to 46 °F
18 to 22 °C, that is 64 to 72 °F
10 to 25 °C, that is 50 to 77 °F
preguntas.explicacion: Rooms used for testing and for storing reagents, kits, controls and patient samples are typically held between 15 and 30 °C, or 59 to 86 °F. The colder band, 2 to 8 °C, belongs to the refrigerator and −25 to −15 °C to the freezer. Whatever the room reads, the manufacturer's instructions decide which condition a given product may be stored in.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Ready? Set? Test! (2024), Appendix B, Temperature Log Instructions
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5B · PBT III.D.1 · CCMA 3E11 k143 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.c

preguntas.pregunta: Which chamber pumps blood into the systemic circuit, and why is its wall so much thicker than its counterpart's?
opciones: The left ventricle; it must overcome the high resistance of the long systemic circuit
The right ventricle; it must push blood through the dense capillary beds of both lungs
The left atrium; it receives oxygen-rich blood from all four of the pulmonary veins
The right atrium; it receives blood from both venae cavae and from the coronary sinus
preguntas.explicacion: The ventricles are the primary pumping chambers, and the left ventricle is the major pump for the systemic circuit, ejecting blood into the aorta. Although both ventricles move the same volume per beat, the left wall is much thicker because it must generate far more pressure to overcome the resistance of the long systemic circuit; the pulmonary circuit is shorter and offers less resistance.
preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 19.1 Heart Anatomy, Chambers and Circulation through the Heart; Layers; Left Ventricle
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k6 (applied D3) · PBT I.A.1 · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1

preguntas.pregunta: A code carries a code also note. What does that instruct the coder to do?
opciones: Report two codes if needed, letting the circumstances of the encounter set the order
Report two codes, with the underlying condition sequenced first in every case
Report a secondary code if it is known, after the code that carries the note
Report only one of the two codes, since they are independent of one another

preguntas.pregunta: A red-top tube is left to clot and then centrifuged. What is the fluid above the clot called, and how does it differ from plasma?

Plasma; it still contains fibrinogen and the other clotting factors
Buffy coat; the pale layer of leukocytes and platelets above the cells
Whole blood; the formed elements are suspended in the fluid again
preguntas.explicacion: Serum is plasma after the clotting factors have been removed: in a clotted tube it is the fluid squeezed out of the clot as it retracts. preguntas.pregunta: A colleague suggests puncturing the back (posterior curve) of a newborn's heel. Why is that spot avoided?
opciones: In a 3 kg baby the skin-to-bone distance there is only 2.33 mm, so the lancet may hit bone
In a 3 kg baby the skin-to-bone distance there is 3.32 mm, too deep for a lancet to reach blood
The posterior heel is where the tibial artery runs closest to the skin surface
The posterior heel is the site the WHO reserves for premature neonates with a 0.85 mm lancet
preguntas.explicacion: In a 7 pound (3 kg) baby the distances from skin to bone are: 3.32 mm at the medial and lateral heel, 2.33 mm at the posterior heel and 2.19 mm at the toe. The posterior heel is to be avoided to reduce the risk of hitting bone. The tibial artery is the risk of the medial aspect of the heel, and the 0.85 mm lancet is simply the size available for premature neonates.

preguntas.pregunta: A 24-hour urine for porphyrins is ordered. Which container feature does this analyte require?

A clear container, so the laboratory can see the color of the pooled urine
A vacuum tube, which draws the sample without opening the container
A sterile container, because porphyrin testing requires a bacteriological culture
preguntas.explicacion: Light-sensitive analytes such as porphyrins and urobilinogen call for amber containers, in addition to the general requirements that the container be non-absorbing and free of interfering agents. preguntas.pregunta: A patient is about to use a metered-dose inhaler. Why is a spacer considered best practice?
opciones: It stops particles from settling on the tongue or drifting away into the room air
It warms the medication so that the airway does not spasm as the mist arrives
It lets the patient inhale strongly and quickly, which is what activates a powder
It counts the doses left in the canister so that a refill is ordered on time
preguntas.explicacion: As the patient breathes in from a metered-dose inhaler, small particles get caught on the tongue or aerosolize into the air and never reach the lungs, so a spacer is fitted to get the whole dose in and to waste less. One space lower, on the other side of the sternum
One space higher, on the other side of the sternum
At the same space, out in the mid-clavicular line

A quantity limit exception, which covers the drug for the remainder of the year
A step therapy exception, granted once she has tried the cheaper drug on the list
A formulary exception, granted automatically for any drug she was already taking
preguntas.explicacion: When drug coverage begins, the member may get a transition fill: a one-time thirty-day supply of a drug she has been taking that the plan either does not cover or subjects to prior authorization or step therapy. preguntas.pregunta: A parent asks about cooling a feverish child with an ice bath or an alcohol rub. What is the instruction?
opciones: Neither is used: both cool the skin and set off shivering, which drives core temperature up
Both are used, but only after an antipyretic, so that the value does not rebound
The ice bath is acceptable; the alcohol rub is avoided because the skin absorbs it
Neither is used, because cooling the skin has no measurable effect on temperature
preguntas.explicacion: Cold baths, ice and alcohol rubs are ruled out: they chill the skin and provoke shivering, and shivering raises the core temperature, so the child ends up worse. A lukewarm bath or sponge bath may help, and it works better after medicine has been given, otherwise the temperature climbs straight back up.

Skip dented cans only, since bulging is caused by normal temperature change
Skip cans past the date only, since packaging damage does not reach the food
Skip glass jars altogether, since only cans can be checked for damage

Lift each tube out of the rack and hold it steady in the free hand
Keep the tubes in the rack and tilt them so the blood runs down the wall
Lift the rack up to eye level so the coloured stoppers stay in view
preguntas.explicacion: Where it can be done, the tubes stay in their rack and the rack is moved towards the worker, with the blood injected downwards into the appropriately coloured stopper. Holding a tube in the free hand is what the needle-stick precaution for this step is meant to avoid.

preguntas.pregunta: Why do devices with safety features reduce needlestick injuries without eliminating them?
opciones: Some cannot be activated until the needle is out, and some users bypass them
Their shields are made of plastic, which a needle can pierce from inside
They are sold only for hypodermic needles, not for blood collection sets
They must be removed before the tube is filled, leaving the tip exposed
preguntas.explicacion: Several things keep the risk above zero. With some designs the safety feature cannot be engaged until the needle has already left the patient; a needle can be dislodged during the procedure and leave the sharp exposed; some workers do not activate the feature at all; the feature itself can fail; and with some systems users can work around it, as when a needle is used to connect parts of a needleless intravenous system. Training and monitoring after implementation are what close that gap.

preguntas.pregunta: How much alcohol-based hand rub goes on the hands, and how is it worked in?
opciones: About 3 to 5 mL, rubbed over every surface until the hands are dry
A single small drop, rubbed into the palms and wiped with a towel
About 15 to 20 mL, poured over the hands and rinsed off with water
Enough to fill a cupped hand, left to evaporate without any rubbing
preguntas.explicacion: When hands are not visibly soiled the alcohol rub is the preferred method, and it is used as the manufacturer directs: roughly three to five millilitres in the palm, rubbed vigorously over all hand surfaces until dry, which takes about twenty seconds. Rubbing until dry is what does the work, so wiping the product off with a towel or letting it sit unrubbed cuts the contact short, and the rub is never rinsed away with water.

preguntas.pregunta: Tubes of blood go from the draw room to the in-house laboratory in a closed rack, and the facility applies Universal Precautions to all specimens. Is a biohazard label required?
opciones: Not while they stay in the facility and are recognizable as specimens; it is required once they leave
Yes, always: every container of blood must carry the fluorescent orange-red biohazard label
No, never: labeling applies to regulated waste containers, not to specimens of blood
Only if the primary container becomes contaminated on the outside and needs a second container
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(2)(xiii)(A) requires specimen containers for storage, transport or shipping to be labeled or color-coded and closed, but it exempts facilities that handle all specimens under Universal Precautions, provided the containers are recognizable as specimens; the exemption holds only inside the facility, and the label returns the moment specimens leave it. preguntas.pregunta: The bevel is inside the vein and blood has appeared. How is the needle advanced from there?
opciones: Along the vein, at whichever angle of entry proves easiest
Straight down at ninety degrees until the hub meets the skin
Back out a few millimetres and then in again at a steeper angle
Sideways across the vein so the bevel opens against the wall
preguntas.explicacion: The vein is entered swiftly at thirty degrees or less, and the needle then continues along the vein at the easiest angle of entry rather than being pushed deeper. Driving it beyond the lumen of the vein is what produces a haematoma, the pooling of blood under the skin.

preguntas.pregunta: Which physical safeguard for PHI applies to the computer at a phlebotomy station?
opciones: Point the screen away from public view and log off when stepping away
Leave the session open so the next phlebotomist can chart without delay
Store the patient list on a personal flash drive as an unencrypted backup
Print the day's schedule and post it at the check-in window
preguntas.explicacion: Physical safeguards regulate access to equipment that holds PHI: computer screens are turned away from public view, privacy barriers are used at reception, PHI is never left unattended, and workstations are logged off whenever the user leaves, even for a few minutes. Portable devices are a known source of breaches, so patient data is not stored on personal laptops or flash drives, and if it must be, it is encrypted. A posted schedule and an open session both expose identifiable information to people not involved in care.

Requiring mail delivery is forbidden, since mail is not a readily producible means of transfer
Requiring a visit is allowed only if the office also offers the same records through its portal

preguntas.pregunta: A study offers an unusually large payment to people who have no other way to pay their bills. What does the Belmont Report call that?
opciones: Undue influence, an excessive reward used to obtain compliance
Coercion, an overt threat of harm presented to obtain compliance
Incomplete disclosure, because the payment hides a real risk
Injustice, because the burden falls on the people who volunteer
preguntas.explicacion: Belmont separates the two: coercion is an overt threat of harm made to get compliance, while undue influence works through an excessive, unwarranted or improper reward. It adds that an inducement that would ordinarily be acceptable can turn into undue influence when the subject is especially vulnerable. Justice in Belmont is about who gets selected for research.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with a sore throat says she gargled with antiseptic mouthwash on the way to the office. Why does that matter for a throat culture?
opciones: Antiseptic mouthwash is specifically to be avoided before the test, which is otherwise unprepared for
Antiseptic mouthwash is required before the test, so the swab picks up only pharyngeal organisms
Antiseptic mouthwash makes the patient gag more, which prevents the swab from reaching the tonsils
Antiseptic mouthwash stains the pharynx, so the provider cannot see where to place the swab
preguntas.explicacion: The one preparation instruction for a throat swab culture is to skip antiseptic mouthwash beforehand, since it works against the organisms the culture is meant to grow. preguntas.pregunta: A patient arrives for a drug level ordered as a trough but says he took this morning's dose an hour ago. What matters?
opciones: Timing relative to the dose changes the result; report it before drawing
The level is stable through the day, so proceed and label the tube as ordered
Draw it now and relabel the sample as a peak level instead of a trough
Wait 30 minutes, which is the standard window for any trough sample
preguntas.explicacion: For TDM the test may need to be scheduled before or after the regular dose depending on the medicine, and the level in the blood varies over time as the body processes the drug. The trough is the point just before the next dose; a sample an hour after dosing is not that. Relabelling it as a peak invents a measurement that was not ordered.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient says her stomach hurts, and the clinician finds tenderness on palpation. Where does each item belong in a SOAP note?
opciones: The reported pain is subjective and the tenderness found on examination is objective
Both belong under objective, since the clinician wrote them down during the same visit
Both belong under subjective, since abdominal complaints cannot be measured directly
The reported pain is objective and the tenderness found on examination is subjective
preguntas.explicacion: A common documentation mistake is blurring symptoms and signs. Symptoms are what the patient describes and go under subjective; signs are the objective findings related to the reported symptom and go under objective. preguntas.pregunta: A claim sits unpaid for weeks and the payer finally reports that the member cannot be matched. The patient's surname was mistyped at registration. Which phase of the revenue cycle should have caught it?
opciones: Patient data verification, which checks the name, age, eligibility and billing address
Charge capture, which assembles the documented visit, the services and the facility fees
Claim scrubbing, which searches the outgoing claim for coding and formatting errors
Remittance processing, which posts the payment and sorts the contractual write-offs
preguntas.explicacion: Verification is the phase whose whole job is to keep claims from being rejected, delayed or denied, and the data it checks are the full name, the age, insurance eligibility, the billing address and, above all, preauthorizations. Insurers have been known to let a claim languish over a misspelled name rather than report the failed match. preguntas.pregunta: Two boxes of gloves list different acceptable quality levels. What does a lower number mean?
opciones: A better glove, with fewer pinholes and micro-perforations
A thicker glove, made to be worn as the outer of two pairs
A cheaper glove, meant for handling clean supplies only
A sterile glove, treated so that microbes are eliminated
preguntas.explicacion: The acceptable quality level is a measure of how many defective units a batch may contain, so a lower figure means a higher quality glove with less potential for micro-perforation and fewer pinholes. The recommended minimum is 1.5 for surgical gloves and 2.5 for medical examination gloves. Sterility is a separate property: surgical procedures call for sterile gloves, which have been treated to eliminate microbes, and evidence supports two layers during surgery.

preguntas.pregunta: Immediately after washing a needlestick with soap and water, what does NIOSH tell the worker to do?
opciones: Report the incident to the supervisor and seek medical care right away
Wait 72 hours to see whether symptoms appear before reporting
Test the discarded needle for virus before deciding whether to report
Start the hepatitis B vaccine series on their own before reporting
preguntas.explicacion: NIOSH's steps are to wash punctures and cuts with soap and water, flush splashes, irrigate eyes, report the incident to the supervisor and immediately seek medical care to determine the risk; it adds that an incident report should be completed where applicable. The 72-hour figure is the outer limit for starting HIV PEP, not a waiting period. WHO's annex specifically says not to test discarded needles or syringes for virus, and any prophylaxis or vaccination is decided during the medical evaluation.

preguntas.pregunta: The prevacuum sterilizer is run each morning with a folded towel pack and a test sheet before the first load. What is being checked?
opciones: Whether air is leaking in or is not being removed, since trapped air blocks steam contact
Whether the resistant spores in the pack survive, which is the direct measure of lethality
Whether the chamber holds pressure long enough for a wrapped load to reach its temperature
Whether the wrap material still lets steam through after repeated laundering and folding
preguntas.explicacion: That is the Bowie-Dick test, and it detects air leaks and incomplete air removal. The sheet goes in the middle of the pack, the pack sits horizontally at the front bottom of an otherwise empty chamber over the drain, and a uniform color change means the vacuum is acceptable; a spot means air kept the steam off the indicator. Spores measure lethality, and that is a different test.

preguntas.pregunta: A trainee is taught the boundaries of the fossa before palpating it. Which muscles form its lateral and medial borders?
opciones: Brachioradialis on the lateral side and pronator teres on the medial side
Pronator teres on the lateral side and brachioradialis on the medial side
Biceps brachii on the lateral side and brachialis on the medial side
Brachialis on the lateral side and supinator on the medial side of the fossa
preguntas.explicacion: The triangle is bounded laterally by the medial edge of brachioradialis and medially by the lateral edge of pronator teres, with an imaginary line between the epicondyles of the humerus closing it above. Brachialis and supinator lie deeper: they form the floor rather than the sides.

preguntas.pregunta: Within what time after a thrombotic stroke does a thrombolytic agent significantly improve the patient's prognosis?
opciones: Within 3 hours
Within 30 minutes
Within 24 hours
Within 72 hours
preguntas.explicacion: A thrombolytic agent given within 3 hours of a thrombotic stroke improves the prognosis significantly, but some strokes are hemorrhagic, so the cause must be established first. Tissue plasminogen activator is the enzyme used. The 30-minute figure is the usual length of vascular spasm and 72 hours is the RhoGAM window after birth; neither applies here.

preguntas.pregunta: A mother phones about her 2-month-old, whose rectal temperature is 38.1 °C (100.6 °F). What does this call for?
opciones: The provider is contacted right away: 38 °C rectally at 3 months or under is reportable
Fluids and a repeat reading in 24 hours, since the value sits only slightly above the normal band
A repeat reading by the axillary route, because a rectal value is read one degree high
A lukewarm sponge bath first, and a call only if the reading has not come down by then
preguntas.explicacion: Infants of 3 months or younger are the one group where the threshold triggers a call on its own: a rectal reading of 38 °C (100.4 °F) or higher is reported to the provider immediately, whatever the baby looks like. Waiting a day applies to older children, and no route correction is applied to a rectal value.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Fever

preguntas.pregunta: Which structures form the central nervous system, and which form the peripheral nervous system?
opciones: Brain and spinal cord centrally; the nerves branching from them peripherally
Brain and cranial nerves centrally; the spinal cord and its nerves peripherally
Spinal cord and ganglia centrally; the brain and its coverings peripherally
Brain and meninges centrally; the spinal cord and the ganglia peripherally
preguntas.explicacion: The central nervous system is the brain and the spinal cord, both inside the dorsal body cavity and both wrapped in bone, meninges and cerebrospinal fluid. The peripheral system is everything that branches out from them, and it forms the communication network between the center and the rest of the body.
preguntas.fuente: SEER Training Modules, Nervous System: The Central Nervous System

preguntas.pregunta: An older patient arrives with her adult son, who answers every question for her. How should you handle the visit?
opciones: Ask the patient how she sees her son's role, and keep addressing her directly
Speak mainly to the son, since he manages her medications at home
Ask the son to leave the room before any question is put to her
Record the son as her legal decision-maker for the rest of the visit
preguntas.explicacion: Check with the patient about how they see the companion's role, to protect privacy, and keep the patient involved, sitting so both can be addressed face to face and not directing remarks only to the companion. Asking the companion to step out is an option for sensitive topics, and legal authority to decide exists only for a named health care agent or proxy.

preguntas.pregunta: A culture is knocked over and spills a large volume in the laboratory. How is the hypochlorite used?
opciones: A 1:10 dilution for the first application before cleaning, then a 1:100 terminal disinfection
A 1:100 dilution for the first application before cleaning, then a 1:10 terminal disinfection
A 1:10 dilution applied once after the visible matter has been cleaned up and discarded
A 1:100 dilution applied twice, with the second application left in place for thirty minutes
preguntas.explicacion: With a large spill, over about 10 mL, or with a laboratory culture spill, the stronger 1:10 dilution goes on first, before cleaning, so that the risk from a sharps injury during the cleanup is already reduced. A terminal disinfection with the 1:100 dilution follows. Visible matter is picked up with disposable absorbent material and discarded in labeled containment.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization (2008), Recommendations 5n: Environmental Surfaces

preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks whether to skip his blood-pressure pill before a fasting draw. What is the correct guidance?
opciones: Do not stop a medicine unless the provider said to; ask the provider
Skip every medicine on the morning of the draw, because all pills break a fast
Take it only with a little juice so that the stomach is protected
Take it after the draw with water, never before a fasting sample
preguntas.explicacion: Patients should ask the provider whether their usual prescription and over-the-counter medicines are fine; for some tests the provider may ask them to stop, but a medicine is never stopped unless the provider says so. Vitamins and supplements should also be reported. Juice is on the list of drinks that break a fast.

preguntas.pregunta: Where should the sharps container sit while a phlebotomist is drawing blood at the bedside?
opciones: Visible and within arm's reach, and sealed once it is used up
On the cart outside the room, so the patient does not see it
In the utility room, where the used needles are carried after
On the floor by the bed, where it cannot be knocked over easily
preguntas.explicacion: The best-practice table asks for puncture and leak-proof containers that are sealed after use, kept visible and within arm's reach, and the reason given is that this prevents needlestick injury to patients, health workers and the wider community. The bloodborne pathogens standard says the same in regulatory language: during use the container is easily accessible and as close as feasible to where sharps are used, kept upright, and replaced before it overfills.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010), Annex A, Table B.1: Sharps containers; OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(4)(iii)(A)(2)

preguntas.pregunta: How is the standard of care defined when negligence is alleged?
opciones: The care a reasonable clinician with similar training and experience would provide
The care described in the facility's written policies, as approved by its governing body
The best care available anywhere in the country at the time of the event
The care the patient expected when consenting, as recorded on the consent form
preguntas.explicacion: Negligence is judged against the standard of care, defined as what a reasonable physician in the community with similar training and experience would do for that patient; it does not demand perfection, and some states speak of gross negligence. Malpractice itself is the failure to provide the degree of care another clinician in the same position with the same credentials would have provided, resulting in injury. Facility policies and patient expectations may be evidence, but the legal yardstick is the reasonable, similarly trained clinician.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Medical Malpractice", Introduction and Negligence or breach of duty

preguntas.pregunta: Why is absorption from a subcutaneous injection slow and sustained?
opciones: The layer beneath the dermis holds few blood vessels, so the drug leaves it gradually
The layer beneath the dermis is richly vascular, so the drug pools there before moving
The drug has to cross the epidermis first, and that barrier slows every molecule down
The drug travels through the portal vein, so the liver removes part of every dose
preguntas.explicacion: A subcutaneous injection is placed in the layer of skin just under the dermis and epidermis. That tissue carries few blood vessels, so what is injected is taken up at a slow, sustained rate. The usual sites are the outer area of the upper arm, the abdomen while staying clear of a two-inch circle around the navel, the front of the thigh, the upper back and the upper buttock behind the hip bone.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Medication Routes of Administration", Anatomy and Physiology: Parenteral Route

preguntas.pregunta: A processor inspects centrifuged serum tubes and sets aside the ones that look pink. Why do current recommendations favour an automated hemolysis index over this visual check?
opciones: Visual detection is inaccurate: serum looks hemolysed only above about 0.2 to 0.3 g/L, whereas the index is reproducible
Visual detection is accurate for serum but not for plasma, so the index is needed only for anticoagulated tubes
Visual detection is reliable above 0.5 g/L, but only the index can detect hemolysis before centrifugation
Visual detection cannot distinguish hemolysis from lipemia, whereas the index reports both as a single value
preguntas.explicacion: Sample quality used to be judged by looking at the tube before and after spinning, but visual detection is inaccurate: after separation, free hemoglobin becomes visible only around 0.2 to 0.3 g/L, while the cut-off for clinically significant interference is 0.5 g/L. Chemistry analyzers measure the serum indices, hemolysis included, with high reproducibility, which is why systematic automated measurement is strongly recommended.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Detection of haemolysis, a frequent preanalytical problem in the serum of newborns and adults" (EJIFCC 2020, PMC7109500), Introduction

preguntas.pregunta: A Medicare patient describes a brief real-time exchange with her doctor that lasted under ten minutes. What is that called?
opciones: A virtual check-in
An online e-visit
A monitoring session
A telephone triage call
preguntas.explicacion: Medicare describes several ways to use telehealth. E-visits are non-face-to-face communications that usually run through an online patient portal. Virtual check-ins are brief, real-time communications that usually last ten minutes or less. Both sit alongside the fuller telehealth visits that replace services normally given in person, such as office visits and psychotherapy.
preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Telehealth

preguntas.pregunta: Which statement about high-level, intermediate-level and low-level disinfectants is accurate?
opciones: A high-level agent kills everything except small numbers of spores; a low-level one spares spores entirely
A high-level agent is sporicidal at any contact time; an intermediate one is sporicidal only if left overnight
An intermediate-level agent reliably kills spores; a high-level one is defined by killing mycobacteria alone
A low-level agent kills mycobacteria and most fungi; a high-level one is limited to vegetative bacteria
preguntas.explicacion: The ladder is built on what survives. High-level agents are the same chemicals used as sterilants but for shorter exposure, so they leave only small numbers of spores. Intermediate-level agents may kill mycobacteria, vegetative bacteria and most viruses and fungi but not spores, and low-level ones handle most vegetative bacteria and some fungi and viruses within about ten minutes.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization (2008), Definition of Terms

preguntas.pregunta: A patient using a cane reaches a step going up. Which leg leads, and how is a turn made?
opciones: The stronger leg steps up first, and turns are made on the strong leg
The weaker leg steps up first, and turns are made on the weaker leg
The stronger leg steps up first, and turns are made on the weaker leg
The weaker leg steps up first, and turns are made on the strong leg
preguntas.explicacion: Going up a step or a curb, the stronger leg goes first. Turning is done by pivoting on the strong leg, not the weak one. While walking on the level, the cane swings forward the same distance as the weaker leg and lands even with that foot, and the strong leg then steps past both.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Patient Instructions: Using a cane — Stepping Up or Down a Step or Curb; and Walking and Turning with a Cane

preguntas.pregunta: Which code set is used to report the patient's diagnosis on a claim?
opciones: ICD-10-CM, the clinical modification used for diagnostic information
ICD-10-PCS, the procedure system used for inpatient facility claims
HCPCS Level II, the system used for supplies, equipment and ambulance
The national drug codes, used for the drugs and biologics dispensed
preguntas.explicacion: Diagnostic information is coded with ICD-10-CM, the clinical modification maintained on the CDC side. The procedure coding system, ICD-10-PCS, is used for procedures on inpatient facility claims under Part A. HCPCS Level II names products, supplies, ambulance services and equipment, and national drug codes identify drugs and biologics, so none of the three carries the diagnosis.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient fasted twelve hours before a blood count on his own initiative, though nobody asked him to. What is the concern?
opciones: Fasting when it was not ordered can itself skew some test results
Fasting beyond eight hours voids any test drawn that same morning
Fasting without an order has to be logged as a protocol deviation
Fasting is harmless here, and the sample is unaffected either way
preguntas.explicacion: Patients are told plainly not to fast unless the provider asks them to, because fasting for some blood tests may itself affect the results and hand the provider an inaccurate picture of the patient's health. The instruction is to follow the preparation instructions given; no rule voids a sample because the fast ran long.

preguntas.pregunta: An office needs to bill for a wheelchair supplied to a patient at home. Which code set covers that item?
opciones: HCPCS Level II, which names durable medical equipment and similar supplies
HCPCS Level I, which names the professional services physicians perform
ICD-10-PCS, which names procedures reported on inpatient facility claims
The code on dental procedures, which names items dispensed to patients
preguntas.explicacion: HCPCS Level II exists precisely because insurers cover services, supplies and equipment that Level I codes do not identify: it names products, supplies, ambulance services and durable medical equipment, prosthetics, orthotics and supplies used outside a physician's office. Level I describes medical procedures and professional services, and dental nomenclature covers dental services.

preguntas.pregunta: A transplant patient is scheduled for a tacrolimus level. What timing does the reported reference range assume?
opciones: The sample is taken 12 hours after the dose
The sample is taken 2 hours after the dose
The sample is taken immediately before the dose
The sample is taken at any hour of the day
preguntas.explicacion: Tacrolimus is reported as 5 to 25 ng/mL with the sample drawn 12 hours after the dose, and the two other drugs used to suppress the immune response against transplanted organs carry the same note: cyclosporine 25 to 525 ng/mL and sirolimus 4 to 14 ng/mL, both at 12 hours. A level drawn off that schedule cannot be read against the published range.

preguntas.pregunta: An unaccompanied 10-year-old with an emergency medical condition needs urgent labs and no parent can be reached. What protects the team that proceeds?
opciones: The emergency exception, also called the doctrine of implied consent
The mature minor doctrine, because the child understands the test
Informed permission, granted on the spot by the hospital administrator
Title X of the Public Health Service Act, covering minors' services
preguntas.explicacion: EMTALA requires a screening exam regardless of consent, and that when an emergency condition is found in an unaccompanied minor, life- or limb-saving care proceeds without waiting for parental consent, protected by the emergency exception rule or doctrine of implied consent, which assumes a reasonable parent would agree. Title X covers reproductive services.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks whether a wristwatch and rings are what is spoiling the tracing. What is the case?
opciones: Watches, glasses, rings and bracelets do not cause it
Watches and rings cause it, although glasses do not
Metal objects cause it whenever they touch a lead wire
They cause it only in a room holding several machines
preguntas.explicacion: Jewelry is not the source of electrical interference: watches, glasses, rings and bracelets are named as things that do not cause it, so the hunt goes to the electrode contact and to nearby equipment. Preparation guidance still has metallic objects removed before the recording begins.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient weighing a Medicare Advantage Plan against Original Medicare asks which one caps what she can spend in a year.
opciones: The plan does, through a yearly limit after which it pays all covered services
The plan does not, and neither does Original Medicare without extra coverage
Original Medicare does, through the deductible she pays once each calendar year
Neither does, since a yearly limit belongs to Medigap policies alone
preguntas.explicacion: Original Medicare sets no yearly limit on what a person pays out of pocket unless she adds supplemental coverage such as a Medigap policy or joins a Medicare Advantage Plan. Advantage plans carry an out-of-pocket limit that varies by plan; once it is reached the plan pays the whole cost of covered services for the rest of the calendar year.

preguntas.pregunta: Where do the coronary arteries arise, and where does most of the blood from the coronary veins drain?
opciones: From the ascending aorta; into the coronary sinus and then the right atrium
From the aortic arch; into the coronary sinus and then the left atrium
From the pulmonary trunk; directly into the superior vena cava
From the ascending aorta; into the four pulmonary veins and left atrium
preguntas.explicacion: The right and left coronary arteries branch from the ascending aorta, and they are the only branches of that segment. After passing through the myocardial capillaries most cardiac veins empty into the coronary sinus, which opens into the right atrium on its posterior wall, just above and medial to the opening of the inferior vena cava.

preguntas.pregunta: Which finding on an arm rules that arm out for a blood pressure cuff altogether, rather than merely calling for caution?
opciones: A dialysis arteriovenous fistula or shunt built into that arm
Swelling from lymphedema that followed surgery on that side
An indwelling venous catheter running in that arm at present
Weakness of that arm left behind by an old cerebrovascular event
preguntas.explicacion: Cuff limitations come in two tiers. A dialysis fistula or shunt, a recent surgical wound and a mastectomy on that side put the limb out of use entirely. Lymphedema, paresis or paralysis, and arterial or venous lines call for caution instead. In either tier the answer is the same: choose the other limb or another site before inflating.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Blood Pressure Measurement", Contraindications

preguntas.pregunta: An insurer asks a substance use disorder treatment program to confirm that a named person is a patient there. What may the program say?
opciones: Nothing that would reveal the person has been diagnosed or treated there
Only the dates of admission and of discharge, with no clinical detail at all
That the regulations bar it from confirming this particular patient
The detail the insurer needs, since payment is a permitted purpose
preguntas.explicacion: An answer that is not permitted has to be given in a way that does not reveal that an identified person has been or is being diagnosed or treated for a substance use disorder. The program may hand the inquirer a copy of the rules and explain that they restrict disclosure in general, but it may not say that they restrict the records of that named patient — which is a confirmation in disguise.

preguntas.pregunta: When must HIV post-exposure prophylaxis begin, and how long does the course last, according to the CDC?
opciones: As soon as possible and within 72 hours; a 28-day course
As soon as possible and within 7 days; a 14-day course
As soon as possible and within 24 hours; a 7-day course
Within 72 hours; a 6-month course, the length of follow-up
preguntas.explicacion: Patients who seek care within 72 hours are evaluated rapidly; PEP is not recommended more than 72 hours after exposure because it is unlikely to work, and the regimen is 28 days of a three-drug antiretroviral combination. WHO's annex gives the same limits: start within 72 hours and take the drugs continuously for 28 days. Six months is the length of antibody follow-up after an exposure, not the length of treatment, and the CDC's occupational page adds that PEP must start within 72 hours.

preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist arrives at room 412 to collect a CBC. Which pair of identifiers satisfies The Joint Commission's NPSG.01.01.01 for laboratory services?
opciones: The patient's stated full name plus the assigned identification number
The room number 412 plus the assigned identification number on the band
The patient's stated full name plus the physical location of the bed
The assigned identification number read from the chart, used on its own
preguntas.explicacion: NPSG.01.01.01 asks for at least two identifiers whenever blood or other specimens are collected. The goal's rationale accepts a name, an assigned identification number, a telephone number or another person-specific identifier, and EP 1 states outright that a room number or physical location is not used as one. A single identifier from the chart does not reach two.

preguntas.pregunta: Which group do a blood pressure cuff, a bedpan and a pair of crutches belong to, and why?
opciones: Noncritical, because they meet intact skin, which blocks most microbes on its own
Semicritical, because they can reach mucous membranes if a patient is moved carelessly
Critical, because a cuff is inflated over a limb where the vascular system runs beneath
Noncritical, because they are cleaned in a central area away from where they get used
preguntas.explicacion: Noncritical items touch intact skin and not mucous membranes, and intact skin is itself an effective barrier, so their sterility is not critical. That is why cuffs, bedpans, crutches and computers can be decontaminated right where they are used instead of travelling to central processing, unlike critical and many semicritical items.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization (2008), A Rational Approach: Noncritical Items

preguntas.pregunta: Two heel-pricks on an infant have failed to give a satisfactory sample. What is the next step?
opciones: Seek a second opinion on whether to try again or cancel the tests
Make a third attempt on the other heel with a longer lancet
Switch to a finger-prick, which is allowed once the heel has failed twice
Repeat the puncture on the same site, since it is already open
preguntas.explicacion: There is a strict limit on the number of times a paediatric patient may be stuck: if no satisfactory sample has been collected after two attempts, seek a second opinion to decide whether to make a further attempt or cancel the tests. Reusing a puncture site is prohibited, and site choice follows age and weight, not the number of failures.

preguntas.pregunta: Which vessels are the only arteries in the post-natal body that carry relatively deoxygenated blood?
opciones: The pulmonary trunk and its branches
The four pulmonary veins to the left atrium
The coronary arteries off the ascending aorta
The venae cavae entering the right atrium
preguntas.explicacion: The pulmonary trunk and the pulmonary arteries it divides into are the only post-natal arteries carrying relatively deoxygenated blood, from the right ventricle toward the lungs, and the pulmonary veins are the only post-natal veins carrying highly oxygenated blood, into the left atrium. The coronary arteries branch from the ascending aorta with oxygenated blood; the venae cavae are veins.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient on an ACE inhibitor has a potassium of 5.6 mEq/L. Which mechanism accounts for the rise?
opciones: Less angiotensin II means less aldosterone, and potassium stops being secreted
More aldosterone is made, sodium and water return, and potassium leaves in urine
The Na-K-2Cl cotransporter is blocked, so potassium cannot return to the lumen
Bradykinin builds up in the lung, which is also what produces the class's cough
preguntas.explicacion: Hyperkalemia here is the mechanism of the drug showing itself. Blocking angiotensin II cuts the aldosterone that follows it; without aldosterone the tubule stops trading sodium reabsorption for the secretion of protons and potassium, so potassium climbs. Kidney disease or potassium-sparing drugs raise the risk further. Bradykinin accumulation explains the cough of this class, not the potassium.

preguntas.pregunta: The ward holds two patients named John Ramirez. Beyond the full name and date of birth, what does the accepted practice add before the draw?

The bed each of the two men occupies, written by hand on both laboratory forms
The middle initial only, since the ward clerk keeps the two charts well apart
The list of tests ordered, because the two requisitions ask for different work
preguntas.explicacion: Every admitted patient carries an ID bracelet, and the name and date of birth are asked and recorded. The accepted consensus adds one more general identifier, a social security number or an address, because supplementary data lowers the rate of preventable errors. Location never counts: the identification goal rules out the room number or physical place.

preguntas.pregunta: A scan is cut horizontally, dividing the body into an upper and a lower portion. Which plane was used?
opciones: The transverse plane, also called the axial plane
The frontal plane, also called the coronal plane
The sagittal plane, also called the lateral plane
The oblique plane, which meets the body at an angle
preguntas.explicacion: The transverse or axial plane is the horizontal one, and it separates upper from lower; the images it produces are called cross sections. preguntas.pregunta: A dressing change reveals thick, opaque, yellow-green drainage in the wound bed. How is that classified and handled?
opciones: Purulent drainage, which is never normal and is reported to the provider each time it appears
Serous drainage, which is normal during the inflammatory stage and is simply documented
Serosanguineous drainage, which is expected while the capillaries are still fragile and new
Sanguineous drainage, which means fresh bleeding and calls for pressure over the wound bed
preguntas.explicacion: Purulent exudate is thick and opaque and can be tan, yellow, green or brown; it is never considered normal in a wound bed, and any new purulent drainage goes to the provider. Serous drainage is clear, thin, watery plasma and is normal in small amounts during the inflammatory stage; serosanguineous adds a little blood, and sanguineous is fresh bleeding.

preguntas.pregunta: Which older adults are at the highest risk of abuse?
opciones: Those with cognitive impairment such as dementia
Those living alone with no relatives in the state
Those with private insurance and several specialists
Those recently discharged after elective surgery
preguntas.explicacion: Prevalence among older adults in the United States is put at 5 to 10 percent, and the abuser is usually someone the person knows: a relative, friend, neighbor, caregiver or facility staff. preguntas.pregunta: A combative patient bites a phlebotomist's forearm and breaks the skin. Under the standard, this contact is best described as which of these?
opciones: A parenteral exposure, since piercing the skin barrier by a human bite is listed as parenteral
Not an exposure incident, because saliva is not OPIM outside dental procedures
An occupational exposure but not an exposure incident, because no needle was involved
A contact exposure that requires Contact Precautions rather than post-exposure follow-up
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (b) defines parenteral as piercing the mucous membranes or the skin barrier through events such as needlesticks, human bites, cuts and abrasions, and an exposure incident as parenteral or mucous-membrane or non-intact-skin contact with blood or OPIM arising from the employee's duties. A bite that breaks the skin is therefore a parenteral route, and if blood is involved the post-exposure evaluation of (f)(3) applies. Saliva is OPIM only in dental procedures, but the bite itself is the parenteral event; needles are one example of the route, not the only one.

preguntas.pregunta: What is the difference between compensatory and punitive damages?
opciones: Compensatory damages cover the actual loss; punitive ones deter misconduct
Compensatory damages cover the legal fees; punitive ones cover the injury
Compensatory damages are set by statute; punitive ones are set by contract
Compensatory damages are paid by the insurer; punitive ones by the patient
preguntas.explicacion: Damages are what the court awards to make the injured party whole, and in most cases they are compensatory: calculated on the party's real losses, which in a tort case run from medical care, property damage and lost wages to pain and suffering. Where the court wants to deter future misconduct, it can add punitive damages on top.

A written program, filed with the Commission before the practice may rely on it
A written program, reviewed each year by the insurer that carries its liability cover
No written program, since the Rule reaches only businesses that face a high risk
preguntas.explicacion: The Rule is deliberately flexible: a business facing a high risk of identity theft may need a comprehensive program while one facing a low risk may need only a streamlined one, and where the risk is low the program might focus on how to respond when someone reports that an identity was misused. preguntas.pregunta: Sutures were placed on a patient's cheek and on the same patient's forearm. Which removal times apply?
opciones: About 5 to 7 days on the face, and 10 to 14 days on the trunk or an extremity
About 10 to 14 days on the face, and 5 to 7 days on the trunk or an extremity
About 2 to 3 days on the face, and 5 to 7 days on the trunk or an extremity
About 5 to 7 days on the face, and 21 to 28 days on the trunk or an extremity
preguntas.explicacion: Timing follows the site and the tension on the wound. Facial sutures usually come out at five to seven days, while the trunk and extremities are safer at ten to fourteen, depending on how active the patient is and on the quality of the tissue. Hold the tube firmly in the free hand and pierce the stopper at an angle toward the fingers
Remove the stopper, rest the tube in the palm and inject slowly against the inner wall of the tube
Hold the tube against the patient's arm so the syringe can be steadied on the skin

The first clinician to document that the patient has lost decisional capacity
The hospital's risk manager, who signs on behalf of the absent patient

Give the patient a state advance directive form already filled out
Give the patient's family a copy of any directive within 90 days
Give the admitting physician a signed directive before care starts

preguntas.pregunta: Under the OSHA Bloodborne Pathogens standard, what does the term "Universal Precautions" mean?
opciones: Treating all human blood and certain body fluids as if they carried a bloodborne pathogen
Treating as infectious only the blood of patients whose chart shows HIV or hepatitis B
Reasonably anticipated contact of skin, eyes or mucous membranes with blood in the course of one's duties
Controls that isolate or remove the hazard from the workplace, such as sharps containers and safer needles
preguntas.explicacion: In the standard's definitions, Universal Precautions is one approach to controlling infection: every specimen of human blood, and certain other body fluids, is handled as though it were known to carry HIV, HBV or another bloodborne pathogen. preguntas.pregunta: A new technician shakes each tube vigorously right after collection to make sure the additive mixes. What does the evidence quoted in the rejection study say about this?
opciones: Tubes should be inverted gently several times; instant vigorous mixing may itself produce hemolysis
Vigorous shaking is required for citrate tubes and optional for EDTA tubes, per manufacturers' data sheets

By the lower rim, which stays clean during a procedure
By the front, folded inward so the outside faces itself
By the strap, and then wiped dry with the gown's sleeve

preguntas.pregunta: Which behaviour is listed as a trigger to look further into a patient's decision-making capacity?

Asking several detailed questions about the tests ordered
Requesting that a relative be present during the draw
Preferring one particular arm for the venipuncture

Dilution of the sample with tissue fluid, as happens when a finger is squeezed

preguntas.pregunta: Blood placed in a plain glass tube clots on its own. Which factor starts that in-vitro clotting, and through which pathway?

preguntas.pregunta: During a surgical hand scrub, how are the hands and forearms held while rinsing, and why?
opciones: Hands above the elbows, so water runs off the least clean part
Hands below the elbows, as in the routine wash at the sink
Hands flat against the sink, so the water reaches the cuticles
Hands at the same height, so the soap is rinsed off evenly

The tubing keeps the shield from sliding over the used needle
The tubing has to be cut with scissors before it is discarded
preguntas.explicacion: A needle on a length of flexible tubing is awkward to get into a sharps container, and that awkwardness is itself an injury hazard. The related habit of parking the needle somewhere convenient, in a drip chamber, an intravenous port or bag, or even the bedding, leaves an exposed sharp behind. Cutting a contaminated needle is not an option either: shearing or breaking one is prohibited by the bloodborne pathogens standard.

preguntas.pregunta: A 24-hour urine was preserved with formaldehyde, and the laboratory is asked to run a dipstick on an aliquot. Which pattern of false results does formaldehyde produce on reagent strips?
opciones: False positives for leukocyte esterase, peroxidase reaction, urobilinogen and glucose
False negatives for leukocyte esterase, with the remaining reagent pads unaffected
False positives for albumin only, with the pH of the specimen shifted toward acidity
False negatives for glucose and ketones, with the specific gravity reading raised
preguntas.explicacion: Preservatives are used only occasionally because they alter the accuracy of the results: formaldehyde can produce false-positive reactions for leukocyte esterase, the peroxidase reaction, urobilinogen and glucose when strips are used. Mercury salts give a false-negative leukocyte esterase, thymol a false-positive albumin, and hydrochloric acid, used to keep cell structures and for steroid assays, changes the pH.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Urinalysis", section Interfering Factors (Preservatives)

preguntas.pregunta: A hospitalized patient is receiving heparin. Which coagulation test is used to monitor that drug, and in which tube is it collected?
opciones: The partial thromboplastin time, in a light blue sodium citrate tube
The prothrombin time with INR, in a light blue sodium citrate tube
The partial thromboplastin time, drawn in a dark green sodium heparin tube
The erythrocyte sedimentation rate, in a black-top citrate tube
preguntas.explicacion: Monitoring people taking heparin is a use of the PTT (also called aPTT), which measures the seconds the sample takes to clot; the PT/INR is the test tied to warfarin. Like all coagulation studies, the PTT goes in the light blue citrate tube of the WHO table, never in a heparin tube. The ESR measures how fast red cells settle and is a marker of inflammation, not of heparin.

preguntas.pregunta: Which notices does HHS OCR say Section 1557 requires covered entities to post?
opciones: Notices of nondiscrimination and of available language assistance
A notice of privacy practices and of patient rights under HIPAA rules
A notice of the two patient identifiers used by the laboratory
A notice of the fee schedule for interpreter services
preguntas.explicacion: Section 1557 requires covered entities to post notices of nondiscrimination and of the availability of language assistance, and HHS OCR offers sample notices in nearly 50 languages. Language assistance is free under Title VI and Section 1557, so a fee schedule would be wrong; privacy notices come from HIPAA, and identifiers from The Joint Commission's goal.

preguntas.pregunta: Which elements do most state statutes set as the minimum for an informed consent discussion?
opciones: Nature, benefits, risks and alternatives, plus the patient's capacity
Cost, insurance coverage, the referral needed and the appointment date
Diagnosis, prognosis, the physician's credentials and the facility's rating
Names of the staff involved, the equipment used and the disposal method
preguntas.explicacion: The statutory minimum in most American jurisdictions covers the nature of the therapy, its benefits, its risks, its reasonable alternatives, and an assessment of the patient's capacity to decide. The reasoning behind the list is that patients own their bodies and decide what risks to take, but cannot know the risks or the alternatives unless the professional tells them. Consent obtained without these pieces is what tort claims are later built on.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Rights and Ethics", Issues of Concern: Informed Consent Prior to Treatment

preguntas.pregunta: A patient scheduled for a 24-hour urine protein test had a CT scan with contrast dye two days ago. Why does this matter?
opciones: Contrast dye given within 3 days before the collection can affect the results, so the provider should be told
Contrast dye given within 3 hours before the collection can affect the results, so a short delay is enough
Contrast dye can affect the results only if it was given during the 24-hour collection period itself
Contrast dye lowers the specific gravity reading, so the collection should be extended to 48 hours
preguntas.explicacion: Among the factors that can distort a 24-hour urine result is radiographic contrast given within the 3 days before the test, along with dehydration, emotional stress, strenuous exercise, vaginal fluid in the urine and urinary tract infection. Three hours would be far too short a window. Contrast media falsely raise, not lower, specific gravity, and the fix is to inform the provider, not to lengthen the collection.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Urine 24-hour volume (003425), How to Prepare for the Test; and StatPearls, "Urinalysis", Results, Reporting, and Critical Findings (Specific Gravity)

preguntas.pregunta: An electronic device reports a very low value in a patient who looks well. How is that handled?
opciones: The value is confirmed manually, since these devices can misread outside the normal band
The value is accepted, since an electronic device removes the human error of listening
The value is repeated on the same device, which is enough to settle the question
The value is charted with a note, and no further reading is taken during that visit
preguntas.explicacion: Automated devices are reliable in the normal range but tend to read hypotensive values too high and hypertensive values too low, and it is exactly the abnormal readings that matter clinically. When a machine gives a suspicious value it is checked by hand. Unexpected findings are repeated with correct technique before decisions are made.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Physiology, Korotkoff Sound", Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k47 · CMA I.A.1.a · RMA III.E.2.c · NCMA 2B.7

preguntas.pregunta: For a finger-prick in an adult, which fingers does WHO Table 7.1 recommend, and which does it say to avoid?
opciones: The middle and ring fingers; avoid the thumb and index finger, and the little finger
The thumb and index finger; avoid the middle and ring fingers, and also the little finger
The index and middle fingers; avoid the thumb, the ring finger and the little finger
Any finger except the thumb, provided the lancet is placed on the fingerprint lines
preguntas.explicacion: Table 7.1 recommends the second and third fingers, that is the middle and ring finger, with the lancet on the side of the ball of the finger perpendicular to the fingerprint lines. It says to avoid the thumb and index finger because of calluses and the little finger because its tissue is thin. The lancet is not placed across the fingerprint lines.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 7.1

preguntas.pregunta: A physician leaves on a three-month sabbatical without telling patients or arranging emergency coverage. How is that treated?
opciones: As inadvertent abandonment, since care stopped with no notice and no substitute clinician
As intentional abandonment, since an absence of that length is planned months beforehand
As no abandonment, because nobody was ever told the relationship had come to an end
As an ending chosen by the patients, who were free to find another clinician meanwhile
preguntas.explicacion: A clinician need not intend to end the relationship to be liable for abandonment. The example given is exactly this: failing to notify patients or arrange emergency coverage during a prolonged vacation or sabbatical. Being unresponsive to a patient's calls or e-mails, and failing to follow up after surgery or a new medication, are treated the same way.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, Abandonment, Clinical Significance

preguntas.pregunta: A patient short of breath sits leaning forward with the elbows resting on the knees. What is this called?
opciones: The tripod position, assumed to enhance lung expansion and air exchange
The lawnchair position, with hips and knees flexed above the level of the heart
The frog-leg position, with hips and knees flexed and rotated outward
The high Fowler position, sitting fully upright at a 90-degree angle
preguntas.explicacion: Patients who cannot get enough air often adopt this posture without being told, leaning forward on their elbows or on a table. It opens the chest and improves air exchange, and it is a visible sign of pulmonary distress during the inspection stage of a chest examination. Lawnchair and frog-leg are variations of supine, used for comfort and for perineal access.
preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 13: Repositioning Patients — Tripod Position
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B4 k61 · RMA III.F.2 · NCMA 2B.9

preguntas.pregunta: If a tourniquet becomes necessary for life-threatening limb bleeding, where is it placed?
opciones: 2 to 3 inches above the wound, avoiding the joint, noting the time
Directly over the wound, tightened until the bleeding stops
4 to 5 finger widths above the wound, released every 2 minutes
Just below the joint nearest the wound, loosened every 10 minutes
preguntas.explicacion: A tourniquet is used only when continuous pressure has not stopped extremely severe bleeding, and it is applied to the limb 2 to 3 inches, 5 to 7.7 centimeters, above the wound, avoiding the joint and moving above it toward the torso if necessary, preferably over clothing or padding rather than bare skin. The time of application is written down or memorized and told to responders, because a tourniquet left on too long injures nerves and tissue. Four to five finger widths and two minutes are venipuncture tourniquet figures, not first-aid ones.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Bleeding, When to Use a Tourniquet
preguntas.subtema: Tourniquet for hemorrhage · CPT D1 1M k37 · CMA I.B.9.a · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2A.10

preguntas.pregunta: A laboratory clearing out its storeroom asks whether the analyser printouts filed with old patient results can be thrown away. What does CLIA require?
opciones: Records of patient testing, printouts included, have to be kept
Printouts may go once the result is reported and verified
Printouts are kept only for tests sent to an outside laboratory
Printouts are kept only when the specimen failed acceptability
preguntas.explicacion: Beyond the four items the record system must contain, the same standard adds a plain sentence: records of patient testing, including instrument printouts where they exist, must be retained. There is no carve-out for tests that were already reported, for referred work, or for problem specimens; the retention rule covers the patient testing record as a whole.
preguntas.fuente: 42 CFR 493.1283(b), Standard: Test records

preguntas.pregunta: How long must a covered entity retain its HIPAA policies, procedures and other required documentation?
opciones: Six years from creation or last effective date, whichever is later
Three years from creation, matching OSHA training records
Thirty years, matching OSHA employee medical records
Ten years from creation, matching the period for Medicare claims documentation
preguntas.explicacion: Section 164.530(j) requires policies and procedures to be kept in written or electronic form, together with every communication the rule requires in writing and every action, activity or designation it requires to be documented, for six years from the date of creation or the date it was last in effect, whichever is later. The same section requires a privacy official, a complaints contact, workforce training, safeguards, a complaint process, sanctions, mitigation and no retaliation. Three and thirty years are OSHA periods, not HIPAA ones.

preguntas.pregunta: Besides the bloodborne pathogens, which vaccination history is reviewed after a puncture wound from a needle?
opciones: Tetanus, since the date of the last dose guides what is given
Influenza, since the season decides whether a dose is due
Measles, since a worker without immunity may be excluded
Hepatitis A, since the wound was contaminated with blood
preguntas.explicacion: A needlestick is a puncture wound, so tetanus risk is assessed along with the bloodborne pathogens, and prophylaxis is decided from the type of wound, the date of the most recent tetanus-containing vaccine and whether the primary series was completed. The hepatitis B vaccination status is reviewed for the same visit, because it decides whether immune globulin is needed. There is no vaccine for hepatitis C, and measles immunity is a work-restriction question, not a wound question.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Needlestick", History and Physical; Evaluation

preguntas.pregunta: Which 1986 measure made the right to refuse treatment enforceable for patients in facilities using federal insurance programs?
opciones: 42 CFR § 482.13, issued by the executive branch
The AHA's 1973 patient bill of rights
Cruzan v. Director, decided by the Supreme Court
The Norwood-Dingell Bill passed by Congress
preguntas.explicacion: 42 CFR § 482.13 dates from 1986 and is the foundational list of enforceable American patient rights, though directly enforceable only where federal health insurance programs are used, and notes it confirmed that a patient with capacity may refuse any treatment. The AHA bill of 1973 had little enforceability, Cruzan came in 1990, and Congress rejected Norwood-Dingell.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Rights and Ethics", sections History (1973, 1986) and Treatment Refusal
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 k14 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7A k215 · CMA E.1.d (both outlines) · RMA I.C.1.c · NCMA 4.7

preguntas.pregunta: Which coverage counts as minimum essential coverage?
opciones: A job-based plan, a Marketplace plan, Medicare, Medicaid or CHIP coverage
A job-based plan or a Marketplace plan, but not a public program coverage
A grandfathered policy bought before March 23, 2010, and no other coverage
Any policy that pays cash benefits toward hospital stays and lost earnings
preguntas.explicacion: Minimum essential coverage is any plan that satisfies the health care law's coverage requirement, and the examples given are Marketplace plans, job-based plans, Medicare, and Medicaid with CHIP; TRICARE and certain other coverage also qualify. Public programs are therefore included. Grandfathered policies are individual plans bought on or before March 23, 2010, a separate category, and a cash indemnity policy is not health coverage in this sense.

preguntas.pregunta: What must a practice's contingency plan under the Security Rule provide for?
opciones: Backing up ePHI, restoring lost data and running critical processes in emergency mode
Buying a second electronic health record from a different vendor as a permanent standby
Printing the whole record of every active patient at the close of each business day
Notifying the Secretary of any system failure that lasts longer than a single work shift
preguntas.explicacion: The contingency plan is the administrative safeguard for responding to emergencies or other events that damage the systems holding ePHI. It has to include plans for backing the information up, restoring whatever is lost, and continuing the critical business processes that protect the security of ePHI while the entity operates in emergency mode.

preguntas.pregunta: The WHO Annex C script for explaining the procedure opens with which three points?
opciones: The worker's name, the facility, and that they are trained to take blood
The worker's name, the tests ordered, and the colours of the tubes needed
The worker's name, the ordering doctor, and when the results are expected
The worker's name, the patient's diagnosis, and the reason for the tests
preguntas.explicacion: Annex C begins with the worker giving their name and saying they work at the facility, then asks the patient's name to check it against the order and any name band, and then states that the worker is trained and experienced in taking blood. The tests and the clinician who will receive the results come later in the script; the diagnosis is never part of it.

preguntas.pregunta: Which needle and which volume are used for a subcutaneous injection in an adult?
opciones: 25 to 31 gauge, half to five eighths of an inch, and no more than 1 mL
25 to 27 gauge, three eighths to five eighths of an inch, and 0.1 mL
18 to 25 gauge, half to an inch and a half, and 2 to 5 mL for an adult
22 to 25 gauge, one inch, and up to 3 mL given at the vastus lateralis
preguntas.explicacion: Subcutaneous needles run from 25 to 31 gauge and from half an inch to five eighths of an inch, and the volume is no more than 1 mL in an adult, or 0.5 mL in infants and small children, because larger amounts may not be absorbed properly and add discomfort. The first alternative describes an intradermal injection, and the other two describe intramuscular ones.
preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, ch. 18.3, Table 18.2, and ch. 18.5

preguntas.pregunta: Blood gas samples from a distant ICU keep arriving clotted, and the wards still draw with syringe, needle and container rather than an evacuated tube system. Which two responses did the emergency laboratory adopt?
opciones: Placing point-of-care blood gas analyzers in the ICUs under laboratory control, and teaching use of the evacuated tube system
Adding heparin to every syringe on arrival in the laboratory, and asking the ICUs to send samples only during the day shift
Accepting clotted gas samples with a cautionary comment, and moving all blood gas testing to the core laboratory
Requiring each ICU to centrifuge gas samples before sending them, and doubling the frequency of the courier rounds
preguntas.explicacion: To reduce clotted blood gas samples attributed to long transport routes, the laboratory set up several point-of-care blood gas analyzers in the ICUs and emergency departments under the control of laboratory specialists; and because collection with the conventional syringe, needle and container system was still seen on the wards and was thought to add to the fibrin-clotted samples, its education seminars covered venipuncture technique, appropriate additive tubes, order of tubes, gentle mixing and transport. Rapid serum tubes were the answer for early-spun serum.

preguntas.pregunta: The patient about to be dismissed belongs to a managed care plan the practice contracts with. What step comes before the letter goes out?
opciones: Asking the insurer whether its contract restricts how and when the practice may end care
Asking the insurer to move her to another clinician in the network before she is told
Asking the insurer to extend her benefits thirty days so that care is not interrupted
No step at all, since a contract with a plan has no bearing on ending a clinical relationship
preguntas.explicacion: Where the patient belongs to a managed care organization the clinician participates in, the insurer should be contacted first to find out what restrictions it places on termination. Contracts with third-party payers often limit referrals to clinicians outside that network, and some insurers require thirty days' notice to the insurer as well as to the patient. Government payers are stricter.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient slid off the drawing chair during a faint and struck the arm of it. What must not be overlooked?
opciones: Injuries from the fall, which need attention straight away
The tube already drawn, which has to be discarded and repeated
The tourniquet, which must be reapplied before the patient moves
The label, which is rewritten because the draw was interrupted
preguntas.explicacion: Any injury sustained in a fall from a faint requires immediate attention, and patients who collapse frequently need a trauma assessment for what they hit on the way down. preguntas.pregunta: Whom must a covered entity train on its privacy policies and procedures?
opciones: All workforce members, as suited to their functions, including new hires
Only clinical staff who document care in the medical record
Only the privacy official and the contact person for complaints
Only paid employees; volunteers and students fall outside the training rule
preguntas.explicacion: Section 164.530(b) requires training of all members of the workforce on the privacy policies and procedures, as necessary and appropriate for their functions: everyone by the compliance date, each new member within a reasonable time after joining, and anyone whose functions are affected by a material change in the policies, with the training documented. preguntas.pregunta: How is a patient draped for a pelvic examination?
opciones: Undressed from the waist down and kept under a sheet until she is properly positioned
Positioned first and then draped, so that the foot supports can be adjusted without a sheet
Draped from the shoulders down, with the absorbent pad laid over the abdominal wall instead
Left uncovered from the start, because the external inspection comes before the speculum
preguntas.explicacion: She undresses from the waist down and stays covered by a drape, uncovered only while the examination is actually running and for as short a time as possible. An absorbent pad goes under the buttocks, not over the abdomen. A chaperone, usually the assistant, stays in the room, and consent is obtained before anything begins.

preguntas.pregunta: Which cards are used to screen color vision?
opciones: Pseudoisochromatic plates, such as the Ishihara set of test cards
Landolt C cards, on which a broken ring faces in several directions
Tumbling E cards, designed for children and non-readers of the alphabet
LEA symbol cards, designed to remove the language barrier in children
preguntas.explicacion: Colour vision is screened with plates carrying numbers formed from dots of particular colours; the Ishihara set is the familiar one, and Hardy-Rand-Rittler plates work the same way. They do not separate the different types of colour deficiency well. The Landolt C, tumbling E and LEA symbol charts are acuity charts, not colour tests.

preguntas.pregunta: A urine specimen for a molecular assay will sit for several hours before extraction. Why is it either processed at once or refrigerated?
opciones: Its low pH and urea denature the nucleic acid at ambient temperature
Its bacteria multiply at ambient temperature and consume the target
Its bilirubin breaks down in the light and quenches the fluorescent dye
Its specific gravity climbs as it evaporates, concentrating inhibitors
preguntas.explicacion: Urine is processed immediately or held at 2 to 8 °C for two reasons. First, the generally low pH of urine and its urea content denature DNA at 25 °C and above. Second, prolonged storage in the cold encourages uric acid, calcium oxalate and phosphorus to precipitate, and those precipitates can themselves inhibit the amplification, so neither extreme is harmless.

preguntas.pregunta: How small a risk must still be disclosed to a patient, according to the federal decision that shaped informed consent?
opciones: A risk of one percent, if it means death or a lasting harm
A risk of ten percent, no matter what harm it would cause
A risk of one percent, but only for elective procedures
A risk of five percent, unless the patient asks for more
preguntas.explicacion: A federal court held that a patient must be told about a risk as low as one percent when the harm in question is death or a life-altering complication such as paralysis. The severity of the outcome, not the size of the probability alone, decides. Because the three branches of government have left the minimum standard vague, these rights are usually enforced after the fact, through tort claims brought by patients.

Integrity, with a mechanism that shows stored information has not been altered
Access control, with unique identifiers and an automatic close of idle sessions
Audit controls, with the mechanisms that record and examine activity in the system
preguntas.explicacion: Transmission security is the standard for information travelling over an electronic communications network. preguntas.pregunta: A primary care office faxes a chart to the specialist it is sending the patient to. What permits that disclosure?
opciones: It is a treatment disclosure, and treatment activities need no authorization from the patient
It is a health care operations disclosure, allowed once both offices sign a shared privacy notice
It is a public interest disclosure, allowed because referrals serve the coordination of care
It is an incidental disclosure, allowed because the fax is a by-product of scheduling the visit
preguntas.explicacion: Treatment is defined as the provision, coordination or management of health care, consultation between providers, and the referral of a patient from one provider to another. A covered entity may disclose PHI for the treatment activities of any provider, and the example given is a primary care provider sending a record to a specialist who needs it. It is shorter than the brand name, so less of it can be misread on the order

When she agrees to a higher premium for the months already gone by this year
When her employer confirms in writing that it offers her no coverage at all
When the yearly window reopens on November 1 and closes on December 15

A machine switched on without its self test

preguntas.pregunta: A nurse auscultating a patient hears the 'lub' and then the 'dub'. What produces the second heart sound, S2?

Closing of the atrioventricular valves during ventricular systole
Opening of the semilunar valves during the ventricular ejection phase
Contraction of the atria pushing blood into a stiff, hypertrophic ventricle
preguntas.explicacion: A healthy heart has two audible sounds: S1, the lub, comes from the atrioventricular valves closing as the ventricles contract, and S2, the dub, from the semilunar valves closing as the ventricles relax. preguntas.pregunta: What distinguishes an endocrine gland from an exocrine gland?
opciones: An endocrine gland has no duct and releases hormones into the blood
An endocrine gland has a duct and releases hormones into the blood
An endocrine gland has no duct and releases enzymes onto a surface
An endocrine gland has a duct and releases enzymes onto a surface
preguntas.explicacion: Exocrine glands have ducts that carry their product to a surface, which is how sweat, sebaceous and mammary glands and the digestive enzyme glands work. Endocrine glands are ductless: their hormones go straight into the blood and travel everywhere, but they act only on the cells that carry a receptor for them.
preguntas.fuente: SEER Training Modules, Introduction to the Endocrine System
