cuerpo: The NCCT National Certified Medical Assistant exam has **150 questions: 125 scored and 25 unscored pretest items**, and you get **3 hours**. That is 72 seconds per question, the most generous pace in this app.

The detailed test plan, **effective January 2024**, has four content categories: Pharmacology and General Medical Knowledge (18 scored questions), Clinical Medical Procedures (72), Medical Administrative Duties (15) and Law and Ethics (20). The clinical category is broken down further into Infection Control and Safety (15), Patient Intake and Care (32), Phlebotomy (15) and ECG (10), and this app treats each of those as its own area.
NCCT says **92 % of the items are standard four-option multiple choice and 8 % are alternative items**: drag and drop, multi-select and hotspot questions where you click a place on an image.
guia.fuente: NCCT, National Certified Medical Assistant (NCMA) Detailed Test Plan, effective January 2024

cuerpo: NCCT reports a **scaled score**; the detailed test plan does not state the percentage of correct answers required to pass. This app uses **70 % as a study target** on practice tests built with the official split.

The plan is explicit that it reflects a national job analysis, and each competency is written as something a working medical assistant does: "follow CDC Standard Precautions", "perform basic medication-related calculations", "recognize common drug classifications". The questions in this app are written to those same tasks.
guia.fuente: NCCT, National Certified Medical Assistant (NCMA) Detailed Test Plan, effective January 2024

cuerpo: These are the areas of the official outline and how many scored questions each one gets in a 125-question practice test in this app:

**Pharmacology and General Medical Knowledge: 18 of 125** (14 %) · **Infection Control and Safety: 15 of 125** (12 %) · **Patient Intake and Care: 32 of 125** (26 %) · **Phlebotomy: 15 of 125** (12 %) · **ECG: 10 of 125** (8 %) · **Medical Administrative Duties: 15 of 125** (12 %) · **Law and Ethics: 20 of 125** (16 %).

Every practice test here draws **exactly that many questions from each area**, so it **matches the official content outline**. A practice test that pulls at random from the whole bank does not follow the outline at all, and it hides the areas where you are weak by burying them in the ones where you are strong. The diagnostic uses the same proportions, which is why its result by area tells you something.
guia.fuente: NCCT National Certified Medical Assistant (NCMA) Detailed Test Plan, effective January 2024

guia.titulo: What the alternative items look like
cuerpo: Roughly one question in twelve on the real exam is not a plain multiple-choice item. A drag-and-drop item may ask you to put the steps of a procedure in order or match tubes to tests; a multi-select item asks for every correct option, not one; a hotspot item asks you to click a location on a picture, such as an injection site or an electrode position.

The knowledge behind those items is the same knowledge this app tests. What is different is the format, and you should practice the format once with NCCT's own sample materials before exam day so that the mechanics do not cost you time.
guia.fuente: NCCT, National Certified Medical Assistant (NCMA) Detailed Test Plan, effective January 2024

cuerpo: Every exam in this app includes questions that do not count. They are pretest (or pilot) items: new questions the certifying body is trying out before using them for real. They are mixed in with the scored ones, they look exactly the same, and **you are not told which is which**.

The practical consequence is simple: **answer every question as if it counts.** Do not burn time trying to spot the experimental ones, and do not let a strange or very hard question rattle you: it may well be one that will never affect your score.

The practice tests in this app have **125 questions and no pretest items**, because there is no point in making you answer questions that do not count. The time limit matches the real exam's time for the scored plus unscored total, so the pace here is slightly more generous than the real thing.
guia.fuente: NCCT National Certified Medical Assistant (NCMA) Detailed Test Plan, effective January 2024

guia.titulo: How the practice tests here are built
cuerpo: **This app does not simulate the 8 % of alternative items** (drag and drop, multi-select, hotspot). Every question here is a four-option multiple-choice item. Expect the real exam to feel slightly different in format, not in content.

Each numbered practice test in this app is a **fixed set of questions**: Practice Test 3 is the same Practice Test 3 every time you open it, and it shares no question with Practice Test 2 or 4. That is what lets you work through them one by one, compare your score with last week's, and finish the set.
The order of the questions, and the order of the four options inside each question, is shuffled every time. You cannot pass by remembering that "the third one is B".

The timer runs at the pace of the real exam. The result screen shows your score against the study target, the time you took, and a breakdown by area, and every question you missed goes into your review list until you get it right three times in a row.

Every explanation names the public document it comes from: an OSHA regulation, a CDC guideline, a CLIA rule, a WHO guideline, a NIH source. None of the questions come from a textbook or from a real exam form.

To be plain about what these practice tests are: they are **not a copy of the real exam** and they are not the questions the certifying body administers. They **match the official content outline** — the areas, their weights, the number of questions and the pace — and every item is written by us from public sources. This app is an independent study aid, and it is not affiliated with or endorsed by any certifying body.
guia.fuente: NCCT National Certified Medical Assistant (NCMA) Detailed Test Plan, effective January 2024

guia.titulo: What is free and what is not
cuerpo: Without paying you can do four things. You can answer the first **3 questions of every area**, always the same ones, so that you see what the questions and the explanations look like in each part of the outline. You can take **a diagnostic** — a short test with the same proportions as the real exam that tells you your score by area — and repeat it every seven days with new questions. Every day you also get **five questions** from the whole bank, with their explanations. And you can read this whole guide.

What you cannot do for free is study an area to the end, take a full-length practice test, or review your mistakes. Those are the product, and they are unlocked with a single one-time purchase for this certification, or one purchase for every certification in the app. There is no subscription and there are no advertisements, and there never will be.

The number of questions and the number of practice tests you see on the home screen and on the purchase screen are read from the content itself. They are never typed in by hand, so they cannot promise more than the app contains.
guia.fuente: NCCT National Certified Medical Assistant (NCMA) Detailed Test Plan, effective January 2024

guia.titulo: What this app does not cover
cuerpo: This app follows the national outline published by the National Center for Competency Testing (NCCT). It does not cover the rules of your state, your employer's protocols, or the eligibility routes to sit the exam (training programs, work experience, documentation). Check those with the certifying body and with your program.

It is not an official product of the certifying body and has no connection with it. The outline is public; the questions and the explanations are ours, written from public sources you can open and read. If you find a mistake, tell us: every report is checked against the source and corrected in the content, without waiting for a new version of the app.
guia.fuente: NCCT National Certified Medical Assistant (NCMA) Detailed Test Plan, effective January 2024

calculos.titulo: Tablets to give: desired over have
calculos.enunciado: The provider orders metformin extended-release 1,000 mg by mouth once daily with the evening meal. The pharmacy stocks 500 mg extended-release tablets. How many tablets does the medical assistant prepare?

pasos.texto: Desired (D) is the ordered dose. Have (H) is the strength on hand. Quantity (Q) is the unit the strength comes in: here one tablet. StatPearls writes it as D/H x Q = x.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Dose Calculation Ratio and Proportion Method

pasos.titulo: Confirm the strength on hand exists
pasos.texto: The label lists extended-release tablets of 500 mg and 1,000 mg. The order is filled from the 500 mg tablet, so H = 500 mg per 1 tablet.
pasos.referencia: DailyMed (NLM/FDA): etiqueta de prescripción — GLUMETZA (METFORMIN HYDROCHLORIDE) TABLET, FILM COATED, EXTENDED RELEASE [SANTARUS, INC.]

pasos.texto: Milligrams cancel; the answer keeps the unit of Q, tablets. The label itself describes a 1,000 mg dose given as 2 x 500 mg tablets.
pasos.referencia: DailyMed (NLM/FDA): etiqueta de prescripción — GLUMETZA (METFORMIN HYDROCHLORIDE) TABLET, FILM COATED, EXTENDED RELEASE [SANTARUS, INC.]

pasos.titulo: Check that the answer is plausible
pasos.texto: Units of measurement must match before dividing: mg over mg. Two whole tablets is a sensible amount; a result of twenty tablets, or of two hundredths of one, means a unit slipped.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Dose Calculation Desired Over Have Formula Method

calculos.trampa: Putting Have over Desired (500 ÷ 1,000) gives 0.5 tablet: half the ordered dose, and an extended-release tablet can never be cut anyway (the label says swallow whole, never crush, cut or chew). The ordered dose always goes on top.

practica.enunciado: Order: 1,500 mg. On hand: 500 mg tablets. Tablets?
Order: 2,000 mg (the label's daily maximum). On hand: 1,000 mg tablets. Tablets?

calculos.titulo: Tablets to give: ratio and proportion
calculos.enunciado: A patient's metformin extended-release dose has been titrated to 1,500 mg once daily. The clinic sample cabinet has 500 mg extended-release tablets. Using ratio and proportion, how many tablets make one dose?

pasos.titulo: Set the known ratio equal to the unknown ratio
pasos.texto: Have on hand over the quantity you have equals the desired amount over x. The same units go in the same position on both sides: mg on top, tablets on the bottom.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Dose Calculation Ratio and Proportion Method

pasos.texto: H is 500 mg, Q is 1 tablet, D is 1,500 mg. The dose is within the label: it lists 1,500 to 2,000 mg/day as the range studied.
pasos.referencia: DailyMed (NLM/FDA): etiqueta de prescripción — GLUMETZA (METFORMIN HYDROCHLORIDE) TABLET, FILM COATED, EXTENDED RELEASE [SANTARUS, INC.]

pasos.texto: Multiply means and extremes, then divide both sides by 500. In colon format the same setup is H:Q::D:x, and Hx = DQ.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Dose Calculation Ratio and Proportion Method

pasos.texto: StatPearls recommends checking one method with another: the formula method lands on the same 3 tablets, so the setup was right.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Dose Calculation Ratio and Proportion Method

calculos.trampa: Writing 500/1 = x/1,500 (mixing the positions of D and x) and cross-multiplying gives x = 750,000, which is obviously not a tablet count. Same units, same position, on both sides of the equals sign.

practica.enunciado: Order: 1,000 mg. On hand: 500 mg tablets. Set up H/Q = D/x. Tablets?
Order: 2,000 mg. On hand: 1,000 mg tablets. Tablets?

calculos.titulo: Milliliters from a vial: desired over have
calculos.enunciado: A provider orders lorazepam 4 mg. The vial on hand is labeled 2 mg/mL. How many milliliters contain the ordered dose? (This is the worked example StatPearls uses for all three methods.)

pasos.titulo: Identify D, H and Q from the label
pasos.formula: D = 4 mg;  H = 2 mg;  Q = 1 mL
pasos.texto: With a liquid, the quantity is the volume that holds the strength: 2 mg are in 1 mL, so Q = 1 mL and H = 2 mg.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Dose Calculation Desired Over Have Formula Method

pasos.formula: D × Q ÷ H = 4 mg × 1 mL ÷ 2 mg = 2 mL
pasos.texto: Dose ordered (4 mg) times quantity (1 mL) divided by have (2 mg) equals the amount to give, 2 mL.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Dose Calculation Desired Over Have Formula Method

pasos.texto: The ordered dose and the available dose are both in mg, so they cancel and only mL is left, which is the unit the question asks for. No further conversion is needed.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Dose Calculation Desired Over Have Formula Method

pasos.texto: 2 mL is the volume drawn up. Because the answer is a volume, it is checked against the syringe size, not against a tablet count.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Dose Calculation Desired Over Have Formula Method

calculos.trampa: Reading 2 mg/mL as "2 mL per mg" and multiplying 4 × 2 gives 8 mL, four times the dose. The strength on the label is always mass per volume: the mg are what you have, the mL is the quantity they come in.

practica.enunciado: Order: 3 mg. On hand: 2 mg/mL. mL?
Order: 1 mg. On hand: 2 mg/mL. mL?

calculos.titulo: Milliliters from a vial: ratio and proportion in colon format
calculos.enunciado: The order is lorazepam 3 mg. The vial is 2 mg/mL. Solve it with ratio and proportion written in colon format, the way it appears on many exam items.

pasos.titulo: Write the proportion in colon format
pasos.texto: Have : Vehicle (the volume it comes in) :: Desired : x. The middle two terms are the means and the outer two are the extremes.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Dose Calculation Ratio and Proportion Method

pasos.texto: 2 mg in 1 mL, and 3 mg in the unknown x mL. Same unit in the same position on both sides.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Dose Calculation Ratio and Proportion Method

pasos.titulo: Product of means equals product of extremes
pasos.texto: Multiply the means (V and D) and the extremes (H and x), set them equal, and divide by H.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Dose Calculation Ratio and Proportion Method

pasos.formula: 2 mg / 1 mL = 3 mg / x  →  x = 1.5 mL
pasos.texto: The fraction form of the same proportion gives the same 1.5 mL, which is the double check StatPearls asks for before drawing anything up.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Dose Calculation Ratio and Proportion Method

calculos.trampa: Multiplying the two inner terms with the two outer terms in the wrong pairing (2 × 3 = 1 × x, x = 6 mL) is the classic colon-format error. Means with means, extremes with extremes: the unknown x is always an extreme, paired with H.

practica.enunciado: 2 : 1 :: 5 : x  (2 mg/mL vial, 5 mg ordered). x?
Vial 4 mg/mL, order 2 mg. Write H : V :: D : x and solve.

calculos.titulo: Milliliters from a vial: dimensional analysis
calculos.enunciado: The order is lorazepam 5 mg. The vial is 2 mg/mL. Set up a single line of factors (dimensional analysis, also called the factor-label method) so that only milliliters survive.

pasos.titulo: Put the unknown on the left and the ordered dose over 1
pasos.texto: The amount you want to find is placed over a denominator of one, and the equation grows into a single solvable line of fractions.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Dose Calculation Dimensional Analysis Factor-Label Method

pasos.titulo: Add the label as a factor with mg on the bottom
pasos.texto: The vial's factor is 1 mL per 2 mg. It is written with mg in the denominator so that the mg of the ordered dose cancels against it.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Dose Calculation Dimensional Analysis Factor-Label Method

pasos.titulo: Cancel like units and multiply across
pasos.texto: Like units in a numerator and a denominator cancel out; what remains is mL, the unit you set out to find. Multiply the numerators, divide by the denominators.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Dose Calculation Dimensional Analysis Factor-Label Method

pasos.titulo: Ask whether the answer is plausible
pasos.texto: The correct dose should be the same regardless of the method applied: D/H × Q gives 5 ÷ 2 × 1 = 2.5 mL as well, so the line was set up correctly.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Dose Calculation Desired Over Have Formula Method

calculos.trampa: Writing the label factor as 2 mg / 1 mL (mg on top) leaves mg² over mL: nothing cancels and the number 10 that comes out has no meaning. Every factor is placed so the unit you want to get rid of sits opposite itself.

practica.enunciado: x mL = 4 mg/1 × 1 mL/2 mg. x?
Cancel zeros first, then solve: 1000/500 × 10/5.

calculos.titulo: Insulin: units to milliliters and the right syringe
calculos.enunciado: A patient is to receive 24 units of U-100 regular human insulin subcutaneously. How many milliliters is that, and which insulin syringe size lets the dose be read most precisely?

pasos.texto: Standard insulin contains 100 units in 1 milliliter; that is what U-100 stands for. Every small notch on a standard 1 mL insulin syringe is 1 unit.
pasos.referencia: MedlinePlus Patient Instructions: Giving an insulin injection (000660)

pasos.texto: Units cancel and 0.24 mL remains. Insulin is drawn up by the unit marks on the syringe, never by converting to mL on a general-purpose syringe.
pasos.referencia: MedlinePlus Patient Instructions: Giving an insulin injection (000660)

pasos.texto: Insulin syringes come in sizes that hold 30, 50 and 100 units. A 24-unit dose fits in the 30-unit syringe, whose marks are the most spread out and therefore the easiest to read exactly.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Human Insulin

pasos.texto: Always use a syringe marked for the insulin's concentration: U-100 insulin in a U-100 syringe. Concentrated insulins (U-500) exist and need their own instructions.
pasos.referencia: MedlinePlus Patient Instructions: Giving an insulin injection (000660)

calculos.respuesta: 0.24 mL, drawn to the 24-unit mark of a 30-unit U-100 syringe
calculos.trampa: Drawing 24 units of U-500 insulin into a U-100 syringe delivers five times the dose. The number of units ordered never changes, but the volume per unit does, so the syringe must match the concentration on the vial.

practica.enunciado: 50 units of U-100 insulin. mL?
12 units of U-100 insulin. mL and best syringe?

calculos.titulo: Weight-based dose: mg/kg/day with pounds to kilograms
calculos.enunciado: A 44 lb child (under 40 kg) has a mild ear infection. The label's pediatric dose is 25 mg/kg/day of amoxicillin in divided doses every 12 hours. What is the daily dose in milligrams, and how many milligrams go in each dose?

pasos.texto: The conversion factor is 1 kg = 2.2 lb. Pounds divided by 2.2 gives kilograms; the label's mg/kg figure cannot be used until the weight is in kg.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Dose Calculation Desired Over Have Formula Method

pasos.titulo: Find the label's dose for this weight
pasos.texto: For patients over 3 months and under 40 kg with a mild or moderate ear, nose, throat, skin or genitourinary infection, the label gives 25 mg/kg/day in divided doses every 12 hours.
pasos.referencia: DailyMed (NLM/FDA): etiqueta de prescripción — AMOXICILLIN TABLET, COATED [REDPHARM DRUG]

pasos.titulo: Multiply dose per kilogram by the weight
pasos.texto: Kilograms cancel and the daily total is 500 mg. This is the whole day's amount, not a single dose.
pasos.referencia: DailyMed (NLM/FDA): etiqueta de prescripción — AMOXICILLIN TABLET, COATED [REDPHARM DRUG]

pasos.titulo: Divide the day into the ordered number of doses
pasos.texto: Every 12 hours means 2 doses in 24 hours, so each dose is 250 mg. The label lists this same pairing (500 mg every 12 hours or 250 mg every 8 hours) for adults, which shows the scale is right.
pasos.referencia: DailyMed (NLM/FDA): etiqueta de prescripción — AMOXICILLIN TABLET, COATED [REDPHARM DRUG]

calculos.trampa: Using 44 as if it were kilograms gives 1,100 mg/day, more than double the dose. Pounds must become kilograms first; and the other common slip is to hand the whole 500 mg over as one dose instead of splitting it into the two doses the order calls for.

practica.enunciado: 33 lb child, 25 mg/kg/day divided every 12 h. Per dose?
66 lb child, 20 mg/kg/day divided every 8 h. Per dose?

calculos.titulo: Weight-based dose divided every 8 hours
calculos.enunciado: A 30 kg child has a severe skin infection. The label's pediatric dose for severe infections is 40 mg/kg/day of amoxicillin in divided doses every 8 hours. How many milligrams per dose?

pasos.titulo: Take the dose per kilogram from the label
pasos.texto: For severe ear/nose/throat, skin or genitourinary infections in patients under 40 kg the label gives 45 mg/kg/day every 12 hours or 40 mg/kg/day every 8 hours. The order chose the every-8-hours form.
pasos.referencia: DailyMed (NLM/FDA): etiqueta de prescripción — AMOXICILLIN TABLET, COATED [REDPHARM DRUG]

pasos.texto: Kilograms cancel. The weight is already in kg, so there is no 2.2 step this time.
pasos.referencia: DailyMed (NLM/FDA): etiqueta de prescripción — AMOXICILLIN TABLET, COATED [REDPHARM DRUG]

pasos.texto: Every 8 hours is three times a day. The dosing interval, not the drug, decides the divisor.
pasos.referencia: DailyMed (NLM/FDA): etiqueta de prescripción — AMOXICILLIN TABLET, COATED [REDPHARM DRUG]

pasos.texto: Each of the three doses is 400 mg. As a scale check, the adult severe-infection dose on the same line is 500 mg every 8 hours, so 400 mg for a 30 kg child is in proportion.
pasos.referencia: DailyMed (NLM/FDA): etiqueta de prescripción — AMOXICILLIN TABLET, COATED [REDPHARM DRUG]

calculos.trampa: Dividing by 2 out of habit (as if every 12 hours) gives 600 mg per dose and 1,800 mg a day, half again the intended total. Read the interval in the order: every 8 hours is 3 doses, every 12 hours is 2, every 6 hours is 4.

practica.enunciado: 20 kg child, 45 mg/kg/day divided every 12 h. Per dose?
15 kg child, 40 mg/kg/day divided every 8 h. Per dose?

calculos.titulo: Weight-based dose with a daily maximum check
calculos.enunciado: A 22 lb toddler is to receive acetaminophen at the StatPearls pediatric dose of 15 mg/kg every 6 hours. What is each dose in milligrams, and does four doses a day stay under the stated maximum of 60 mg/kg/day?

pasos.texto: 1 kg = 2.2 lb. Dividing the weight in pounds by 2.2 gives 10 kg.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Dose Calculation Desired Over Have Formula Method

pasos.texto: The pediatric dose is 15 mg/kg every 6 hours. Kilograms cancel and each dose is 150 mg.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Pain Management Medications (analgésicos)

pasos.formula: 24 h ÷ 6 h = 4 doses  →  4 × 150 mg = 600 mg per day
pasos.texto: Every 6 hours is four doses a day, so the child would receive 600 mg in 24 hours.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Pain Management Medications (analgésicos)

pasos.texto: The stated ceiling is 60 mg/kg/day, which for 10 kg is 600 mg. The plan reaches the ceiling exactly and does not exceed it.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Pain Management Medications (analgésicos)

calculos.respuesta: 150 mg per dose; 600 mg/day, equal to the 60 mg/kg/day maximum, not above it
calculos.trampa: Giving 150 mg every 4 hours "because the adult interval is 4 to 6 hours" makes 6 doses and 900 mg a day, 50 percent over the pediatric maximum. The daily-maximum check is a separate step, every time, not something the per-dose arithmetic guarantees.

practica.enunciado: 44 lb child, 15 mg/kg every 6 h. Per dose, and daily total vs 60 mg/kg/day?
8 kg infant, 15 mg/kg every 6 h. Per dose and daily maximum?

calculos.titulo: Adult daily maximum: grams and milligrams
calculos.enunciado: An adult takes acetaminophen 1,000 mg every 6 hours around the clock. StatPearls gives the adult dose as 650 to 1,000 mg every 4 to 6 hours with a maximum of 4 grams per day. Is the patient at, under, or over the maximum?

pasos.texto: Four doses of 1,000 mg in 24 hours make 4,000 mg.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Pain Management Medications (analgésicos)

pasos.titulo: Put the maximum in the same unit
pasos.texto: The maximum is stated in grams and the dose in milligrams. Convert one of them before comparing: 4 g × 1,000 mg/g = 4,000 mg.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Dose Calculation Desired Over Have Formula Method

pasos.texto: The patient is exactly at the maximum of 4 grams/day, not over it. Anything added on top, including combination products that also contain acetaminophen, would exceed it.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Pain Management Medications (analgésicos)

pasos.texto: Toxicity develops at 7.5 g/day to 10 g/day, and the drug is considered safe only when used appropriately, which is why the daily total is always checked and documented.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Pain Management Medications (analgésicos)

calculos.respuesta: 4,000 mg/day: exactly at the 4 g maximum
calculos.trampa: Comparing 4,000 with 4 and concluding the patient is a thousand times over (or reading 4 g as 400 mg and concluding he is far under) both come from skipping the unit conversion. Grams and milligrams are compared only after both are in the same unit.

practica.enunciado: 650 mg every 4 hours. Daily total vs the 4 g maximum?
1,000 mg every 4 hours. Daily total vs the 4 g maximum?

calculos.titulo: A daily total divided into doses, then into tablets
calculos.enunciado: The order reads: amoxicillin 1,750 mg per day in divided doses every 12 hours. The clinic stocks 875 mg scored tablets. How many milligrams per dose, and how many tablets per dose?

pasos.titulo: Confirm the daily total is on the label
pasos.formula: 750 to 1,750 mg/day in divided doses every 8 to 12 hours
pasos.texto: The adult range on the label is 750 to 1,750 mg/day divided every 8 to 12 hours, so 1,750 mg/day is the top of the labeled range.
pasos.referencia: DailyMed (NLM/FDA): etiqueta de prescripción — AMOXICILLIN TABLET, COATED [REDPHARM DRUG]

pasos.texto: Every 12 hours is two doses in 24 hours. Each dose is 875 mg.
pasos.referencia: DailyMed (NLM/FDA): etiqueta de prescripción — AMOXICILLIN TABLET, COATED [REDPHARM DRUG]

pasos.formula: D ÷ H × Q = 875 mg ÷ 875 mg × 1 tablet = 1 tablet
pasos.texto: The tablet on hand is 875 mg, film-coated and scored on one side, so one whole tablet is one dose.
pasos.referencia: DailyMed (NLM/FDA): etiqueta de prescripción — AMOXICILLIN TABLET, COATED [REDPHARM DRUG]

pasos.titulo: Check against the label's dosing table
pasos.texto: The table lists 875 mg every 12 hours as a standard adult regimen for severe infections, so the result matches a regimen the manufacturer prints.
pasos.referencia: DailyMed (NLM/FDA): etiqueta de prescripción — AMOXICILLIN TABLET, COATED [REDPHARM DRUG]

calculos.respuesta: 875 mg per dose = 1 tablet every 12 hours
calculos.trampa: Reading "1,750 mg" as the single dose and handing over 2 tablets twice a day doubles the daily total to 3,500 mg. When the order states a per-day amount, the first move is always to divide it by the number of doses.

practica.enunciado: Order 1,500 mg/day every 12 h with 875 mg tablets. Per dose? Can it be made from this tablet?
practica.respuesta: 750 mg; no, 750 ÷ 875 is not a whole or half tablet: call the provider or pharmacy

practica.enunciado: A patient takes 1 tablet of 875 mg every 12 h. Daily total?

calculos.titulo: Grams to milligrams and an extended-release tablet that must not be split
calculos.enunciado: The provider writes metformin extended-release 2 g once daily with the evening meal, which is the label's maximum. The clinic has 1,000 mg extended-release tablets. How many tablets, and what must the patient be told about taking them?

pasos.texto: Multiply grams by 1,000 to get milligrams. The order becomes 2,000 mg.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Dose Calculation Desired Over Have Formula Method

pasos.titulo: Confirm it is within the label
pasos.texto: The label increases the dose in 500 mg steps up to a maximum of 2,000 mg once daily with the evening meal, so 2,000 mg is the ceiling, not above it.
pasos.referencia: DailyMed (NLM/FDA): etiqueta de prescripción — GLUMETZA (METFORMIN HYDROCHLORIDE) TABLET, FILM COATED, EXTENDED RELEASE [SANTARUS, INC.]

pasos.texto: Two 1,000 mg extended-release tablets. The 1,000 mg strength is one of the two the label lists.
pasos.referencia: DailyMed (NLM/FDA): etiqueta de prescripción — GLUMETZA (METFORMIN HYDROCHLORIDE) TABLET, FILM COATED, EXTENDED RELEASE [SANTARUS, INC.]

pasos.titulo: The instruction that goes with the count
pasos.texto: Swallow the tablets whole; never crush, cut or chew an extended-release tablet. The count is right only if each tablet stays intact.
pasos.referencia: DailyMed (NLM/FDA): etiqueta de prescripción — GLUMETZA (METFORMIN HYDROCHLORIDE) TABLET, FILM COATED, EXTENDED RELEASE [SANTARUS, INC.]

calculos.trampa: Treating 2 g as 200 mg (dropping a zero) leads to "a fifth of a tablet", and the fix some people reach for, cutting an extended-release tablet, destroys the release mechanism. Grams to milligrams is times 1,000, and extended-release tablets are never divided.

practica.enunciado: Order: 0.5 g. On hand: 500 mg tablets. Tablets?
Order: 1.5 g. On hand: 500 mg and 1,000 mg extended-release tablets. How is it made up?
practica.respuesta: 1,500 mg = three 500 mg tablets (or one 1,000 + one 500); never half a tablet

calculos.titulo: Epinephrine for anaphylaxis: mg/kg in a child
calculos.enunciado: A 15 kg child develops anaphylaxis after a vaccine. StatPearls gives the pediatric intramuscular dose as 0.01 mg/kg, or a fixed 0.15 mg from a pediatric auto-injector. What weight-based dose does the mg/kg rule give, and does it agree with the fixed dose?

pasos.titulo: Dose per kilogram from the source
pasos.texto: Pediatric dosing is 0.01 mg/kg, or 0.15 mg intramuscularly with the pediatric auto-injector. The thigh is preferred to the deltoid.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Anaphylaxis

pasos.texto: Kilograms cancel. Keep the decimal point where it is: 0.01 times 15 is 0.15, not 1.5.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Anaphylaxis

pasos.titulo: Compare with the fixed pediatric dose
pasos.texto: For a 15 kg child the weight-based dose and the fixed 0.15 mg pediatric auto-injector dose are identical, which is a useful sanity check on the arithmetic.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Anaphylaxis

pasos.titulo: Do not delay for the calculation
pasos.texto: Providers often wait too long before giving epinephrine; it is the treatment of choice, and repeat doses may be given every 5 to 10 minutes if symptoms persist. The math must be fast or pre-computed.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Anaphylaxis

calculos.respuesta: 0.15 mg intramuscular, the same as the fixed pediatric dose
calculos.trampa: Sliding the decimal one place (0.1 mg/kg × 15 kg = 1.5 mg) gives ten times the dose. With doses written as hundredths of a milligram, the decimal is checked twice, and the fixed auto-injector dose on the same line is the reference the answer must land near.

practica.enunciado: 10 kg child, 0.01 mg/kg. Dose in mg?
30 kg child, 0.01 mg/kg. Dose in mg, and how does it compare with the adult 0.3 to 0.5 mg?
practica.respuesta: 0.3 mg: the bottom of the adult range

calculos.titulo: A liquid dose in household measures
calculos.enunciado: A parent will give 10 mL of an oral liquid at home and asks how many teaspoons that is, and how much a tablespoon would be. Convert using the clinical household equivalents.

pasos.texto: The clinical conversion is 1 teaspoon = 5 mL, so 10 mL is 2 teaspoons.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Dose Calculation Desired Over Have Formula Method

pasos.texto: A tablespoon is 15 mL, three times a teaspoon. A tablespoon would deliver 15 mL, half again the ordered 10 mL.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Dose Calculation Desired Over Have Formula Method

pasos.texto: One fluid ounce is 30 mL, or two tablespoons, on the same clinical table.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Dose Calculation Desired Over Have Formula Method

pasos.texto: Patients use the household system (teaspoons and tablespoons) although the medication was dispensed in mL, so the instruction should name both: 10 mL, which is 2 teaspoons of 5 mL each on a marked dosing spoon or oral syringe.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Dose Calculation Desired Over Have Formula Method

calculos.respuesta: 2 teaspoons (10 mL); a tablespoon would be 15 mL
calculos.trampa: Confusing tsp and tbsp on a written instruction triples the dose (15 mL for 5 mL). Write the words out, and remember that NIST measures an actual kitchen teaspoon at about 4.93 mL: the clinical 5 mL is a convention, which is why a marked oral syringe beats the silverware.

practica.enunciado: 7.5 mL in teaspoons?
2 tablespoons in mL and in fluid ounces?

calculos.titulo: Weight: pounds to kilograms (and why two factors exist)
calculos.enunciado: The scale reads 154 lb and the chart, the growth record and every mg/kg order need kilograms. Convert with the clinical factor, then check with the NIST factor.

pasos.texto: Pounds divided by 2.2 gives kilograms. 154 lb is 70 kg exactly.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Dose Calculation Desired Over Have Formula Method

pasos.texto: NIST's approximate conversion card multiplies pounds by 0.45 to get kilograms, giving 69.3 kg. It is rounded to two digits, which is why it comes out 0.7 kg lower than the clinical answer.
pasos.referencia: NIST Office of Weights and Measures: Approximate Conversions from U.S. Customary Measures to Metric

pasos.texto: Dose-calculation sources teach 2.2 pounds = 1 kg, and exam items are written with it; the NIST card is a rounded classroom aid. When the division does not come out whole, round to the nearest tenth of a kilogram and say so.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Pharmacy Calculations

calculos.respuesta: 70 kg (69.3 kg with the rounded NIST factor)
calculos.trampa: Multiplying by 2.2 (154 × 2.2 = 338.8) instead of dividing gives a number that is bigger, not smaller. Kilograms are always fewer than pounds: if the kg figure is larger, the operation was backwards.

practica.enunciado: 110 lb in kg?
187 lb in kg?

calculos.titulo: Weight: kilograms to pounds for the patient
calculos.enunciado: A patient weighed on a metric scale is 80 kg and asks what that is in pounds. Convert.

pasos.titulo: Set up the factor the other way
pasos.texto: Going from kilograms to pounds, multiply by 2.2: the number gets larger, as pounds should.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Dose Calculation Desired Over Have Formula Method

pasos.texto: 80 kilograms is 176 pounds.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Pharmacy Calculations

pasos.texto: Dividing the answer by 2.2 returns the original 80 kg, so the direction was right.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Dose Calculation Desired Over Have Formula Method

calculos.trampa: Dividing (80 ÷ 2.2 = 36.4) tells the patient he weighs 36 pounds. The check that catches it is the same as always: pounds must be the larger number.

practica.enunciado: 65 kg in lb?
102 kg in lb (nearest tenth)?

calculos.titulo: Height: feet and inches to centimeters
calculos.enunciado: An adult measures 5 ft 8 in on the stadiometer. Record the height in centimeters, to the nearest tenth.

pasos.texto: Five feet is 60 inches; with the extra 8 inches the height is 68 inches.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Dose Calculation Desired Over Have Formula Method

pasos.texto: Multiply inches by 2.54, the exact inch-to-centimeter factor NIST lists.
pasos.referencia: NIST Office of Weights and Measures: Approximate Conversions from U.S. Customary Measures to Metric

pasos.titulo: Round as the measurement is read
pasos.texto: Height is read to 0.1 cm (or one-eighth of an inch) on the stadiometer, so the converted value is recorded to the nearest tenth: 172.7 cm.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Anthropometric Measurement

calculos.trampa: Typing 5.8 into the calculator and multiplying by 30.48 (the foot factor) gives 176.8 cm, almost two inches too tall: 5 ft 8 in is not 5.8 ft. Convert the mixed unit to inches first.

practica.enunciado: 5 ft 2 in in cm?
6 ft 0 in in cm?

calculos.titulo: Small weights: ounces to grams
calculos.enunciado: A 2-week-old is 6 oz lighter than at the last visit, and the provider wants the change in grams. Convert.

pasos.texto: NIST lists ounce × 28.35 = grams.
pasos.referencia: NIST Office of Weights and Measures: Approximate Conversions from U.S. Customary Measures to Metric

pasos.texto: Six ounces is 170.1 grams; recorded as 170 g if the scale reads to the gram.
pasos.referencia: NIST Office of Weights and Measures: Approximate Conversions from U.S. Customary Measures to Metric

pasos.titulo: Keep ounces and fluid ounces apart
pasos.texto: The ounce here is a weight (16 oz = 1 lb). The fluid ounce used for intake (30 mL clinical) is a different unit that happens to share the name.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Dose Calculation Desired Over Have Formula Method

calculos.trampa: Reaching for the fluid-ounce factor (6 × 30 = 180 mL) confuses a weight with a volume. Infant weights are in pounds and ounces or in kilograms and grams, never in milliliters.

practica.enunciado: 10 oz in grams?
4 oz in grams?

calculos.titulo: Intake: fluid ounces to milliliters
calculos.enunciado: A patient drank an 8 fl oz cup of water. Record the intake in milliliters, and explain why one reference says 240 mL and another says about 237 mL.

pasos.texto: The dose-calculation table gives 8 oz = 240 mL = 1 glass, built on the clinical 1 oz = 30 mL.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Dose Calculation Desired Over Have Formula Method

pasos.texto: NIST's factor for the fluid ounce is 29.57 mL, so 8 fl oz is 236.56 mL, about 237 mL.
pasos.referencia: NIST Office of Weights and Measures: Approximate Conversions from U.S. Customary Measures to Metric

pasos.texto: Intake and output charts and exam items use the clinical 30 mL per ounce: 240 mL. The 3 mL difference per cup is below what an intake record resolves; what matters is using one convention consistently on the same chart.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Pharmacy Calculations

calculos.respuesta: 240 mL on the intake record (236.6 mL by the NIST factor)
calculos.trampa: Mixing the two conventions on one chart (240 for one cup, 237 for the next) makes totals look like arithmetic errors. Pick the clinical 30 mL per ounce and stay with it.

practica.enunciado: 4 fl oz in mL (clinical)?
A 12 fl oz can in mL (clinical)?

calculos.titulo: Household to metric: tablespoons to milliliters for a total quantity
calculos.enunciado: A liquid is to be taken 1 tablespoon twice daily for 10 days. How many milliliters must be dispensed to cover the course?

pasos.texto: The clinical equivalent of a tablespoon is 15 mL.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Pharmacy Calculations

pasos.texto: Twice daily is two tablespoons, 30 mL a day (which is also 1 fluid ounce).
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Dose Calculation Desired Over Have Formula Method

pasos.texto: Ten days of two 15 mL tablespoons is 300 mL to dispense.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Dose Calculation Desired Over Have Formula Method

pasos.texto: Three teaspoons of 5 mL each also make 15 mL, so a household measuring spoon set gives the same dose either way.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Dose Calculation Desired Over Have Formula Method

calculos.trampa: Reading tbsp as tsp gives 5 mL × 2 × 10 = 100 mL, one third of the course, and the patient runs out on day 4. On a hand-written label, spell out "tablespoon" and give the mL.

practica.enunciado: 1 tsp three times daily for 7 days. mL to dispense?
2 tbsp twice daily for 5 days. mL?

calculos.titulo: Temperature: Fahrenheit to Celsius at the fever threshold
calculos.enunciado: A tympanic reading is 100.4 °F. The chart is kept in Celsius. Convert it, and say what that value means.

pasos.texto: NIST gives the exact conversion from Fahrenheit to Celsius as (°F − 32) / 1.8.
pasos.referencia: NIST Office of Weights and Measures: SI Units — Temperature (fórmulas °C/°F/K)

pasos.texto: 100.4 minus 32 is 68.4; divided by 1.8 gives exactly 38.0 °C.
pasos.referencia: NIST Office of Weights and Measures: SI Units — Temperature (fórmulas °C/°F/K)

pasos.texto: StatPearls states it as subtract 32, multiply by 5, divide by 9; 5/9 and 1/1.8 are the same number.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Pharmacy Calculations

pasos.texto: A temperature over 100.4 °F (38 °C) most often means a fever caused by an infection or illness; 38.0 °C is exactly that threshold.
pasos.referencia: MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia: Body temperature norms (001982)

calculos.trampa: Dividing before subtracting (100.4 ÷ 1.8 − 32 = 23.8) or subtracting 32 after dividing by 9/5 both give impossible body temperatures. The 32 always comes off first when going from °F to °C.

calculos.titulo: Temperature: Celsius to Fahrenheit and the normal range
calculos.enunciado: An oral temperature of 37.2 °C must be reported to a patient who thinks in Fahrenheit. Convert it and place it against the normal range.

pasos.texto: NIST gives the exact conversion from Celsius to Fahrenheit as (°C × 1.8) + 32.
pasos.referencia: NIST Office of Weights and Measures: SI Units — Temperature (fórmulas °C/°F/K)

pasos.texto: Multiply by 1.8, then add 32. Rounded to the nearest tenth, 99.0 °F.
pasos.referencia: NIST Office of Weights and Measures: SI Units — Temperature (fórmulas °C/°F/K)

pasos.titulo: Place it in the normal range
pasos.texto: MedlinePlus gives the average normal as 98.6 °F (37 °C) with a range from 97 °F (36.1 °C) to 99 °F (37.2 °C); 37.2 °C sits at the top of that normal range, not in fever territory.
pasos.referencia: MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia: Body temperature norms (001982)

pasos.texto: NIST's reference table lists body temperature as 37 °C, 310 K and 99 °F (rounded), with freezing at 0 °C = 32 °F and boiling at 100 °C = 212 °F: three checkpoints for catching a wrong conversion.
pasos.referencia: NIST Office of Weights and Measures: SI Units — Temperature (fórmulas °C/°F/K)

calculos.respuesta: 99.0 °F, at the upper end of normal
calculos.trampa: Adding 32 before multiplying (37.2 + 32 = 69.2 × 1.8 = 124.6 °F) produces a reading no living patient has. Going from °C to °F the multiplication comes first and the 32 is added last.

practica.enunciado: 36.1 °C in °F (nearest tenth)?

calculos.titulo: Adult BMI in metric units and its category
calculos.enunciado: An adult weighs 70 kg and measures 1.75 m. Calculate the body mass index and name the CDC category it falls in.

pasos.texto: CDC's metric formula is weight in kilograms divided by height in meters squared.
pasos.referencia: CDC: BMI Frequently Asked Questions

pasos.texto: Height squared is 3.0625 m². 70 divided by 3.0625 is 22.857; CDC reports BMI to one decimal (its own worked example is 30.4), so 22.9.
pasos.referencia: CDC: BMI Frequently Asked Questions

pasos.texto: For adults 20 and older the categories apply regardless of age or sex: 22.9 sits inside 18.5 to 24.9, Healthy Weight.
pasos.referencia: CDC: Adult BMI Calculator (categorías)

pasos.texto: BMI is a screening measure and is not intended to diagnose disease or illness; the category is recorded and left to the provider to discuss with the patient.
pasos.referencia: CDC: Adult BMI Calculator (categorías)

calculos.trampa: Dividing by the height once (70 ÷ 1.75 = 40) instead of by the height squared gives an alarming 40 that would be class 3 obesity. The height is squared every time; a BMI of 40 for a 70 kg adult should stop you.

practica.enunciado: 55 kg, 1.60 m. BMI and category?
95 kg, 1.80 m. BMI and category?

calculos.titulo: Adult BMI from pounds and inches: the 703 factor
calculos.enunciado: An adult is 5 ft 8 in tall and weighs 200 lb. Calculate the BMI in U.S. customary units and classify it. (This is the example CDC works in its BMI FAQ.)

pasos.texto: CDC's formula for pounds and inches divides weight by height squared and multiplies by 703; the 703 converts the lb/in² result to kg/m².
pasos.referencia: CDC: BMI Frequently Asked Questions

pasos.texto: Five feet eight inches is 68 inches, and 68 squared is 4,624. The 703 applies only to inches: never to feet, never to centimeters.
pasos.referencia: CDC: BMI Frequently Asked Questions

pasos.texto: 200 divided by 4,624 is 0.04325; times 703 is 30.41. CDC's FAQ gives exactly 30.4 for an adult who is 5 feet 8 inches and 200 pounds.
pasos.referencia: CDC: BMI Frequently Asked Questions

pasos.texto: 30.4 is at or above 30.0, so the category is Obesity (class 1, 30.0 to 34.9).
pasos.referencia: CDC: Adult BMI Calculator (categorías)

calculos.trampa: Forgetting the 703 gives 0.04, and applying 703 to a height in centimeters gives a number in the thousands. Metric inputs use the plain kg/m² formula; the 703 exists only for pounds and inches.

practica.enunciado: 150 lb, 5 ft 4 in. BMI and category?
180 lb, 6 ft 0 in. BMI and category?

calculos.titulo: Adult BMI from kilograms and centimeters: the 10,000 factor
calculos.enunciado: The stadiometer reads 168 cm and the scale 82 kg. Calculate the BMI directly from centimeters, without converting to meters first, and classify it.

pasos.titulo: CDC's centimeter form of the metric formula
pasos.texto: Dividing by the height in centimeters twice and multiplying by 10,000 is the same as dividing by meters squared, because 100² is 10,000.
pasos.referencia: CDC: BMI Frequently Asked Questions
CDC: BMI Frequently Asked Questions

pasos.texto: 29.1 falls in 25.0 to 29.9, Overweight, just under the 30.0 obesity line.
pasos.referencia: CDC: Adult BMI Calculator (categorías)

pasos.texto: People with a lot of muscle can land in the overweight (25.0 to less than 30.0) or obesity category because BMI cannot distinguish fat, muscle and bone; the category is reported, not judged.
pasos.referencia: CDC: BMI Frequently Asked Questions

calculos.trampa: Forgetting the × 10,000 leaves 0.0029, and dividing by 168 only once gives 0.49. Using centimeters means two divisions and one multiplication by 10,000; using meters means one division by the square.

practica.enunciado: 60 kg, 165 cm. BMI?
100 kg, 180 cm. BMI and category?

calculos.titulo: Obesity classes: where a BMI of 39.8 falls
calculos.enunciado: An adult weighs 115 kg and is 1.70 m tall. Calculate the BMI and state the obesity class, paying attention to the rounding.

pasos.texto: Weight in kilograms over height in meters squared.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Anthropometric Measurement

pasos.texto: 39.79 rounds to 39.8, which sits inside the 35.0 to 39.9 band.
pasos.referencia: CDC: Adult BMI Calculator (categorías)

pasos.texto: Obesity is subdivided: class 1 is 30.0 to 34.9, class 2 is 35.0 to 39.9, class 3 (severe obesity) starts at 40.0. 39.8 is class 2.
pasos.referencia: CDC: Adult BMI Calculator (categorías)

pasos.titulo: Do not round into the next class
pasos.texto: Class 3 is 40.0 or greater. Rounding 39.8 to "about 40" would move the patient into severe obesity on paper; the category is read from the one-decimal value.
pasos.referencia: CDC: Adult BMI Calculator (categorías)

calculos.trampa: Rounding to a whole number before classifying puts 39.8 at 40 and class 3, and puts 34.95 at 35 and class 2 when it is class 1. Classify with the value to one decimal, exactly as the CDC table is written.

practica.enunciado: 92 kg, 1.65 m. BMI and class?
125 kg, 1.75 m. BMI and class?

calculos.titulo: Child BMI: same number, different reading (BMI-for-age percentile)
calculos.enunciado: A 7-year-old girl weighs 26 kg and measures 1.20 m. Her BMI plots at the 88th percentile on the CDC girls' BMI-for-age chart, where the 95th percentile for her age is 21.0 kg/m². Calculate her BMI, classify it, and state the threshold for severe obesity at her age.

pasos.titulo: Calculate the BMI the same way as for an adult
pasos.texto: BMI is recommended for all children older than 2 years and is computed with the same formula as adults: weight over height squared, 18.1 kg/m² here.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Anthropometric Measurement

pasos.titulo: Read the percentile, not the adult table
pasos.texto: CDC's own example is a 7-year-old girl at the 88th percentile: her BMI is the same or higher than 88 percent of 7-year-old girls in the reference population, and she falls in the overweight category, defined as the 85th to less than the 95th percentile.
pasos.referencia: CDC: BMI Frequently Asked Questions

pasos.formula: Overweight: 85th to less than the 95th percentile
pasos.texto: Underweight is below the 5th percentile, healthy weight the 5th to less than the 85th, overweight the 85th to less than the 95th, and obesity the 95th percentile or greater.
pasos.referencia: CDC: BMI Calculator for Children and Teens

pasos.titulo: Severe obesity threshold at her age
pasos.texto: Severe obesity is 120 percent of the 95th percentile or greater, or a BMI of 35 kg/m² or greater. With a 95th percentile of 21.0 for her age, 120 percent of it is 25.2.
pasos.referencia: CDC: BMI Calculator for Children and Teens

calculos.respuesta: BMI 18.1 kg/m²: Overweight (88th percentile); severe obesity would start at 25.2 at her age
calculos.trampa: Reading 18.1 against the adult table (18.5 to 24.9 healthy) would call this child underweight. For ages 2 through 19 the number means nothing until it is placed on the sex- and age-specific percentile chart; the same BMI can be healthy at 12 and overweight at 7.

practica.enunciado: Boy, 20 kg, 1.10 m, at the 96th percentile. BMI and category?
95th percentile for a child's age is 20.5. Severe-obesity threshold?

calculos.titulo: EKG heart rate: 300 divided by the large squares
calculos.enunciado: On a regular rhythm strip, there are 4 large squares between two consecutive R waves. What is the heart rate, and is it in the normal range?

pasos.formula: rate = 300 ÷ number of large squares between R waves
pasos.texto: The rate can be calculated by dividing 300 by the number of big squares between two R waves.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Electrocardiogram

pasos.texto: Four large squares gives 75 bpm. Counting from one R wave to the next, the square the second R wave sits on is not counted twice.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Electrocardiogram

pasos.texto: Normal heart rate is 60 to 99 beats per minute; less than 60 is bradycardia, greater than 100 tachycardia. 75 is normal.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Electrocardiogram

pasos.formula: 25 mm/s → 5 large squares per second → 300 per minute
pasos.texto: The paper moves at 25 mm/sec; one second is five large squares of 0.2 sec, so a minute is 300 large squares. That is why the rule only works at standard paper speed.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Electrocardiogram

calculos.trampa: Counting small squares and dividing by 300 (20 small squares → 15 bpm) or counting large squares and dividing by 1500 (→ 375 bpm) both come from mixing the two rules. 300 goes with the large squares, 1500 with the small ones.

practica.enunciado: 3 large squares between R waves. Rate?
5 large squares between R waves. Rate?

calculos.titulo: EKG heart rate: 1500 divided by the small squares
calculos.enunciado: The R-R interval on a regular strip spans 18 small squares. Calculate the rate with the small-square method and show that it agrees with the large-square method.

pasos.formula: rate = 1500 ÷ number of small squares between R waves
pasos.texto: Alternatively, divide 1500 by the number of small squares between two R waves. This is the more precise of the two methods when the interval is not a whole number of large squares.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Electrocardiogram

pasos.texto: 1500 divided by 18 is 83.3; heart rate is reported as a whole number, so 83 bpm.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Electrocardiogram

pasos.texto: Each large square (0.2 s) is divided into five small squares, so 18 small squares are 3.6 large squares, and 300 ÷ 3.6 gives the same 83.3.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Electrocardiogram

pasos.titulo: Why the small-square count is worth the effort
pasos.texto: One small box is 40 milliseconds. Rounding the interval to "about 4 large squares" would report 75 bpm instead of 83; the small squares carry the precision.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Electrocardiogram

calculos.trampa: Counting the small squares inside the R-R interval but dividing by 300 gives 16.7 "bpm". The divisor follows the unit counted: small squares, 1500.

practica.enunciado: 25 small squares. Rate?
12 small squares. Rate?

calculos.titulo: EKG heart rate on an irregular rhythm: beats in 10 seconds times 6
calculos.enunciado: A rhythm strip is irregularly irregular. In the standard 10-second strip you count 12 QRS complexes. What is the heart rate, and why not use the 300 rule here?

pasos.texto: The routine recording is a standard 10-second strip; that fixed length is what makes the multiplication work.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Electrocardiogram

pasos.texto: For an irregular rhythm, count the number of beats in a 10-second strip and multiply by 6 (six 10-second periods in a minute).
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Electrocardiogram

pasos.titulo: Why the R-R methods fail here
pasos.texto: The 300 and 1500 rules measure one R-R interval and assume every interval is the same. When the intervals vary, one interval is not the rate; the 10-second count averages them.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Electrocardiogram

pasos.texto: 72 is within the normal adult resting range of 60 to 100 bpm. An irregularly irregular pattern is characteristic of atrial fibrillation and is reported to the provider regardless of the rate.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Vital Sign Assessment

calculos.trampa: Applying 300 ÷ squares to the one R-R interval that happens to be easiest to read gives a rate for that beat only; on an irregular strip the answer can swing from 50 to 120 depending on which interval is picked. Irregular rhythm means count the strip.

practica.enunciado: 9 beats in 10 seconds. Rate?
19 beats in 10 seconds. Rate?

calculos.titulo: EKG heart rate from the R-R interval in seconds
calculos.enunciado: The R-R interval on a regular strip measures 6 large squares. Express the interval in seconds, derive the rate from it, and classify the rhythm's rate.

pasos.formula: 1 large square = 0.2 s;  1 small square = 0.04 s
pasos.texto: At 25 mm/sec each large square represents 0.2 sec and each small square 0.04 sec.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Electrocardiogram

pasos.texto: Six large squares is 1.2 seconds between beats (equivalently 30 small squares × 0.04 s).
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Electrocardiogram

pasos.titulo: Beats per minute from seconds per beat
pasos.texto: Sixty seconds divided by 1.2 seconds per beat is 50 beats per minute, identical to the 300-rule result.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Electrocardiogram

pasos.texto: 50 bpm is below 60, so the rate is bradycardic; whether that matters depends on the patient (athletes and sleep are common benign causes) and is for the provider to judge.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Electrocardiogram

calculos.trampa: Reading a large square as 0.04 s (the small-square value) makes a 6-square interval 0.24 s and a rate of 250 bpm. Large square, 0.2 s; small square, 0.04 s; the two differ by a factor of five, exactly like 300 and 1500.

practica.enunciado: R-R interval of 4 large squares. Seconds and rate?
R-R interval of 15 small squares. Seconds and rate?

calculos.titulo: Infant weight: pounds and ounces to kilograms
calculos.enunciado: A newborn's birth weight is recorded as 7 lb 8 oz. Convert it to kilograms for the metric record and for any weight-based dose.

pasos.titulo: Ounces to a fraction of a pound
pasos.texto: There are 16 ounces in a pound, so 8 ounces is half a pound and the weight is 7.5 lb.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Dose Calculation Desired Over Have Formula Method

pasos.texto: Divide the 7.5 lb by 2.2 to get kilograms: 3.409 kg before rounding.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Dose Calculation Desired Over Have Formula Method

pasos.titulo: Round as infant weights are recorded
pasos.texto: For children under 2 the weight is measured to the nearest 0.01 kg or 0.5 ounce, so record 3.41 kg.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Anthropometric Measurement

calculos.trampa: Reading 7 lb 8 oz as 7.8 lb (as if ounces were tenths) gives 3.55 kg, 140 g too heavy: enough to shift a growth-chart percentile or a mg/kg dose. Ounces are sixteenths of a pound, not tenths.

practica.enunciado: 6 lb 4 oz in kg?
8 lb 12 oz in kg?

calculos.titulo: Height: centimeters back to feet and inches
calculos.enunciado: A patient's height is recorded as 165 cm and she asks what that is in feet and inches. Convert.

pasos.texto: Divide centimeters by 2.54 to get inches: 64.96 in.
pasos.referencia: NIST Office of Weights and Measures: Approximate Conversions from U.S. Customary Measures to Metric

pasos.texto: Twelve inches make a foot: 5 × 12 = 60, leaving 4.96 inches.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Dose Calculation Desired Over Have Formula Method

pasos.titulo: Round to the resolution of the measurement
pasos.texto: Height is read to 0.1 cm or one-eighth of an inch, and 4.96 is within an eighth of 5, so 5 ft 5 in.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Anthropometric Measurement

calculos.trampa: Reporting 64.96 in as "6 ft 4.96 in" comes from dividing by 10 instead of 12, and reporting "5.4 ft" for 5 ft 5 in comes from treating the remainder as a decimal. Feet and inches are a base-12 pair.

practica.enunciado: 180 cm in feet and inches?
152.4 cm in feet and inches?

calculos.titulo: Mean arterial pressure and the blood pressure category
calculos.enunciado: A seated reading is 130/85 mm Hg. Calculate the mean arterial pressure and place the reading in its NHLBI category.

pasos.texto: Mean arterial pressure is the diastolic pressure plus one third of the pulse pressure (systolic minus diastolic); it approximates the average tissue perfusion pressure.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Vital Sign Assessment

pasos.texto: The difference is 45; one third of 45 is 15; added to the diastolic 85 gives 100 mm Hg.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Vital Sign Assessment

pasos.formula: 130 to 139 systolic OR 80 to 89 diastolic = Stage 1
pasos.texto: 130/85 meets Stage 1 on both numbers: systolic 130 to 139, and diastolic 80 to 89. Either one alone is enough, because the rule is OR.
pasos.referencia: NHLBI: High Blood Pressure - Diagnosis

pasos.titulo: One reading is not a diagnosis
pasos.texto: The ACC/AHA definition of hypertension is 130/80 mm Hg or greater, confirmed with 3 or more measurements at separate visits; the medical assistant records and flags, the provider diagnoses.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Vital Sign Assessment

calculos.respuesta: MAP 100 mm Hg; Stage 1 range (130 to 139 or 80 to 89)
calculos.trampa: Averaging the two numbers ((130 + 85) ÷ 2 = 107.5) overstates the MAP because the heart spends longer in diastole; the formula weights the diastolic twice. And a systolic of 128 with a diastolic of 85 is still Stage 1: the OR means the higher category wins.

practica.enunciado: 110/70. MAP and category?

calculos.titulo: Orthostatic vital signs: is the drop significant?
calculos.enunciado: After 5 minutes supine a patient's blood pressure is 128/82 mm Hg. Standing, measured within 1 to 3 minutes, it is 104/76 mm Hg. Calculate the changes and say whether they meet the definition of orthostatic hypotension.

pasos.titulo: The protocol the numbers come from
pasos.formula: supine ≈ 5 min → stand → measure within 1 to 3 min
pasos.texto: Orthostatic blood pressure is measured after the patient has been supine for approximately 5 minutes and again within 1 to 3 minutes of standing.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Vital Sign Assessment

pasos.texto: The systolic pressure fell 24 mm Hg, which is at or beyond the 20 mm Hg criterion.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Vital Sign Assessment

pasos.texto: The diastolic fell 6 mm Hg, short of the 10 mm Hg criterion on its own.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Vital Sign Assessment

pasos.texto: Orthostatic hypotension is a decrease of 20 or greater mm Hg systolic or 10 mm Hg or higher diastolic within 3 minutes of standing. The systolic criterion alone is met, so the finding is positive and is reported.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Vital Sign Assessment

calculos.respuesta: Systolic −24, diastolic −6: positive for orthostatic hypotension (systolic criterion met)
calculos.trampa: Requiring both numbers to drop ("the diastolic only fell 6, so it's negative") misreads the OR in the definition. And measuring the standing pressure at 5 minutes instead of within 1 to 3 can miss a drop that has already recovered.

practica.enunciado: Supine 118/78, standing 102/66. Positive?
Supine 134/84, standing 120/78. Positive?
practica.respuesta: No: 14 systolic and 6 diastolic, both under threshold
